Org. Setting and Reporting
In its Resolution A/RES/72/279, the United Nations General Assembly endorsed the transformation of the Development Operations Coordination Office (DCO) as a stand-alone coordination office within the United Nations Secretariat. DCO exercises managerial and oversight functions of the resident coordinator system under the oversight of the Chair of United Nations Sustainable Development Group (UNSDG). In 2026, DCO undertook a recalibration to ensure the RC system remains optimally configured to support the acceleration of the 2030 Agenda and embodies the UN 2.0 shift- anchored in data, digital, innovation, behavioral science, strategic foresight, and a mission-driven organizational culture. The position is located in the Leave No One Behind Unit under the Development Programme Cycle Section in the United Nations Development Coordination Office (UNDCO) in New York and reports to the Chief, Development Programme Cycle Section. The Human Rights Officer works closely with the other sections under the Policy, Programme, and Data Division, as well as with OHCHR and other entities of the UN system as required. The proposed position would focus on four areas: 1. Strategic human rights policy advice to DCO, Resident Coordinators and UN Country Teams. 2. Human rights mainstreaming in Common Country Analyses and Cooperation Frameworks. 3. System-wide coordination and partnerships with OHCHR, UNSDG entities and other stakeholders. 4. Normative analysis and guidance, including relevant international human rights mechanisms and recommendations.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Human Rights Officer will be responsible for the following duties: 1. Strategic human rights policy advice to DCO, Resident Coordinators and UN Country Teams. • Advises the United Nations Sustainable Development Group's (UNSDG) efforts on policy development and guidance on human rights and the normative agenda for Resident Coordinators (RCs) and United Nations Country Teams (UNCTs), as the lead focal point for relevant human rights and normative agenda task forces and working groups. • Manage the collection and evaluation of multi-source information to identify human rights trends and measure implementation of international obligations and human rights mechanism recommendations. 2. Human rights mainstreaming in Common Country Analyses and Cooperation Frameworks. • Provide advice on policy and strategies, and technical guidance to integrate human rights—including gender equality and leave-no-one-behind—into UN country analysis, United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Frameworks, humanitarian planning and other preparedness, response and recovery tools. • Supports the Section's efforts to champion UN 2.0 approaches, including foresight, innovation, data, digitalisation (including harnessing Artificial Intelligence (AI)), and behavioural science, and to advance the uptake at national level, via RCs and UNCTs, to identify potential pathways for systems transformations. 3. System-wide coordination and partnerships with OHCHR, UNSDG entities and other stakeholders. • Lead and coordinate the office's partnership building and creation of new partnerships. • Leads system-wide integrated policy support to RCs and UNCTs on coordination and policy matters on the Secretary-General's Call to Action on human rights and the normative agenda, ensuring an effective policy-practice feedback loop on sustainable development policy matters; brief representatives and provides, as appropriate suggestions and recommendations. • Normative analysis and guidance, including relevant international human rights mechanisms and recommendations. • Coordinate and lead the support to UN Country Team /Humanitarian Country Team and national partners in engaging with and following up on UPR, treaty bodies, special procedures and regional mechanisms. • Lead and coordinate substantive research, analysis, guidance and policy advice on human rights issues in the context of economic policy and sustainable development, with a focus on poverty, inequalities and development financing, including as relevant to UN Common Country Analysis and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Frameworks. • Ensures up-to-date information regarding substantive matters in the field of human rights and makes recommendations for RCs and UNCTs on actions to take. • Collect and analyse data to identify trends or patterns and provide insights through graphs, charts, tables, and report using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation, and reporting. • Design and coordinate the capacity building initiatives for the UN Country Team / Humanitarian Country Team to apply a human rights-based approach, including through theme groups and tailored training. • Performs other related duties as required. Work implies frequent interaction with the following: Counterparts in OHCHR, EOSG, UNSSC Staff of specialized agencies, UNHCR, representatives of non-governmental organisations, regional intergovernmental organisations, etc. University professors, students and interested public Results Expected: Takes a lead role in identifying the underlying cause of human rights violations; negotiates with conflicting factions to identify causes of human rights violations and discusses possible bases for resolution. Serves as an effective spokesperson, and forms strong partnerships with relevant parties involved to engender support for and advance the institution's human rights agenda.
Competencies
• PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of and exposure to a range of human rights issues including approaches and techniques to address sensitive and complex human rights problems in their political, ethnic, racial, gender and socio-economic dimensions. Knowledge of institutional mandates of human rights organizations, prevailing policies and procedures. Ability to evaluate and integrate information from a variety of sources and assess impact on the human rights situation in the region or country of assignment, including the political environment and legal statutes as they pertain to human rights. Ability to complete in-depth studies and reach conclusions on possible causes and solutions to human rights problems in specific societies and systems. Demonstrated skills in training civil authorities and members of advocacy groups to recognize warning signs of civil unrest and take preventive action to avert hostilities. Ability to relate to human rights issues and perspectives, including their gender equality dimensions, to political, social, economic and humanitarian programmes in affected countries and areas. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. • COMMUNICATION: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. • TEAMWORK: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others' ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings.
Education
Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in law, political science, international relations, social sciences or related field. A first-level university degree in combination with qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Successful completion of both degree and non-degree programs in data analytics, business analytics or data science programs is an advantage.
Job - Specific Qualification
Not available.
Work Experience
A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in human rights, political affairs, international relations, law or related area is required. Demonstrated experience with the sustainable development programme cycle is required. A minimum of five years experience with human rights based approaches to sustainable development is required. Field experience with the UN or a related international organisation is desirable. Two years or more of experience in data analytics or related area is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. In this context, all staff are expected to move periodically to new functions in their careers in accordance with established rules and procedures. This information is the basis for the hiring manager to assess your eligibility and suitability for the position and to contact you. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. The United Nations is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. The United Nations recruits and employs staff regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, religious, cultural and ethnic backgrounds or disabilities. Reasonable accommodation for applicants with disabilities may be provided to support participation in the recruitment process when requested and indicated in the application. Subject to the funding source of the position, the eligibility for this temporary job opening may be limited to candidates based at the duty station. This temporary job opening may be limited to "internal candidates," who have been recruited through a competitive examination administered according to staff rule 4.16 or staff selection process including the review of a central review body established according to staff rule 4.15. Staff members of the United Nations common system organizations who will reach the mandatory age of separation or retirement within the duration of the current temporary need period are not eligible to apply. Submitting an application or selection for the current temporary job opening does not delay or increase the mandatory age of separation. Retirees above the mandatory age of separation who wish to be considered for the current temporary job opening must indicate the reason for their last separation as "retirement." Such retirees shall not be employed by the Organization, unless (a) the operational requirements of the Organization cannot be met by staff members who are qualified and available to perform the required functions; and (b) the proposed employment would not adversely affect the career development or redeployment opportunities of other staff members and represents both a cost-effective and operationally sound solution to meet the needs of the service. .
United Nations Considerations
According to article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. Candidates will not be considered for employment with the United Nations if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. The term “sexual exploitation” means any actual or attempted abuse of a position of vulnerability, differential power, or trust, for sexual purposes, including, but not limited to, profiting monetarily, socially or politically from the sexual exploitation of another. The term “sexual abuse” means the actual or threatened physical intrusion of a sexual nature, whether by force or under unequal or coercive conditions. Further, staff members in the Professional and higher category up to and including the D-2 level and the Field Service category are normally required to move periodically to discharge functions in different duty stations under conditions established in ST/AI/2023/3 on Mobility, as may be amended or revised. Org. Setting and Reporting
These positions are located within the United Nations Support Office in Haiti (UNSOH). Pursuant to Security Council resolution 2793 (2025), UNSOH has been mandated to provide support; primarily to the Gang Suppression Force (GSF), the United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH), the Haitian National Police (HNP), and the Haitian Armed Forces in the context of any joint operations with the GSF. Additionally, UNSOH is tasked with delivering technical assistance to the Organization of American States (OAS). The incumbent will perform the following main duty(ies): Provision of air transport services in support of activities of a field mission in accordance with the functional responsibilities of the Mission Air Operations Centre. These positions are based in Port au Prince and located in the Aviation Unit of the Office of the Chief Service Delivery and report to the Chief, Mission Air Operations Center (MAOC) under delegated authority from Chief of Unit- Air Operations- P4.
Responsibilities

Competencies
Professionalism: Knowledge of diverse aviation operations. Knowledge of aviation industry procurement and logistics processes. Knowledge of institutional mandates, ICAO Standards and Recommended Practices and Annexes of the Chicago Convention, policies and guidelines pertaining to air transport operations and related matters. Ability to review alternative options and select most effective and cost-efficient mode of transport of equipment, supplies and personnel. The ability to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. Shows pride in work and achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; Solicits input by genuinely valuing others' ideas and expertise; Is willing to learn from others; Places team agenda before personal agenda; Supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; Shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. Planning and Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; Identifies priority activities and assignments and adjusts priorities as required; Allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; Foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; Monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; Uses time efficiently.
Education
High school diploma or equivalent is required.
Job - Specific Qualification
Training and certification as a Commercial or Private Pilot, or a Flight Operations Officer/Flight Dispatcher, or an Aircraft Maintenance Technician, or a Ground Operations Officer, or an equivalent military qualification is required. Training in quality management is desirable.
Work Experience
A minimum of eight (8) years of progressively responsible experience in air transport operations or aviation safety is required. Experience in the use of ICAO standards and recommended practices is required. Experience in aircraft operation and aircraft contract management is required. Experience in international operations in a post conflict environment is desirable.

Duties and Responsibilities
The Department of Global Communications is responsible for informing the public, civil society and Member States with trusted information and communicating the UN story around the world through its global networks and United Nations Information Centres and Services. The internship is in the Strategic Impact and Innovation Section of the Office of the Under-Secretary-General (OUSG), Department of Global Communications (DGC). The team translates the Department's strategic objectives into practical workflows and measurable outcomes by strengthening cross-divisional collaboration and integrating innovation, impact measurement and insights across programmatic areas. Its work includes guiding the ethical and responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the Department, leading public messaging and communications on AI, convening the inter-agency UN Communications Group AI Lab, monitoring global AI communications trends, and piloting innovative content and outreach formats in line with UN 2.0. The internship is for three (3) months with an opportunity for extension up to six (6) months maximum, depending on the needs of the Section and the availability of the candidate. The internship is unpaid and full-time. Interns work five days a week (35 hours), in person or in a hybrid format, under the supervision of the AI lead in the Section. Under the supervision of the AI lead, the selected intern may perform some of the following functions: • UNCG AI Lab: Support the monthly inter-agency AI Lab meetings, including agendas, notes, follow-up actions and logistics. Document challenges, solutions and pilots shared by participating agencies. Support the research of sub-themes related to the group, ranging from content provenance and disclosure standards to AI visibility to agentic AI. • AI Governance Group: Help capture and maintain a DGC inventory of AI use cases and projects. Document challenges and opportunities and help turn them into case studies to supplement DGC’s Guidelines on the Ethical and Responsible Use of AI in Communications. Support the Governance group in meetings through note-taking and follow-up actions. • Communications guidelines enquiries: Help log colleagues' enquiries on DGC’s Guidelines on the Ethical and Responsible Use of AI in Communications. Identify recurring questions and identify opportunities of further guidance and exploration to support the annual review of the DGC Guidelines. To this end, support the research of emerging areas of AI use in communications. • AI content visibility (SEO, GEO, AEO): Help produce UN content on 1-2 priority topics, in collaboration with the thematic leads, to boost visibility of content in LLMs. • AI trends: Track developments in the broader AI landscape as well as new AI technologies that affect communications work, such as agentic AI, AI-generated media, and content provenance and labelling, and the broader landscape of AI messaging. Help prepare monthly trend digests. • Creative innovation ideas/pilots: Propose new ideas for creative and digital innovation in UN communications, such as new storytelling formats, AI-assisted production approaches or audience engagement experiments. Develop the most promising ideas into short concept notes and pilots in safe testing ("sandbox") environments, in line with the DGC Guidelines on the Ethical and Responsible use of AI in Communications. • Emerging areas: Support the research of emerging areas, ranging from content provenance and disclosure standards to AI visibility to agentic AI, and transform them into tip sheets. The intern will gain hands-on experience of how the UN system develops and applies AI governance and adoption in communications, and of inter-agency coordination through the UNCG AI Lab. They will build skills in evaluating AI tools and their risks and turning research into concise briefs and tips. They will also gain exposure to the UN 2.0 areas of data, innovation, digital, foresight and behavioural science. Depending on skills and interest, the intern may also lead a small project, such as building an AI pilot relevant to public communications. The intern will meet weekly with their supervisor and receive feedback at the mid-point and end of the internship.
Qualifications/special skills
To qualify for the United Nations Internship Programme, applicants must meet one of the following requirements: a. Be enrolled in, or have completed, a graduate school programme (second university degree or equivalent, or higher); or b. Be enrolled in, or have completed, the final academic year of a first university degree programme (minimum bachelor's level or equivalent). Relevant fields include communications, journalism, multimedia, data journalism, AI, computer science, digital media, or a related field. Applicants must also have: • Hands-on experience using AI and digital tools for communications, for example large language model (LLM) assistants, custom or agentic AI tools, Adobe Creative Cloud or Figma. • Experience in basic data skills (spreadsheets, simple analysis or visualization). • An in interest in AI ethics and communications. • An interest in creative communications, innovation and Agentic AI is a strong asset. Examples include building custom AI assistants or agents; experimenting with new forms of AI-assisted storytelling and journalism; creating data visualizations, interactive or immersive content; and prototyping tools. • A demonstrated keen interest in the work of the United Nations and a personal commitment to the ideals of the UN Charter. • A demonstrated ability to interact successfully with individuals of different cultural backgrounds and beliefs. A completed online application (Cover Note and Personal History Profile) is required. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. The Cover Note must include: • Degree programme (what you are currently studying) • Graduation date (when you will graduate or graduated from the programme) • Why you are the best candidate for this specific internship • Your interest in the United Nations Internship Programme • One example of how you have used, tested or critically assessed an AI tool In your online Personal History Profile, be sure to include all past work experiences, IT skills, and three references. Due to the high volume of applications received, ONLY successful candidates will be contacted. Applicants who are children or siblings of a staff member are not eligible to apply for an internship at the United Nations. Interns will need to provide all necessary hardware (computer), software and internet connection to perform the internship remotely. Interns must follow UN rules on information security and use only approved AI tools, without entering confidential or personal information into external services. Interns are not financially remunerated by the United Nations. Costs and arrangements for travel, visas, accommodation and living expenses are the responsibility of interns or their sponsoring institutions. No working experience is required to apply for the United Nations Internship Programme. Your training, education, advance course work or skills should benefit the United Nations during your internship. Applicants must be a student in the second to last year of the first university degree (bachelor or equivalent), or have completed a Bachelor’s Programme. Do you meet any of the above criteria? If yes, please indicate which one and attach proof to the application. Please note that you will have to provide an official certificate at a later stage.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this position, fluency in English is required. Knowledge of another official United Nations language is an advantage.
Additional Information
Not available.
Intern Specific text
Interns are not financially remunerated by the United Nations. Costs and arrangements for travel, visas, accommodation and living expenses are the responsibility of interns or their sponsoring institutions. Interns who are not citizens or permanent residents of the country where the internship is undertaken, may be required to obtain the appropriate visa and work/employment authorization. Successful candidates should discuss their specific visa requirements before accepting the internship offer.

vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
El objetivo de esta contratación es que la o el consultor/a ejecute, bajo la supervisión de la Estadística de la División de Asuntos de Género, las actividades técnicas necesarias para el desarrollo e implementación piloto de un sistema web integrado al Observatorio de Igualdad de Género de América Latina y el Caribe para la recolección del indicador de feminicidio, que permita a los puntos focales nacionales ingresar, consultar, actualizar y descargar información, mantener registros históricos y generar reportes, facilitando la compilación y gestión de la base de datos regional.
Work Location

Provides leadership and takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work; demonstrates knowledge of strategies and commitment to the goal of gender balance in staffing. vacancies.jobTitle: Expert on Development of a Competency-Based Public Policy Training Package for the Civil Service Board of Lebanon
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
The objective of this assignment is to develop a comprehensive, Arabic-language, competency-based public policy training manual and accompanying materials that cover the entire public policy cycle, from problem identification and agenda setting through policy design, planning and decision-making, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. The manual shall directly map learning objectives and training modules to the public-policy competencies and the four proficiency levels set out in the CSB’s RIME framework. The complete package shall be suitable for independent and sustainable delivery by ENA and shall be provided in editable formats to allow the institution to adapt, update and reuse its contents.
Work Location
Beirut / Remote
Expected duration
4 Months
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Background The United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA), through its Governance and Conflict Prevention Cluster, supports member States in strengthening public administration, governance and institutional capacities. Its work aims to promote effective, accountable and inclusive public institutions and improved public service delivery, in line with Sustainable Development Goal 16 and other objectives of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. ESCWA has supported regional efforts to strengthen the competencies of public officials, including the initiative “Towards a Common Arab Regional Framework for the Job Competencies of Senior Public Officials in the Context of the 2030 Agenda and Public Policies” and its accompanying implementation guide. These efforts recognize that effective policy formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation depend on the knowledge and skills of public servants, particularly those exercising management and leadership responsibilities. Within this context, Lebanon’s Civil Service Board (CSB) has developed a Reference Framework for Job Descriptions and Competencies in the Public Sector (RIME). The framework defines reference job profiles and the required competencies across four categories: core, leadership, common technical and specialized technical competencies. ESCWA will provide technical assistance to develop an integrated, competency-based training package in public policy, covering the full policy cycle. The package will be aligned with the public-policy-related competencies and proficiency levels identified in the CSB reference framework. The National School of Administration (ENA) is expected to deliver the training independently following completion of ESCWA’s support. The training package will serve public officials at different career stages and according to their training needs, including: newly recruited public officials entering the civil service; officials eligible for promotion to Category II; participants in specialized training programmes according to job category and the nature of their functions; and senior public administration leaders and managers. ESCWA therefore seeks to engage an expert with expertise in public policy, competency-based instructional design and the Lebanese public administration to develop the training manual, associated materials and implementation tools. 2. Tasks - duties and responsibilities Under the direct supervision of the Head of ESCWA’s Governance and Conflict Prevention Cluster and the Regional Adviser, in coordination with the President of the Civil Service Board, the expert will undertake the following tasks: 1. Reference review and inception - Review leading and recent academic and institutional references on the policy cycle, including policy formulation, planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. - Review relevant ESCWA publications in the fields of public administration and public policies, particularly the regional initiative on senior public officials’ job competencies and its participatory methodology and implementation guide. - Analyze the CSB’s reference job descriptions and competency framework, emphasizing public policy competencies, proficiency levels and applicable functions. 2. Detailed instructional design Based on the review findings, the expert shall develop a detailed design for the training manual, including: - An integrated overall structure for the training curriculum and chapters of the manual. - A map aligning competencies with training modules. - Identification of training pathways for each proficiency level and each target group. - The general methodology and proposed training methods. - A matrix linking each target group to its required proficiency level and appropriate training modules (group × level × module). - The proposed scope of the manual: the number of training modules and the anticipated duration of each module and each level (in hours). The expert shall discuss this design with ESCWA and the Civil Service Board and shall not begin preparing the chapters until it has been approved. 3. Development of the manual and training materials For each training module, the manual shall include: - Learning outcomes defined for each proficiency level. - Training session plans (objectives, duration, activities and sequence). - A trainer’s guide (delivery instructions, suggested questions and pedagogical notes). - Training materials for participants (presentations, reference texts, exercises and worksheets). - Case studies drawn from Lebanese, regional and international practice. - Identification of the most appropriate training methods for each module. - Cross-cutting topics integrated into modules, as appropriate, including evidence-based policies, data and indicators; policies based on risk and vulnerability analysis; policy coherence (horizontal and vertical); stakeholder engagement and consultation; gender and inclusion; alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals; policymaking in crisis situations and under resource constraints; and the use of technology and artificial intelligence, among others. The manual shall cover all stages of the public policy cycle: problem identification and agenda-setting; policy design and formulation; planning and decision-making; implementation; and policy monitoring and evaluation. 4. Learning assessment and certification - Design a pre-training assessment instrument to determine each participant’s existing competency level and place the participant in the appropriate training level. - Design a post-training assessment instrument to verify the effective acquisition of the required competency level, rather than relying solely on attendance or participation. - Develop a certification framework and level-specific certificate templates, with certificates awarded on the basis of post-training assessment results. 5. Pilot training and training of trainers - Design and implement an initial pilot training exercise for each training level (four pilot exercises), jointly with trainers from the National School of Administration, and refine the package on the basis of the results to develop its final version. The Civil Service Board and the National School of Administration shall identify and mobilize the participants, whose number will be agreed when the design is approved. Pilot exercises shall be conducted in parallel with approved chapters, without waiting for completion of the entire manual, so that the development of subsequent chapters can benefit from their results. - Prepare and implement a Training of Trainers (ToT) programme enabling the Civil Service Board to establish a pool of trainers capable of effectively delivering each training module at the different proficiency levels.
Qualifications/special skills
A Masters degree in Public Policy, Public Administration or a related field is required. A PhD in Public Policy, Public Administration or a related field is desirable. All candidates must submit a copy of the required educational degree. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. A minimum of ten years of proven practical experience in designing training programmes and preparing training manuals is required. vacancies.postingTitle: UNEP Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) - Senior EU Policy Engagement Expert
vacancies.jobTitle: UNEP Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) - Senior EU Policy Engagement Expert
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
The purpose of this assignment is to contribute to UNEP FI’s strategic engagement with European Union (EU) policymakers, regulators, and financial institutions to advance the bankability and financing of the transition to a sustainable, competitive, and inclusive European economy. The Senior EU Policy Engagement Expert will play a central role in operationalizing two main activities: Activity 1: Building a value proposition and toolkit for EU sectoral policy engagement for banks. Activity 2: Promoting innovative finance solutions: from sectoral transition to policy to bankability. These activities aim to bridge the gap between EU industrial and sectoral policies and the financial sector’s capacity to mobilize capital at scale. This includes developing sector-specific policy engagement approaches, facilitating structured dialogue between banks and non-financial policymakers, and identifying and scaling innovative financing solutions that support industrial decarbonization, circular economy transition, and broader EU Green Deal priorities. The consultant’s work will also contribute to upholding UN core values, ensuring that human rights-based approach, the principle of leaving no one behind and gender equality and women’s empowerment are integrated throughout their work at UNEP FI’s.
Work Location
Working remotely / Home-based
Expected duration
12 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. UNEP’s work is firmly grounded in the UN core values, including the human rights-based approach, the commitment to leaving no one behind, and the promotion of gender equality and women’s empowerment across all activities. The overall objective of the UNEP’s Industry and Economy Division is to encourage decision makers in government, local authorities and industry to develop and adopt policies, strategies and practices and technologies that promote sustainable patterns of consumption and production, make efficient use of natural resources, ensure safe management of chemicals and contribute to making trade and environment policies mutually supportive. It promotes the development, use and transfer of policies, technologies, economic instruments, managerial practices and other tools that assist in environmentally sound decision making and the building of corresponding activities. The United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) is the strategic partnership between the United Nations and over 500 banks, insurers, and investors. For over 34 years UNEP FI has been shaping and driving the international sustainable finance agenda, setting global standards, and growing a global network of leading financial institutions. Through its work-streams and regional activities, peer learning, methodology development, training and research, UNEP FI promotes sustainable finance and helps the financial industry align with and contribute to the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals. The political landscape within the EU underscores the growing importance of supporting the European Commission with its competitiveness agenda. UNEP FI is strategically positioned to turn this agenda into a practical business opportunity—helping the finance industry mobilize capital toward real-economy transformation that creates jobs, strengthens supply chains, and drives sustainable innovation. Banks increasingly need clear, sectoral policies that are both effective and bankable—providing predictable frameworks and tangible investment pathways that can translate ambition into financeable action. By linking sustainability goals with competitiveness, UNEP FI can further support a meaningful involvement of the finance industry in driving the Green Deal and the transition of the real economy, demonstrating that decarbonisation and value creation can go hand in hand. The initiative aims to direct capital toward tangible projects—such as clean industrial production, circular economy investments, and low-carbon infrastructure—that deliver measurable impact on the ground and support resilient, competitive value chains. Equally essential is the integration of social policy measures—such as fair transition mechanisms and social protection schemes—which serve as enablers of decarbonisation and ensure the transition is equitable and sustainable. Objectives: The Senior EU Policy Engagement Expert will: • Design and implement a structured value proposition for banks’ engagement in EU sectoral policy processes, including the development of toolkits, guidance, and engagement frameworks. • Contribute to aligning EU industrial policy (e.g., Clean Industrial Deal and sectoral initiatives) with financial sector practices and investment capabilities. • Provide technical expert advice on the identification, analysis, and prioritization of key EU sectoral policies (e.g., energy, transport, real estate, chemicals, circular economy) and translate them into actionable financing pathways for banks. • Facilitate the development of outputs including sectoral policy briefs, engagement toolkits, and practical guidance to support banks’ participation in policy dialogue. • Coordinate and facilitate multi-stakeholder dialogues (banks, policymakers, industry, public finance institutions) to strengthen policy–finance alignment and support implementation. • Develop a compendium of innovative financial solutions, including blended finance instruments, guarantees, securitization, and other bankable models supporting industrial decarbonization and transition investments. • Ensure coherence between policy engagement and financing realities from a banking/lending perspective, including risk-return considerations, capital allocation, and regulatory constraints. • Engage with EU institutions (European Commission, EIB, ECB, platforms) and relevant initiatives to position UNEP FI as a key interlocutor linking policy ambition with finance. • Work closely with UNEP FI teams (e.g., policy, banking, climate, nature, communications) to ensure integrated delivery of outputs. The result of the consultant’s work will be the following successful high-quality outputs. The deliverables listed below constitute the agreed outputs of the assignment. Any proposed adjustments arising from implementation, stakeholder consultations, or expert recommendations shall be subject to prior review and approval by the UNEP FI supervisor and where necessary, formal contract amendment: Key Deliverables • Development of a structured value proposition and toolkit for sectoral policy engagement for banks. • Delivery of sectoral policy briefs across priority sectors aligned with EU Green Deal priorities. • Organization and facilitation of expert dialogues, roundtables, and stakeholder convenings. • Delivery of a completed draft compendium of innovative financial solutions supporting industrial decarbonization and circular economy investments. • Contribution to policy platforms and working groups, including documented inputs and engagement outcomes. • Evidence of strengthened policy–finance alignment (e.g., uptake of recommendations, stakeholder engagement, participation metrics). • The above deliverables will be developed and implemented in alignment with UNEP FI’s Social Action Plan and guided by the UN’s core values. Specific tasks and responsibilities: The consultant will provide assistance in the following tasks: a. Coordination and Policy Engagement • Coordinate the policy team engagement with EU policy processes related to the Green Deal, Clean Industrial Deal, and sectoral transition strategies. • Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders including the European Commission, EIB, national authorities, industry associations, and financial institutions. b. Delivery of Activity 1: EU Sectoral Policy Engagement Value Proposition • Develop sectoral policy engagement frameworks for banks. • Develop and implement the production of sectoral policy briefs, engagement toolkits and guidance, and recommendations for policy–finance alignment. • Facilitate expert sessions, roundtables, and dialogues bringing together banks, policymakers, and industry actors. c. Delivery of Activity 2: Innovative Finance and Bankability for the Transition • Coordinate the identification and scaling of innovative financial instruments with UNEP FI members (e.g., blended finance, guarantees, Carbon Contracts for Difference (CCfD), securitization structures). • Ensure alignment between financing solutions and EU policy frameworks, including public financing instruments (e.g., InvestEU, EIB guarantees, and Industrial Decarbonization Bank). • Promote peer learning and knowledge exchange among banks and stakeholders on bankable transition solutions. • Provide technical expert advice on how policy design affects bankability and capital mobilization. d. Stakeholder Coordination and Representation • Coordinate and support representation of UNEP FI in EU platforms, working groups, and policy dialogues. • Coordinate internal and external stakeholders to ensure consistency and impact of engagement activities. • Contribute to communications and dissemination of outputs. • Ensure that all communications outputs reflect UNEP and UN core values, including human rights-based approach, the principle of leaving no one behind and gender equality and women’s empowerment and contribute to internal awareness on these values. • Support the implementation of UNEP FI’s 2026–2029 Social Action Plan by including all relevant measures from the plan in their work. The consultant will report to: Overall supervisor: The Head of UNEP FI. Direct Supervisor: The Policy Lead, UNEP FI. Close coordination: The consultant will work closely with colleagues across the UNEP FI policy team and, where relevant, with the UNEP FI banking team.
Qualifications/special skills
Education: A master’s degree in finance, law, economics, business administration, international relations is required. A bachelor’s degree could be taken in lieu of master’s degree provided the selected candidate has 12 years of relevant experience. Professional Experience: At least ten (10) years of professional experience and expertise in investment and/or lending activities, development finance and/or investment banking, banking regulation, supervision, and sustainable finance is required. At least five (5) years of professional experience in the banking sector, including experience in a European policy and banking setting, would be an advantage.
Languages
Languages: English is the working language of UNEP FI. Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish or other United Nations languages is an asset.
Additional Information
Skills & Knowledge: • Professional network among relevant financial sector regulators, policy makers, investors, or their respective organizations. • Strong interpersonal and communications skills and good public speaking. • Ability and willingness to travel up to once per quarter. • Self-starter, enjoys building up, testing, and adapting new structures and models. • Ability to collaborate horizontally across the team.
No Fee

vacancies.jobTitle: C–Best Practices for the Cassava Value Chain in the Nord Department, Haiti
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
At the end of the consultancy, the consultant will deliver a document identifying and analyzing national and international best practices relevant to addressing the key constraints of the cassava value chain in the Nord department of Haiti, assessing their relevance and transferability to the local context. The findings will serve as a key input for the subsequent formulation of strategies and together with the strategies will be presented at the second roundtable. Also, findings will contribute to promote economic and social upgrading and climate change adaptation through the adoption of climate-smart technologies, with particular strategies for integration of women and youth. It contributes to the expected outcomes of the project “rural agricultural value chains and climate-smart technology policies at the subnational level in Latin America and the Caribbean” and to the implementation of ECLAC’s workplan.
Work Location
Haiti
Expected duration
15.12.26-22.02.2027
Duties and Responsibilities
Background Within the framework of the project “Rural agricultural value chains and climate-smart technology policies at the subnational level in Latin America and the Caribbean”, implemented by the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC) during the period 2025–2028, the objective is to strengthen technical and institutional capacities at the national and subnational levels in order to promote more productive, inclusive and climate-resilient agriculture. This project is financed through the 17th tranche of the United Nations Development Account and is being implemented in four pilot countries: Colombia, Cuba, Chile and Haiti. Component 3 of the project, led by the ECLAC Subregional Office in Mexico, aims to promote economic and social upgrading in selected rural value chains through a participatory and territorial approach. Key activities include the preparation of technical diagnostics, dialogue roundtables, action plans, training workshops and online learning materials. These activities focus on identifying productive, technological, economic and institutional bottlenecks, and on proposing strategies to strengthen value chains, with particular emphasis on climate change adaptation and the inclusion of women and youth. In the case of Haiti, the project focuses on the cassava value chain in the Nord department. As part of the second phase of work on this value chain, ECLAC seeks to engage a specialized consultant to prepare a document that systematizes national and international best practices to address the systemic constraints and those specific to individual links identified in the diagnostic study of the cassava value chain in the Nord department of Haiti. This work will be based on ECLAC’s methodology for strengthening value chains (ECLAC, 2016) and will integrate gender, youth and environmental sustainability considerations as cross-cutting themes. 2026-SP11-PRO-1 OP3.4 Activities to be performed: Under the supervision of the ECLAC team, the consultant will carry out the following activities: 1. Conduct a critical review of the value chain diagnostic and the main discussions from the first roundtable, identifying the principal constraints of the value chain. 2. Conduct, if necessary, interviews with key stakeholders to gain a deeper understanding of the situation of the cassava value chain in the Nord department, Haiti. 3. Develop a research proposal for the identification and analysis of best practices, including objectives, a work plan, methodology, an annotated outline, and suggested relevant information sources. 4. Identify, select, and analyze national and international best practices in cassava value chains facing challenges similar to those encountered in in the Nord department, Haiti. 5. Conduct an analysis highlighting the relevance and transferability of the selected best practices and lessons learned to the cassava value chain in the Nord department, Haiti. 6. Incorporate comments and suggestions from the ECLAC team and project counterparts after review of the deliverables. 7 If the timing of the contracts allows, coordinate with the person responsible for developing the strategies for the cassava value chain in the Nord department to determine how best to integrate the identified best practices into these strategies. Consultant Obligations: a) Provide any clarifications or additional information requested by the supervisor and supply any further information deemed necessary to fulfill the agreed deliverables. b) Certify that he/she is the original author of the work and documents produced under the contract with ECLAC. The consultant must also state that the content of the work and documents submitted constitutes his/her intellectual contribution and that neither the form nor the content is being simultaneously submitted to any other editorial outlet. c) Grant ECLAC the copyrights, patents and any other intellectual or industrial property rights, where applicable, over the work and documents produced by the consultant under contracts financed with ECLAC resources. d) If traveling on mission, complete the security courses required by the Organization, submit the mission report through the Mission Report System (MRS) (or provide the necessary information to the Unit for submission to the MRS), and submit the travel claim within two weeks after the mission has concluded. e) Ensure that all data and references to materials and publications are properly identified with their respective credits and included in the bibliographic notes and citations. f) Declare that the appropriate authorizations have been obtained from the holders of the relevant intellectual property rights, where applicable. g) Reports must be written in French, using Word or Excel from the Microsoft Office 2013 package or compatible, using Times New Roman 12-point font and 1.5-line spacing, with the minimum possible use of instructions, specifications, codes or special formatting (for example, only one type of font should be used) and include index. The ECLAC editorial manual and bibliography formatting standards must be followed. Tables, graphs, diagrams, etc. must be submitted in editable format (Excel, PowerPoint or other relevant software). Performance Indicators: • Quality of analysis and substantive inputs produced • Timely delivery of outputs and regular communication • Transparent management of data and information collected during the research Place of Work: Nord Department, Haiti.
Qualifications/special skills
The consultant must hold a Bachelor’s degree in economics, agronomy, rural development or related fields. At least 7 years of experience in economic development, productive development, rural development or related areas. Technical knowledge of the cassava value chain is desirable. Knowledge of the key actors in the cassava value chain of Haiti is desirable. A Master’s degree in these areas is desirable.
Languages
The consultant should have excellent command of French; intermediate command of English or Spanish is desirable.
Additional Information
Not available.

Background The main mandate of the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is to promote sustainable development of human settlements and policies conducive to adequate housing for all. Within this framework, UN-Habitat supports central and state governments, as well as local authorities and other partners for the implementation of the Habitat Agenda, the 2030 Agenda with the Sustainable Development Goals and the New Urban Agenda. UN-Habitat helps the urban poor by transforming cities into safer, more inclusive, compact, integrated, resilient and connected places with better opportunities where everyone can live with dignity. It works with organizations at every level, including all spheres of government, civil society, and the private sector to help build, manage, plan, and finance sustainable urban development. The Regional Office for Latin American and the Caribbean – ROLAC – is based in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The Agency puts emphasis on developing and managing activities in the host country. Indeed, for the past years, UN-Habitat has expanded its portfolio in Brazil by working with the three tiers of government to support the formulation and implementation of more effective, sustainable, participative, and socially fairer urban economic, social, and environmental policies. vacancies.jobTitle: UNEP Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) - Nature and Social Junior Consultant
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
Through these services the Initiative will be able to engage a broad range of financial institutions, including commercial banks, asset managers, insurers, and multilateral development banks and agencies in implementing global finance sector principles to catalyse integration of sustainability into financial market practice. The frameworks UNEP FI is supporting implementation include the Principles for Responsible Banking (PRB), now committed to by more than 210 banks collectively holding USD 53 trillion in assets, or one third of the global banking sector, and the Principles for Sustainable Insurance (PSI), established in 2012 by UNEP FI and today applied by one quarter of the world’s insurers (25% of world premium). The services will strengthen delivery of the Nature team’s project portfolio and policy engagement and help ensure that social and human rights considerations are integrated consistently across nature projects. The services will also help promote sustainability into all aspects of the financial sector’s operations and services. Finally, the services will help the Initiative to broaden its outreach both within UNEP / UN and external to banks, insurers and investors, governments, regulators, private sector and multi-stakeholders, including supporting institutions. The consultant’s work will also contribute to upholding UN core values, ensuring that the human rights-based approach, the principle of leaving no one behind and gender equality and women’s empowerment are integrated throughout their work at UNEP FI.
Work Location
Working remotely / Home-based
Expected duration
2 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. UNEP’s work is firmly grounded in the UN core values, including the human rights-based approach, the commitment to leaving no one behind, and the promotion of gender equality and women’s empowerment across all activities. The overall objective of the UNEP’s Economy Division is to encourage decision makers in government, local authorities and industry to develop and adopt policies, strategies and practices and technologies that promote sustainable patterns of consumption and production, make efficient use of natural resources, ensure safe management of chemicals and contribute to making trade and environment policies mutually supportive. It promotes the development, use and transfer of policies, technologies, economic instruments, managerial practices and other tools that assist in environmentally sound decision making and the building of corresponding activities. The United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) is the strategic partnership between the United Nations and over 500 banks, insurers, and investors. For over 34 years UNEP FI has been shaping and driving the international sustainable finance agenda, setting global standards, and growing a global network of leading financial institutions. Through its work-streams and regional activities, peer learning, methodology development, training and research, UNEP FI promotes sustainable finance and helps the financial industry align with and contribute to the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals. UNEP FI needs a junior consultant to support the Nature team’s project delivery and policy engagement activities, including Revenues for Nature (R4N) and the team’s participation in major global policy events. This support is required to advance the Nature team’s growing agenda and is not currently available in sufficient capacity within the team. Objectives: The consultant will support the Nature team through the delivery of defined project and policy engagement outputs under the Revenues for Nature (R4N) project and UNEP FI's nature-related policy work. Performance will be measured against the timely completion of the following deliverables: • Research, drafting and coordination support provided for R4N activities, contributing to the delivery of at least one knowledge product and the delivery of one stakeholder engagement activity, such as a consultation process or partner roundtable within agreed project timelines. • A comprehensive record of stakeholder engagements related to at least one major global policy event (e.g. Post COP / BBNJ meetings) compiled and submitted within 10 working days of the event, covering 100% of relevant meetings, consultations and follow-up actions coordinated by the Nature team, including relevant social and human rights considerations. • A post-event outcome note produced within 15 working days of the event, summarising key decisions, stakeholder engagements, follow-up actions and implications for the financial sector. • Follow-up actions arising from policy engagement activities tracked and maintained through completion, with progress updates provided to the Nature team monthly. • All deliverables reviewed and aligned with UNEP and UN core values, including gender equality, human rights-based approaches and the principle of leaving no one behind, with compliance demonstrated across 100% of submitted outputs. The consultancy will be deemed successful upon delivery of the above outputs in accordance with agreed quality standards, timelines and reporting requirements. This support is required to advance the Nature team’s growing agenda and does not currently exist in sufficient capacity within the team. Specific tasks and responsibilities: The consultant will provide assistance across the following tasks in support of UNEP FI’s Nature team: • Support delivery of the Revenues for Nature (R4N) project, including research, drafting and review inputs to knowledge products, and coordination of consultations and partner engagement. • Backstop the Nature team’s post-event engagement following major global policy events, including compiling and maintaining a record of all relevant engagements, synthesizing key outcomes and decisions, coordinating follow-up actions with partners and organizers, and assessing implications and opportunities for the financial sector. • Ensure that all communications outputs reflect UNEP and UN core values, including human rights-based approach, the principle of leaving no one behind and gender equality and women’s empowerment, and contribute to internal awareness on these values. • Support the implementation of UNEP FI’s 2026–2029 Social Action Plan by including all relevant measures from the plan in their work. Outputs and Deliverables: • Research, drafting and coordination input delivered to support R4N project activities, including at least one knowledge product and the delivery of one stakeholder engagement activity, such as a consultation process or partner roundtable. • Briefing, coordination and follow-up materials prepared for the Nature team’s participation in at least one large global policy event, including a short note of outcomes relevant to the financial sector. • The above deliverables will be developed and implemented in alignment with UNEP FI’s Social Action Plan and guided by the UN’s core values. The consultant will report to: Overall supervisor: The Head of UNEP FI. Direct Supervisor: The Head of Nature, UNEP FI. Close coordination: The candidate will work closely with the UNEP FI social team and the relevant Nature team project leads.
Qualifications/special skills
Education: A master’s degree in environmental management, sustainable development, geography, finance, economics, public policy, international relations, or a related discipline is required. A bachelor’s degree could be taken in lieu of a master’s degree provided the selected candidate has 4 years of relevant experience. Professional Experience: At least two (2) years of experience in the environmental non-profit sector, the financial services sector, public policy, commercial consulting, or applied academic research on sustainable finance is required. Relevant experience in nature finance, nature markets, or the social and human rights dimensions of nature-related finance is desirable. Experience with biodiversity or nature credit markets, supporting international policy processes, or working with Indigenous Peoples and local communities is an asset.
Languages
Languages: English is the working language of UNEP FI. Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Spanish, Portuguese or other United Nations languages is an asset.
Additional Information
Skills & Knowledge: Excellent oral and written communications skills in English, strong interpersonal skills and ability to work across different topics, ability to cope with juggling multiple tasks across diverse projects in an organised and timely manner; attention to detail. Knowledge of nature finance and nature markets is desirable, as is familiarity with social safeguards, human rights due diligence or social action planning, and experience of writing reports and briefing notes. The consultant is expected to support colleagues in implementing the Nature team’s strategy and work plans. The consultant should have the ability to establish and maintain good working relations in a multicultural and geographically dispersed team working across functions. A hands-on, pragmatic approach is desirable. An interest in nature finance and the social dimension of sustainable finance is desirable.

Result of Service
1. A comprehensive Gender Plan of Action to support the implementation of Sierra Leone’s NBSAP 3.0 (2026- 2035) aligned with national and global goals. 2. Awareness raising and dissemination/communication activities to spread the GPA and make target group aware and support uptake 3. Training and support to national level MDA and local council amin incl. toolkits and training events and materials as well as a detailed report of capacity building support provided to the EPA, Other MDA’s and Local Councils. 4. Provided gender disaggregated data to evaluate how conservation policies impact men and women differently. 5. Integrated a robust monitoring and evaluation framework to track gender metrics for the NBSAP 3.0 (2026-2035).
Work Location
Remote
Expected duration
3 months
Duties and Responsibilities
Background The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. Its mandate is to coordinate the development of environmental policy consensus by keeping the global environment under review and bringing emerging issues to the attention of governments and the international community for action. UNEP’s Ecosystems Division engages with governments and other partners to develop and promote ecosystem-based solutions for sustainable development. This assignment is in the Nature Frameworks Support Unit of the Biodiversity and Land Branch, Ecosystems Division. UNEP is also one of the key agencies hosting the NBSAP Accelerator Partnership. The NBSAP Accelerator Partnership is a country-led global initiative that supports the development and implementation of ambitious National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) and collectively achieve the goals and targets of the Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) and, ultimately, the global vision of living in harmony with nature by 2050. The NBSAP Accelerator Partnership provides technical and financial support for the implementation of GBF-aligned NBSAPs. This includes strengthening country-driven coordination, fostering collaboration among stakeholders, facilitating knowledge sharing and best practices, and addressing country-specific needs. It also helps raise national profile of countries' NBSAPs, and fast-track implementation through a matchmaking service, increased access to expertise, knowledge and capacity development, and in-country facilitation support. A National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) is a country’s principal document for implementing the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). It outlines a nation’s approach to conserving its biodiversity, ensuring its sustainable use, and fairly sharing the benefits derived from genetic resources. Sierra Leone is a party to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). They signed and ratified the convention in 1994 and 1996, respectively. The Country also acceded to the Cartagena Protocol in 2020 and the Nagoya Protocol in 2017. Duties and Responsibilities The NBSAP Accelerator Partnership’s Facilitator Programme is looking for a consultant to assist the Government of Sierra Leone through its Environment Protection Agency (EPA) to develop a gender plan of action for NBSAP implementation. This will integrate gender equality into conservation policies, driven by the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework Target 22 and 23 and the CBD Gender Plan of Action which has been aligned with the National Framework specifically target 22 and 23. It ensures women’s full, effective and meaningful participation in biodiversity planning, fair resource access, and gender responsive monitoring. The Consultant will help develop a gender plan of action that reflects meaningful participation and leadership, fair resources of right and access, gender disaggregation, gender specific indicators and target financing. The rationale for developing a Gender Plan of Action for the NBSAP 3.0 (2026-2035) is essential because women disproportionately rely on natural resources for their livelihoods but face systemic inequalities in resource access and decision making. Integrating gender into the NBSAP ensures both fair conservation benefits and more effective environmental protection. Globally, nearly one third of women’s employment is in agriculture, forestry and fishing. In many developing countries, women play essential roles in managing water, food, fuel, forests and agricultural systems. They are often among the first to observe the effects of biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation and climate change on households and communities. At the same time, women frequently face barriers to accessing land, natural resources, finance, information, technology and decision-making processes. These barriers limit not only women’s rights and opportunities, but also the effectiveness of biodiversity policies and programmes. Women’s knowledge, environmental stewardship, leadership and agency are therefore indispensable to achieving national and global biodiversity objectives and advancing equitable and sustainable development. Specific Task I. Gender Plan of Action a. Conduct gender analysis b. Conduct multi- stakeholder consultations to engage local communities, women-led civil society organization, traditional leaders and youth groups, inclusive of marginalized groups to inform the plan building on the whole of society approach. c. Report summarizing results of Gender Analysis and local consultations- Summarizing results and key messages and needs of consulted groups and based on the data and information that is present. Conduct a localized gender assessment focusing on access to land, natural resources, and biodiversity -dependent livelihoods (e.g. agriculture, forestry, coastal resilience), Identify baseline barriers preventing women and youth from participating in environmental decision making, national biodiversity committees, decision making bodies, and consultation workshops, Address systemic inequalities by linking NBSAP to women’s rights to own, access, and manage land, fisheries and forest resources and Provide sex-disaggregated data to evaluate how conservation policies impact men and women differently. d. Develop a Gender Plan of Action and validate policy makers/stakeholders in workshop at national level- Since ABS is important and relevant topic in Sierra it is paramount to address the topic of benefit sharing to ensure that benefits from the utilization of genetic resources and traditional knowledge are shared equitably with women in the GPA. e. Present the draft Gender Plan of Action at national or regional validation workshops with government and international stakeholders. f. Develop target financing scheme, that is a budget allocation to dedicate specific national funds or international donor support exclusively to gender mainstreaming components and women led conservation initiatives. Aligned the gender action with national and global policy, ensure the plan fulfils national target 23 of Sierra Leone NBSAP, which mandate a gender responsive approach to biodiversity, explicitly align with the GEWE Act by actively promoting at least 30% female representation. Setting Smart targets and actionable goals that boost women’s resilient livelihood within communities, districts, region and national. II. Raise awareness and disseminate the gender plan of action to support uptake and implementation– enabler to understand (non-technical level catered to the needs of the target group, target group: communities) maybe also consider if documents or event in local language needed III. Technical training and support to MDAs and local councils’ administration a. Provide technical training capacity- building for the Gender Units across the Environment Protection Agency -Sierra Leone and other Ministries Departments and Agencies (MDA’s). b. Develop and distribute specified toolkits detailing gender responsive budgeting The scope of the Gender Plan of Action for the NBSAP 3.0 (2026-2035) will actively embed the principles of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (Targets 22 and 23) and the CBD Gender Plan of Action, aligning with the Country’s Gender Equality and Women Empowerment Act. The strategic scope of this integration revolves around equitable decision making, sector specific livelihood protections and resources right. The consultant will report to the Programme Management Officer, Nature Frameworks Support Unit in close collaboration with the national facilitator for Sierra Leone and relevant government partners.
Qualifications/special skills
Advance Degree in Gender Studies, Sociology, International Development, and other related disciplines. A first level degree with additional two years of qualifying experience maybe accepted in lieu of advanced degree. A minimum of 5 years in gender mainstreaming, policy development, and project cycle management is required Proven expertise in developing and implementing gender strategies, particularly at institutions or national level is required Demonstrated experience working on gender for sustainable development, biodiversity, or environmental issues is required Strong understanding of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and the Kunming Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KM GBF) is desirable Previous experience working with UNEP, UNDP or similar international organization is desirable
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. Fluency in written and spoken English is required. Knowledge of Sierra Leone local languages is an added advantage
