Result of Service
The consultant will develop a high quality Impact Report for the Global EbA Fund that presents evidence of the Fund’s results, innovation, EbA barriers addressed, catalytic influence, and contribution to EbA in a compelling, accessible, and visually engaging format.
Work Location
Home Based
Expected duration
12 weeks
Duties and Responsibilities
The Global EbA Fund (GEbAF) is an initiative implemented by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) in partnership with the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and funded by the International Climate Initiative (IKI) of the German Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN). The Global EbA Fund is a funding mechanism supporting innovative approaches to Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA) for climate change. It aims to overcome barriers to upscaling EbA by catalysing innovative initiatives. The Global EbA Fund has been operational since 2020 and supports innovative initiatives that create enabling environments for the uptake, scaling, and mainstreaming of EbA to climate change. To date, the Fund has supported 63 projects across 39 countries, with 30 projects completed and 15 projects in the pipeline. Funded projects address a range of barriers to EbA, including financial, governance, knowledge, and awareness-related gaps, among others. The portfolio spans diverse ecosystems and landscapes, including coastal and marine areas, drylands, grasslands, forests, mountains, urban areas, river basins, and wetlands, demonstrating the broad applicability of EbA approaches across different environmental and socio-economic contexts. As the Fund continues to expand its portfolio, there is a need to consolidate evidence of its results, effectiveness, and broader influence. The Global EbA Fund seeks to produce a high-quality, evidence-based, and visually compelling Impact Report that effectively communicates its results and achievements to grantees, donors, partners, broader stakeholder groups, and prospective funders, including philanthropic organizations that are increasingly investing in climate adaptation. As the global adaptation agenda places greater emphasis on resilience, locally led action, responsiveness to community needs, and measurable impact, the report will showcase the Fund’s contribution to advancing EbA and its role in delivering wider sustainable development outcomes through addressing barriers to EbA. The overall objective of this consultancy is to develop a Global EbA Fund Impact Report that presents evidence of the Fund’s results, innovation, catalytic influence, and contribution to EbA in a compelling, accessible, and visually engaging format. The report should: • Demonstrate the Fund’s contribution to EbA outcomes, how it addresses EbA barriers, and showcase the catalytic nature of Fund-supported interventions; • Synthesize key lessons and highlight innovation, scalability, partnerships, and leverage, including how projects mobilise additional finance, influence policy, and enable wider uptake and replication of EbA approaches; • Communicate measurable results using accessible high-quality photos, graphic illustrations, infographics, data visualisations, maps, and compelling narrative storytelling; • Present human-centered stories that illustrate how communities and ecosystems have benefited from the funded projects in accordance with the Fund’s inclusive and gender-responsive approach and Environmental and Social Management System; The consultant will design a clear, and engaging Impact Report, organized around the key barriers to EbA addressed by Global EbA Fund. The report should combine portfolio-level analysis with project-level examples to demonstrate the Fund’s contribution to enabling, scaling, and mainstreaming EbA globally. The indicative structure of the publication will be as follows: I. Preface • Executive summary presenting key achievements and lessons from the Fund • Forewords from UNEP, IUCN, and BMUKN/IKI II. Introducing the Global EbA Fund • Background and rationale for the Fund (what makes the Fund unique?) • Overview of the partnership and funding arrangements. • Timeline of key milestones (2020–2026). • Global footprint, including the geographic distribution of projects and countries reached. • Highlights of the Fund’s alignment with UNEP, IUCN, and IKI strategies, as well as relevant global frameworks (drawn from MTR findings). III. The Global EbA Fund Approach • The Fund’s theory of change and strategic objectives. • How the Fund operates, including grant modalities and support mechanisms. • The Fund’s role in creating enabling environments for EbA. IV. Portfolio Overview and Key Results • Summary of the portfolio and key performance indicators. • Funding allocations • Projects funded, countries/regions covered • Diversity of ecosystems and landscapes represented in the portfolio • Overview of beneficiaries • Overview of partnerships generated, including evidence of collective impact across stakeholders. • Highlights of major achievements and emerging trends, including examples of scalability and replication across projects. V. Addressing Barriers to Ecosystem-based Adaptation The report should present results according to the categories of barriers addressed by the Fund: Financial Barriers; Governance and Policy Barriers; and Knowledge, Capacity, and Awareness Barriers and sub-categories under these. Each barriers sub-section should include: • Headline statistics and key metrics; • Analytical narratives demonstrating progress and outcomes; • Illustrative case studies and individual project examples including innovative methodologies, tools, and mechanisms, highlighting enabling factors and success drivers to overcome barriers; The project examples should be usable as standalone project briefs. • Gaps, key lessons learned and emerging opportunities; • Stakeholder quotes and testimonials, where available; • Visual elements, maps, infographics, and photographs. VI. Conclusions and key messages • Summary of good practices and lessons learned • The way forward: key messages for scaling EbA VII. Annexes • Portfolio summary table of all projects funded; • Acronyms and abbreviations; • List of Fund-specific definitions • Fund Secretariat and Steering Committee • List of grantees and project partners. The material for all points will be provided by UNEP and IUCN. The selected vendor will be responsible for the following tasks: 1. Content planning and development • Review materials and project documentation including updated data provided by the Fund Secretariat, support with data analysis to distil relevant information and provide data insights for the report. • Develop draft messages on project impacts, success stories, lessons learned, and best practices from grantees provided by the Fund Secretariat. • Synthesize gathered information into accessible and inclusive language, and draft clear and engaging narratives and draft infographics. • Propose a concept and storytelling approach for the publication. 2. Development of visuals, design and layout • Develop and gather visual elements including photos, illustrations, infographics, and maps, including provision of editable files. • Produce a creative and professional layout and design for the publication. 3. Draft submission, feedback and finalization • Integrate UNEP and IUCN feedback into the draft publication (at least 3-4 rounds of comments). • Provide UNEP with the final publication in both high-resolution PDF and web-optimized formats.
Qualifications/special skills
Advanced university degree in communications, journalism, knowledge management, education, environment or related disciplines is required. A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, combined with an additional two years of experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree. At least 7 years of relevant professional experience in impact assessment, evaluation, data analysis, and results reporting is required. At least 5 assignments producing high-impact, visual publications for international organisations, agencies, NGOs, or donors is required. Strong analytical and data visualization skills is required. Strong experience in knowledge management and storytelling, with a proven ability to capture local impacts and lessons learned into compelling narratives for diverse audiences is desirable Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, engaging narratives is desirable. Strong stakeholder engagement and interviewing skills is desirable.

Fluency in writing and communication skills in English is required

Org. Setting and Reporting
The One Executive Office ("One EO") provides the full range of administrative and operational services required by New York–based Secretariat client entities to fulfil their mandates, including human resources management, financial administration, travel, and general administrative support. This position is located within the Common Administrative Platform at United Nations (UN) Headquarters, referred to as the One EO under the Division of Administration in the Department of Operational Support (DOS). One EO started its transition phase on 1 January 2026 as part of the UN80 reform initiative, which aims to consolidate common administrative functions across Secretariat entities into unified service platforms. Specifically, this position is in the Specialized Desk 4 (Travel) providing administrative and operational support to client entities with the certification of individual, group and conference travel, procurement and general related activities. The Senior Administrative Assistant will report to the Associate Administrative Officer.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Senior Administrative Assistant will be responsible for the following duties: Budget and Finance • Provides expert assistance in the preparation and development of the Unit’s work programme and budget. • Assists in monitoring budget/work programme with respect to various budgets, trust funds, grant and other funds on a regular basis, and suggests reallocations of resources and implements the reallocations as necessary. • Collects data from relevant databases and prepares customized financial reports. • Provides assistance in the review, and preparation of the medium-term plan and its revisions. • Reviews, analyses and assists in the finalization of cost estimates and budget proposals, in terms of staff and non-staff requirements from departments/offices at Headquarters and in the field, including programmatic aspects; ensures compliance with the medium-term plan and other legislative mandates. • Assists managers in the elaboration of resource requirements for budget submissions. • Monitors budget implementation/expenditures and recommends reallocation of funds as necessary. • Reviews requisitions for goods and services to ensure: (a) correct objects of expenditure have been charged, and (b) availability of funds. • Monitors extra-budgetary resources, including review of agreements and cost plans, ensuring compliance with regulations and rules and established policies and procedures. • Assists in the preparation of budget performance submissions. • Assists in finalization of budget performance reports, analysing variances between approved budgets and actual expenditures. • Acts as Certifying Officer for travel and other commitments. General Administration • Provides guidance, training and daily supervision to other general service staff in the area of responsibility. • Provides assistance in drafting of host country agreements, budget agreements, or contributions for grants or other activities as appropriate. • Identifies and resolves diverse issues/problems as they arise, and determines appropriate actions; ensures that all related activities of the Specialized Travel desk are implemented in compliance with intergovernmental recommendations and decisions as well as with United Nations policies and procedures. • Coordinates extensively with service units and liaises frequently with internal team members both at Headquarters and in the field. • Performs other related administrative duties, as required (e.g., operational travel programme, monitoring accounts and payment to vendors and individual contractors for services, physical space planning and the identification of office technology needs and maintenance of equipment, software and systems, organize and coordinate seminars, conferences and translations). • Assists with the collection and analysis of data as well as preparation of data presentations and reports for information sharing, responding to queries, knowledge management, planning and decision making. • Assists management during audit and reviews by oversight bodies. Duties and Responsibilities
Background The main mandate of the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is to promote sustainable development of human settlements and policies conducive to adequate housing for all. Within this framework, UN-Habitat supports central and state governments, as well as local authorities and other partners for the implementation of the Habitat Agenda, the 2030 Agenda with the Sustainable Development Goals and the New Urban Agenda. UN-Habitat helps the urban poor by transforming cities into safer, more inclusive, compact, integrated, resilient and connected places with better opportunities where everyone can live with dignity. It works with organizations at every level, including all spheres of government, civil society, and the private sector to help build, manage, plan and finance sustainable urban development. The Regional Office for Latin American and the Caribbean – ROLAC – is based in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The Agency puts emphasis on developing and managing activities in the host country. Indeed, for the past years, UN-Habitat has expanded its portfolio in Brazil by working with the three tiers of government to support the formulation and implementation of more effective, sustainable, participative, and socially fairer urban economic, social, and environmental policies. UN-Habitat has initiated a project with the Government of the State of Rio de Janeiro (GERJ) aimed at strengthening urban resilience in the State of Rio de Janeiro based on the implementation of the 2030 Agenda and the principles of the New Urban Agenda. The Inclusive and Sustainable Rio project supports the State in achieving urban prosperity while implementing global agendas for sustainable urban development. In particular, the proposal focuses on increasing urban resilience through the engagement of civil society to promote inclusion within the climate agenda of the State of Rio de Janeiro. The revision of the State Solid Waste Plan of Rio de Janeiro (PERS-RJ) is part of the scope of this project and constitutes a strategic instrument for strengthening the state policy on solid waste, in alignment with national guidelines and international sustainable development agendas. The process involves the preparation of an updated diagnosis, the development of scenarios, and the definition of strategies, actions, targets, and implementation instruments, considering the territorial, institutional, and socio-environmental diversity of the municipalities of Rio de Janeiro State. It adopts an integrated approach with the participation of state agencies, municipalities, public consortia, the productive sector, waste picker cooperatives, civil society organizations, and other relevant stakeholders. To properly implement the projects in Brazil, a Data Analyst is required. Report to UN-Habitat Manager The Data Analyst reports to the Head of Brazil Office, who will evaluate him/her. Responsibilities The Data Analyst will support the implementation of the projects in Brazil, and their activities, with the following responsibilities: a) Identify, collect, organize, and systematize solid waste data and information from federal, state, municipal, and institutional sources. b) Structure and maintain integrated, organized, and up-to-date databases, ensuring consistency, traceability, and accessibility of information for the projects’ technical teams. c) Develop and manage shareable geographic and non-geographic databases compatible with the analytical needs of the project. d) Manipulate, process, and analyze quantitative and qualitative data to support technical studies, reports, and deliverables. e) Produce thematic maps, charts, tables, and data dashboards to support territorial analyses and the communication of project results. f) Contribute to the spatialization of information and territorial analysis through Geographic Information System (GIS) tools. g) Integrate data from different consultants and thematic areas, ensuring methodological standardization and compatibility among datasets. h) Collaborate to the consolidation of information from participatory processes when necessary, including the systematization of territorial data and contributions relevant to the diagnosis and subsequent stages. i) Review and update databases and cartographic products as new information is incorporated into the products. j) Ensure the proper organization, documentation, and archiving of produced data, enabling its future use by the team and partner institutions. k) Participate in technical meetings, in person or virtual, as requested by the supervisors. l) Maintain continuous communication with the technical team, ensuring alignment regarding information needs and established deadlines. m) Ensure the technical quality, integrity, and reliability of the information produced and used within the scope of any consultancy that may be contracted. n) Participate in missions as requested. o) Attend meetings and conferences promoted by UN-Habitat and the projects’ partners as requested. p) Have compliance with UN-Habitat quality standards and project requirements, ensuring consistency with institutional guidelines, methodologies and expected outcomes. q) Ensure the adoption of ethical principles during the consultancy, particularly regarding active listening, respect for diversity, and the promotion of a safe, inclusive and participatory learning environment. r) Perform any other management-related duties assigned by the Head of Brazil Office, consistent with the functions of the position. The consultant will be responsible for completing all courses and training activities that are indicated to him/her by his/her supervisor. The security course BSAFE, from UNDSS, is required to be accredited during the first month of employment. The consultant will be responsible for his/her own security, so the person should get familiarized with United Nations security mechanisms and comply with them according to the Framework of Accountability for the United Nations Security Management System. Outputs/Work Assignment The consultant will support the implementation of projects in Brazil according to the stated responsibilities.

Skills • Proficiency in data analysis and visualization tools is required. • Good computer skills, including Microsoft Office, Outlook, and collaborative tools, are required. • The ability to organize and systematize large volumes of information is required. • Basic experience with platforms for sharing programming and version control such as GitHub or GitLab is desirable. • Good command of programming languages such as R or Python is desirable. Competencies • Professionalism: Demonstrates professional competence and mastery of financial management principles and practices; applies sound judgment; shows persistence in meeting commitments and achieving results; demonstrates integrity and accountability. • Planning and organization: Develops clear goals and priorities; identifies priority activities and assignments; allocates appropriate time and resources for completing work and meeting deadlines. • Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others and responds appropriately; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping stakeholders informed. • Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues and partners to achieve organizational goals; values diversity; contributes to an inclusive and respectful work environment. Duties and Responsibilities
Créé en 1964, le Centre du commerce international (ITC) est l’agence de coopération technique conjointe des Nations Unies et de l’Organisation mondiale du commerce (OMC) en charge de la promotion durable du commerce et en particulier des exportations des pays en développement et des économies en transition. Le but de l’ITC est de rendre les entreprises des pays en développement plus compétitives sur les marchés mondiaux, d’accélérer le développement économique et de contribuer à la réalisation des Objectifs de développement durable (ODD) des Nations Unies. Ainsi, l’organisation contribue à la création d’emplois au niveau de segments de chaînes de valeurs agricoles et des services porteurs en particulier pour les jeunes et les femmes. Le Programme de "Renforcement de capacités en matière de commerce des services en Afrique centrale dans le cadre de la ZLECAf " – CEEAC Services – vise à contribuer à l'augmentation des échanges intrarégionaux, continentaux et bilatéraux dans le secteur des services. Financé par l'UE et mis en œuvre par le Centre du Commerce International (ITC), ce programme de quatre ans a pour objectif spécifique d'accroître la libéralisation et les exportations des services dans des secteurs spécifiques au niveau continental, régional ou bilatéral conformément à la Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine (ZLECAf). En donnant la priorité aux entreprises dirigées par des femmes et des jeunes, le programme vise également à favoriser l'inclusion économique et encourager des pratiques commerciales durables. Résultats escomptés : • Produit 1 : Les barrières commerciales pour les secteurs prioritaires de commerce des services sont analysées et les politiques liées sont correctement définies. • Produit 2: Appui aux États de la CEEAC pour l'élaboration des listes d'engagements spécifiques dans le cadre du Protocole de ZLECAf sur le commerce des services. • Produit 3: La sensibilisation aux opportunités d'exportation est renforcée pour le secteur privé, en particulier pour les entreprises dirigées par des femmes et des jeunes. • Produit 4: Des réglementations appropriées, harmonisées et transparentes en matière de commerce des services en intégrant des dispositions sociales et liées au climat sont développées et plus accessibles. Le programme couvre les 11 pays de la Communauté Économique des États de l'Afrique centrale (CEEAC) à savoir : Angola, Burundi, Tchad, Guinée équatoriale, Gabon, Cameroun, République Centrafricaine, République Démocratique du Congo, République du Congo, Rwanda et Sao Tomé-et-Principe. Un bureau local basé à Yaoundé au Cameroun accueille les équipes de professionnels et de personnel de soutien en charge de la mise en œuvre du programme CEEAC Services. L’équipe CEEAC Services est composée d’un consultant en suivi et évaluation, d’une assistante administrative et financière, et d’une consultante visibilité, tous rattachés au Bureau de Yaoundé. En parallèle, le manager du programme CEEAC Services basé au siège de l’ITC à Genève assure la liaison entre le bureau local de Yaoundé, les experts techniques de l’ITC, et les fonctions support (juridique, finances, achats, communication, ressources humaines). Il finalise également les rapports finaux. L’expert-e / Spécialiste du commerce des services en Afrique centrale sera basé à Libreville Gabon dans les locaux de la CEEAC. DESCRIPTION DES RESPONSABILITES Le Consultant travaillera à 100% pour le programme CEEAC-Services. Sous la supervision générale du Gestionnaire du programme au sein du Bureau pour l’Afrique au siège de l’ITC à Genève, et en collaboration avec le Point Focal du programme au sein de la CEEAC, l’expert(e) technique spécialiste du commerce des services en Afrique centrale sera chargé(e) de fournir un appui spécialisé et de contribuer à la mise en œuvre efficace des activités prévues, en ligne avec les objectifs spécifiques du programme. Responsabilités et tâches clés : 1. Coordination et gouvernance du projet : • Apporter une assistance complémentaire à la coordination du programme sur toutes les questions ponctuelles et pertinentes dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du projet ; • Faciliter la collaboration et la coopération entre les parties prenantes (Commission de la CEEAC, États membres, Haut Conseil des Affaires, siège de l’ITC), y compris le suivi rigoureux des demandes, des questionnaires et des documents requis. • Participer aux réunions, ainsi qu’à la planification, au suivi des progrès et à l’évaluation des résultats du projet ; • Veiller à la mise en œuvre effective des recommandations issues des comités de pilotage. 2. Appui technique et gestion des expertises • Proposer et élaborer, le cas échéant, les termes de référence pour les consultants nationaux, ayant l’expertise adéquate pour entreprendre certaines activités selon les besoins ; • Coordonner et renforcer le travail des experts nationaux et régionaux impliqués dans les activités du projet ; • Identifier des organisations nationales et régionales pertinentes susceptibles de collaborer avec l’ITC dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre des activités ; • Assurer la collecte et le suivi des demandes émanant de la Commission de la CEEAC, des États membres concernés et des parties prenantes du secteur privé, notamment en matière de renforcement des capacités, d’appui technique et d’assistance ; • Assurer une veille continue des développements en matière de commerce des services dans la région, y compris sur les nouveaux instruments adoptés et l’évolution des négociations. 3. Renforcement des capacités et partenariats • Appuyer les institutions nationales / régionales collaborant avec l’ITC dans la mise en œuvre des activités, notamment à travers des protocoles d’accord ; • Contribuer au renforcement des capacités des partenaires institutionnels pour assurer une exécution efficace du projet. 4. Activités opérationnelles et techniques • Participer, le cas échéant, aux ateliers organisés dans le cadre du projet et préparer les comptes rendus et rapports correspondants ; • Intervenir en qualité d’expert(e) et animer des séminaires, ateliers ou conférences sur le commerce des services en Afrique centrale ; • Formuler une feuille de route stratégique pour les secteurs des services de la CEEAC sélectionnés dans le cadre du projet, dotée d’un Plan d’action et le soumettre à la CEEAC pour validation. 5. Planification et reporting • Contribuer à l’élaboration des plans de travail annuels et trimestriels du programme sur la base du document de description de l’action ; • Contribuer à la préparation des rapports techniques du projet ; • Produire un rapport annuel sur l’état de mise en œuvre de l’accord sur le commerce des services dans le cadre de la ZLECAf, avec un focus sur les États membres de la CEEAC. 6. Autres tâches • Exécuter toute autre tâche pertinente contribuant à la bonne mise en œuvre du programme et en appui à la Commission de la CEEAC dans le cadre du commerce des services. Droit d’auteur : Le Consultant s’assure qu’il/elle a obtenu les permissions nécessaires concernant les droits de propriété intellectuelle requis pour la fourniture des services faisant l’objet du présent contrat de consultant, ainsi que pour la diffusion ultérieure par l’ITC des résultats de ces services sous quelque forme ou par quelque procédé que ce soit. Les preuves documentaires de ces permissions sont conservées et soumises à l’ITC. Si des droits de licence sont exigés pour l’utilisation de matériel protégé par des droits d’auteur de tiers, le Consultant doit demander l’autorisation préalable écrite de l’ITC. Il/elle doit s’assurer à obtenir l’accréditation à/aux l’événement(s), selon les besoins.
Qualifications/special skills
• Une Licence en Economie, Management, Commerce international, ou toute autre discipline associée. • Ou un Master en Economie, Management, Commerce international ou toute autre discipline associée. • Pour une licence / Bachelor, avoir au moins quatre (04) années d’expérience dans le domaine du commerce des services ; • Pour un Master avoir au moins deux (02) années d’années d’expérience dans le domaine du commerce des services. Compétences • Expérience de travail réussie dans le commerce des services en Afrique et Afrique centrale ; • Expérience professionnelle multi-pays dans les projets de développement ; • Très bonne connaissance des protocoles la ZLECAf et du cadre des affaires en Afrique centrale ; • Très bonne compréhension des problématiques liées au secteurs des services prioritaires de la ZLECAf (transport, tourisme, services professionnels aux entreprises, TIC, finance) notamment en Afrique centrale ; • Bonne compréhension des attentes et problématiques du secteur public et du secteur privé en Afrique centrale ; • Réseau relationnel solide au sein de la communauté des affaires dans la CEEAC ; • Expérience avérée dans la rédaction de rapports et la réalisation d’études économiques ; • Compétences en développement de contenus de formation et de tenues d’ateliers ; • Bonne connaissance des procédures administratives et financières de l'ONU.

Excellente maîtrise du Français et de l’Anglais obligatoire.

Not available.

Duties and Responsibilities
BACKGROUND: The International Trade Centre (ITC) supports SMEs in developing countries by enhancing their competitiveness, promoting digital trade, and strengthening business ecosystems through initiatives such as Youth & Trade, ecomConnect, SheTrades, and tech sector development programmes. In Sierra Leone, ITC is implementing the “Empowering youth through digital technologies” project (2024-2028), which aims to boost youth employment and entrepreneurship by building digital skills, strengthening SMEs’ competitiveness, and improving support systems and policies within the digital economy. As part of this initiative, selected MSMEs will receive branding and communication support to strengthen their market positioning, improve the presentation of their products and services, and enhance their visibility across offline and digital channels. To support this component, ITC is recruiting a Graphic Designer Consultant to develop branding and promotional materials for a portfolio of 12-15 MSMEs from different sectors. DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES Under the direct supervision of the E-commerce Programme Officer, the Consultant will undertake the following tasks: Activity 1 - Branding Needs Review and Coordination (November 2026) The consultant will: ● Participate in introductory in person meetings and briefing sessions with assigned MSMEs and the Branding Support Consultant. ● Review and analyse the branding brief developed for each MSME. ● Ensure a clear understanding of each enterprise's products, services, target market and branding objectives. ● Coordinate regularly with the project team and relevant consultants to ensure consistency and alignment throughout implementation. Activity 2 - Branding Assets Development (December 2026) The consultant will develop branding packages for 12-15 MSMEs. The branding package may include: ● Logo design: Develop a logo where required by the MSME, including appropriate logo variations and digital formats. ● Mini branding guidelines: Develop a concise 3-4 page branding guideline covering: ○ Logo usage ○ Colour palette ○ Typography ○ Graphic elements/patterns, where applicable ○ Basic imagery/visual style ○ Basic brand tone/voice ● Business card: ○ Design a professional business card, including contact and social media information. ○ Digital contact/business card: Develop an adapted digital version suitable for sharing through WhatsApp and other digital channels. ● Thank-you card: Design a reusable thank-you/customer appreciation card. ● Product and packaging branding: Develop appropriate bag labels, product labels, stickers and/or packaging elements, depending on the MSME's products and business model. ● Social media templates: Develop three editable social media templates for use across platforms such as Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp. The templates should cover: ○ Product/service promotion ○ Customer testimonial/social proof ○ Educational or storytelling content ● Social media profile assets: Develop appropriate profile/cover assets where relevant, such as a branded profile image, cover image or WhatsApp catalogue asset. The consultant will: ● Produce visually coherent, professional and practical branding materials that reflect each MSME’s identity, target market and business objectives. ● Ensure that all branding materials are suitable for digital use and future printing, with appropriate file formats and dimensions. ● Incorporate feedback and provide up to three rounds of revisions per MSME, based on consolidated feedback from the MSME/project team. ● Provide all editable source files and final high-resolution/production-ready files, organised in a clearly structured digital folder for each MSME. ● Ensure that editable templates, particularly social media templates, can be easily updated and reused by the MSMEs using accessible design tools such as Canva, where applicable. Activity 3 - Quality Assurance and Finalization (January 2027) The consultant will: ● Ensure consistency across all branding assets produced. ● Incorporate feedback received from MSMEs and the project team. ● Finalize and submit all deliverables according to agreed standards and timelines. ● Prepare a brief summary of work completed and deliverables produced for each MSME. ITC Communication and Visibility Guidelines ● All communication products delivered under this assignment must comply, where applicable, with ITC’s visual identity, communication and visibility guidelines, particularly where materials are intended for promotion through ITC corporate or project channels or include the ITC logo. ● The Consultant will review and follow the relevant guidance and supporting materials available on ITC’s Communications and Events SharePoint, including corporate templates, Canva templates, partner identity guidelines and multimedia guidelines, as applicable. ● No new project-specific logo or project social media account shall be created under this assignment. Copyright Clause: The consultant has to ensure that she has obtained the necessary permissions with regard to intellectual property rights required to perform her services under this consultancy contract and for the subsequent dissemination by ITC in any form. Documentary proof is to be submitted to ITC. Should any license fee be due for the use of copyrighted materials of third parties, the consultant shall request the prior written permission from ITC. Org. Setting and Reporting
This position is located in the United Nations Regional Office for Central Africa (UNOCA) in Libreville, Gabon. Libreville is classified as a "A" hardship duty station and a family duty station. The incumbent reports to the Special Representative of the Secretary-General and Head of UNOCA. UNOCA covers the countries of the Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS), namely: Angola, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Republic of Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Rwanda and Sao Tome and Principe. Read about the mandate on https://unoca.unmissions.org/ The Chief of Staff (COS) is responsible for ensuring the integrated and coherent functioning of the mission across all areas, components and locations. To that effect the Chief of Staff oversees the core mechanisms and processes that enable the integrated delivery of UNOCA's mandate in particular strategic and operational planning, policy and coordination, senior-level decision - making and information management. The Chief of Staff may be requested to perform other relevant duties, as required.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Chief of Staff will be responsible for the following duties: Management : Ensures the effective direction and integrated management of all the mission's activities in line with the strategic vision and guidance of the SRSG. Oversees the internal management of the mission on behalf of the SRSG, including the development of advice on and promotion of policies on management issues, including risk management. Facilitates the translation of policy intent and highlevel direction of mission leadership into viable tasks and works with components to ensure their effective implementation. Directs and oversees core integrated processes and mechanisms that enable the integrated delivery of the mission's mandate, including programme management, information management and crisis management. Holds the overall management responsibility for and oversees the work of the staff working in the office of the SRSG, as appropriate. Serves as the focal point in the Office of the SRSG for all sensitive personnel and management issues, as well as for contacts with the Office of Internal Oversight Services and the Resident Auditor. Serves as interface between the Office of SRSG and the Mission Support component on all personnel matters and oversees the recruitment of senior mission management appointments. Planning and budgeting. Oversees Mission-wide planning processes, ensuring coherence is maintained between mandated tasks, component plans/concepts of operations as required by policies, guidelines and best practices on planning. Ensures the proper conduct of processes critical to the delivery of mandate implementation, particularly strategic planning, policy coordination and senior level decision making. The Chief of Staff also ensures a clear understanding between substantive priorities and support capacities; and liaises with all components to advise and ensure the use of the best methods for achieving the objectives and priorities of the mission. Facilitates the translation of policy intent and high-level direction by the SRSG into viable work plans, and works with components to ensure the implementation of those work plans. In coordination with the Chief Mission Support, ensures an integrated approach to the results-based budget process, including alignment with strategic and operational plans and adequate provisions to meet resource requirements, and oversees the process as it relates to substantive mission components. Periodically reviews, with the mission leadership team, the delivery of component work plans, identifying necessary adjustments to mission plans and/or revised assumptions, as appropriate. Policy. Provides guidance on United Nations policies and procedures. Coordinates the development and implementation of cross-cutting and management policies among the various components of the Mission. Ensures that advice and information on crosscutting issues is coordinated with all relevant components of the Mission prior to submission to the SRSG. Reporting, communications and information management. Ensures effective functioning of coherent communications structures and systems and serves as the focal point for communication with United Nations Headquarters in New York.. Oversees mission-wide, integrated procedures and systems for information analysis and management, including intra-mission information sharing, reporting requirements, security classification, records management and publication of Intranet content. Oversees the implementation of knowledge management approaches throughout the mission, such as handover notes, after-action reviews and end-of-assignment reports. Protocol. In close consultation with the SRSG and Chief Mission Support, facilitates discussions between the mission and national government on issues related to UNOCA's functions Advises the SRSG on protocol matters and supervises and provides guidance on the preparation and coordination of official visits. Performs other duties as required. Duties and Responsibilities
Background: This position is located in the United Nations Office of the Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa (OSE-HoA) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The Office of the Special Envoy is mandated to promote peace and conflict prevention in the region, working closely with IGAD under the UN-IGAD cooperation framework signed in Djibouti on 17 November 2015, and other regional organizations. vacancies.jobTitle: Expert on Inclusive Insurance and Social Protection Mechanisms With experience in Latin America
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
Propose Nano‑Insurance Scheme for Egypt and Presentation to Stakeholders Build on the provided documents, a systematic literature review, and feedback from ESCWA, GIZ, and country stakeholders, the consultant will prepare a short design proposal presenting one or more nano‑insurance models suitable for further exploration in Egypt. The document should outline the scheme’s preliminary design parameters, including proposed target population(s); potential benefits (short‑term and/or shock‑related); contribution/payment modalities suited to irregular incomes; feasible distribution and administrative channels; basic institutional and operational requirements; parameters necessary for preliminary costing.
Work Location
Remote
Expected duration
6 weeks
Duties and Responsibilities
Backgroumd Women’s labour force participation in the Arab region remains among the lowest globally, with wide gender gaps and a high concentration of women in informal or irregular employment. This exclusion from contributory social protection systems is reflected in very low coverage of benefits such as maternity insurance, far below global averages. The situation is particularly pronounced in countries such as Egypt, Morocco, Tunisia, and Jordan, where many women rely on social assistance rather than comprehensive social insurance. In particular, informal employment constitutes the majority of the labour market in the region, especially in Egypt, where over 70% of workers operate informally. Shifts in employment patterns toward own account work and away from formal employer–employee arrangements exacerbate vulnerabilities, leaving workers without pensions, health insurance, or income protection. Barriers such as high contribution requirements, administrative complexity, and irregular incomes make it difficult for informal workers—particularly women—to enroll in and maintain participation in traditional social insurance systems. This context strengthens the case for complementary, flexible solutions that can accommodate fluctuating earnings and provide entry level protection. These structural gaps underline the need for innovative mechanisms—such as nano insurance and other ultra low cost schemes—that can extend social protection to women working outside formal employment arrangements. Emerging practices from Latin America offer valuable lessons on how digital tools and nano scale products can expand access to social protection. Across the region, governments and social partners have used electronic registration systems, mobile payments, and platform-based services to reduce transaction costs and increase visibility of informal work. Nano and microinsurance initiatives—such as MAPFRE’s bundled funeral insurance with CODENSA utility bills in Colombia or Bancamía and BBVA Seguros’ maternity related microinsurance products—demonstrate how small, embedded, low premium schemes can effectively reach low income and irregular workers. These models leverage technology, private sector capabilities, and daily life payment channels to overcome trust gaps, simplify enrollment, and address gender specific vulnerabilities. ESCWA is partnering with the GIZ Hiya MENA project—which operates in Jordan, Tunisia, Egypt, and Morocco with a strong focus on improving the economic security of women in the informal sector—to advance innovative solutions for inclusive social protection. Building on this partnership, ESCWA will leverage its longstanding cooperation with the Economic and Social Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean, and other local partners and its expertise in regional knowledge exchange to produce targeted policy analysis and knowledge products on nano insurance and other ultra low cost insurance mechanisms. Through this joint effort, the two institutions aim to adapt successful international and Latin American experiences to the specific needs of women informal workers in the MENA region, supporting governments in designing practical and scalable insurance options Considering this, there is a clear need to engage a senior consultant with deep expertise in the design of insurance products in Latin America—particularly those involving low fees, low transaction costs, and delivery channels suitable for workers with irregular incomes. The consultant should have direct experience with government led schemes targeting informal or low income populations, and the integration of such models into broader social protection frameworks. Crucially, they must understand how to adapt Latin American experiences to contexts like Egypt and the wider HIYA MENA, ensuring relevance for government programs that extend coverage to female informal workers and other vulnerable groups. Duties and responsibilities The international consultant is expected to undertake the following tasks in strong collaboration and coordination with ESCWA’s SP team, GIZ Hiya MENA and relevant national stakeholders: 1. Identification and Discussion of Suitable Scheme Options for Egypt. Based on the review and discussions with ESCWA, GIZ, and relevant stakeholders, identify one or more nano‑insurance scheme options adapted to the Egyptian context. Work with the project team providing the actuary with all design‑related inputs required for preliminary costing—such as target groups, benefit structures, payment channels, and basic operational assumptions. 2. Presentation to Egyptian Stakeholders. Present the proposed preliminary scheme options and findings to Egyptian institutions, collect feedback, and support ESCWA and GIZ in facilitating technical discussions. 3. Contribution to an Action Plan for Egypt. Support ESCWA over approximately in drafting a short action plan outlining next steps for testing and refining nano‑insurance options tailored to Egypt’s institutional and policy landscape. 4. Attending meetings – scheduled and ah-hoc – with ESCWA, GIZ and national stakeholders to receive inputs and feedback
Qualifications/special skills
A master’s degree in development studies, Public Policy, Economics, or a related area is required. A Ph.D. is desirable. All candidates must submit a copy of the required educational degree. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. A minimum of 12 years of professional work experience in in the inclusive finance and insurance sector, social protection, or related fields is required. At least 5 years of experience in the design, implementation, or advisory support of insurance, financial inclusion and/or social protection policies, programmes, or strategies in middle-income countries is required. A minimum of 4 years of experience working with government institutions or public agencies on social protection development is required. Experience working in Latin America is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat; and Arabic is a working language of ESCWA. For this position, fluency in English is required. Note: “Fluency” equals a rating of ‘fluent’ in all four areas (speak, read, write, and understand) and “Knowledge of” equals a rating of ‘confident’ in two of the four areas.

Result of Service
Opening of a Geneva based liaison facility: The establishment of a UNCCD Liaison facility in Geneva, a major multilateral headquarters bringing together 181 Permanent Missions, United Nations specialized agencies, international organizations, and private sector stakeholders, would undoubtedly strengthen the Secretariat's ability to engage, mobilize, and raise awareness among the Geneva-based specialized hub and further promote consensus building around core aspects of the process. It will also strengthen the secretariat’s ability to access funding from donor countries, the private sector, philanthropic foundations, and the City and Canton of Geneva. Collaborate closely with the Swiss Permanent Mission, the City and Canton of Geneva and UNOG's Legal Office on opening procedures for the Liaison Office, including drafting the letter and reference documents, as required. Liaise with UNOG's administration to arrange the allocation of office space.
Work Location
Home-based.
Expected duration
80 days between November 2026 and February 2027.
Duties and Responsibilities
Background note: Desertification, along with climate change and the loss of biodiversity were identified as the greatest challenges to sustainable development during the 1992 Rio Earth Summit. Established in 1994, the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) is the sole legally binding international agreement linking environment and development to sustainable land management. The Convention seeks to support countries to address Desertification, Land Degradation, and Drought (DLDD). (www.unccd.int) Climate crises, high temperatures, extreme heat, increasing drought, and land degradation are all factors that threaten global food security and contribute to conflicts and population displacement in several regions of the world. Duties & Responsibilities: Under direct supervision of the Director of New York Office the C/IC will have the following tasks : Representation and Institutional Liaison: - Represent the UNCCD, before international organizations and multilateral processes based in Geneva. - Maintain relations with Permanent Missions and the relevant Swiss Federal and Geneva authorities. - Participate in inter-agency coordination mechanisms and relevant international meetings. - Monitor international processes that may have an impact on the implementation of the Convention. Development of Partnerships and Synergies: - Identify and develop partnerships with United Nations agencies, international organizations, and other Geneva-based actors. - Facilitate informal briefings, consultations, and bilateral exchanges with Geneva-based interlocutors, factoring in elements stemming from the UNCCCD process. Support to Resource Mobilization and Development Cooperation: - Contribute to the mobilization of financial and technical resources for the implementation of the Convention and the outcomes and recommendations of COPs. - Develop relationships with donors, foundations, financial institutions, and development partners based in Geneva. - Identify opportunities for joint financing and inter-institutional cooperation. Advocacy, Communication, and Knowledge Sharing: - Promote the UNCCD's priorities and key messages in Geneva-based international forums. -Disseminate knowledge and best practices related to land restoration, sustainable land management, and drought resilience. Foresight Analysis and Support to the Secretariat: - Conduct strategic monitoring of relevant international policies and negotiations. - Identify opportunities to integrate UNCCD objectives into the programmes and strategies of international partners.
Qualifications/special skills
- A first-level university degree in political science, international relations, international economics or other related area is required. - A minimum of two years of progressively responsible experience in political science, international relations, law, development management, or related areas is required.
Languages
- Fluency in spoken and written English is required. Knowledge of an additional official UN language is an advantage.
Additional Information
Only individuals who can act as independent, individual economical operators are qualified to apply. Individuals who can provide their services only on account of an institution or enterprise are not eligible under this procedure. Individuals engaged under a consultancy or individual contract will not be considered “staff members” under the Staff Regulations and Rules of the United Nations Secretariat and will not be entitled to benefits provided therein (such as leave entitlements and medical insurance coverage). Their conditions of service will be governed by their contract and the General Conditions of Contracts for the Services of Consultants and Individual Contractors. Consultant and individual contractor is responsible for determining tax liabilities and for the payment of any taxes and/or duties, in accordance with local or other applicable laws. For remote consultancies, the selected candidate will be required to have a laptop or desktop PC (with Windows 11 or newer) or Mac (with the latest MacOS update), as well as a reliable, high-speed internet connection. An Office 365 license will be provided by the UNCCD to enable the candidate to access official emails, SharePoint, OneDrive and other office applications, such as Word and Excel. Further computer requirements: An antivirus application which receives regular updates; Browsers must be a newer version with regular updates enabled; Regular Windows 11 updates should be enabled with Windows laptop or PC. In addition, a mobile phone will be required to enable Multifactor Authentication (MFA) through SMS or the Authenticator App.

Result of Service
• A portfolio-wide design framework for PCCP MENA funding proposals and concept notes, determining implementation priorities and their technical translation into results-based design and performance indicators. • One gender-responsive assessment for PCCP activities in Lebanon, including methodology design and integration of findings into programme planning and gender mainstreaming measures. • Donor reporting outputs for the PCCP MENA portfolio, with content and framing determined by the consultant in line with donor priorities and results-based reporting requirements. • Provide operational, drafting, and advisory support for the implementation of PCCP activities addressing illicit trafficking and supply chain security in Lebanon and other MENA countries, including advisory input on activity sequencing, risk and contextual considerations, and alignment with donor and technical requirements, in coordination with the relevant Project Officer(s) and national counterparts.
Work Location
Home-based with travel
Expected duration
10.11.26-31.03.27
Duties and Responsibilities
In 2025, the Passenger and Cargo Control Programme (PCCP) was established by merging the UNODC WCO Container Control Programme (CCP) with the INTERPOL WCO Airport Communication Programme (AIRCOP). The programme’s objective is to improve the capacity of Member States and their law enforcement agencies active at air, sea and land borders, to disrupt illicit flows of containers, cargo and mail, intercept high-risk passengers and identify victims of trafficking, while facilitating legitimate trade and the movement of people. PCCP builds high-risk cargo and passengers risk assessment, identification and inspection capacities through establishment of nationally owned Port Control Units (PCUs), Air Control Units (ACUs) and Land Control Units (LCUs), staffed by customs, police, and other law enforcement officers. The programme is rolled out in multiple phases from initial technical needs assessments, through establishment of specialist units, to training and ongoing operational support, with a strong emphasis on intelligence-sharing and interagency cooperation at both national and international levels. In the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, PCCP operates in Algeria, Egypt, Iraq, Lebanon, Libya, Jordan, Tunisia, Morocco, Syria, and Yemen. The portfolio is supported by a diverse donor base, including an extended German-funded project supporting PCCP implementation in Lebanon. Sustaining and expanding this portfolio requires coordinated donor engagement, technically sound funding proposals aligned with implementation priorities, and regular donor reporting at the regional level. In parallel, PCCP is strengthening the gender-responsiveness of its programming, including through a gender assessment of activities in Lebanon, to ensure interventions are inclusive and aligned with donor expectations on gender mainstreaming. The assignment will be carried out under the framework of the PCCP and will serve to maximize funding opportunities for the implementation and maintenance of PCUs/ACUs/LCUs and delivery of specialized trainings, while providing technical and advisory support for donor reporting, resource mobilization, and gender-responsive programming at the regional level. The purpose of the assignment is to design and align funding proposals and concept notes for the PCCP MENA portfolio with implementation priorities, results-based design, and monitoring frameworks, in order to sustain and expand PCCP activities, particularly in the MENA region. The assignment includes leading the technical design of the Lebanon gender-responsive assessment methodology and integrating assessment findings into programme planning and gender mainstreaming efforts, in coordination with a Lebanon-based gender expert responsible for data collection and contextual/sensitivity guidance, as part of the German-funded project in Lebanon. It also includes determining the content and framing of donor reports and fundraising documentation for the MENA portfolio, ensuring alignment with donor priorities and results-based reporting requirements. In the current phase of the programme, the assignment provides technical and advisory support to PCCP resource mobilization and donor engagement, complemented by operational and drafting support for the implementation of activities in Lebanon and other MENA countries, in coordination with field-based Project Officers and national counterparts. Under the supervision of the Regional Programme Coordinator for the MENA region, the consultant will: • Determine the programmatic and technical content of funding proposals across the PCCP MENA portfolio, under authority of the PCCP Regional Coordinator, ensuring alignment of implementation priorities with technical components, results-based design, and monitoring frameworks, including performance indicators. • Lead the technical design of the Lebanon gender-responsive mapping methodology and integrate assessment findings into programme planning and gender mainstreaming efforts, in coordination with a Lebanon-based gender expert responsible for data collection and contextual/sensitivity guidance. • Draft and determine the content and framing of donor reports and fundraising documents for the PCCP MENA portfolio, aligned with donor priorities and results-based reporting requirements, under authority of the PCCP Regional Coordinator. • Provide operational and drafting support for the implementation of PCCP activities addressing illicit trafficking and supply chain security in Lebanon and other MENA countries, including preparation of activity documentation and reporting inputs, in coordination with the relevant Project Officer(s) and national counterparts. All tasks will be completed in close cooperation with the Head of PCCP and UNODC Headquarters in Vienna (DO/BMB) and MENA
Qualifications/special skills
An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in the fields of international relations, criminology, law or related fields is required. A first level university degree in similar fields in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree Work experience A minimum of five years of professional experience in border management, programme development, donor engagement, or related areas is required. Demonstrated experience in the design of funding proposals and concept notes on crime, illicit goods, rule of law, and supply chain security, including alignment with results-based design and monitoring frameworks is required. Experience in gender-responsive programming or gender assessments is required. Experience in donor reporting and resource mobilization is required. Work experience with the United Nations or related organizations is desirable. Coursework/specialization in programme management, logical frameworks, workplans and fundraising is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this post, fluency in oral and written English and French is required. Knowledge of another UN language is an advantage.

Not available.

vacancies.jobDescription:
Org. Setting and Reporting
UNRWA is a United Nations agency established by the General Assembly in 1949 and is mandated to provide assistance and protection to a population of some 5.8 million registered Palestine refugees. Its mission is to help Palestine refugees in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, West Bank and the Gaza Strip to achieve their full potential in human development, pending a just solution to their plight. UNRWA's services encompass education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure and improvement, microfinance, and emergency assistance. UNRWA is the largest UN operation in the Middle East with more than 30,000 staff.UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions. If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to make a tangible difference for one of the most vulnerable communities in the world, UNRWA would like to hear from you. The incumbent of this post is responsible to the Field Administration Officer-A16. The incumbent of this post supervises and provides technical support to a team of support staff.
Responsibilities
Provides management support to the Field Administration Officer (FAO) in planning, integrating, monitoring, and reporting the activities of the Field Administration Office; contributes to the improvements of Field Administration Office policies, processes, and procedures. Advises and assists FAO in the preparation of the biennium budget of Field Administration Office and periodic budget reviews; monitors expenditures effectively and recommends necessary adjustments as required. Negotiates, prepares, concludes, and finalizes lease contracts, including financial matters, within the Field; assists the FAO in managing office and distribution centers' rental contracts; liaises with landlords and/or local authorities in this regard. UN Core Values of Integrity, Professionalism and Respect for Diversity, and Core Competencies of Communication, Working with People and Drive for Results apply by default. English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English and Arabic are required. vacancies.jobTitle: Local Consultant – Specialized Technical Consultancy for Advising Municipalities in Pernambuco on the Development of Municipal Plans for Crime and Violence Prevention.
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
DELIVERABLE 1: Report containing the partial version of the last five municipal prevention plans. Each partial plan shall include the overall objective, specific objectives, expected results, and the consolidated record of the problem tree and objectives tree. DELIVERABLE 2: Report containing the final five completed municipal prevention plans, developed in a participatory manner. Each plan shall present the overall and specific objectives, those responsible for implementation, targets, estimated financial investments, and monitoring indicators.
Work Location
Home-based with travel
Expected duration
19.11-31.12.2026
Duties and Responsibilities
Under the supervision of the UNODC Pernambuco Project Coordinator in Brazil, the consultant will provided technical support and contribute to the following activities: • Establish contact with the focal points of the ten previously selected municipalities, namely: Ipojuca, Palmares, Cabo de Santo Agostinho, Jaboatão dos Guararapes, Vitória de Santo Antão, Belo Jardim, São Bento do Una, Lajedo, Garanhuns and Limoeiro. • Support actions aimed at mobilizing municipalities to participate in an in-person meeting with the UNODC team, with the objective of presenting the initiative, aligning expectations, and promoting engagement; • Review UNODC institutional and operational documents, as well as the diagnostic assessments provided for the ten designated municipalities; and, based on technical exchanges with municipal managers, identify and systematize the main local demands, ongoing initiatives (such as campaigns, projects, or programs), and strategic elements to inform the development of municipal prevention plans; • Provide technical support to the planning and implementation of the first official in-person visits to the ten municipalities, with the aim of strengthening dialogue, ensuring clarity regarding initiatives, and local needs; • Propose and systematize a participatory methodological planning framework for the technical advisory services, informed by the specific contexts and identified demands of the municipalities, and aligned with the objectives of the “Together for Safety” (Juntos pela Segurança) and “Together for Citizenship” (Juntos pela Cidadania) Programs and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs); • Provide technical support to actions that facilitate the municipalities’ adherence to the partnership with the Government of the State of Pernambuco for crime and violence prevention; • Provide technical input to implementation of strategies for articulation, mobilization, and awareness-raising in the territories, together with municipal managers, regarding the Prevention Plan; • Plan and implement the design and logistical strategy for periodic technical visits to the municipalities, aimed at strengthening the Project and enabling the continuous collection of information, suggestions, and recommendations; • Participate in and contribute technically to the two in-person seminars planned under the Project; • Conduct at least two virtual mentoring meetings with municipal partners, one collective meeting with all municipalities and one individual meeting with each municipality; • Participate, when required, in strategic meetings with Pernambuco state secretariats and other partners linked to the Project; • Provide technical support to the UNODC Project Coordination in activities related to the municipalities, including participation in internal meetings for validation of deliverables; • Contribute to the development of training courses, particularly in the design of content and in the identification of demands for their implementation.
Qualifications/special skills
An advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in social science, psychology, law, international relations, or related field is required. A first-level university degree in similar fields in combination with two (2) additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Limited professional experience in at least one of the following activities: social research; design, implementation, evaluation, and/or monitoring of public policies, especially in the areas of drugs, public security, crime and violence prevention, social assistance, social urbanism, and/or urban management is required. Proven research experience, including the use of qualitative and quantitative methods, as well as experience in drafting technical and academic reports, is required; Professional experience in articulation, mobilization, awareness-raising, or facilitation of participatory processes within the context of social projects and/or public policies, is required.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this post, fluency in Portuguese is required. Knowledge of another United Nations Language is an advantage.
Additional Information
Not available.
No Fee

vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
the consultant will revise the beta version of GETSI Tunis and adjust sectoral and geographical coverage.
Work Location
Remote
Expected duration
2 months
Duties and Responsibilities
Scope and Objectives The Arab Trade Simulator Interface (ATSI), developed by ESCWA in 2020, covered 18 Arab countries individually, along with a limited number of trading partners. Since the development of the first version of ATSI, several Arab countries have approached ESCWA to develop tailored versions of the simulator to meet the specific analytical needs of their respective ministries. In response to a request from the Tunisian Ministry of Commerce and Export Development, ESCWA developed a customized national version known as the Global Economywide Trade Simulator Interface (GETSI Tunisia). Unlike the original ATSI, which relies on a standardized sectoral and geographical classification, GETSI Tunisia reflects the Ministry’s specific requirements regarding sectoral disaggregation and the individual representation of trading partners. The purpose of this consultancy is to further revise the beta version of GETSI Tunisia by adjusting its sectoral and geographical coverage to reflect the Ministry’s requirements regarding the sectors and trading partners to be represented individually in the simulator. The consultancy will also update the baseline scenario to incorporate the latest available projections for GDP and other key exogenous variables for Tunisia and the rest of the world. Activities and tasks The consultant is expected to undertake the following tasks: 1. Assist ESCWA’s team in revising the global database used for the beta version of GETSI Tunisia by adjusting the geographical and sectoral aggregation to reflect the comments and recommendations received from the Tunisian Ministry of Commerce and Export Development. 2. Recalibrate GETSI Tunisia using the revised global database, including the updated interlinked Social Accounting Matrices (SAMs), and incorporate the latest available projections for key exogenous variables. 3. Test the model’s functionality and performance through the implementation of selected simulations and the validation of the results. 4. Provides any additional files that may be required for uploading the model on GAMS-MIRO.
Qualifications/special skills
A Master's degree in applied economics or related area is required. A PhD in applied economics or related area is desirable. All candidates must submit a copy of the required educational degree. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. A minimum of 10 years of experience in developing and applying dynamic global CGE models to trade analysis is required. Knowkledge of major Global CGE models (MIRAGE or LINKAGES) is required. Strong experience in coding and solving optimization models using GAMS is required.

Org. Setting and Reporting The United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is mandated by the UN General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities. UN-Habitat is the focal point for all urbanization and human settlement matters within the UN system. UN-Habitat works with partners to build inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable cities and communities. UN-Habitat promotes urbanization as a positive transformative force for people and communities, reducing inequality, discrimination and poverty. The Policy and Legislation Section (PLS) is one of the two Sections of the Planning, Finance and Policy Branch of UN-Habitat. This Section works on Policies, Legislation, Urban-Rural Linkages and Metropolitan Management for sustainable urban development. The Section plays a critical role in implementing the relevant UN-Habitat Assembly resolutions, the relevant Sustainable Development Goals, and the New Urban Agenda. Legislation is embedded within means of implementation 2 (Planning, Finance, Policy, Localization & Governance) of the UN-Habitat Strategic Plan (2026-2029). The Plan calls for clear and transparent legal frameworks for urban development to further establish appropriate rules and regulation systems that respond to real needs, actual capacity, and available resources. These can provide solid, forward-looking frameworks to guide urban development based on accountability, the rule of law, and clear implementation mechanisms, which can be continuously enforced as part of efforts to harness the transformative force of urbanization. vacancies.postingTitle: Consultant to Support the Fifth Forum for Equality
vacancies.jobTitle: Consultant to Support the Fifth Forum for Equality
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
Timely and effective logistical and coordination support provided for the Fifth Arab Forum for Equality (AFE5), contributing to the successful planning, organization and implementation of the Forum, as well as the effective engagement of participants and partners.
Work Location
ESCWA Premises
Expected duration
2 months
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Background Reducing inequality remains a major development challenge in the Arab region, with disparities in access to employment, education, social protection, and economic opportunities continuing to affect current and future generations. In response to these challenges, the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA) established the Arab Forum for Equality (AFE) as a regional platform for dialogue, knowledge exchange, and policy engagement on inequality. Since its launch, the Forum has brought together government representatives, United Nations entities, academia, civil society organizations, development partners, and youth from across the Arab region to discuss emerging dimensions of inequality and identify practical policy solutions. Previous editions of the Forum have examined inequality in youth employment, food security, multiple crises, and social protection, contributing to regional discussions on inclusive and sustainable development. Building on the success of previous editions, ESCWA will convene the Fifth Arab Forum for Equality (AFE5) in Muscat, Oman, on 26-27 January 2027 under the theme “Intergenerational Equality: A Path Forward.” The Forum will bring together policymakers, experts, development partners, civil society organizations, and youth representatives to examine how inequalities are transmitted across generations and to identify policies and strategies that promote equal opportunities, social justice, and inclusive development. The Forum will also serve as a platform for knowledge exchange and peer learning, highlighting successful policy experiences and innovative practices from the Arab region and beyond. 2. Objective ESCWA seeks to engage a consultant to support the preparation and implementation of the Fifth Arab Forum for Equality by providing logistical and coordination support to ensure the effective planning, organization and delivery of the Forum's activities and related outputs. 3. Duties and Responsibilities: The consultant is requested to: • Provide guidance and support in preparing correspondence and communications related to the Forum, including follow-up with participants, speakers, and partners, as required. • Support the development, organization, and updating of contact lists and participant databases to facilitate effective coordination and communication. • Provide support and recommendations for the effective coordination of participant registration processes. • Advise on and support the coordination of travel arrangements, logistics, and visa-related requirements for speakers and participants, as required. • Liaise and coordinate with conference services, interpreters, and other relevant service providers and operational partners to support Forum requirements. • Provide substantive coordination, administrative, and logistical support throughout the preparation and organization of the Forum. • Provide advice and support on other Forum-related matters within the scope of the consultancy, as required.
Qualifications/special skills
A bachelor's degree or equivalent in Social Sciences, International Relations, Public Administration, Project Management, Social Policy, Social Development, Economic Policy, Financial Policy or another relevant field. All candidates must submit a copy of the required educational degree. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. 4 years of progressively responsive experience in administrative support, project coordination, event management, or a related area is required. Experience supporting conferences, forums, workshops, or large-scale events is desirable. Previous experience with the United Nations system or other international organizations is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat; and Arabic is a working language of ESCWA. For this position, fluency in in Arabic and English is required. Fluency in French is desirable. Note: “Fluency” equals a rating of ‘fluent’ in all four areas (speak, read, write, and understand) and “Knowledge of” equals a rating of ‘confident’ in two of the four areas.
Additional Information
Recruitment for this position is on a local basis. The incumbent is required to have the legal right to live and work in the specified working location.
No Fee

Competencies
Professionalism: Shows pride in work and in achievements; Demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; Is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; Is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges. Tailors language, tone, style and format to match the audience. Demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. Technological awareness: Keeps abreast of available technology; Understands applicability and limitations of technology to the work of the office; Actively seeks to apply technology to appropriate tasks; Shows willingness to learn new technology.
Education
High school diploma or equivalent is required. University degree in political science, international relations, social sciences, law, public administration, international economics, economics, journalism is desirable.
