UNRWA's services encompass education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure and improvement, microfinance, and emergency assistance. UNRWA is the largest UN operation in the Middle East with more than 30,000 staff. UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions. If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to make a tangible difference for one of the most vulnerable communities in the world, UNRWA would like to hear from you.- The incumbent is responsible for the provision of technical support towards equitable inclusive quality education to all staff assigned to him/her in the area and will monitor and support their professional development in cooperation with the School Principal to enhance inclusive teaching and learning and promote safe and effective learning environment in schools. *Supervisor: The incumbent reports to the Deputy, Chief Field Education Programme through the Head of the Education Development Centre or to the Area Education Officer as assigned. * Supervisees: The incumbent will supervise a large number of Teachers (Technical Support) as assigned
Responsibilities
1. Supports schools and assists teachers directly through team/model, co-teaching (plan, teach, and evaluate a lesson with the teacher seeking assistance), and classroom observation. Provides, explains, and demonstrates instructional resources and materials, and monitors the implementation of up-to-date equitable inclusive quality teaching methods and techniques at all schools he/she supports. 2 Supports schools and teachers in continuing professional development and school-based teacher development programs, and advises on developing and implementing comprehensive, professional development plans that are aligned with teachers' competencies, applying a coherent model of support, adult learning strategies and appropriate models of technical support and research-based practices. 3 Assists and advises the School Principals in setting, implementing and evaluating their School Development Plan, and coordinates continuing professional development needs for all schools he/she supports to enhance school ethos and ensures that the needs of the schools are met. 4 Provides support in curriculum analysis and enrichment to meet the new curricular challenges and innovations and the different aspects of inclusive education and advises on identifying appropriate teaching and learning tools, materials and resources to ensure that the needs of all students, teachers and schools are met. 5 Works as a team member and assists on quality assurance implementation to enhance inclusive educational services against set standards and performance indicators for improving quality of schools. 6 Supports teachers and schools in assessing and analyzing students' achievement by identifying different strategies for all learners in order to improve the quality of teaching and learning. 7 Participates in preparing for interviewing and selection of candidate for teaching posts to ensure criteria applied, and the most qualified and capable teachers are hired; assists School Principals in the performance management of teachers in relation to technical aspects. 8 Performs other duties as may be assigned by the supervisor.
Competencies
UN Core Values of Integrity, Professionalism and Respect for Diversity, and Core Competencies of Communication, Working with People and Drive for Results apply by default. Functional: i. Applying Technical Expertise ii. Analyzing iii. Formulating Strategies and Concepts iv. Planning and Organizing v. Creating and Innovating For guidance on how to prepare for competency-based interviews: https://hr.un.org/page/prepare-competency-based-interview

Desirable Qualification: - Advanced degree in a related subject - Related training in the subject of Human Rights
Job - Specific Qualification
Not available.
Work Experience
Indicate your current involvement in any outside activities, as it is required. Including but not limited to employment, independent contractor/freelance consultant, board member (corporate, academic, etc), expert group, lobby, public speaking/writing (article, book, blog, social media etc), teaching, conferences, training, press statement, voluntary work, political activity, fundraising/donation for non-UNRWA entity, running for public office, role in political party or orgs, owning business, work for gov./NGO/private company/charity, UNRWA partner/vendor, full/part-time, paid or not. At least eight years of satisfactory teaching experience in any of subject taught in UNRWA schools is required Possession of a valid driving license is desirable
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. vacancies.jobTitle: Statistical Analysis and Knowledge Product Development Consultant
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
The Consultant will deliver four outputs that strengthen data management, provide statistical analyses and visualizations, and support the preparation and review of project reports and policy recommendations. The outputs will also support technical consultations and stakeholder meetings, while ensuring data coherence, analytical consistency and alignment with UN statistical and publishing standards.
Work Location
UN House - ESCWA
Expected duration
4 Months
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Background and Objective The Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA) supports economic and social development in its 22 Arab member States. Cluster 6 on Governance and Conflict Prevention serves as a regional platform for policy dialogue, knowledge exchange, and consensus-building to strengthen governance institutions and promote inclusive, transparent, and accountable public administration systems across the Arab region. In this context, and in line with its efforts to promote evidence-based policymaking and balanced development, ESCWA is supporting the Sultanate of Oman in the development and implementation of the Governorate Competitiveness Index (GCI). This initiative aims to assess and enhance competitiveness across Oman’s governorates, contributing to the achievement of Oman Vision 2040 and the country’s decentralization and sustainable development objectives. The GCI provides a comprehensive framework for evaluating performance across economic, social, governance, and environmental dimensions. It serves as a diagnostic and policy tool to identify strengths and challenges, guide resource allocation, and promote equitable growth across regions. By fostering data-driven decision-making, the Index will support local authorities in developing tailored strategies that leverage the unique potential of each governorate. Building on the development of the GCI, ESCWA will produce analytical reports, policy briefs, and capacity-building activities to strengthen the ability of national and local stakeholders to utilize the index effectively. These efforts aim to promote transparency and accountability as well as support Oman’s transition toward a more decentralized, competitive, and sustainable governance model. The consultant will provide specialized technical expertise in statistical analysis, data modeling, and policy research to strengthen ESCWA’s regional data frameworks and evidence-based decision-making. primarily to support the implementation and updating of the Oman Governorate Competitiveness Index (OGCI), alongside other related ESCWA analytical assignments. The consultancy aims to lead the development of robust analytical products, validated datasets, and technical reports that support the OGCI and broader evidence-based decision-making objectives. 2. Duties and Responsibilities Under the overall supervision of the Project Coordinator: The Consultant will support the implementation and updating of the Oman Governorate Competitiveness Index (OGCI) and related ESCWA analytical assignments. The Consultant will validate, clean, harmonize and organize data; maintain indicator databases; and conduct statistical analysis and modelling to identify trends, comparative findings and policy implications. The Consultant will prepare dashboards and other visualizations, draft technical reports and policy briefs, and develop evidence-based policy recommendations. The Consultant will also provide technical inputs to expert meetings, consultations and workshops, prepare related materials and outcome summaries, and ensure data coherence and analytical quality in accordance with ESCWA statistical and publishing standards.
Qualifications/special skills
A Master’s degree or equivalent in Economics, Statistics, Data Science, Development Studies, or a related is required. All candidates must submit a copy of the required educational degree. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. A minimum of one year of professional work experience in Economics, Statistics, Data Science, Development Studies, or a related field is required. Advanced proficiency in statistical software (STATA, R, Python, or advanced SPSS/Excel) and data visualization tools (Power BI, Tableau, or similar) is required. Exposure to indices or governance monitoring tools is desirable. Familiarity with data analysis, statistics, or governance-related research is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat; and Arabic is a working language of ESCWA. For this position fluency in English and Arabic is required. Knowledge of French is desirable. Note: “Fluency” equals a rating of ‘fluent’ in all four areas (speak, read, write, and understand) and “Knowledge of” equals a rating of ‘confident’ in two of the four areas.

vacancies.jobTitle: National Consultant for Advancing Early Warnings for All and Resilience in Mongolia
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
The consultant effectively supports the development and implementation of the EW4All Roadmap, strengthens coordination among relevant stakeholders, and provides effective support to the UN Resident Coordinator’s Office in Mongolia in advancing its resilience agenda and integrating disaster risk reduction into UN programming.
Work Location
Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
Expected duration
5 Nov 26-4 May 27
Duties and Responsibilities
Background Created in December 1999, the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) is the designated focal point in the United Nations system for the coordination of efforts to reduce disasters and to ensure synergies among the disaster reduction activities of the United Nations and regional organizations and activities in both developed and less developed countries. Led by the United Nations Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Disaster Risk Reduction (SRSG/ASG), UNDRR has over 160 staff located in its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, and in regional offices. UNDRR guides, monitors, analyses, and reports on progress in the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030. It supports regional and national implementation of the Framework and catalyzes action and increases global awareness to reduce disaster risk working with UN Member States and a broad range of partners and stakeholders, including civil society, the private sector, parliamentarians and the science and technology community. Mongolia faces increasing risks from climate-induced disasters such as dzuds, droughts, floods and dust storms, as well as geophysical hazards including earthquakes. In response, the Government of Mongolia has prioritized strengthening disaster risk reduction, including multi-hazard early warning systems, and resilience building through national policies and international cooperation. The United Nations Resident Coordinator's Office (RCO), together with resident and non-resident UN entities, supports these efforts through resilience building, climate change adaptation, anticipatory action and risk-informed development initiatives as part of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) for Mongolia 2023-2027. RCO also serves as the secretariat for the Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) where the government and non-government partners gather to take a coordinated actions for disaster risk prevention, preparedness, anticipatory action in the context of dzud and other natural hazards that could potentially translate into disasters. UNRCO is currently preparing for the development of the next phase of UNSDCF (2028-2032) and undertaking the stock-taking the existing progress, risk landscape, existing challenges and capacity gaps to prioritize the actions under the next UNSDCF. Early Warning Systems are critical for disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation. To accelerate progress towards universal coverage of early warning systems by 2027, the United Nations Secretary-General launched the Early Warnings for All (EW4All) initiative (https://earlywarningsforall.org/site/early-warnings-all). Aligned with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030 and the Paris Agreement, EW4All promotes risk-informed, people-centred and actionable multi-hazard early warning systems across four pillars: (i) disaster risk knowledge; (ii) detection, observation, monitoring, analysis and forecasting of hazards and possible consequences; (iii) warning dissemination and communication; and (iv) preparedness and response capabilities. UN Resident Coordinators (RCs) play a key role in coordinating support from UN entities and partners, while the UNDRR, World Meteorological Organization (WMO), International Telecommunication Union (ITU), and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) serve as the global leads for each of these Pillars. The Government of Mongolia, through the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), has recently expressed interest in advancing EW4All Initiative. Several assessments, including the diagnosis conducted under Capacity for Disaster Reduction Initiative (CADRI) and EW4All-related assessments, have identified priority gaps and investment needs in Mongolia's multi-hazard early warning system, particularly in coordination, forecasting capacities, risk information and early warning applications. The Rapid Assessment of Pillar 2 capacities by WMO revealed key areas requiring improvement, such as coordination inefficiencies, technological infrastructure gaps, and capacity limitations at various administrative levels. The workshop on ‘Strengthening the Capacity for Multi-Hazard Risk Assessment and Early Warning in North-East Asia’, which was held in November 2024 in Beijing China and, brought together Mongolian representatives from all Pillars as well as from the global Pillar leads, provided crucial insights on Mongolia’s end-to-end early warning system, particularly on the status of and needs for impact-based forecasting, GIS-based impact modelling, and sector-specific early warning applications in agriculture, energy, and health. The most recent and more in-depth assessment of the national hydrometeorological and agrometeorological services capacities by WMO and revealed that (1) the strongest foundations are the existing institutional mandates, nationally functional observation networks, and routine forecasting and data operations; but that (2) the weakest areas are hydrological forecasting, interoperability across systems, impact-based service delivery, and institutionalized readiness for AI-enabled applications. These findings provide a strong basis for strengthening end-to-end early warning systems and resilience planning. In parallel, Mongolia has also advanced a nationally led Anticipatory Action agenda through the development of an Anticipatory Action (AA) Strategic Framework. The framework provides a common vision for scaling anticipatory action across priority hazards and sectors by strengthening the institutional, operational and financing arrangements required for early action. It also promotes stronger linkages between risk information, forecasting, early warning systems, preparedness, and early action protocols. As implementation of the AA Strategic Framework and the EW4All initiative are mutually reinforcing, there is a growing opportunity to align investments and coordination efforts across early warning systems, anticipatory action and broader resilience-building priorities, consistent with Mongolia's National DRR Strategy and its 2026-2030 National Action Plan. In this context, UNDRR seeks to engage a consultant to support the development of an EW4All roadmap for Mongolia, operationalization of anticipatory action priorities, and broader resilience coordination efforts led by the Mongolia UNRCO. The consultancy will help ensure coherent engagement of resident and non-resident UN entities, strengthen alignment across resilience-related initiatives, which is represented through EW4All and AA Strategic Framework and will be an integral part of the new UNSDCF 2028-2032. Under the supervision of the Programme Management Officer at the UNDRR Regional Office for Asia-Pacific (ROAP), the consultant will be based in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia and work closely with the Government of Mongolia, the RCO, regional EW4All Pillar Leads, resident (UNCT and HCT) and other non-resident UN entities and other key stakeholders to undertake the following tasks. Task A. EW4All Roadmap Development and Coordination (70%) The consultant will support the Government of Mongolia, regional EW4All Pillar Leads, other UN agencies (both resident and non-resident), and relevant stakeholders in the following areas: 1. Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement: Support the national roll-out of the EW4All initiative and respective coordination among government entities, regional EW4All Pillar Leads, and other UN agencies and partners, while engaging wider stakeholders into the consultations. 2. Assessment and Validation: Map key stakeholders, policies, and projects/initiatives and review existing assessments related to Mongolia's multi-hazard early warning system. Support validation of priority gaps, capacity needs, investment requirements and help identify financial and technological opportunities and partners across the four EW4All pillars and cross-cutting areas. 3. EW4All Roadmap Development: Support the development of a both strategic and action-oriented and costed EW4All Roadmap in Mongolian and English, including priority actions, implementation arrangements, roles and responsibilities, and financing opportunities, while ensuring alignment with national disaster risk reductio, climate change adaptation and resilience priorities such as Anticipatory Action Strategic Framework and related policies. Support the design and facilitation of respective consultations and workshops, also to promote coherence between the EW4All Roadmap and the Anticipatory Action Strategic Framework validation process. Task B. RCO Resilience Coordination and UN Programming Support (30%) 1. Support the RC and RCO in coordinating the HCT and related humanitarian and disaster risk reduction work. Provide coordination support to UNCT and HCT members, in close coordination with the NEMA, including follow-up on agreed actions and priorities. 2. Lead the coordination and regular updating of the 5W dashboard (Who does What, Where, When and for Whom), working with HCT members to strengthen information sharing, preparedness and coordination. 3. Support coordination among resident and non-resident UN entities on disaster risk reduction, preparedness, anticipatory action, climate resilience and risk-informed development, particularly priorities discussed through the HCT mechanism in coordination with NEMA. 4. Provide technical and coordination support to the RCO for integrating disaster risk management, resilience and risk-informed development considerations into the preparation of the new UNSDCF 2028–2032, including relevant analysis, consultations and formulation of priorities.
Qualifications/special skills
Advanced higher degree (Master’s or equivalent) inenvironmental science, international development, or areas related to disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation. A first-level university degree in combination with a minimum of two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. A minimum of 10 years of professional work experience in environmental, climate, or sustainable development policy, economics, or management with a specialization in disaster risk reduction or climate change adaptation is required. Experience working with national and sub-national level, including development partners and multistakeholder in policy and strategy development and institutional strengthening for disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation in Mongolia is required. Experience working with the United Nations system to support the process of UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Frameworks is required.
Languages
Fluency in English and Mongolian is required.
Additional Information
Due to the high volume of applications received, only successful candidates will be contacted.
No Fee
THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS.

Result of Service
The ultimate purpose of this consultancy is to strengthen UNDRR’s institutional capacity and leadership accountability for advancing gender equality and the empowerment of women, in alignment with the Sendai GAP, the United Nations Secretary-General’s GEAP, and the UN-SWAP. Through a tailored GRL Training for the 17 members of UNDRR’s senior management, the consultancy will equip senior leaders with the knowledge, skills and practical tools to systematically integrate gender equality considerations into strategic leadership, decision-making, people management and organizational accountability.
Work Location
Home base
Expected duration
16 Nov 26-15 Nov 27
Duties and Responsibilities
Background Created in December 1999, the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) is the designated focal point in the United Nations system for the coordination of efforts to reduce disasters and to ensure synergies among the disaster reduction activities of the United Nations and regional organizations and activities in both developed and less developed countries. Led by the United Nations Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Disaster Risk Reduction (SRSG), UNDRR has over 160 staff located in its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, and in regional offices. Specifically, UNDRR guides, monitors, analyses, and reports on progress in the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030, supports regional and national implementation of the Framework and catalyses action and increases global awareness to reduce disaster risk working with UN Member States and a broad range of partners and stakeholders, including civil society, the private sector, parliamentarians and the science and technology community. Disaster risk reduction (DRR) straddles both development and humanitarian action. In line with the guiding principles of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, UNDRR has been strengthening its institutional work on gender-responsive and inclusive disaster risk reduction and advancing women’s leadership, including through the flagship Women’s International Network for Disaster Risk Reduction (WIN DRR) and the dissemination and implementation of the Sendai Gender Action Plan (GAP) across regions. In alignment with the GAP, the United Nations Secretary-General’s Gender Equality Acceleration Plan (GEAP), and the United Nations System-wide Action Plan on Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN-SWAP), UNDRR seeks to reinforce leadership accountability and advance the systematic integration of gender equality and women’s empowerment across its organizational practices and disaster risk reduction work. The purpose of this consultancy is to design and facilitate a tailored Gender-Responsive Leadership (GRL) Training for the UNDRR Senior Management. The training aims to strengthen senior leaders’ capacities to integrate gender equality and the empowerment of women into strategic leadership, decision-making, people management and organizational accountability. Specifically, the consultancy will support the application of gender-responsive leadership principles and practices through practical application, peer learning and a follow-up session. Through this process, the consultancy will contribute to strengthening leadership accountability and fostering a more gender-responsive organizational culture within UNDRR. Duties and Responsibilities The consultant will be homebased and will work under the overall guidance of UNDRR ROAP Global Gender Advisor and Associate Expert. UNDRR will provide existing reference materials, facilitate access to designated reviewers, and provide consolidated feedback. The consultant will be responsible for designing and facilitating the training and ensuring consistency across all components as listed in this ToR. The consultant will undertake the following work: Inception and document review • Review relevant UNDRR policies, strategies, assessments and institutional documents, as well as relevant UN frameworks, guidance and resources on gender equality, women’s empowerment and gender-responsive leadership. • Review relevant UN-SWAP requirements and the UN Secretary-General’s GEAP to ensure alignment with institutional priorities and reporting commitments. • Identify key leadership competencies, emerging issues and good practices to inform the training content and approach. Learning Needs Assessment • Conduct a Learning Needs Assessment (LNA) to identify senior managers’ existing knowledge, competencies, experiences and learning priorities in gender-responsive leadership. • Conduct 15-minute one-on-one introductory calls with each participant to identify common and individual learning needs, leadership challenges and opportunities for applying gender-responsive leadership within UNDRR. • Use the findings to inform the training design, learning objectives, session content and approaches to measuring progress. Design and facilitate Gender-Responsive Leadership Training and workbook • Design and facilitate ten (10) one-hour online learning sessions monthly over the 10 months period, tailored to UNDRR’s institutional context and informed by the LNA. • Ensure each session has clear learning objectives, relevant content, interactive exercises and practical application opportunities that enable participants to apply gender-responsive leadership knowledge and skills, develop strategic GRL action plans, and implement and measure results. • Review and adapt session content, as appropriate, to reflect evolving gender equality issues, changes in the socio-political context and participants’ progress throughout the training. • Respond to participants’ questions and requests for clarification, additional resources or guidance to support their engagement and practical application of learning. • Develop a practical participant workbook to accompany the learning sessions and support continued reflection and application between sessions. • Incorporate mechanisms for documenting leadership commitments, tracking implementation progress, measuring results and reflecting on lessons learned throughout the training programme. A follow-up peer review session after 6 months • Conduct a follow up peer review session after 6 months to bring all participants together to review the progress in implementing their individual gender-responsive leadership action plans, assess achievements against agreed objectives and indicators, exchange experiences and lessons learned, identify challenges and opportunities, and strengthen mutual learning and accountability for sustained application of gender-responsive leadership practices within UNDRR.
Qualifications/special skills
• An advanced degree in a social science discipline associated with gender studies such as social anthropology, economics, social sciences, management, international studies, or other relevant fields is required. • A minimum of 10 years of training and advisory experience in gender equality and women’s empowerment in international organizations is required; • Experience in capacity building, development of training programmes and training facilitation in gender equality is required; • Strong experience and track record in development and facilitation of workshop as well as training on gender mainstreaming for staff project personnel and gender focal points within the UN system and/or similar international organizations is desirable; • Experience with frameworks to support the integration of gender equality issues, including gender transformative approaches is desirable.
Languages
Fluency in English is required.

Due to the high volume of applications received, only successful candidates will be contacted.

Result of Service
1.      Provide strategic leadership, technical oversight, and supervisory direction for the planning, implementation, and management of facilities, infrastructure, maintenance, rehabilitation, and construction programmes across multiple locations. 2.      Ensure effective management and coordination of multidisciplinary teams, international and national personnel, contractors, and service providers to achieve organizational objectives. 3.      Oversee the development and implementation of strategic work plans, technical standards, performance indicators, and resource allocation strategies in alignment with organizational priorities. 4.      Ensure effective governance and control of project scope, budgets, schedules, quality, risks, and contractual obligations, promoting accountability and value for money. 5.      Provide high-level technical advice and recommendations to senior management on infrastructure development, asset management, operational challenges, risk mitigation, and resource optimization. 6.      Strengthen performance management, workforce development, capacity building, and knowledge transfer to enhance institutional effectiveness and operational sustainability. 7.      Lead stakeholder engagement and interdepartmental coordination to facilitate decision-making, resolve complex technical and operational issues, and ensure timely delivery of organizational commitments. 8.      Ensure the timely completion, commissioning, handover, and closeout of projects, supported by comprehensive technical documentation, financial accountability, and appropriate asset management records.
Work Location
Abyei
Expected duration
6 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA), through the Facility Management Unit (FMU), manages the planning, development, construction, operation, maintenance, rehabilitation, optimization, and decommissioning of mission facilities and infrastructure across all camps and locations. These include accommodations, offices, power, water and sanitation systems, waste management, workshops, warehouses, drainage networks, and other mission-support facilities. The Project Manager serves as the FMU focal point for project management and compound maintenance operations, responsible for planning, managing, designing, coordinating, overseeing, and monitoring infrastructure projects and facility operations. The role ensures facilities are safe, functional, sustainable, and cost-effective while providing technical and managerial oversight throughout the project lifecycle, from planning and design through construction, commissioning, close-out, operation, maintenance, rehabilitation. Under the supervision of the Chief, FMU, the incumbent provides technical, operational, and advisory support in developing and implementing infrastructure strategies, camp development plans, maintenance programs, and project priorities in compliance with UN regulations, engineering standards, and mission requirements. Responsibilities The incumbent will be based at UNISFA Abyei Headquarters and will travel frequently to field locations. Administration • Lead assigned projects throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring delivery of approved scope, schedule, budget, quality, and safety requirements. • Develop project plans, schedules, resource requirements, risk registers, and monitoring tools. • Manage and oversee the construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, operation, maintenance, and improvement of mission facilities and infrastructure. • Coordinate preventive, corrective, and emergency maintenance programs across mission camps. • Ensure compliance with UN engineering standards, environmental policies, and occupational health and safety requirements. • Coordinate and monitor the implementation of construction, alteration, repair and maintenance works, ensuring timely completion and effective utilization of available resources • Maintain accurate project, asset, contract, maintenance, and technical documentation. • Conduct technical inspections, condition assessments, and facility audits, recommending corrective actions where required. • Prepare and review Statements of Work (SoWs), Bills of Quantities (BoQs), technical specifications, cost estimates, and procurement documents. • Review contractor submissions, drawings, and technical documentation for compliance with approved specifications, contractual requirements, and applicable technical standards. • Utilize project management and other relevant tools for project tracking, procurement, asset management, and financial monitoring. • Advise management on project risks, resource requirements, operational constraints, and corrective actions. • Coordinate infrastructure priorities, workplans, budgets, and procurement plans with relevant mission stakeholders. Planning • Develop and implement construction infrastructure development, rehabilitation, maintenance and project management plans in support of camp operation. • Lead infrastructure projects from initiation through design, procurement, implementation, commissioning, handover, and closure. • Develop project plans, schedules, resource requirements, risk management strategies, and monitoring tools. Coordinate with engineering, logistics, procurement, finance, ICT, security, medical units, and other stakeholders to ensure integrated project delivery. • Conduct feasibility studies, technical assessments, site surveys, and infrastructure evaluations. • Assess changing operational requirements and recommend infrastructure improvements. • Prepare and review project scopes, designs, technical specifications, BoQs, and cost estimates for technical and operational suitability. • Identify project risks and implement mitigation measures. • Support annual and multi-year infrastructure investment and maintenance planning. • Develop contingency plans to ensure continuity of critical services and infrastructure. Operations • Manage contractor performance, ensuring compliance with contractual, safety, quality, and technical requirements. • Monitor project progress, costs, schedules, and resource utilization, recommending corrective actions where required. • Supervise multidisciplinary technical teams, contractors, consultants, and service providers. • Conduct site inspections, progress reviews, testing, commissioning, handovers, and acceptance activities. • Identify defects and non-conformities, coordinate corrective measures, and verify satisfactory completion of remedial works • Review completed works and verify quality, quantities, and compliance prior to acceptance or payment. • Coordinate infrastructure modifications, relocations, rehabilitation, and repurposing activities. • Coordinate construction and maintenance activities to minimize disruption to ongoing mission operations and ensure safe execution of works • Promote resource efficiency and sustainability initiatives in construction, maintenance, and facility operations. Ensure compliance of construction and maintenance operations with applicable environmental standards, regulations, and waste management requirements.. • Respond to technical emergencies and coordinate remedial actions. • Implement corrective action plans and continuous improvement initiatives. • Participate in technical evaluations, inspections, project reviews, and asset management activities. • Ensure completed projects are incorporated into mission asset inventories and maintenance programs. Reporting and Compliance • Prepare periodic reports on project implementation, camp operations, maintenance activities, risks, and contractor performance. • Maintain project monitoring and reporting systems, including progress tracking, risk management, corrective actions, and performance monitoring.Monitor KPIs related to infrastructure operations, maintenance, service delivery, and project performance. • Support audits, inspections, management reviews, and UN Headquarters reporting requirements. • Ensure project and operational records are complete, accurate, traceable, and audit ready. • Prepare technical briefings, management reports, presentations, and decision papers. • Monitor compliance with UN policies, engineering standards, environmental requirements, safety procedures, and contractual obligations. • Analyze recurring infrastructure and operational issues and recommend sustainable solutions. • Support mission planning, budget preparation, infrastructure strategies, and operational decision-making.
Qualifications/special skills
A minimum of Seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in construction project management, facilities management, construction supervision, or infrastructure support operations in field or complex environments is required. A minimum of seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in planning, design coordination, implementation, and supervision of construction and infrastructure projects is required. Experience in project scheduling, cost control and risk management is required. Experience in coordinating multi-disciplinary technical teams and contractors s is required.. Ability to prepare and evaluate technical reports and documentation is desirable Proficiency in computer-aided design (CAD), project scheduling and management software (e.g., AutoCAD, MS Project, Primavera P6), and standard office applications is desirable Knowledge of construction methodologies, materials, quality assurance and quality control, and applicable engineering standards is desirable. Driving License for cars is required.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For the post advertised, fluency in English is required.
Additional Information
Not available.

Result of Service
1.      Provide strategic technical leadership and supervisory oversight in structural engineering, infrastructure development, and the planning, design, execution, and management of complex construction projects. 2.      Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary engineering teams, consultants, contractors, and stakeholders to ensure the effective delivery of construction and infrastructure projects in accordance with approved objectives. 3.      Oversee structural analysis, design review, technical assessments, and verification of engineering solutions to ensure structural integrity, safety, durability, and compliance with applicable international standards and specifications. 4.      Direct project planning, scheduling, budgeting, resource allocation, risk management, and performance monitoring to ensure timely, cost-effective, and quality delivery of projects. 5.      Provide expert technical advice to senior management on structural engineering, construction methodologies, infrastructure development, design optimization, and project implementation strategies. 6.      Ensure effective contract administration, technical evaluation of bids, review of BOQs and cost estimates, variation assessment, and monitoring of contractor performance in accordance with contractual requirements and organizational procedures. 7.      Establish and implement quality assurance, quality control, occupational safety, environmental compliance, and engineering risk management systems throughout the project life cycle. 8.      Oversee site supervision, construction progress monitoring, technical inspections, testing, commissioning, and project handover to ensure compliance with approved designs, specifications, budgets, and schedules. 9.      Lead the identification, assessment, and resolution of complex structural, geotechnical, construction, and project management challenges, ensuring appropriate corrective and preventive actions. 10. Develop and implement project performance indicators, reporting systems, and risk mitigation strategies to support evidence-based decision-making, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Work Location
Abyei
Expected duration
6 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA), through the Facility Management Unit (FMU), is responsible for the planning, design, construction, operation, maintenance, rehabilitation, and management of engineering infrastructure in support of mission operations. This includes roads, airfields, drainage systems, utility networks, accommodation facilities, retaining structures, water supply systems, environmental infrastructure, and other mission-critical assets. The Structural Engineer serves as the FMU technical focal point for structural engineering, structural design & integrity, and associated geotechnical and civil engineering activities. The incumbent is responsible for planning, designing, assessing, coordinating, supervising, and monitoring civil, structural engineering works and related infrastructure development activities to ensure that mission infrastructure is safe, resilient, sustainable, cost-effective, and compliant with applicable engineering standards and international best practices. Under the supervision of the Chief, FMU, the officer provides technical expertise and advisory support on structural engineering, geotechnical investigations, infrastructure planning, construction quality assurance, risk management, and asset sustainability. The incumbent will contribute to infrastructure development strategies, camp master plans, maintenance programs, rehabilitation initiatives, and engineering assessments across all UNISFA locations. Responsibilities The Structural Engineer will be based at UNISFA Abyei Headquarters and will travel frequently to field locations. The Structural Engineer will be responsible for the following duties: Administration Coordinate geotechnical investigations, site assessments, soil testing programs, and conduct foundation evaluations for new construction and rehabilitation projects. Review geological, hydrological, and geotechnical data to determine site suitability and engineering requirements. Review and evaluate geotechnical data, including soil characteristics, bearing capacity, settlement behavior, groundwater conditions, and slope stability to support infrastructure design. Provide technical recommendations on foundation systems, earthworks, retaining structures, pavement design, and ground improvement requirements. Perform structural design of buildings, structures, and their components. Review and technically verify structural designs, calculations, drawings, and reports prepared by consultants and contractors including relevant geotechnical design inputs. Ensure compliance with applicable engineering design codes and standards, international building codes, safety requirements, and environmental regulations. Maintain comprehensive records of geotechnical investigations, laboratory test results, structural assessments, construction inspections, and engineering documentation. Prepare technical specifications, Statements of Work (SoWs), Bills of Quantities (BoQs), cost estimates, and procurement documents for civil, structural, and geotechnical projects. Coordinate with engineers, environmental specialists, procurement officers, and contractors throughout project implementation. Provide technical advice to management on engineering risks, infrastructure condition, project feasibility, and resource requirements. Planning and Design Lead structural assessments and coordinate associated geotechnical investigations for roads, bridges, culverts, drainage systems, retaining walls, helipads, accommodation and office facilities, warehouses, workshops, utility structures, and other mission infrastructure. Develop and review structural designs, site development plans, foundation designs, structural systems, and associated civil engineering works. Conduct feasibility studies, engineering evaluations, and technical investigations for new infrastructure and rehabilitation projects. Assess infrastructure requirements resulting from camp expansion, relocation, reconstruction, emergency deployment, or mission transition. Identify and evaluate structural and geotechnical hazards, including erosion, flooding, expansive soils, settlement, scour, slope instability, and other site-related risks. Develop mitigation measures and engineering solutions to minimize infrastructure vulnerability and operational disruptions. Support long-term infrastructure planning and asset management strategies based on engineering assessments and operational needs. Review design submissions to ensure structural adequacy, operational functionality, constructability, sustainability, and cost-effectiveness. Participate in the preparation of camp master plans, infrastructure development programs, and engineering investment priorities. Coordinate site investigations, topographic surveys, geophysical studies, hydrological assessments, and material testing programs. Operation Supervise and monitor construction, rehabilitation, and maintenance activities to ensure compliance with approved designs, specifications, quality standards, and safety requirements. Conduct regular inspections of buildings, foundations, roads, bridges, culverts, drainage systems, retaining structures, water infrastructure, and other engineering assets. Assess the structural integrity and serviceability of existing facilities and recommend repair, strengthening, rehabilitation, or replacement measures. Monitor contractor performance, work quality, construction methods, testing activities, and compliance with contractual obligations. Review material submittals, laboratory test results, work procedures, and construction methodologies. Identify structural defects and non-conformities, recommend corrective measures, and verify satisfactory completion of remedial works. Verify quantities, quality standards, and completed works prior to recommending acceptance, certification, or payment. Establish and monitor implemention of quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) procedures for infrastructure projects. Maintain a central database of geotechnical information, material test results, structural inspection reports, and infrastructure condition assessments. Monitor infrastructure performance and recommend preventive maintenance, remediation, and asset preservation measures. Investigate structural failures, pavement distress, foundation problems, drainage deficiencies, and other engineering issues, coordinate specialist investigations where required, and recommend corrective actions. Respond to engineering emergencies affecting mission infrastructure and coordinate immediate technical interventions. Provide technical mentoring and capacity-building support to engineers, technicians, and national staff. Support the preparation of engineering budgets, procurement plans, material requirements, and project implementation schedules. Coordinate with military engineering units, UN agencies, local authorities, contractors, and other stakeholders on infrastructure-related activities. Reporting and Compliance Prepare periodic and ad hoc technical reports on project progress, infrastructure condition, structural assessments, geotechnical findings, risks, and recommendations. Maintain engineering records, inspection reports, risk management documentation, technical drawings, test certificates, and project documentation. Monitor compliance with approved project scope, engineering standards, environmental requirements, health and safety procedures, and contractual obligations. Prepare technical evaluations, management briefings, project summaries, and decision-support papers for senior management. Support internal and external audits, inspections, technical reviews, and engineering compliance assessments. Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) related to infrastructure reliability, structural safety, maintenance effectiveness, and project performance. Identify recurring engineering issues and develop sustainable corrective and preventive measures. Participate in technical evaluation panels, inspection committees, boards of survey, contractor evaluations, and engineering review meetings. Provide inputs for mission planning, budget preparation, infrastructure strategies, disaster risk reduction measures, and long-term asset management programs. Ensure all completed infrastructure assets are properly documented, commissioned, handed over, and incorporated into mission asset registers and maintenance programs.
Qualifications/special skills
Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Structural Engineering, or a related field is required. A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) in the above fields, in combination with three (3) additional years of relevant professional experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. A minimum of Seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in structural engineering including design technical assessments, and construction supervision, is required. Experience in applying internationally recognized structural design codes and engineering standards (e.g., Eurocodes, British Standards, ACI, AISC, ASTM), including applicable geotechnical and construction material testing standards, is required. Experience in the design and implementation of infrastructure projects in complex or remote operational environments is desirable. Experience in using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for infrastructure planning and site assessment is desirable. Professional certification in Practicing Professional Structural Engineer, professional registration as a Chartered Engineer or Chartered Structural Engineer is desirable. Additional certifications in structural/geotechnical analysis software (e.g., SAP, ETABS, STAAD. Pro, Autodesk Robot Structural Analysis, AutoCAD Civil 3D) is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For the post advertised, fluency in English is required.
Additional Information
Not available.

UNRWA is a United Nations agency established by the General Assembly in 1949 and is mandated to provide assistance and protection to a population of some 5.8 million registered Palestine refugees. Its mission is to help Palestine refugees in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, West Bank and the Gaza Strip to achieve their full potential in human development, pending a just solution to their plight. UNRWA's services encompass education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure and improvement, microfinance, and emergency assistance. UNRWA is the largest UN operation in the Middle East with more than 30,000 staff. UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions. If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to make a tangible difference for one of the most vulnerable communities in the world, UNRWA would like to hear from you.- The incumbent is responsible for the provision of technical support towards equitable inclusive quality education to all staff assigned to him/her in the area and will monitor and support their professional development in cooperation with the School Principal to enhance inclusive teaching and learning and promote safe and effective learning environment in schools. *Supervisor: The incumbent reports to the Deputy, Chief Field Education Programme through the Head of the Education Development Centre or to the Area Education Officer as assigned. * Supervisees: The incumbent will supervise a large number of Teachers (Technical Support) as assigned

Org. Setting and Reporting
UNRWA is a United Nations agency established by the General Assembly in 1949 and is mandated to provide assistance and protection to a population of some 5.8 million registered Palestine refugees. Its mission is to help Palestine refugees in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, West Bank and the Gaza Strip to achieve their full potential in human development, pending a just solution to their plight. UNRWA's services encompass education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure and improvement, microfinance, and emergency assistance. UNRWA is the largest UN operation in the Middle East with more than 30,000 staff. UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions. If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to make a tangible difference for one of the most vulnerable communities in the world, UNRWA would like to hear from you.- The incumbent is responsible for the provision of technical support towards equitable inclusive quality education to all staff assigned to him/her in the area and will monitor and support their professional development in cooperation with the School Principal to enhance inclusive teaching and learning and promote safe and effective learning environment in schools. *Supervisor: The incumbent reports to the Deputy, Chief Field Education Programme through the Head of the Education Development Centre or to the Area Education Officer as assigned. * Supervisees: The incumbent will supervise a large number of Teachers (Technical Support) as assigned.
Responsibilities
1. Supports schools and assists teachers directly through team/model, co-teaching (plan, teach, and evaluate a lesson with the teacher seeking assistance), and classroom observation. Provides, explains, and demonstrates instructional resources and materials, and monitors the implementation of up-to-date equitable inclusive quality teaching methods and techniques at all schools he/she supports. 2 Supports schools and teachers in continuing professional development and school-based teacher development programs, and advises on developing and implementing comprehensive, professional development plans that are aligned with teachers' competencies, applying a coherent model of support, adult learning strategies and appropriate models of technical support and research-based practices. 3 Assists and advises the School Principals in setting, implementing and evaluating their School Development Plan, and coordinates continuing professional development needs for all schools he/she supports to enhance school ethos and ensures that the needs of the schools are met. 4 Provides support in curriculum analysis and enrichment to meet the new curricular challenges and innovations and the different aspects of inclusive education and advises on identifying appropriate teaching and learning tools, materials and resources to ensure that the needs of all students, teachers and schools are met. 5 Works as a team member and assists on quality assurance implementation to enhance inclusive educational services against set standards and performance indicators for improving quality of schools. 6 Supports teachers and schools in assessing and analyzing students' achievement by identifying different strategies for all learners in order to improve the quality of teaching and learning. 7 Participates in preparing for interviewing and selection of candidate for teaching posts to ensure criteria applied, and the most qualified and capable teachers are hired; assists School Principals in the performance management of teachers in relation to technical aspects. 8 Performs other duties as may be assigned by the supervisor.
Competencies
UN Core Values of Integrity, Professionalism and Respect for Diversity, and Core Competencies of Communication, Working with People and Drive for Results apply by default. Functional: i. Applying Technical Expertise ii. Analyzing iii. Formulating Strategies and Concepts iv. Planning and Organizing v. Creating and Innovating
Education
A University degree from an accredited educational institution in the subject to be supported and at least one year of professional teacher training; or A University degree from an accredited educational institution in the subject to be supported and an advanced degree in education. Desirable Qualification: Advanced degree in a related subject.
Job - Specific Qualification
Not available.
Work Experience
Indicate your current involvement in any outside activities, as it is required. Including but not limited to employment, independent contractor/freelance consultant, board member (corporate, academic, etc), expert group, lobby, public speaking/writing (article, book, blog, social media etc), teaching, conferences, training, press statement, voluntary work, political activity, fundraising/donation for non-UNRWA entity, running for public office, role in political party or orgs, owning business, work for gov./NGO/private company/charity, UNRWA partner/vendor, full/part-time, paid or not. A “yes” answer doesn’t necessarily lead to exclusion from future work at UNRWA, yet misrepresentation in providing accurate/complete info can lead to disqualification/termination of appointment, if hired. -Please confirm if you live/ reside in West Bank or Jerusalem? And if you have West Bank or Jerusalem ID. please to mention its number down, as it is desirable. At least eight years of satisfactory teaching experience in the subject s/he will support is required Possession of a valid driving license is desirable

vacancies.postingTitle: Senior Legal Officer (Temporary Job Opening), P5
vacancies.jobDescription:
Org. Setting and Reporting
The Office of Staff Legal Assistance is headed by the Chief (Senior Legal Officer) who is accountable to the Executive Director of the Office of Administration of Justice, without prejudice to his or her responsibility to provide legal assistance to staff members in an independent and impartial manner. This post is located in the Office of Staff Legal Assistance (OSLA) in New York, Office of Administration of Justice (OAJ). Under the authority of the Executive Director, the Chief is responsible for the management and proper functioning of the programme of legal assistance to staff members in the internal justice system, including in administrative, disciplinary and appellate proceedings before the United Nations Dispute Tribunal and the United Nations Appeals Tribunal. The Senior Legal Officer (Chief) will report to the Executive Director of OAJ.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Senior Legal Officer (Chief) will be responsible for the following duties: • Ensures the effective and efficient discharge of OSLA's mandate; • Coordinates and supervises the work of legal officers and the other staff of the unit; • Provides strategic legal and policy advice and managerial support to legal officers to maximize resource utilization and efficiencies; • Advises clients on matters relating to appeals against administrative decisions and the imposition of disciplinary measures; • Provides legal advice on diverse and complex substantive and procedural questions with a view to resolving workplace disputes; • Represents clients and coordinates the representation of clients in the formal internal justice system including before the United Nations Dispute Tribunal and the United Nations Appeals Tribunal; • Prepares written and oral submissions to the Tribunals in accordance with procedural requirements; • Manages the human, financial and other resources allocated to the unit, as required; • Develops and maintains standard procedures and monitoring and reporting mechanisms as well as innovative ideas in problem prevention and dispute resolution; • Ensures the maintenance of the unit's registers (electronic and online) and database; • Prepares input for reports on the work of the unit to the General Assembly and other bodies, as may be mandated, and represents the unit in relevant bodies; • Analyses the implications of emerging issues in the unit and makes recommendations on possible strategies and measures; • Coordinates and participates in outreach and training activities by OSLA; • Establishes, manages and coordinates a reliable network of volunteer/pro bono counsel and legal interns and ensures their supervision and support; • Advises the Executive Director on administrative, human resources and logistical matters related to the unit's operational activities.
Competencies
Professionalism: Knowledge of administrative and employment law and judicial procedures, preferably including in the United Nations or other international public organization; Ability to apply legal expertise to analysing a diverse range of complex and unusual legal issues and problems and in developing innovative and creative solutions; Strong analytical skills and ability to conduct comprehensive legal research on a range of issues, including those of a unique and/or complex nature; proficiency in legal writing and expression and ability to prepare legal briefs, opinions or legal submissions/motions, and a variety of legal instruments and related documents. Ability to lead and cross-examine witnesses and make substantive legal arguments and oral submissions before the United Nations Appeals Tribunal and United Nations Dispute Tribunal. Discretion and sound judgment in applying legal expertise to sensitive, complex legal issues. Strong negotiating skills and ability to influence others to reach agreement. Ability to work to tight deadlines and handle multiple concurrent projects/cases. Knowledge of UN system, organization and interrelationships. Knowledge of staff rules and regulations, policies, procedures and operations of the United Nations, as well as the jurisprudence of the United Nations Appeals Tribunal and United Nations Dispute Tribunal. Strong managerial and interpersonal skills. Ability to use electronic search engines. Ability to oversee maintenance of OSLA database. Shows pride in work and in achievements. Demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter. Is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results. Is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns. Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Provides leadership and takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work; demonstrates knowledge of strategies and commitment to the goal of gender balance in staffing. Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. Client Orientation: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be "clients" and seeks to see things from clients' point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients' needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients' environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in cases; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client. Leadership: Serves as a role model that other people want to follow: empowers others to translate vision into results; is proactive in developing strategies to accomplish objectives; establishes and maintains relationships with a broad range of people to understand needs and gain support; anticipates and resolves conflicts by pursuing mutually agreeable solutions; drives for change and improvements; does not accept the status quo; shows the courage to take unpopular stands. Provides leadership and takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work; demonstrates knowledge of strategies and commitment to the goal of gender balance in staffing. Managing Performance: Establishes priorities and plans, coordinates and monitors work of others; delegates the appropriate responsibility, accountability and decision-making authority; makes sure that roles, responsibilities and reporting lines are clear to each staff member; accurately judges the amount of time and resources needed to accomplish a task and matches task to skills; monitors progress against milestones and deadlines; regularly discusses performance and provides feedback and coaching to staff; encourages risk-taking and supports creativity and initiative; actively supports the development and career aspirations of staff; appraises performance fairly.
Education
An advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent degree) in law is required. A first-level university degree (Bachelor's degree or equivalent degree) in law with two additional years of qualifying work experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.
Job - Specific Qualification
Not available.
Work Experience
• A minimum of ten years of progressively responsible experience in law, including legal analysis, research and writing is required. • A minimum of five years' experience as a litigator appearing before courts and tribunals in the areas of administrative law, labor or employment law is required • A minimum of three years' experience in managing teams or an office, including the management of lawyers, is required. • Experience in giving legal advice in the areas of civil procedure, administrative law or employment law is required. • A minimum of one year of experience in criminal law litigation is desirable. • Experience within the UN common system or other similar international organizations is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. French is desirable. Such retirees shall not be employed by the Organization, unless (a) the operational requirements of the Organization cannot be met by staff members who are qualified and available to perform the required functions; and (b) the proposed employment would not adversely affect the career development or redeployment opportunities of other staff members and represents both a cost-effective and operationally sound solution to meet the needs of the service. • At the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the recruitment and employment of staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, with due regard to geographic diversity. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. The United Nations is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. The United Nations recruits and employs staff regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, religious, cultural and ethnic backgrounds or disabilities. • The United Nations Secretariat is committed to achieving 50/50 gender balance and geographical diversity in its staff. Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for this position.
United Nations Considerations
According to article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. Candidates will not be considered for employment with the United Nations if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. The term “sexual exploitation” means any actual or attempted abuse of a position of vulnerability, differential power, or trust, for sexual purposes, including, but not limited to, profiting monetarily, socially or politically from the sexual exploitation of another. The term “sexual abuse” means the actual or threatened physical intrusion of a sexual nature, whether by force or under unequal or coercive conditions. The term “sexual harassment” means any unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature that might reasonably be expected or be perceived to cause offence or humiliation, when such conduct interferes with work, is made a condition of employment or creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, and when the gravity of the conduct warrants the termination of the perpetrator’s working relationship. Due regard will be paid to the importance of recruiting the staff on as wide a geographical basis as possible. The United Nations places no restrictions on the eligibility of men and women to participate in any capacity and under conditions of equality in its principal and subsidiary organs. The United Nations Secretariat is a non-smoking environment. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. By accepting a letter of appointment, staff members are subject to the authority of the Secretary-General, who may assign them to any of the activities or offices of the United Nations in accordance with staff regulation 1.2 (c). Further, staff members in the Professional and higher category up to and including the D-2 level and the Field Service category are normally required to move periodically to discharge functions in different duty stations under conditions established in ST/AI/2023/3 on Mobility, as may be amended or revised. This condition of service applies to all position specific job openings and does not apply to temporary positions. Applicants are urged to carefully follow all instructions available in the online recruitment platform, inspira, and to refer to the Applicant Guide by clicking on “Manuals” in the “Help” tile of the inspira account-holder homepage. The evaluation of applicants will be conducted on the basis of the information submitted in the application according to the evaluation criteria of the job opening and the applicable internal legislations of the United Nations including the Charter of the United Nations, resolutions of the General Assembly, the Staff Regulations and Rules, administrative issuances and guidelines. Result of Service
The International individual contractor will support the pollution-related work of the UNEP Law Division’s in particular related to chemicals. The international individual contractor, under the supervision of the Head of the Pollution Section or his/her designated representative, will carry out the activities as per the ToR.
Work Location
Nairobi-Based
Expected duration
12 Months
Duties and Responsibilities
Background: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system, and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. The UNEP Law Division is the lead division responsible for carrying out UNEP's functions in the field of environmental law, governance, and related policy issues, including matters relating to multilateral environmental agreements (MEAs). To fulfil its mandate, the Law Division works to promote the progressive development of environmental law, support States in developing and implementing legal, institutional, and policy frameworks to address environmental challenges, facilitate cooperation and coordination among MEAs, support Parties in implementing treaty obligations, and foster policy dialogue on international environmental law and governance. UNEP has been working to create enabling conditions that accelerate the transition towards circular and sustainable economies and contribute to the prevention and reduction of pollution. In this context, the development and implementation of effective legal, policy, and institutional frameworks are critical to achieving a just and sustainable transition. The Pollution Section of the Law Division works closely with UNEP's Industry and Economy Division to support legislative, regulatory, and institutional reforms in priority sectors, including chemicals and waste, plastics, textiles, and minerals. The Section also contributes to the implementation of relevant resolutions and decisions adopted by the United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA) and provides legal support on pollution-related matters. The Pollution Section seeks to engage an international individual contractor to support its legal and policy work on pollution-related issues, with a particular focus on chemicals and waste management. The international individual contractor will contribute to the Section's efforts to provide technical legal assistance and capacity-building support to developing countries and countries with economies in transition undertaking policy, regulatory, and institutional reforms. This work will support, inter alia, the implementation of the Global Framework on Chemicals – For a Planet Free of Harm from Chemicals and Waste (GFC), adopted by the Fifth International Conference on Chemicals Management in September 2023, and advance broader efforts to promote sustainable and sound chemicals and waste management throughout their lifecycle. Duties and Responsibilities: Under the guidance of the Head of the Pollution Section or his/her designated representative and in close consultation with the Industry and Economy Division, the individual contractor will undertake the following tasks, with a primary focus on the chemicals sector and, where required, support for other sectoral areas of the Section, including but not limited to extended producer responsibility (EPR) schemes, mineral governance, textiles, and plastics: (a) Support the work of the Pollution Section through legal research, analysis, and the preparation of recommendations and legal options to support effective and sustainable policy and regulatory outcomes. (b) Support the development of knowledge products and tools related to technical legal assistance and capacity-building activities. (c) Assist in providing legal and technical support for the development and strengthening of policies, laws, regulations, and related legal frameworks in targeted developing countries. (d) Assist in programme planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, and coordination activities, as required. (e) Support the preparation and formulation of project concepts and proposals, including legal and policy analyses and drafting inputs. (f) Assist the development and delivery of training programmes for policymakers and other stakeholders on international best practices, legislative approaches, and regulatory measures. (g) Undertake basic and in-depth reviews of legal documents, instruments, policies, legislation, and other materials related to environmental law, with a particular focus on pollution-related legal issues. (h) Prepare, or assist in the preparation of, presentations, background papers, briefing notes, reports, correspondence, and other written materials on environmental law matters, with a particular focus on pollution-related legal issues. (i) Collect, organize and analyse legal, policy and programme-related information, identify emerging trends and prepare analytical reports, presentations and data visualizations to support decision-making and reporting.
Qualifications/special skills
Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in environmental law, international law, human rights or a related field. A first-level university degree in law in combination with 2 additional qualifying years of experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. A minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in law, including legal analysis, research and writing is required. Prior experience working on international and/or national environmental law relating to pollution issues is required. Excellent research and analytical skills, in particular in legal analysis, and expertise in independent research and review is required. Excellent writing and communications skills is required. Prior experience working with the UN or similar international organizations is desirable. A minimum of two (2) years or more of experience in data analytics or related area is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For the position advertised, fluency in English (both oral and written) is required. Knowledge of French or another official UN language is an asset.
Additional Information
Not available.
No Fee
