vacancies.jobTitle: Sustainable Development Officer, Regional Liaison, Europe and Central Asia
vacancies.jobDescription:
Org. Setting and Reporting
The Development Coordination Office (DCO) is a stand-alone coordination office within the United Nations Secretariat. DCO exercises managerial and oversight functions of the Resident Coordinator System (RCS) under the oversight of the Chair of United Nations Sustainable Development Group (UNSDG). In 2026, DCO undertook a recalibration to ensure the RC system remains optimally configured to support the acceleration of the 2030 Agenda and embodies the UN 2.0 shift anchored in data, digital, innovation, behavioral science, strategic foresight, and a mission driven organizational culture. The position is part of the Regional Office for Europe and Central Asia and performs liaison functions based in New York, hosted in the Strategic Partnerships and Engagement Division. The position reports to both the respective Senior Programme Management Officer in the Regional Office and the Chief of the Inter-governmental Section in the Strategic Partnerships and Engagement Division. The Regional Director for Europe and Central Asia is the second reporting officer.
Responsibilities
Summary of Functions: 1. Substantive analysis, briefings and support to senior leadership: 2. Substantive support to intergovernmental processes and senior-management engagement. 3. Coordination and liaison support between Headquarters and the Regional Office 1. Substantive analysis, briefings and support to senior leadership: • Prepares drafts of briefing notes, key messages, mission packs, and meeting readouts for senior leadership, including for complex development, crisis and transition settings. • Collects, maintains, and analyzes quantitative and qualitative information on regional and country-level sustainable development trends, cross-border dynamics and emerging risks, required for recurrent and ad/hoc assignments. • Identifies regional trends or patterns and provides insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization and other UN 2.0 approaches to support anticipatory evidence-informed planning, decision-making, and reporting. • Prepares inputs for reports to High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development and other intergovernmental bodies, inter-agency or expert groups on issues relating to sustainable development fora. 2. Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system, and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. The Basel, Rotterdam and Stockholm (BRS) Conventions are multilateral environmental agreements that share the common objective of protecting human health and the environment from hazardous chemicals and wastes. The Basel Convention addresses the environmentally sound management of hazardous wastes throughout their lifecycle. The Rotterdam Convention promotes shared responsibility in the international trade of hazardous chemicals and pesticides. The Stockholm Convention protects human health and the environment from persistent organic pollutants by reducing and ultimately eliminating their production, use, and release. The internship is located in the Executive Office (EO) of the BRS Secretariat. The Executive Office provides strategic, coordination, and administrative support to the Executive Secretary in carrying out the leadership and management functions of the Secretariat. The EO supports organizational planning, decision-making processes, coordination among Secretariat units, and engagement with key stakeholders, including Parties, United Nations entities, and development partners. The internship is designed to provide practical exposure to the work of an international organization and the functioning of a multilateral environmental agreement secretariat. The intern will support the Executive Office in research, information analysis, coordination, documentation, and organizational planning activities, while gaining hands-on experience in governance processes, strategic coordination, and executive support. Through this experience, the intern will develop analytical, organizational, and professional skills while contributing to the effective functioning of the Executive Office. The intern will assist with: Research & Analysis: • Conduct background research on policy and programmatic issues. • Compile and summarize information from reports, publications, meeting documents, and other reference materials. • Assist in preparing background notes, briefing materials, and summaries for internal use. Coordination & Support: • Assist in organizing internal and external meetings, including preparing agendas and compiling meeting materials. • Support the preparation of meeting summaries and follow-up on agreed action points. • Assist in compiling and organizing documentation for meetings and engagements involving Parties, partners, and United Nations entities. • Provide logistical and administrative support for meetings, events, and other Executive Office activities, as required. Documentation & Reporting: • Draft reports, presentations, briefing materials, and other substantive documents. • Support the organization and maintenance of information repositories, databases, and filing systems. • Help compile and organize information for reporting, planning, and monitoring purposes. • Contribute to knowledge management activities by ensuring documents and reference materials are appropriately stored and accessible. Other Tasks: • Provide support for additional assignments and activities as requested by the Executive Office.
Qualifications/special skills
- Applicants must be enrolled in, or have graduated within the past year from, a graduate programme or the final year of an undergraduate programme in International Affairs, Environmental Science and Policy, Engineering and Public Policy, Public Administration, or a related field. - Applicants to the United Nations Internship Programme are not required to have professional work experience. However, applicants must be enrolled in, or have graduated within the past year from, a graduate programme or the final year of an undergraduate programme in International Affairs, Environmental Science and Policy, Engineering and Public Policy, Public Administration, or a related field. Please indicate your field of study and explain how it relates to this internship. - Applicants must be enrolled in the final year of a Bachelor's degree programme (or equivalent), be enrolled in a Master's or Ph.D. programme, or have completed a Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. programme within the past year. Please note that an official certificate may be requested at a later stage. - Interest in environmental governance, chemicals and waste management, sustainable development, or international environmental policy is desirable. Please describe how your academic studies, coursework, research, or other activities relate to these areas. - Experience conducting academic research and preparing written assignments, policy papers, reports, dissertations, presentations, or other analytical documents is desirable. Please provide examples that demonstrate your research, analytical, and drafting skills. - Experience participating in university projects, student organizations, volunteer initiatives, conferences, workshops, or other collaborative activities is desirable. Please describe any experience supporting or coordinating activities, organizing events or meetings, or working as part of a team. - Strong organizational skills and attention to detail are desirable. Please provide an example of how you managed multiple assignments, deadlines, or responsibilities in an academic, volunteer, or extracurricular setting. Please explain your interest in the work of the Basel, Rotterdam and Stockholm Conventions and how this internship would contribute to your academic and professional development.
Languages
Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of another UN official language is an asset. Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish are the official languages of the United Nations Secretariat.

Not available.

Org. Setting and Reporting
This position is located within the Common Administrative Platform at United Nations Headquarters, referred to as the One Executive Office (OneEO), under the Division of Administration in the Department of Operational Support (DOS). OneEO has been officially launched on 1 July 2026 as part of the UN80 reform initiative, which aims to consolidate common administrative functions across Secretariat entities into unified service platforms. The Department of Operational Support was established to provide end-to-end operational support, advisory services and other solutions to operating entities across the Secretariat, including departments, offices away from headquarters, peace operations, and regional commissions. OneEO provides the full range of administrative and operational services required by New York–based Secretariat client entities to fulfill their mandates, including human resources management, financial administration, travel, and general administrative support. Specifically, this position is located in the Specialized Desk 4. The Finance and Budget Assistant reports to the Associate Administrative Officer.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Finance & Budget Assistant will be responsible for the following duties: BUDGET • May act as Certifying Officer on behalf of and in the absence of programme managers at offices outside of headquarters. • Prepares interim and final financial statements for each trust fund contribution for approval by Account Division, in compliance with the reporting requirements stipulated in contribution agreements. • Prepares supporting documents (narrative and supporting tables) with respect to finalization of cost estimates and budget proposals, in terms of staff and non-staff requirements. • Assists managers in the elaboration of resource requirements for budget submissions. • Undertakes research and provides support to higher level Finance & Budget Officers with respect to budget reviews of relevant intergovernmental and expert bodies. • Monitors expenditures and compares with approved budget; prepares adjustments as necessary. • Reviews requisitions for goods and services to ensure (a) correct objects of expenditure have been charged, and (b) availability of funds. • Assists in preparation of budget performance submissions and finalization of budget performance reports, analyzing variances between approved budgets and actual expenditures. • Monitors integrity of various financial databases and extra-budgetary resources administered by the Headquarters Client Support Service, including review of agreements and cost plans, ensuring compliance with regulations and rules and established policies and procedures. • Verifies accuracy of input data, ensuring consistency of data in previous allotments to new allotments issued. • Co-ordinates with other finance and budget staff on related issues during preparation of budget reports. GENERAL • Keeps up-to-date on documents/reports/guidelines that have a bearing on matters related to programme, ensuring compliance with intergovernmental recommendations and decisions as well as with United Nations policies and procedures. • Drafts or prepares correspondence to respond to enquiries in respect to relevant financial and budget matters. • Maintain and keep up-to-date files. • May be responsible for providing guidance, training and daily supervision to other general service staff in the area of responsibility. • Assists with the collection and analysis of data as well as preparation of data presentations and reports for information sharing, responding to queries, knowledge management, planning and decision making. • Assists with visualizations and updating information material such as web pages or client portal. • Performs other related duties, as assigned.
Competencies
PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of, and ability to apply financial rules, regulations and procedures in the UN environment. Knowledge, skills and ability to extract, interpret, analyse and format data across the full range of finance and budget functions, including programme development and database management, claims and treasury operations. Ability to identify and resolve data discrepancies and operational problems. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Commitment to implementing the goal of gender equality by ensuring the equal participation and full involvement of women and men in all aspects of work. The ability to perform analysis, modeling and interpretation of data in support of decision-making. TEAMWORK: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others' ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. CLIENT ORIENTATION: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be "clients"; and seeks to see things from clients' point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients' needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients' environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client.

Not available.

The focus of the position is twofold: The first focus is to identify, structure and underpin data-and analytics-driven solutions in all areas of Inter-Agency Human Resources matters ranging from demographics and cost-related topics to behavioral aspects. A strong conceptual and scientific foundation is expected to underpin such solutions, in order to ensure objectivity and credibility of the proposed solutions. The second focus is to generate and communicate Human Resources-related data-driven analyses and insights in support of decision-making processes, by looking at historical trends, current data and predictions.

Within delegated authority, the Data and Behavioral Scientist will be responsible for the following duties: • Works with stakeholders across the CEB organizations to identify opportunities for leveraging data to drive business solutions. • Develops and implements databases, data collection systems, data analytics and other strategies to optimize statistical efficiency and quality including automation scripts and internal software. • Applies causal inference and experimental methods such as randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental designs, and causal modeling of observational data to estimate the impact of system-wide policies and inform evidence-based decisions. • Collects, mines, scrapes and analyzes data including those shared by organizations shared by organizations to drive optimization and improvement of inter-agency coordination in behavioral sciences, human resources, organizational management and compensation. • Assesses and tests the effectiveness and accuracy of new datasets and data processing procedures. • Develops custom predictive algorithms to apply to data sets. • Coordinates with different functional teams in CEB organizations to implement models and monitor outcomes • Performs other duties as assigned.

Ability to apply judgment in the context of assignments given, plan own work and manage conflicting priorities. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules. Supports subordinates, provides oversight and takes responsibility for delegated assignments. Experience with data science and statistics-related programming languages such as R and Python, with SQL and relational database design and management is required. Responsibilities

regional organizations, as well as UN agencies, programmes and funds. • Cooperates with the Front Office of Mission Support Division, in particular with activities linked to host government support needed in the areas of transport, aviation, customs clearances, cargo movements, etc. as necessary. • Familiarizes staff members with local laws when interacting with government authorities. • Helps the Mission to educate initiatives regarding local customs, values, and norms. • Works in collaboration with Mission Support sections in order to obtain relevant clearances from the host government. • Coordinates with the local authorities, in case of medical emergency and provides assistance to the Medical Services Section as required. • Performs other duties as required.

vacancies.jobDescription:
Work Location
ITC Headquarters - Geneva, Switzerland
Expected duration
Nov. 26 - May 27
Duties and Responsibilities
The International Trade Centre (ITC) is the joint agency of the World Trade Organization (WTO) and the United Nations (UN). ITC supports the international competitiveness of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and inclusive, sustainable development through trade and enterprise development. In Iraq, ITC implements complementary European Union-supported initiatives contributing to economic inclusion of Women, Youth and Vulnerable Communities (WYVC), decent employment, business development and stronger institutions. This internship will support three linked workstreams: • JOBS (Jobs and entrepreneurship Opportunities to Build Sustainable inclusive Development – SAAVI Phase 2), Expected Result 4 (ER4): enhancing self-reliance and durable solutions for displacement-affected populations and vulnerable groups, particularly women and youth, through demand-driven skills, access to employment and entrepreneurship opportunities, financial inclusion and awareness of relevant rights. • BEIT (Building Equitable and Inclusive Transformation: Towards Decent Work and Affordable Housing in Iraq), Objective 3.3: support to ITC’s work in housing and construction, with particular attention to investment facilitation, sector governance, MSME participation and opportunities for sustainable, affordable housing. • MASAR, Expected Result 3 (ER3): operationalisation of relevant technical and vocational education and training (TVET) policies and institutional frameworks, including inter-ministerial protocols, standard operating procedures, implementation tools and targeted support to institutional adoption. The intern will contribute to desk research, stakeholder and institutional mapping, technical documentation, coordination, reporting and knowledge management across these workstreams, under staff supervision. The internship is a learning assignment and does not entail independent policy advice or responsibility for project delivery. DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES / RESPONSIBILITIES Under the direct supervision of the designated ITC Senior Programme Officer, and in collaboration with the Iraq projects’ team, the intern will undertake the following tasks: JOBS – ER4 | Economic inclusion, self-reliance and durable solutions • Conduct desk research on economic inclusion barriers and opportunities for internally displaced persons, returnees, refugees, women, youth and other vulnerable groups in targeted areas of Iraq. • Support mapping of labour-market opportunities, employers, business support organizations (BSOs), vocational training providers, entrepreneurship initiatives and financial service providers relevant to employment and self-employment pathways. • Assist in consolidating information on beneficiary outreach, skills development, employment referrals, enterprise support, access-to-finance linkages and rights-awareness activities; organize evidence for progress reporting with appropriate data protection and disaggregation. • Prepare background briefs, analytical summaries, presentations and meeting records for coordination with implementing partners and other stakeholders. BEIT – Objective 3.3 | Housing and construction sector support • Support the preparation and documentation of technical consultations with public institutions, private-sector representatives, investors and business support organizations. • Help maintain action trackers, stakeholder contact matrices and records of outputs relevant to the workstream, as requested by the supervisor. MASAR – ER3 | TVET governance and reform operationalization • Assist in mapping TVET institutions, coordination mechanisms, stakeholder mandates, focal points and decision-making or approval processes, with emphasis on private-sector engagement. • Support evidence reviews on institutional and procedural bottlenecks affecting work-based learning, occupational standards, curriculum approval, assessment and labour-market feedback. • Prepare working matrices, meeting minutes and draft inputs for inter-ministerial protocols, standard operating procedures, coordination terms of reference and implementation tools, under technical guidance. • Support follow-up on consultations, pilot operationalisation and institutional adoption of selected reform measures, including maintenance of agreed actions and validation milestones. Cross-cutting support • Prepare well-referenced research notes, PowerPoint presentations, meeting documentation and concise progress updates. • Support the planning and follow-up of online and in-person stakeholder meetings, workshops and technical events. • Maintain organized project files and knowledge products, respecting confidentiality, safeguarding, gender equality, inclusion and conflict-sensitive approaches. INDICATIVE OUTPUTS (UNDER SUPERVISION) • Stakeholder and institutional mapping matrices for relevant workstreams. • Short research notes and presentation materials on ER4 inclusion pathways, BEIT housing/construction issues and MASAR TVET institutional operationalisation. • Meeting briefs, minutes, action trackers and documented follow-up on consultations and technical working sessions. • A consolidated end-of-internship handover note describing outputs, lessons learned and pending follow-up. ITC champions workforce diversity, inclusion, gender equality and gender parity and considers all qualified persons equally, including persons with disabilities, without discrimination or prejudice of any kind.
Qualifications/special skills
Applicants to the programme shall, at the time of application, meet one of the following requirements: a) Be enrolled in a graduate school programme (second university degree or equivalent, or higher); or b) Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (minimum bachelor’s level or equivalent); c) Have graduated with a university degree (as defined in a or b above) and, if selected, shall commence the internship within one year of graduation. Relevant studies include economics, international development, public policy, international relations, business administration, social sciences or a related field. SKILLS • Interest in inclusive economic development, labour markets, entrepreneurship, private-sector development, housing/construction or TVET governance, preferably in fragile or displacement-affected contexts. • Ability to conduct structured desk research, critically assess sources, synthesize findings and prepare clear, accurately referenced written outputs. • Strong organizational and communication skills; proficiency in standard office software, spreadsheets and presentation tools. Data visualization and basic monitoring skills are assets.
Languages
• Fluency in English; • Arabic and/or other UN languages would be a strong asset.

Not available.

Interns are not financially remunerated by the United Nations. Costs and arrangements for travel, visas, accommodation and living expenses are the responsibility of interns or their sponsoring institutions. Interns who are not citizens or permanent residents of the country where the internship is undertaken, may be required to obtain the appropriate visa and work/employment authorization. Successful candidates should discuss their specific visa requirements before accepting the internship offer.

Duties and Responsibilities
The Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (UN Human Rights) is the leading UN entity on human rights. We represent the world's commitment to the promotion and protection of the full range of human rights and freedoms set out in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Both the High Commissioner and the Office have a unique role to: • Promote and protect all human rights: We speak out objectively in the face of human rights violations and help elaborate the standards that are used to evaluate human rights progress worldwide. • Help empower people: Our research, education, and advocacy activities, contributes to the increased awareness and engagement by the international community and the public on human rights issues. This means thousands of people in all regions of the world are empowered to claim their rights. • Assist Governments: Through our field presences, we help prevent abuses and contribute to defusing situations that could lead to conflict. Our monitoring and analysis feeds sensitive decision-making and development programming. We also provide capacity-building and legal advice to thousands, supporting the development and judicious enactment of laws and policies the world around. • Inject a human rights perspective into all UN programmes: We mainstream human rights into all UN programmes to ensure that peace and security, development, and human rights - the three pillars of the UN - are interlinked and mutually reinforced. The Programme Support and Management Service (PSMS) delivers comprehensive administrative support within the Office and is responsible for overseeing and managing the financial, human, and physical resources that support delivery of the human rights mandate. The Human Resources Management Section (HRMS) at OHCHR serves as a strategic partner in advancing the Office's global mandate by delivering effective, people-centered human resources services. The Recruitment Unit within the Human Resources Management Section of OHCHR offers comprehensive support and guidance for filling staff positions, whether temporary or long-term. Org. Setting and Reporting
This position is located in the Human Resources Management Service, Division of Administration, UNOG. The incumbent is the Chief of the Medical Services Section (MSS). S/he will report directly to the Chief of HRMS, UNOG. S/he will work under the overall policy guidance of the Medical Director, DHMOSH, for medical, clinical and occupational health matters.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority and overall direction of the Director-General of UNOG, as well as the overall healthcare management, occupational safety and health, and public health service policy guidance by the Medical Director, DHMOSH in New York, the Senior Medical Officer will be responsible for the following duties: Clinic Management: - Oversees the delivery of high-quality occupational health services in the UN workplace, including employment clearances, travel medicine services and travel clearances. - Oversees the provision of workplace clinical services including first aid and emergency care, access to UN programmes such as PEP kits, vaccination campaigns, and effective referral to local healthcare services. - Oversees clinical practice in relation to in-person occupational health clinical reviews and examinations. - Develops and oversees the delivery of occupational health and safety programs including workplace and home ergonomics programs and workplace safety and health risk assessments, as well as developing and implementing risk treatment action plans. - Oversees and provides specialist guidance on workplace (reasonable) accommodation requests with a medical component in line with UN policies. - Oversees the delivery of effective workplace or general health promotion programs. - Develops, exercises and provides a local emergency response / mass casualty capability integrated with local security plans. - Advises on other aspects of health including public health relevant to the duty station, through liaison and in close coordination with the health authorities of the Host Country. - Ensures quality in services including the implementation of quality control mechanisms and procedures, the use of published UN clinical guidelines, and adherence to patient safety and adverse event reporting requirements. Medical Administration: - Oversees the provision of recommendations or determinations related to medical entitlements. - Oversees the certification of sick leave, including where required liaison with individual staff members and their healthcare providers to ensure effective sick leave management. - Oversees the development and implementation of return-to-work program. - Monitors sick leave usage in conjunction with human resources staff and prepares and finalizes disability summaries and reports for the Medical Director and UNJSPF. - Oversees medical evacuation and repatriation services where required. - Oversees the provision of advisory services to the Geneva based office of the Advisory Board on Compensation Claims Committee (ABCC). - Undertakes mediation and informal dispute resolution related to medical entitlements and, where required, represents the Medical Services Section in formal dispute resolution bodies such as medical boards or the UN Dispute Tribunal. Supervisory: - Manages the work and results of all staff working in the Medical Services Section, including occupational safety and health staff - Ensures medical confidentiality and release of medical records/information is in accordance with UN policies and requirements. - Manages access to the EarthMed medical record system. - Undertakes annual planning. - Plans and prepares budgets and reports on budget performance and results. - Ensures the development, generation and reporting of relevant key performance indicators documenting health support performance including responses to audit requests on health performance. - Ensures timely recruiting and training of all new staff, and effective performance management. - Ensures effective continuous professional development of staff and their career management. Advisory, liaison and representation: - Coordinates with the Office of the Director, DHMOSH UNHQ, contributes to the development of UN healthcare policy, including through participation in the working groups of the UN Medical Directors, and ensures alignment of policy and practice in UN health care services. - Represents the Medical Services Section at events and meetings with other UN entities and in national and international fora. - Oversees workplace health and MSS communication products, and liaison/outreach with external actors. - Briefs and advises the Director-General and senior management of client departments on all health matters relevant to the workplace (including mental health and staff well-being), such as health policies, business continuity, enterprise risk management and representation at crisis response and related bodies, makes recommendations taking into consideration the local context, whenever warranted. - Represents MSS on health and medical entitlements matters before the UN judicial system and UN investigative bodies. - Ensures effective occupational health representation at the local occupational health and safety committee, or similar body. General: -Performs other related duties as required.
Competencies
Professionalism: Knowledge of clinical, occupational safety and health and tropical/travel medicine. Ability to manage a diverse and multicultural team and to operate efficiently under stressful circumstances. Good drafting ability in English and French. Shows pride in work and in achievements. Demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter. Is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results. Is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns. Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Accountability: Takes ownership of all responsibilities and honours commitments. Delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within prescribed time, cost and quality standards. Operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules. Supports subordinates, provides oversight and takes responsibility for delegated assignments. Takes personal responsibility for his/her own shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable. Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively. Listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately. Asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication. Tailors language, tone, style and format to match the audience. Demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. Leadership: Serves as a role model that other people want to follow. Empowers others to translate vision into results. Is proactive in developing strategies to accomplish objectives. Establishes and maintains relationships with a broad range of people to understand needs and gain support. Anticipates and resolves conflicts by pursuing mutually agreeable solutions. Drives for change and improvement; does not accept the status quo. Shows the courage to take unpopular stands. Provides leadership and takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work; demonstrates knowledge of strategies and commitment to the goal of gender balance in staffing. Judgement/decision making: Identifies the key issues in a complex situation, and comes to the heart of the problem quickly. Gathers relevant information before making a decision. Considers positive and negative impacts of decisions prior to making them. Takes decisions with an eye to the impact on others and on the Organization. Proposes a course of action or makes a recommendation based on all available information. Checks assumptions against facts. Determines that the actions proposed will satisfy the expressed and underlying needs for the decision. Makes tough decisions when necessary.

Doctorate (MD) or equivalent in medicine, including residency/internship in one of the medical specialties, preferably internal or occupational safety and health medicine, is required.
Job - Specific Qualification
Certification in internal and/or travel medicine is desirable. Certification in occupational safety and health medicine is desirable.
Work Experience
A minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible clinical experience in one of the areas of medicine, including at least five (5) years in the Occupational Safety and Health field are required. Two (2) years of managerial experience in the medical field including budgeting, supervisory responsibilities and resource management are required. Experience in mental health is desirable. Experience with project management is desirable. Experience in travel medicine related to Occupational Safety and Health is desirable. Experience in an international organization is desirable.

Result of Service
The consultant will support ECA's work on health financing, innovative finance, capital market development and domestic resource mobilization for health through policy analysis, technical advice, knowledge generation and stakeholder engagement. The assignment will contribute to strengthening African member States' capacity to mobilize sustainable financing for health, leverage domestic and international resources, develop investment-ready health projects, and identify and structure innovative financing solutions for priority health investments.
Work Location
Addis Ababa
Expected duration
12 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The Macroeconomics and Governance Division (MGD) is headed by a Director and reports to the Deputy Executive Secretary (Programme). The Division is responsible for supporting African member States in their efforts to accelerate economic transformation and inclusive growth through effective development planning, improved macroeconomic management and economic governance as well as better mobilization and allocation of domestic and international public finance. It is divided into three main sections: Macroeconomic Analysis, Institutions & Economic Governance Section (MIGS) , Sustainable Development and Integrated Planning Section (SDIPS), Economic Governance and Public Finance Section (EGPFS), and Finance and Domestic Resource Mobilization Section (FDRMS). Duties and Responsibilities: Under the overall guidance of the Director and the direct supervision of the Chief of the Finance and Domestic Resource Mobilization Section, the consultant will support the Division's work on Health Financing through the following tasks: Economic and Sector Analysis • Develop analytical databases, policy research, and knowledge products on health financing, financing gaps, investment opportunities and related issues across Africa. • Assess innovative financing instruments and mechanisms to support health financing, including debt-for-health conversions, blended finance mechanisms, results-based financing, guarantees, risk-sharing facilities, social and thematic bonds, diaspora finance and other relevant financing instruments. • Undertake analysis of African capital markets and their role in mobilizing long-term financing for health investments. • Analyze policy, regulatory, fiscal and institutional frameworks required to mobilize domestic, institutional and private capital for health. • Assess opportunities for strengthening domestic resource mobilization and leveraging institutional investors for sustainable health financing. • Undertake analysis to support health investment readiness and transaction preparation, including the identification, screening and development of priority health investments suitable for public, private, institutional and catalytic financing. • Assess financing and investment risks and relevant de-risking approaches for health investments, including guarantees, concessional finance, results-based payments and other risk-sharing mechanisms. • Develop analytical inputs and policy recommendations to inform ECA's work on health financing and support member States in strengthening sustainable financing for health. • Monitor regional and global policy developments on health financing, innovative finance, sustainable finance and related financing mechanisms. Intergovernmental Support • Prepare analytical inputs for the preparation and participation in health financing, development finance and domestic resource mobilization related events and meetings. • Follow relevant meetings and processes on health financing, development finance and domestic resource mobilization and prepare summary reports. • Draft inputs to statements, speeches and presentations for ECA senior leadership on health financing, innovative finance, domestic resource mobilization and related financing issues. • Support consultations with African member States, development finance institutions, regional organizations, development partners, institutional investors, private-sector actors and other stakeholders on health financing and other areas of the Section's work. • Assist in the organization of panels, round tables, expert group meetings, policy dialogues, peer-learning activities, side events and high-level forums on health financing, development finance, domestic resource mobilization and other thematic areas related to the work of the Section. Technical Cooperation • Participate in missions and provide substantive support to ECA leadership on health financing, innovative finance and health investment initiatives. • Support the design and implementation of technical cooperation projects related to sustainable health financing. • Contribute to initiatives aimed at improving African countries' access to finance for health and mobilizing domestic and international resources for health investment. • Support technical work on the development and structuring of financing solutions for health, including domestic resource mobilization, institutional capital, innovative finance, blended finance and private-sector financing. • Support ECA's analytical and technical assistance work on health investment readiness, project and transaction preparation, innovative financing mechanisms, de-risking approaches and sustainable health financing for member States. General • Perform other related duties as required in support of ECA's health financing and sustainable finance work programme. • Undertake on-the-job and other training activities, both internally and externally. • Collect and analyse data to identify trends or patterns and provide insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. Outputs / Work Assignment The consultant will be expected to deliver the following outputs: • Technical analyses and policy inputs on health financing, innovative finance, domestic resource mobilization, institutional capital and capital market development to inform ECA's health financing work programme. • Policy briefs, background papers, concept notes and analytical reports on key issues related to health financing, innovative financing mechanisms, health investment readiness and access to finance for health in Africa. • Technical inputs and analytical support for country-specific health financing activities, including health investment readiness, transaction preparation, financing instrument design and technical cooperation initiatives. • Policy recommendations and advisory notes on innovative financing mechanisms for health; domestic resource mobilization; institutional investor participation; capital market financing; health investment readiness; debt-for-health conversions; blended finance; de-risking mechanisms; and other approaches to mobilizing sustainable financing for health. • Briefing materials, talking points, speeches and presentations for ECA senior management's participation in health financing related meetings, forums and high-level engagements. • Meeting reports and summary notes from consultations, expert group meetings, policy dialogues, peer-learning activities, roundtables and other relevant forums. • Data analysis products and visualization materials, including databases, dashboards, graphs, charts and presentations to support evidence-based policymaking and reporting.

Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in economics, finance, health economics, public policy or related areas is required. A first-level university degree in combination with additional two years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the master's degree. • A minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in economic research and analysis, policy formulation, development finance, health financing, public finance or related areas is required. • Two years or more of experience in data analytics or related areas is desirable. • Experience in Africa or on African-related issues is desirable. • Experience in multi-lateral/intergovernmental processes is desirable • Experience in financing for sustainable development in the regional and or global level is desirable. • Experience in technical cooperation and engagement with governments, development finance institutions and/or development partners is desirable .

vacancies.jobTitle: UNEP Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) Pollution and Circular Economy Support Internship
vacancies.jobDescription:
Work Location
Remote or in Geneva, Switzerland
Expected duration
6 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. The overall objective of the UNEP’s Industry and Economy Division is to encourage decision makers in government, local authorities and industry to develop and adopt policies, strategies, practices and technologies that promote sustainable patterns of consumption and production, make efficient use of natural resources, ensure safe management of chemicals and contribute to making trade and environment policies mutually supportive. It promotes the development, use and transfer of policies, technologies, economic instruments, managerial practices and other tools that assist in environmentally sound decision making and the building of corresponding activities. The United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) is the strategic partnership between the United Nations and over 500 banks, insurers and investors. For over 34 years UNEP FI has been shaping and driving the international sustainable finance agenda, setting global standards and growing a global network of leading financial institutions. Through its work-streams and regional activities, peer learning, methodology development, training and research, UNEP FI promotes sustainable finance and helps the financial industry align with and contribute to the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals. Pollution and Circular Economy is a thematic focus area recently launched by UNEP FI. Pollution has a pervasive impact on people and society, on biodiversity loss and on climate change. One of the root causes of pollution – as well as climate change and biodiversity loss- is the unsustainable use of natural resources in our production and consumption models. A key part of the solution to the three planetary crises on climate, nature and pollution is to transition to a more resource efficient and circular economy, where waste and pollution are eliminated, products and materials are kept in use at their highest value and natural systems are regenerated. This is a priority, not only for our planet and our health, but also to achieve the UN Sustainable Development Goals and the Paris Agreement on Climate Change, and to build more resilient economies. The global financial sector has a pivotal role to play to transition to a circular economy. UNEP FI works with members and partners to support the transition to less polluting and more circular economies. We provide research and guidance, we raise awareness and build capacity within the financial community, we facilitate peer exchange and collective action, at global and regional level. We engage with policymakers, such as in the context of the negotiation of the future international legally binding plastics treaty which is expected to be finalised by end of 2024. The intern will join the Pollution and Circular Economy workstream, working on a range of exciting and cutting-edge initiatives, in collaboration with other UNEP FI’s thematic streams and external stakeholders. Tasks: The intern will assist with implementing UNEP FI’s work programme related to its Pollution and Circular Economy workstream. Daily responsibilities may vary depending on the individual’s background. Duties include, but are not limited to: • Support internal work on the topics of pollution -especially plastic and chemicals pollution- and circular economy. We expect the intern to take initiative on a piece of applied research on a relevant topic and/or other additional duties relevant to their own areas of interest in this field (can be technological, creative or otherwise innovative in relation with pollution and/or circular economy), as agreed with the supervisor. • Support the on-going development of the UNEP FI support, guidance materials, case studies, capacity building program and other work related to pollution and circular economy. • Support the work of the Circular Economy Working Group, which develops a series of guidance documents for banks on how to operationalise the nexus between circular economy and the broader sustainability agenda, especially in sectors with high impact and strong circular potential. • Support the establishment and activities of a Circular Economy Community of Practice, which aims to foster knowledge sharing and peer exchange within the finance sector, as well as multistakeholder exchange, including with development banks. • Support the work of the Pollution Working Group, which develops a guidance on pollution for banks, especially in high impact sectors like agriculture and buildings and construction. • Support the work of the Finance Leadership Group on Plastics, a core group of financial institutions contributing to the development process of the future international plastics treaty currently under negotiation by Member States, and co-developing resources to support financial institutions to tackle the issue of plastic pollution in their portfolios. • Carry out research on pollution, circular economy and finance-related themes, especially around metrics, indicators and data, as well as norms and practices. • Collate information on pollution and circular economy from various sources including technical reports, industry publications, webinars, company disclosures, etc. Monitor academic publications on related themes and convert these into digestible highlights. • of Practice and other interest groups (general liaison, setting up meetings), and with other UNEP FI teams as relevant. • Provide project coordination, administrative and communications support on Duties and Responsibilities
Organizational Setting and Reporting: The Registry of the United Nations International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals ("Mechanism") invites applications for internships with the Library starting from 1 November 2026 to 31 December 2026 in Arusha, United Republic of Tanzania. The Mechanism was established by the Security Council of the United Nations in 2010 to carry out a number of essential functions of the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda ("ICTR") and the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia ("ICTY"), after the completion of their respective mandates. The Registry, operating from both branches of the Mechanism, located in Arusha, the United Republic of Tanzania, and The Hague, The Netherlands, provides administrative, legal, policy, and diplomatic support services. The Registry's main duties include the provision of administrative services to the Mechanism, including court support services; the supervision of the enforcement of sentences; monitoring of cases referred to national courts; preservation, including the management and providing of access to the ICTR, ICTY and Mechanism archives; the protection of victims and witnesses; and assistance to national jurisdictions. The internship is in the Library of the Mechanism's Registry in Arusha, and under the direct supervision of the Library Assistant. The library offers a wide selection of books covering various fields including international law, international criminal law, genocide, and human rights. Additionally, the library offers a diverse range of services such as Online Public Access Catalogues, document delivery via email for both internal and external users, as well as in-person reference services and research assistance tailored to individual user needs. Interested candidates may visit the Mechanism website's internship page at https://www.irmct. org/en/recruitment/internship/internship-programme to obtain general information including: • Programme Guidelines; • Internship programme; and • Terms and Conditions of the Mechanism's Internship Programme. UNOCA covers Angola, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Rwanda and Sao Tome and Principe and works closely with the Economic Community of Central African States and other sub-regional organisations.

Carries out regular in-depth research on emerging or persisting peace and security challenges facing the Central Africa region or the countries under the purview of UNOCA and recommends options for good offices and other UN actions. - Monitors national and regional level political developments and provides advice to Headquarter and field mission/UN agencies active on the ground, through the preparation of regional, country-specific and thematic reports including, but not limited to weekly situation reports, briefing notes, analytical notes, options papers, code cables and reports of the Secretary-General to the Security Council, General Assembly or other bodies. - The United Nations Convention against Cybercrime; Strengthening International Cooperation for Combating Certain Crimes Committed by Means of Information and Communications Technology Systems and for the Sharing of Evidence in Electronic Form of Serious Crimes, was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in its resolution 79/243 of 24 December 2024. It represents the first global treaty addressing cybercrime and enhancing international cooperation on electronic evidence of serious crimes. Article 16 of the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime represents the first criminal prohibition at the global level of the non-consensual sharing of intimate images (NCII). As part of broader efforts to promote the ratification and implementation of the Convention, UNODC is developing a range of knowledge products to promote understanding and implementation of Article 16. The consultant will develop and finalize a suite of knowledge products that offer a clear, accurate, globally relevant, and compelling insight into the phenomenon of NCII and benefits of Article 16 and its implementation. Result of Service
To establish the technical foundation for a national GHS capacity-building programme in Vietnam by assessing the existing legal, regulatory and institutional framework, identifying priority capacity-building needs, and developing a comprehensive training programme and supporting materials tailored to the Vietnamese context.
Work Location
Home-based / Working remotely
Expected duration
70 days over 10 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. The overall objective of the UNEP’s Economy Division is to encourage decision makers in government, local authorities and industry to develop and adopt policies, strategies and practices and technologies that promote sustainable patterns of consumption and production, make efficient use of natural resources, ensure safe management of chemicals and contribute to making trade and environment policies mutually supportive. It promotes the development, use and transfer of policies, technologies, economic instruments, managerial practices and other tools that assist in environmentally sound decision making and the building of corresponding activities. The Chemicals and Health Branch of the Industry and Economy Division leads UNEP's sub-programme on Chemicals, Waste and Air Quality. UNEP’s programme of work centers around assistance to countries and multilateral environmental agreement (MEA) secretariats to assist in technical-scientific issues related to priority chemicals and implementation of the United Nations Environment Assembly and Governing Council resolutions. The Chemicals and Health Branch promotes scientific approaches and knowledge for the sound management of chemicals including through implementation of United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA) resolutions and Global Environment Facility (GEF) projects. The Branch also addresses chemicals and waste topics highlighted by governments, such as the issues of concern, the Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling (GHS) and chemicals management systems. Under the overall supervision of the Chief, Chemicals and Health Branch, Industry and Economy Division, and direct supervision of the Programme Management Officer, Agrifood and Health Unit, Chemicals and Health Branch, the Consultant will be responsible for the following: • Inception and Technical Planning o Review relevant national legislation, policies, regulations, guidance documents, institutional arrangements, and existing training resources related to the implementation of the Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals (GHS) in Vietnam. o Consult with UNEP, ICCA, Vinachemia, and other relevant stakeholders to identify technical priorities, target audiences, existing capacities, and priority capacity-building needs. o Prepare an inception overview outlining the proposed methodology, detailed workplan, workshop approach, preliminary programme structure, learning objectives, and implementation schedule. • Assessment and Design of the GHS Capacity-Building Programme o Assess priority technical and institutional capacity-building needs based on the desk review and stakeholder consultations. o Design a comprehensive GHS capacity-building programme tailored to the Vietnamese context and the identified needs of government authorities, industry, and other relevant stakeholders. o Develop the proposed workshop agenda, learning objectives, training methodology, and structure of the technical sessions. o Prepare an initial draft of the training programme and core technical content for review by UNEP and relevant stakeholders. • Development of the GHS Capacity-Building Package o Develop the technical content and materials required for the training programme, including presentations, participant materials, trainer's guide, practical exercises, case studies, and technical reference materials. o Develop practical examples and exercises supporting the application of GHS requirements, including, as appropriate, hazard classification, chemical labelling, Safety Data Sheets (SDS), and hazard communication. o Prepare pre- and post-training assessments, participant evaluation tools, and other workshop resources to support effective learning and subsequent evaluation of the training. o Ensure that the training materials are technically accurate, practical, user-friendly, and appropriately adapted to the Vietnamese context. • Review and Finalization of the GHS Capacity-Building Package o Present the draft capacity-building package for review by UNEP and relevant technical stakeholders and respond to comments and technical inputs received. o Revise and finalize the GHS capacity-building package based on the feedback received. o Submit the complete package in editable formats, ready for subsequent use in the delivery of the national GHS training workshop.

Education: Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Toxicology, Environmental Sciences, Occupational Health and Safety, Chemical Safety, or a closely related field is required. Experience: A minimum of five (5) years of professional experience in chemical management, chemical safety, or the implementation of GHS is required. Experience supporting international organizations, industry associations, or multi-stakeholder initiatives related to chemical safety, chemicals management, or GHS implementation is desirable.

Result of Service
Under the supervision of the Programme Management Officer, the consultant will support the implementation of activities related to how product sustainability information can support sustainable consumption and production through consumer information tools, with a particular focus on ecolabels and digital product information systems.
Work Location
Remote
Expected duration
13 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environment authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. UNEP’s Economy and Industry Division addresses environmental issues at global and regional levels, provides leadership and encourages partnership in caring for the environment by inspiring, informing and enabling nations and people to improve their quality of life without compromising that of future generations. The Industry and Economy Division also works with many partners, including Member States, national and local governments, business and industry and non-governmental organizations, to develop and implement policies, strategies and practices that are cleaner and safer, incorporate environmental costs, use natural resources efficiently, reduce pollution and risks for humans and the environment, and enable the implementation of conventions and international agreements. The 10-Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Consumption and Production (10YFP), adopted by Heads of State at the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development (Rio+20) in 2012, is a global framework for action to accelerate the shift towards Sustainable Consumption and Production (SCP) worldwide. As reflected in the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the 10YFP plays a central role in achieving the shift to SCP: its implementation is the first target of Sustainable Development Goal 12 on "Ensuring sustainable consumption and production". The 10YFP is also recognized as the Framework of reference for decoupling economic growth from environmental degradation in SDG8. The 10YFP generates impact through multi-stakeholder programmes and partnerships, which develop, replicate, and scale up SCP policies and practices at all levels and which form together the One Planet Network. UNEP was mandated by the UN General Assembly to serve as the Secretariat of the 10YFP. UNEP, serving as 10YFP Secretariat, supports the implementation of the Global Strategy for SCP (2023-2030) with a strategic focus on the key enablers for change that can help steer and shape markets, practices and behaviors, both from the supply and demand side, towards sustainable models, empowering governments, stakeholders and individuals to trigger long-term, sustainable and fair economic and social transformations across high-impact sectors and value chains. This includes partnerships and initiatives aimed at enhancing sustainability and circularity information sharing and disclosure, as well as at empowering consumers to make informed decisions based on transparent and reliable information, working in close cooperation with UNEP’s core partners through the One Planet Network Consumer Information Programme and other key initiatives. The Consumer Information Programme serves as a global platform to support the provision of quality information on goods and services, and the identification and implementation of the most effective strategies to engage consumers in sustainable consumption. The Programme is co-led by Germany through the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety, and Consumers International. The consultant will work with the 10YFP Secretariat, Materials and Systems Innovation Unit, Industry Innovation Branch, Industry and Economy Division. Specific tasks and responsibilities The consultant will have the following responsibilities: • In collaboration with UNEP's high-impact sector teams, starting with the textile sector, support the development of a common approach to defining product sustainability information (a common minimum data set), building on UNEP's existing work on ecolabels and voluntary sustainability standards. • Coordinate with relevant UNEP teams to promote consistency and alignment of sustainability criteria across initiatives. • Provide recommendations on how product sustainability information can be integrated into existing and emerging tools and systems, including Digital Product Information Systems (DPIS), Voluntary Sustainability Standards (VSS) and ecolabels. • Conduct research and analysis on emerging trends, challenges, and opportunities related to consumer information and sustainability information systems, particularly in high-impact sectors. • Draft and contribute to reports, technical papers, publications, briefs, guidance materials, and other technical outputs. • Support stakeholder consultations and engagement with standards organizations, industry representatives, researchers, policymakers, and other relevant partners. • Identify opportunities for UNEP to strengthen its thought leadership and contribute to international discussions on product sustainability information. • Prepare presentations, consultation materials, and other communication products to support UNEP's work on consumer information. • Participate in weekly team meetings and other meetings as required.
Qualifications/special skills
Education - Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in business administration, economics, environmental management, international relations or related field. - A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in combination with at least 2 (two) years of qualifying and relevant professional experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. - At least 4 years of progressively responsible working experience in development/sustainability related projects. - At least 1 year of working experience in Ecolabels. - At least 1 year of working experience at the international level is required. - Proven record of drafting or editing articles, reports or publications is required. - Knowledge of the textile sector would be an asset. - Knowledge of digital product passports would be an asset. - Experience working for UNEP, the UN system, or an international organization would be an asset.
Languages
Language - Fluency in oral and written English is required. - Knowledge of other official languages in the United Nations System is an advantage.

Not available.

• Support the substantive and operational implementation of CPCJ activities across its six outcomes and related criminal justice reform priorities • Assist in the preparation and updating of activity workplans, implementation calendars, travel schedules, mission plans, procurement trackers and follow-up matrices. • Coordinate administrative arrangements for meetings, workshops, trainings, consultations, missions and field activities, including venue arrangements, participant lists, invitations, attendance sheets, travel follow-up, materials and post-event documentation. • Draft meeting notes, minutes, activity reports, back-to-office reports and action-point trackers, and follow up with relevant team members and implementing partners on agreed actions. • Maintain organized electronic and physical records of programme activities, correspondence, approvals, procurement files, participant documentation and relevant evidence for audit, monitoring and reporting purposes. • Support coordination with CPCJ implementing partners and government counterparts to facilitate timely implementation and follow-up of agreed activities. 3.2 Research, analysis and knowledge support • Conduct desk research and compile information on crime prevention, criminal justice, access to justice, legal aid, prison reform, alternatives to imprisonment, case management and justice-sector coordination. • Assist in collecting, organizing and summarizing quantitative and qualitative information from programme reports, policy documents, legal instruments, stakeholder inputs and field consultations. • Prepare research briefs, literature summaries, analytical notes, consultation summaries and evidence tables to inform programme planning, monitoring and decision-making. • Support the compilation of information on training needs, target institutions and beneficiaries, stakeholder engagement and results achieved under the CPCJ programme. • Monitor relevant criminal justice sector developments, reforms, policies and emerging trends and prepare concise updates for internal use by the programme team. • Support the preparation and consolidation of programme results, indicators, beneficiary figures and other evidence required for programme monitoring and donor reporting. 3.3 Administrative and operational support • Provide day-to-day administrative support to the Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice Programme, including scheduling, correspondence, document formatting, filing, scanning, records management and logistical follow-up. • Assist in the preparation of procurement plans, requisitions, terms of reference, technical specifications, evaluation documentation and follow-up correspondence with procurement colleagues, vendors and service providers. • Support procurement processes by tracking timelines, compiling documentation, following up on goods and services delivery, supporting receipt and inspection processes, and maintaining complete procurement records. • Assist in preparing budget estimates, expenditure estimates, financial reports, payment-supporting documentation and budget-monitoring summaries. • Coordinate with project staff in the preparation and review of expenditure reports and support monitoring of expenditures to help ensure that spending remains within authorized levels. • Support compliance with applicable United Nations and UNODC rules, regulations, financial procedures, audit requirements and internal controls. • Assist with asset management, including recording, monitoring, receipt and inspection reports, transfer or disposal documentation, and support to audit or inventory verification missions. • Support shipment, receipt and clearance of programme equipment and materials, where required, in coordination with relevant administrative, procurement and logistics units. 3.4 Field missions, stakeholder liaison and communication support • Support arrangements for field missions within Uganda, including draft itineraries, travel requests, security-clearance follow-up, accommodation coordination, transport arrangements, mission packs and post-mission documentation. • Liaise with implementing partners, Government counterparts, consultants, vendors, civil society organizations and programme participants on administrative and logistical matters, under the guidance of programme staff. • Support the preparation of background documents, presentations, briefing notes, summaries, talking points, speeches and other materials for meetings, missions and programme events. • Support the development of fact sheets, newsletters, human-interest notes, reports and other communication materials highlighting CPCJ results and the work of UNODC in Uganda. • Compile draft content for social media and visibility products, ensuring that content is accurate, cleared through appropriate channels and aligned with donor and UNODC visibility requirements. • Contribute to the development of co-funding proposals, concept notes and donor-reporting inputs by compiling background information, data, results, activity updates and partner inputs

Background of the assignment As the global guardian of the United Nations Standards and Norms in Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice, UNODC is mandated to support Member States in upholding the rule of law and promoting effective, fair, humane and accountable criminal justice systems in line with international standards and relevant legal instruments. UNODC in Uganda is implementing the Strengthening Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice in Uganda (CPCJ) programme, with financial support from the Government of the Netherlands. The programme aims to increase the scope and coverage of ongoing UNODC support to Uganda’s criminal justice system, improve business processes, create an enabling environment for equitable access to justice, and strengthen national responses to organized crime. The CPCJ programme provides technical assistance and advisory services to Access to Justice institutions and supports the strengthening of criminal justice systems in accordance with international human rights standards and norms. The programme also supports a range of initiatives to improve the quality, effectiveness and efficiency of the criminal justice process, including strengthening oversight, accountability and integrity; promoting alternatives to imprisonment and prison decongestion; supporting offender rehabilitation and prevention of recidivism; and improving access to justice and legal empowerment for vulnerable groups. The programme also strengthens national capacities to prevent and respond to organized crime a related threat. The programme is implemented in close collaboration with Government institutions and other justice-sector stakeholders, including the Judiciary, Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, Uganda Police Force, Uganda Prisons Service, Ministry of Internal Affairs, Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, Judicial Training Institute, Financial Intelligence Authority, Uganda Human Rights Commission, Law Development Centre, Uganda Law Society, Justice and Constitutional Unit, civil society organizations and other relevant national partners. 2. The Individual Contractor will support activity planning and implementation, procurement and logistics processes, research and documentation, financial and compliance follow-up, stakeholder coordination, communication and visibility outputs, and the preparation of reports, concept notes, briefing materials and project proposals.
