vacancies.postingTitle: NATIONAL CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT THE  TECHNOLOGY NEEDS ASSESSMENT (TNA) IN ZAMBIA
vacancies.jobTitle: NATIONAL CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT THE  TECHNOLOGY NEEDS ASSESSMENT (TNA) IN ZAMBIA
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
The consultancy will also include the following activities: • Facilitating stakeholder engagements/workshops. • Supporting participatory assessment processes to collect qualitative and quantitative data, including surveys, focus group meetings and interviews. • Collecting, organising, and synthesising relevant information into short analytical inputs. • Carrying out high-quality research and producing supporting knowledge inputs. • Supporting project planning and reporting arrangements, including working in professional teams.
Work Location
Zambia
Expected duration
9 months
Duties and Responsibilities
Science, technology, and innovation (STI) are key instruments for the socio-economic transformation of the Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and their sustainable development. For the purposes of this study, technology refers to hardware, technical know-how, technical skills, and software applied to solve development-related challenges. LDCs suffer from deficits in their Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) capacities, absorptive as well as adaptive capacities, and lag substantially behind both emerging and advanced economies. The importance of STI is recognised both in the Doha Programme of Action for the LDCs for the Decade 2022-2031 (DPoA) as well as the Decade of Action for the SDGs. The DPoA highlights the importance of using STI to address multiple vulnerabilities and achieve the SDGs, making this a central priority for sustainable and lasting graduation of LDCs. It calls for renewed and stronger partnerships between LDCs and their development partners, including governments, the private sector, and civil society. The DPoA also recognises the UN Technology Bank for Least Developed Countries as the main focal point for LDCs in the area of STI. Since 2019, the UN Technology Bank has been conducting Technology Needs Assessments (TNAs) in LDCs. The primary purpose of the TNA is to identify the technologies and technical know-how that the LDCs need to address key development challenges and, in the long term, assist them to develop the technological and innovative capabilities required to achieve growth, promote structural transformation, and attain the SDGs. It is in this context that the UN Technology Bank has been requested by the Government of Zambia to undertake a new generation Technology Needs Assessment, in close partnership with the Ministry of Technology and Science (MoTS) as the national focal institution and under the guidance of an inter-sectoral TNA Steering Committee. The project aims to strengthen the capacities of LDCs to harness the potential of science, technology, and innovation in line with their national development goals. Zambia has been classified as a Least Developed Country (LDC) since 1991 and is working towards graduation from the category, supported by efforts to strengthen productive capacities, diversify the economy and enhance human capital. Zambia’s long-term development vision, Vision 2030, aims to transform the country from a predominantly agrarian economy into a prosperous middle-income country driven by knowledge, innovation and value addition. Science, technology and innovation (STI) play a central role in this transformation, and addressing remaining gaps in innovation capabilities, technology adoption and knowledge-intensive production through the targeted and strategic use of STI will be critical to sustaining Zambia’s development gains and advancing its ambition for inclusive, resilient and innovation-led growth. The Government of Zambia, through the Ministry of Technology and Science, leads the TNA as a nationally owned and stakeholder-validated process. The timing is opportune: the preparation of the Ninth National Development Plan (9NDP) offers a chance to anchor the TNA’s findings and recommendations in national planning, budgeting and implementation. Zambia’s Eighth National Development Plan (2022–2026), the forthcoming Ninth National Development Plan and other national strategies will inform the identification of sectors, sub-sectors, economic activities, STI entry points and technology needs for the TNA. The priority sectors will be confirmed through consultations with the Government of Zambia and validated through the agreed TNA governance arrangements. Following Government validation of the priority sectors and confirmation of the TNA work plan, one or more rostered consultants may be invited to participate in a final selection and recruitment process, subject to applicable procedures and availability of funds. Purpose and Scope of Assignment In general, the challenges facing LDCs are numerous, and they cut across sectors and income levels. Thus, in principle, LDCs need different types of technologies, both hard and soft, to tackle immediate challenges and accelerate the development process. However, access to the diverse range of technologies they need is neither easy nor feasible — partly because of the high cost of acquiring technologies and partly because LDCs have low absorptive capacity, which limits their ability to absorb, learn, assimilate, and upgrade acquired technologies. This makes TNA a useful tool for pinpointing specific areas where appropriate and relevant technological solutions can be used to help LDCs overcome obstacles to development. The TNA will rely on a wide conceptualisation of technology, understood as the systematic knowledge and skills used in the process of production or service delivery. This knowledge can be embodied in products or processes. From the UN Technology Bank’s perspective, TNAs are policy tools designed to serve the following purposes: 1. Identify the specific sectors, sub-sectors or economic activities in LDCs that require technological input solutions and assess the level of technological development in each of them. 2. Ensure that the technological solutions identified are appropriate and compatible with LDCs’ level of development and aligned with their national development strategies. 3. Appraise the absorptive capacities of LDCs by reviewing the STI ecosystem, particularly the skills base, technology policy, and the institutional and regulatory environment governing the national innovation system (NIS). The rationale for appraising local absorptive capacities is to gauge the ability of the country to utilise and learn from transferred technologies and absorb and assimilate technology locally through adaptation and upgrading. 4. Consult with key national stakeholders, particularly the private sector, to determine technological needs from a wider perspective. 5. Recommend technological solutions and the specific sectors and sub-sectors where private and public investment and STI-related capacity building are needed and could enable LDCs to address immediate development challenges and narrow the technological gap with more developed economies. The overarching goal of the national consultancy is to support the preparation of the Zambia TNA by facilitating country-level data collection, stakeholder consultations, validation processes and short analytical inputs to inform the assessment. The National Consultant will support analysis of the sectors and thematic areas subsequently confirmed by the Government and the TNA governance arrangements. Until those areas are confirmed, the consultant may be considered for the roster on the basis of relevant expertise, networks and demonstrated ability to contribute across one or more potential sectors or thematic areas. The International Consultant remains responsible for the overall methodology, analytical coherence and drafting of the TNA report. In conducting the assignment, the National Consultant is expected to: • support the collection and organisation of relevant national, sectoral and sub-sectoral information within the sectors, sub-sectors and thematic areas confirmed for the TNA, and, where applicable, in the area subsequently assigned to the consultant and its related value chains, including policies, strategies, statistical data, studies, investment information, evidence on technology adoption and other relevant documentation; • liaise with relevant government institutions, statistical agencies, sector ministries, research institutions, private sector actors, and other data holders to identify, collect, compile and validate available sectoral, sub-sectoral and productivity-related information; • support stakeholder consultations to validate findings, identify technology needs, assess barriers to technology adoption and gather information on implementation conditions, investment drivers and constraints; and • prepare short input reports and supporting documentation to inform the TNA chapters prepared by the International Consultant. Additionally, the National Consultant will support the identification of opportunities to leverage public and private investment to support Zambia’s development through technology. This will include collecting relevant information on existing investment flows, potential private sector engagement, public-private partnerships, investment drivers and constraints, and opportunities for technology adoption and value-chain upgrading, in the sector, sub-sector or thematic area subsequently assigned to the consultant, where applicable. Under the supervision of the UN Technology Bank for LDCs, the National Consultant will work closely with Zambia’s Ministry of Technology and Science (MoTS) and the International Consultant to undertake the following tasks: 1. Support country-level data collection and stakeholder consultations to inform the analysis of Zambia’s development context, sectors, sub-sectors, economic activities and STI entry points identified for the TNA, with attention to the area subsequently assigned to the consultant, where applicable. 2. Liaise and follow up with national counterparts, including government institutions, statistical agencies, sector ministries, research institutions, private sector actors and other data holders, to obtain relevant sectoral, sub-sectoral and productivity-related information. 3. Collect, compile and organise available productivity-related information and related evidence, and document data sources, gaps and limitations where information is incomplete, dispersed or unavailable. 4. Facilitate in-country participatory processes, including interviews, focus group discussions, workshops and surveys, to support the collection of qualitative and quantitative information required for the TNA. 5. Support stakeholder consultations to identify relevant technologies and technical know-how capable of addressing sectoral development challenges and supporting sustainable structural transformation, considering existing STI initiatives and indigenous or locally developed technologies where relevant. 6. Collect stakeholder inputs on how relevant technologies can be implemented and scaled up within the national context, considering existing capacities, institutional arrangements, market conditions and investment considerations. 7. Collect and synthesise information on barriers and challenges hindering the acquisition, deployment, diffusion and scale-up of relevant technologies, including policy, regulatory, institutional, financing, skills, capacity, infrastructure, market and investment-related constraints. 8. Support the integration of cross-cutting considerations, including trade and export diversification, reduction of import dependence, gender equality, social inclusion, environmental sustainability and climate-related considerations, where relevant to the TNA analysis. 9. Liaise closely with the UN Technology Bank, Zambia’s Ministry of Technology and Science (MoTS) and the International Consultant to coordinate data collection, stakeholder consultations, validation processes and inputs to the TNA report.
Qualifications/special skills
- An advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Economics, Business Administration, International Development and Trade, Science, Technology and Innovation Policy or related areas is required. A first-level university degree in similar fields, in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree - At least three (3) years of relevant working experience in international development, trade, science, technology and innovation, or in one or more sectors relevant to Zambia’s development agenda and potential TNA priorities is required. - Experience in qualitative and quantitative research methods, data collection, and data analysis techniques is required. - Knowledge of technologies and key issues/policies in science, technology, and innovation is required. - A good understanding of the local context, including the national development agenda, science, technology and innovation policies and LDC transition strategy, as well as well-established networks in the country, is required. - Strong analytical writing and communication skills are required. - Demonstrated knowledge of one or more relevant sectors, sub-sectors or thematic areas in Zambia, including related value chains, public institutions and private sector stakeholders, is desirable. - Publications on international development-related matters are desirable. - Previous work experience with the United Nations or other international organisations is desirable.
Languages
Fluency in oral and written English is required. Knowledge of a Zambian local language is desirable.
Additional Information
The National Consultant will report directly to the UN Technology Bank and work in close collaboration with the International Consultant and Zambia’s Ministry of Technology and Science (MoTS).
No Fee

Facilitate and provide technical guidance to the UPF Technical Working Group in consolidating key achievements, challenges, lessons learned, emerging corruption risks and priority areas for strengthening anti-corruption systems and mechanisms. iii. Home-based

21 November-15 December 2026
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Background of the assignment: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) is mandated to support Member States in strengthening crime prevention, criminal justice systems, and the rule of law in line with international standards and norms. In Uganda, UNODC is implementing the project “Promoting Accountability, Integrity and Transparency in Justice”, with the support of the Austrian Development Agency (ADA), aimed at enhancing institutional accountability, integrity, and effectiveness across the justice and anti-corruption landscape. As part of the project, UNODC is supporting the Uganda Police Force (UPF) to strengthen its institutional framework for preventing and responding to corruption. The UPF implemented its Anti-Corruption Strategy (2017-2022), which provided a framework for strengthening integrity and accountability and addressing corruption risks within the institution. Building on the achievements, challenges and lessons learned from its implementation, UPF is developing a successor Anti-Corruption Strategy (2026-2031) that responds to emerging corruption risks and institutional priorities. To inform the development of the successor strategy, UPF will undertake an internal review through a Technical Working Group comprising 12 UPF technical personnel, followed by regional consultations to obtain perspectives and recommendations from relevant stakeholders. The findings from the internal review, end-term evaluation of the previous strategy and regional consultations will provide the evidence base for the subsequent strategy development process. Within this context, UNODC seeks to engage a national consultant to support UPF in consolidating and analysing the available evidence and stakeholder inputs and facilitating the development and finalisation of the UPF Anti-Corruption Strategy (2026-2031). The successor strategy is expected to be evidence-based and forward-looking, with clear priorities, interventions, targets and implementation arrangements, supported by a costed implementation framework and monitoring and evaluation plan, and aligned with relevant national anti-corruption frameworks, human rights, gender equality and good governance principles. 2. Purpose of the assignment: The purpose of this assignment is to support the Uganda Police Force (UPF) in the development and finalisation of its successor Anti-Corruption Strategy (2026-2031), building on the end-term evaluation of the previous Anti-Corruption Strategy (2017-2022), the internal review undertaken by the UPF Technical Working Group, and findings and recommendations from the regional consultations. The consultant will review and consolidate the available evidence to identify key achievements, challenges and lessons learned from implementation of the previous strategy, assess the adequacy of existing anti-corruption systems and mechanisms, and identify emerging corruption risks and institutional priorities that should be addressed in the successor strategy. The assignment will facilitate a consultative and evidence-based strategy development process, translating the findings from the preceding reviews and consultations into clear strategic priorities, objectives, interventions, targets and implementation arrangements. The process will also ensure that relevant considerations relating to institutional integrity, accountability, human rights, gender equality and good governance are appropriately integrated into the successor strategy. The assignment will result in a comprehensive and forward-looking UPF Anti-Corruption Strategy (2026-2031), supported by a costed implementation framework and monitoring and evaluation plan to guide implementation, performance measurement, learning and accountability throughout the strategy period. Costed implementation framework and monitoring and evaluation framework developed, including priority actions, responsibilities, timelines, resource requirements, indicators and targets. 5. Validation of the draft strategy conducted with UPF, UNODC and relevant stakeholders, and feedback documented and incorporated into the strategy. 6. Final UPF Anti-Corruption Strategy (2026-2031) submitted, incorporating stakeholder feedback and accompanied by the final costed implementation and monitoring and evaluation frameworks.

Result of Service
The consultancy will also include the following activities, undertaken in coordination with the national consultant(s): ● Institutional and capacity assessments in what relates to Science, Technology, and Innovation in the country. ● Participate in stakeholder engagements/workshops facilitated by the national consultant. ● Oversee, in close consultation with the national consultant(s), and provide quality assurance to participatory assessment processes to collect qualitative and quantitative data, including surveys, focus group meetings and interviews. ● Parsing and synthesizing large amounts of information into analytical insights ● Carrying out high-quality research and producing knowledge products. ● Developing policy and action-oriented recommendations in science, technology, and innovation. ● Project planning and reporting arrangements, including working in professional teams
Work Location
Remote
Expected duration
12 months
Duties and Responsibilities
Science, technology, and innovation (STI) are key instruments for the socio-economic transformation of the Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and their sustainable development. For the purposes of this study, technology refers to hardware, technical know-how, technical skills, and software applied to solve development-related challenges. LDCs suffer from deficits in their Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) capacities, absorptive as well as adaptive capacities, and lag substantially behind both emerging and advanced economies. The importance of STI is recognized both in the Doha Programme of Action for the LDCs for the Decade 2022-2031 (DPoA) as well as the Decade of Action for the SDGs. The DPoA highlights the importance of using STI to address multiple vulnerabilities and achieve the SDGs, making this a central priority for sustainable and lasting graduation of LDCs. It calls for renewed and stronger partnerships between LDCs and their development partners, including governments, the private sector, and civil society. The DPoA also recognizes the UN Technology Bank for Least Developed Countries as a focal point for LDCs in the area of STI. Since 2019, the UN Technology Bank has been conducting Technology Needs Assessments (TNAs) in LDCs. The primary purpose of the TNA is to identify the technologies and technical know-how that the LDCs need to address key development challenges and, in the long term, assist them to develop the technological and innovative capabilities required to achieve growth, promote structural transformation, and attain the SDGs. It is in this context that the UN Technology Bank has been requested by the Government of Zambia to undertake a Technology Needs Assessment. The TNA is implemented in close partnership with the Ministry of Technology and Science (MoTS) as the national focal institution and under the guidance of an inter-sectoral TNA Steering Committee. Zambia has been classified as a Least Developed Country (LDC) since 1991 and is working towards graduation from the category, supported by efforts to strengthen productive capacities, diversify the economy, and enhance human capital. Zambia’s long-term development vision, Vision 2030, aims to transform the country from a predominantly agrarian economy into a prosperous middle-income country driven by knowledge, innovation, and value addition. Science, technology, and innovation (STI) play a central role in this transformation, and addressing remaining gaps in innovation capabilities, technology adoption, and knowledge-intensive production through the targeted and strategic use of STI will be critical to sustaining Zambia’s development gains and advancing its ambition of inclusive, resilient, and innovation-led growth. The Government of Zambia, through the Ministry of Technology and Science, leads the TNA as a nationally owned and stakeholder-validated process. The timing is opportune: the preparation of the Ninth National Development Plan (9NDP) offers a chance to anchor the TNA’s findings and recommendations in national planning, budgeting, and implementation. Purpose and Scope of Assignment In general, the challenges facing the LDCs are numerous, and they cut across sectors and income levels. Thus, in principle, LDCs need all sorts of technologies (both hard and soft) to tackle immediate challenges and accelerate the development process. However, access to the diverse range of technologies they need is neither easy not feasible - partly because of the high cost acquiring technologies and partly because LDCs have low-level of absorptive capacities, which limit their ability to absorb, learn, assimilate, and upgrade the acquired technologies. This makes the TNA a useful tool for pinpointing specific areas where appropriate and relevant technological solutions can be used to help LDCs overcome some of the obstacles to development. The assessment intends to provide critical insights about the functioning of the national innovation system, present an overview of the existing gaps and challenges in accessing, utilizing and developing technologies, and understand how the national policy framework in the areas of STI impacts national sustainable development. The TNA will rely on a wide conceptualization of technology and look at technology as the systematic knowledge and skills used in the process of production or service delivery. This knowledge can be embodied in products or processes. The consultancy will help Zambia achieve its medium- and long-term development goals by prioritizing technologies and technical know-how that advance structural transformation, productivity, and sustainable development. The consultant will: (a) identify sectors, activities, social concerns, and environmental challenges where technology can boost value addition, competitiveness, and inclusive growth; (b) determine the technologies and know-how needed to meet development objectives in these priority areas; and (c) identify ways to mobilize public and private investment in technology-driven development. The assessment will be conducted in close coordination with national consultant(s), who will lead stakeholder consultations. Under the supervision of the UN Technology Bank, the international consultant will work closely with a national consultant(s) to undertake the following tasks: ● Analyze Zambia’s national development context and Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) ecosystem, including the functioning of the National Innovation System (NIS), policy and institutional frameworks, innovation and R&D capacities, skills base, technology absorption capacity, and ongoing STI initiatives, including indigenous technologies, with due consideration to existing national frameworks such as Zambia’s Vision 2030, the Eighth National Development Plan (8NDP, 2022–2026), the Ninth National Development Plan (9NDP) currently under preparation, and the Transformative Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) Policy and Implementation Plan (2025). ● Lead inclusive stakeholder engagement across government, academia, business, research institutions, and other relevant actors to identify high-potential sectors, subsectors, and economic activities within Zambia’s national development priorities. Assess their development trends, technology needs, and FDI implications. Use a transparent, evidence-based methodology combining development and STI indicators, qualitative analysis, and stakeholder consultations. Agree on the methodology and selection criteria with the TNA Steering Committee for validation; the Committee will then select two to three priority sectors. ● Identify and prioritize technologies using transparent weighted scoring, with criteria and weights agreed by the Technology Experts Group and validated by the TNA Steering Committee. Assess alignment with Zambia’s development goals, the SDGs, structural transformation and sustainable LDC graduation, alongside barriers to technology acquisition, deployment, diffusion and scale-up. Evaluate feasibility, including potential institutional or market adopters and a credible deployment pathway; high scores alone are insufficient without these conditions. ● Assess country readiness to adopt prioritized technologies, including policy, regulatory, financing, institutional, capacity, and skills factors. Evaluate their suitability for public and private investment by reviewing existing investment flows, potential private-sector engagement, and public-private partnerships that could drive adoption and innovation. ● Integrate cross-cutting considerations throughout the analysis, including trade and export diversification, import substitution, gender equality and inclusion, environmental sustainability, and regional and South–South cooperation opportunities. ● Develop actionable and investment-oriented recommendations to strengthen STI capabilities, address identified barriers, enhance capacity-building and skills development, and support sustainable technology transfer, adoption, and diffusion. ● Identify concrete, bankable opportunities for investment in STI areas, including technology adoption for value chain upgrading and related capacity development, that can engage the private sector, investment promotion agencies, and development partners, fostering an implementation-focused approach for technology adoption and innovation-led growth. ● Coordinate with the UN Technology Bank, MoTS as the national focal institution, the TNA Steering Committee, its Technical Working Group, and national consultants to agree on methodology, analyze findings, draft and revise chapters, incorporate feedback, and finalize a high-quality report consistent with UN Technology Bank guidance. The Working Group will coordinate and review technical work; additional experts may participate only with MoTS and Steering Committee approval.
Qualifications/special skills
- An advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Economics, International Development and Trade, Science, Technology and Innovation Policy, Innovation Studies or related areas is required. A first-level university degree in similar fields in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. - At least ten (10) years of working experience in research, international development, trade, science, technology and innovation, or related area is required. - Extensive knowledge of the innovation systems, technological learning and absorption processes and the policy and regulatory environment required for capacity building in STI is required. - Experience in qualitative and quantitative research methods, data collection, and data analysis, including gender disaggregated data analysis, techniques is required. - Strong analytical writing, communication and stakeholder-engagement skills are required. - Research and publications on international development related matters are required. - Good understanding of the development challenges facing developing countries, especially Least Developed Countries (LDCs), is desirable. - Practical experience of foreign direct investment gained through working with an investment promotion agency, industrial park, special economic zone or similar organization or experience working on foreign investment projects is desirable. - Familiarity with Zambia or the Southern African region, and prior experience with Technology Needs Assessments or comparable country-level STI assessments, is desirable.
Languages
Fluency in oral and written English is required.
Additional Information
● The international consultant will report directly to the UN Technology Bank and work in close collaboration with the national consultant(s) and the Ministry of Technology and Science. ● All reports and supporting matrices to be submitted to the UN Technology Bank in electronic form in English.
No Fee

Result of Service
The consultant will support the Coordination Desk of the One Planet Network Consumer Information Programme. The consultant will also support the Environmental Alliance of the Americas (referred to as "the Alliance"), a regional initiative of Latin American countries hosting the regional ecolabel "Sello Ambiental de América".
Work Location
Remote
Expected duration
6 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environment authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. UNEP’s Economy and Industry Division addresses environmental issues at global and regional levels, provides leadership and encourages partnership in caring for the environment by inspiring, informing and enabling nations and people to improve their quality of life without compromising that of future generations. The Industry and Economy Division also works with many partners, including Member States, national and local governments, business and industry and non-governmental organizations, to develop and implement policies, strategies and practices that are cleaner and safer, incorporate environmental costs, use natural resources efficiently, reduce pollution and risks for humans and the environment, and enable the implementation of conventions and international agreements. The 10-Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Consumption and Production (10YFP), adopted by Heads of State at the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development (Rio+20) in 2012, is a global framework for action to accelerate the shift towards Sustainable Consumption and Production (SCP) worldwide. As reflected in the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the 10YFP plays a central role in achieving the shift to SCP: its implementation is the first target of Sustainable Development Goal 12 on "Ensuring sustainable consumption and production". The 10YFP is also recognized as the Framework of reference for decoupling economic growth from environmental degradation in SDG8. The 10YFP generates impact through multi-stakeholder programmes and partnerships, which develop, replicate, and scale up SCP policies and practices at all levels and which form together the One Planet Network. UNEP was mandated by the UN General Assembly to serve as the Secretariat of the 10YFP. UNEP, serving as 10YFP Secretariat, supports the implementation of the Global Strategy for SCP (2023-2030) with a strategic focus on the key enablers for change that can help steer and shape markets, practices and behaviors, both from the supply and demand side, towards sustainable models, empowering governments, stakeholders and individuals to trigger long-term, sustainable and fair economic and social transformations across high-impact sectors and value chains. This includes partnerships and initiatives aimed at enhancing sustainability and circularity information sharing and disclosure, as well as at empowering consumers to make informed decisions based on transparent and reliable information, working in close cooperation with UNEP’s core partners through the One Planet Network Consumer Information Programme and other key initiatives. The Consumer Information Programme serves as a global platform to support the provision of quality information on goods and services, and the identification and implementation of the most effective strategies to engage consumers in sustainable consumption. The Programme is co-led by Germany through the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety, and Consumers International. The consultant will work with the 10YFP Secretariat, Materials and Systems Innovation Unit, Industry Innovation Branch, Industry and Economy Division. This post is remote. Specific tasks and responsibilities: Consumer information Programme: • Coordinate overall planning and delivery as part of Coordination Desk, including developing the Programme’s strategy aligned with the 10YFP Global Strategy for SCP (2023-2030), monitoring progress and implementation of activities and coordinating reporting activities, such as for the high-level political forum on sustainable development. • Support the mainstreaming, coordination and visibility of UNEP consumer information activities through the Consumer Information Programme, fostering alignment, knowledge sharing, coherent implementation and greater impact across UNEP's sustainable consumption and production portfolio. • Update the website content to align with current activities and endorsed initiatives of the Consumer Information Programme • Convene, organize and/or support key meetings of the Programme, including regular coordination desk meetings, Multistakeholder Advisory Committee (MAC) meetings, as well as support the Programme’s contributions to other strategic 10YFP/OPN meetings. • Ensure active involvement and accountability for delegated tasks of MAC members and partners in the implementation of the Programme’s activities, and support further stakeholder engagement across regions, including from the private sector. • Establish cooperation with other 10YFP/OPN programmes and flagship initiatives, with the objective of building synergies. • Coordinate the Programme’s contributions and inputs to key intergovernmental processes on climate, biodiversity and pollution, as relevant, and support the organization of outreach/high-level events to promote the key messages and outputs of the Programme. • Communicate on the Programme's activities, outputs and results through the bimonthly newsletter, the Programme’s dedicated website on the One Planet Network online platform and social media. • Support administrative processes. Alianza Ambiental de America : • Contribute with research analysis and technical inputs to product selection and sustainability criteria development processes under the Alliance, as needed. • Contribute to the preparation of briefing notes, presentations, and other materials to support the Alliance's activities and visibility. • Support engagement with businesses and industry associations to promote participation in Alliance activities, gather industry perspectives on sustainability criteria. • Assist with knowledge management, documentation, and reporting related to Alliance activities and outcomes. • Participate in periodic meetings with UNEP and the Alliance Secretariat to review progress and identify priorities for support.
Qualifications/special skills
Education - Advanced University Degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in relevant field. - A first-level university degree (Bachelor‘s degree) in combination with at least 2 (two) years of qualifying and relevant professional experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. - A minimum of 5 years of demonstrated professional experience in Sustainable Consumption and Production (SCP) tools is required. - At least 2 years of experience in ecolabelling is required. - At least 2 years of working experience at the international level is required. - Working experience in Latin America and the Caribbean region is required. - Experience working for UNEP, the UN system, or an international organization would be an asset.
Languages
Language - Fluency in oral and written Spanish and English is required. - Knowledge of other official languages in the United Nations System is an advantage.
Additional Information
Not available.
No Fee
THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS.

Work Location
Bangkok, Thailand
Expected duration
4-6 months
Duties and Responsibilities
Org. Setting and Reporting The Environment and Development Division, Sustainable Urban Development Section, is seeking 1-3 interns for a minimum period of four months (preferably six months, which is the maximum duration for internships). The internship is UNPAID and full-time in-person. Interns work five days per week (35 hours) under the supervision of a staff member in the department or office to which they are assigned. The Sustainable Urban Development Section works with ESCAP member States and key stakeholders to advance resilient and sustainable urban development across Asia and the Pacific. Its programme of work focuses on: (i) facilitating intergovernmental processes to strengthen regional cooperation and the implementation of global and regional frameworks; (ii) providing technical assistance and supporting capacity development; (iii) developing and disseminating knowledge products that enhance awareness and support evidence-based decision-making; and (iv) facilitating networking and partnerships to mobilize knowledge, resources, and innovation. Daily responsibilities will depend on the individual's background, the assigned team within the section and the internship period. Duties may include, but are not limited to: 1. Provide support to organizing and conducting meetings (Expert Group Meetings, Side-Events and Ninth Asia Pacific Urban Forum etc.) relevant to the work of the Section, including drafting of concept notes, documents and communications materials, preparing for and backstopping intergovernmental meetings, and supporting follow-up activities (30%) 2. Assist with various tasks linked to organizational and substantive dimensions of programme and project implementation on sustainable and resilience urban development, including work on SDG localization, urban resilience, sinking cities, smart cities, equitable sanitation for low-income urban communities etc. (30%) 3. Conduct research and identify and develop case studies on urban development, policies and programmes and their contribution to inclusive, sustainable and resilient development in the Asia-Pacific region (20%) 4. Support day-to-day operational tasks of the Section, including responding to requests for information, assisting in the preparation of presentations, and updating webpages related to the Section’s work. (20%)
Qualifications/special skills
To qualify for an internship with the United Nations Internship Programme, applicants must, at the time of application, meet one of the following requirements: (a) Be enrolled in, or have completed, a graduate school programme (second university degree or equivalent, or higher related to international development, sustainable development, urban planning, urban development, policy analysis, environmental management, social science, development practice, international relations, or related disciplines; or (b) Be enrolled in, or have completed, the final academic year of a first university degree programme (minimum bachelor's level or equivalent related to sustainable development, urban planning, urban development, environmental management, development practice, international relations, or related disciplines. Special skills (a) Good command of Microsoft Suite beyond Word, Excel and PowerPoint is desirable. (b) Video-editing skills are desirable. (c) Graphic design or illustration skills related to urban design work are desirable. Familiarity with the responsible use of AI tools to improve work quality and efficiency, in line with UN guidelines, is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. Fluency in spoken and written English is required for the Internship Programme. Knowledge of another language used in Asia-Pacific is an asset (Laotian, Khmer, Bengali, Nepali, Japanese).
Additional Information
Not available.
Intern Specific text
Interns are not financially remunerated by the United Nations. Costs and arrangements for travel, visas, accommodation and living expenses are the responsibility of interns or their sponsoring institutions. Interns who are not citizens or permanent residents of the country where the internship is undertaken, may be required to obtain the appropriate visa and work/employment authorization. Successful candidates should discuss their specific visa requirements before accepting the internship offer.

Org. Setting and Reporting
UNRWA is a United Nations agency established by the General Assembly in 1949 and is mandated to provide assistance and protection to a population of some 5.8 million registered Palestine refugees. Its mission is to help Palestine refugees in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, West Bank and the Gaza Strip to achieve their full potential in human development, pending a just solution to their plight. UNRWA’s services encompass education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure and improvement, microfinance, and emergency assistance. UNRWA is the largest UN operation in the Middle East with more than 30,000 staff. UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions. If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to make a tangible difference for one of the most vulnerable communities in the world, UNRWA would like to hear from you. Supervisor: The incumbent is responsible to the Chief, Construction Management Division (CCMD).
Responsibilities
• Reviews the Bills of Quantities for construction projects, compares with architectural, structural, mechanical, and electrical design drawings; identifies discrepancies and recommends amendments or modifications ; follows up corrective actions and provides advise for their clearance as needed; • Conducts analysis for construction items and advises Chief, Construction Management Division (CCMD) on cost effectiveness and contractual matters including proposing new construction materials used in the industry; • Reviews the architectural, structural, mechanical, and electrical drawings, as appliable and prepared at HQA; prepares bills of quantities, non-standard specifications, particular conditions, and other tender documentation utilizing specialized software; • Serves as a member of project management team responsible for costing and contract aspects; • As advised by supervisor, carries out random technical monitoring of measurements, construction site reports, tests and final accounts for construction projects; • Provides technical advice related to maintenance of the Agency's premises at HQ (Amman); • Maintains standard forms, specifications, cost information and data; makes recommendations on update and improvement; • Performs other duties as may be assigned by the supervisor.
Competencies
UN Core Values of Integrity, Professionalism and Respect for Diversity, and Core Competencies of Communication, Working with People and Drive for Results apply by default. • Creating and Innovating • Deciding and Initiating Action • Analyzing • Coping with Pressure and Setbacks • Applying Technical Expertise • Continuous updating of his/her knowledge in methods of construction and materials in the Middle East; • Excellent technical English writing skills (descriptive side);
Education
• University degree from an accredited educational institution in civil engineering.
Job - Specific Qualification
• Formal training in computer applications related to quantity surveying is required.
Work Experience
Indicate your current involvement in any outside activities, as it is required. Including but not limited to employment, independent contractor/freelance consultant, board member (corporate, academic, etc), expert group, lobby, public speaking/writing (article, book, blog, social media etc), teaching, conferences, training, press statement, voluntary work, political activity, fundraising/donation for non-UNRWA entity, running for public office, role in political party or orgs, owning business, work for gov./NGO/private company/charity, UNRWA partner/vendor, full/part-time, paid or not. A “yes” answer doesn’t necessarily lead to exclusion from future work at UNRWA, yet misrepresentation in providing accurate/complete info can lead to disqualification/termination of appointment, if hired. • You are required to have at least four years of progressively responsible and relevant work experience in the preparation of bills of quantities, cost estimates and tender documentation for projects. • You are required to have experience in utilizing Quantity Surveying software (billing, estimating, cost control, cash flow, etc.) and other standard computer applications. • You are required to have a university degree from an accredited educational institution in civil engineering. • Good command of written and spoken English and Arabic is required. • Do you currently hold a contract of 1 year or more with UNRWA? If yes, please confirm whether you have completed your mandatory probation period is required. • Are you currently residing in Duty Station. It is required that you specify your current location.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. Arabic is required. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult https://languages.un.org for details).

Assessment
During the assessment, the applications will be given preference based on the following desirable qualifications: • Experience in low-cost construction similar to that undertaken by UNRWA. • Knowledge of market prices related to his/her line of work in the Middle East; • Provided very good understanding of the context of Palestine refugees and UNRWA operations. The shortlisted candidates will be afterward evaluated based on: • Technical Test • Competency-based Interview Candidates who meet the post requirements and the required language level will be considered for the ongoing competitive process. To ensure alignment with the UN language levels, please refer to the guidance below: Level I: Basic knowledge. Level II: Good to very good command. Level III: Excellent language skills. Level IV: Expert level or native proficiency.
Special Notice
Providing incorrect, incomplete or misleading information on an application form will result in the immediate disqualification of the candidate. Contract Type: Fixed Term Appointment for 1 year; 1 year probation period, with the possibility of further extension, subject to the availability of funds, satisfactory performance, and continuing need. Grade and Salary: Grade 14 Monthly basic salary JD 919.800 fils. Special Occupational Allowance (SoA) 60% of basic salary. The salary may be subject to a reduced work schedule. Other benefits: Other benefits include monthly Provident Fund contribution (15.4% of basic salary paid by the Agency), compulsory medical insurance, 30 days of annual leave, and dependency allowance (if applicable). Additional benefits: -2 days of sick leave for each completed month of service. -14 weeks of Maternity Leave. -2 weeks paternity leave. Department/Office: UNRWA - Programme Infrastructure/Engineering - Construction Management Duty Station: Headquarters Amman Equivalency: Equivalency may apply for this post. • Candidates with a combination of additional relevant academic qualifications and/or additional years of progressive work experience may also be considered on equivalency. NB: Work experience alone or formal qualifications with no relevant work experience are not considered an acceptable combination. General Information: • This vacancy notice is open to internal candidates only. Only candidates residing in Jordan, and within commuting distance of the duty station with authorization to work in the duty station at the time of application are eligible to apply. • The Agency will not assume responsibility or accountability to support or facilitate the issuance of work permit in Jordan, and without a valid work permit, the appointment may be rescinded. • Since the Vacancy is an Area Staff post, the Agency will not provide coverage for relocation costs. • Preference will be given to registered Palestine refugees and candidates assisting the Agency to meet its commitment to gender parity. To do so applicants should select under "Category" RLG, scroll down to see all categories, then select their local grade. • Please find below the link to a video that guides applicants on how to apply to Job Openings: https: //drive.google.com/file/d/1MH-IYA6Y8kxA1fgao5qyTV8VwNajgx4u/view?usp=sharing • Advertisements published only in English will only accept applications in English, and Arabic submissions will not be considered. • UNRWA has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNRWA, including sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), sexual harassment, racism/racial discrimination and other forms of conduct, including but not limited to discrimination, abuse of authority and harassment. To uphold these standards, background checks are conducted for all recommended candidates and those placed on a roster to help ensure that individuals with a history of such conduct are not hired. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s), employment history, ClearCheck and INTERPOL, as well as certification of non-conviction, where available. By applying for a position with UNRWA, candidates acknowledge and consent to these verification processes. • The Agency may disqualify applicants whose name appears on the UN Sanctions List or a UN database of staff separated for reason of misconduct or of staff who separated whilst misconduct processes were pending. • UNRWA shares investigation and misconduct information with other UN Agencies, and past and prospective employers about staff members who have been separated for misconduct, or who have separated while an investigation and/or disciplinary process for misconduct was underway; and those individuals may be prohibited from employment with the United Nations. • The Agency will immediately disqualify applicants who are ineligible for any reason in accordance with the Agency regulatory framework. • UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions from UN member states, regional bodies, business foundations and individual contributions. The mission of UNRWA is to help Palestinerefugees achieve their full potential in human development under the difficult circumstances in which they live. • For more details on UNRWA, please visit: https://www.unrwa.org • Applications from UNRWA staff member who had been demoted with deferred eligibility for promotion will not be considered. • Applications from Staff members who were recipients under the Early Voluntary Retirement or Exceptional Voluntary Separation Schemes will not be considered. • Applications from Internal candidates serving for less than one year in their current post will not be considered. • The Agency reserves the right not to make an appointment, to make an appointment at a lower grade, or to make an appointment with a modified job description or to change the contract Modality. • A candidate is not eligible for consideration if he or she was short-listed and found not suitable for the same post within the previous 12 months unless the post description has since been altered by 30% or more, as determined by ODCS. • UNRWA reserves the right to proceed only with internal candidates or proceed with the candidates of an under-represented gender for any vacancy announcement when it determines that the short-list for a single post at any grade level is excessively long.
United Nations Considerations
Staff members are subject to the authority of the Commissioner-General of UNRWA and to assignment by him or her. UNRWA is committed to achieving gender parity at all levels of staffing under the current UN-wide gender agenda and strongly encourages applications from qualified applicants from under-represented groups. At UNRWA, the paramount consideration in the recruitment and employment of staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, with due regard to geographic diversity. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. UNRWA is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. Reasonable accommodation for applicants with disabilities may be provided to support participation in the recruitment process when requested and indicated in the application. UNRWA Considerations UNRWA staff are expected to uphold the highest standards of efficiency, competence, neutrality, impartiality and integrity. This includes respect for and commitment to human rights, diversity and non-violent means of dealing with all kinds of conflict. Only persons who fully and unconditionally commit to these values should consider applying for UNRWA jobs. Candidates will not be considered for employment with UNRWA if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. Candidates who have committed crimes other than minor traffic offences may not be considered for employment. The Agency may disqualify applicants who have separated for reason of misconduct, who left a UN Agency while misconduct processes were pending, or who appear on the UN Sanctions List. Result of Service
The consultant contributes to the successful implementation and expansion of the City Resilience Global Programme by providing high-quality technical expertise, analytical support, capacity-building services, and programme development assistance to partner cities, territories, and institutions. The consultant supports the achievement of UN-Habitat's objective of fostering inclusive, sustainable, climate-resilient, and risk-informed urban and territorial development by strengthening the capacity of public institutions, communities, and key stakeholders to understand risks, make informed decisions, mobilize resources, and implement integrated resilience and climate adaptation actions. The expected outcome is enhanced technical expertise and analytical support to the implementation, development, and expansion of the Programme, contributing to urban and territorial resilience, climate adaptation, risk-informed development, and capacity-building initiatives across partner cities, regions, and institutions.
Work Location
Homebase
Expected duration
6 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is the United Nations agency mandated by the General Assembly to promote socially, economically, and environmentally sustainable towns and cities. UN-Habitat works with national and local governments, civil society, academia, development partners, and the private sector to advance sustainable urbanization and improve the quality of life in human settlements worldwide. As the lead UN agency for sustainable urban development and human settlements, UN-Habitat plays a key role in supporting countries and local authorities to address increasing urban challenges, including climate change, disaster risk, environmental degradation, rapid urbanization, inequality, and vulnerability to shocks and stresses. Through its urban resilience programming, UN-Habitat promotes integrated, people-centered, and systems-based approaches that strengthen the capacity of cities and territories to anticipate, absorb, adapt, and transform in the face of current and future challenges. UN-Habitat's resilience work builds on global frameworks including the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the New Urban Agenda, the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030, and the Paris Agreement on Climate Change, supporting local and regional governments in translating these commitments into effective action at territorial level. Recognizing that resilience challenges extend beyond administrative boundaries, UN-Habitat supports multi-level governance approaches that strengthen coordination among cities, metropolitan areas, regions, and national institutions. Its resilience interventions combine risk-informed planning, climate adaptation, disaster risk reduction, urban regeneration, nature-based solutions, governance strengthening, and inclusive stakeholder engagement to support sustainable territorial development. The programme works closely with local and regional governments, public institutions, civil society organizations, community groups, academia, and development partners to design and implement resilience-building initiatives. Attention is given to vulnerable populations, including women, youth, older persons, displaced populations, and other groups disproportionately affected by climate change, disasters, and socio-economic shocks. Under the direct supervision of the Head of the City Resilience Global Programme (CRGP), the consultant will provide technical expertise and analytical support for the enhancement, deployment, and scaling of the City Resilience Profiling Interactive Tool (CRPiT), including the development of advanced analytical functionalities, support to the NewMed2030 programme, and capacity-building activities. Task 1: Provide Technical Support to enhance the CRPiT Platform: • Improve the functionality, usability, performance and scalability of the City Resilience Profiling Interactive Tool (CRPiT), considering user feedback and programme requirements. • Support in strengthening the integration of geospatial data, resilience indicators, interactive visualizations and downloadable outputs. • Together with the technical team to ensure the timely delivery, testing and deployment of agreed technical outputs. . Task 2: Provide Technical Support for development of Advanced Analytical Functionalities: • Develop functionalities to compare the resilience profile of the same city or territory across different periods of time. • Develop and test pilot Artificial Intelligence-assisted capabilities to support the preliminary interpretation of resilience indicators, trends, strengths and vulnerabilities. All AI-assisted outputs shall be clearly identified as preliminary and subject to human validation before deployment. Support the development and dissemination of guidance materials, toolkits, case studies, and knowledge products related to resilience-building. Task 3: Support Adaptation of CRPiT to NewMed2030 Requirements and Global Replicability: • Adapt and configurate CRPiT modules according to the methodological, territorial and data requirements of the NewMed2030 programme, including modifications to indicator sets, workflows and visualization configurations, while ensuring replicability across other CRGP implementations. • Support the development of multilingual and translation functionalities to facilitate the use of CRPiT across different regional and linguistic contexts. • Contribute to the design and validation of a globally adaptable CRPiT configuration that can be replicated in different urban and regional contexts. Task 4: Support Generation, Validation and Replication of Resilience Profiles: • Generate the initial resilience profiles for the eight participating NewMed2030 localities to support local participatory validation processes. • Incorporate technical feedback, validation results and supplementary datasets arising from stakeholder consultations. • Generate additional resilience profiles in other urban and regional contexts, as agreed with CRGP, to assess the applicability, comparability and replicability of the enhanced CRPiT module. • Ensure that all resilience profiles are developed following established methodological and quality assurance standards. Task 5: Testing, Deployment and Documentation: • Conduct technical testing, troubleshooting and quality assurance of the platform and its analytical functionalities. • Support deployment of the agreed functional version and develop necessary technical and user documentation • Provide training to the team in the use, administration, updating and basic maintenance of the tool. • Ensure appropriate knowledge transfer to the CRGP technical team.
Qualifications/special skills
- Advanced university degree or equivalent professional qualification in urban and regional planning, urban studies, urban geography, development studies, or public policy for the consultancy with knowledge of Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field is required. - A 1st level university degree with two qualified years of experience will be accepted in lieu of the advance degree. A minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible professional experience in urban planning, urban and territorial resilience, GIS, software development, geospatial data engineering or related fields is required. At least two (2) years of specialized experience developing interactive, data-driven web applications or Web GIS platforms is required. Experience developing and maintaining automated geospatial data-processing workflows using Python is required. Experience integrating front-end applications with back-end services, APIs and SQL-based data structures is required. - Practical experience with web technologies, geospatial processing tools, mapping libraries and version-control systems relevant to the CRPiT technology stack is required. Experience processing and visualizing vector, raster, statistical and time-series data is desirable. Experience supporting local governments, international organizations or development programmes is desirable Experience with data analysis, visualization, and reporting tools is desirable Experience in the Mediterranean or MENA region, particularly Lebanon or Morocco, is an asset. Ability to work independently and manage multiple assignments under tight deadlines is desirable Ability to work effectively in multicultural and multidisciplinary teams is desirable Commitment to gender equality, inclusion, and the empowerment of vulnerable and marginalized groups is desirable Commitment to the principles and values of the United Nations is desirable
Languages
- Fluency in spoken and written English is required. - Knowledge of other UN languages would be an additional asset. - Knowledge of French and/or Arabic is desirable.
Additional Information
Not available.

Duties and Responsibilities
This internship is expected to start on 11 January 2027, and is located in the Office of the Director, Human Rights Council and Treaty Mechanisms Division (CTMD), namely its Civil Society Team which is responsible for the civil society's engagement with the United Nations human rights mechanisms. The Office of the United Nations (UN) High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) is the Secretariat department responsible for strengthening international human rights mechanisms; enhancing equality and countering discrimination; combating impunity and strengthening accountability and the rule of law; integrating human rights in development and in the economic sphere; widening the democratic space; and early warning and protection of human rights in situations of conflict, violence and insecurity. Consisting of three branches, the Human Rights Council and Treaty Mechanisms Division has a core mandate to support the Human Rights Council (HRC) and its mechanisms, as well as the ten human rights treaty bodies and the administration of a number of Voluntary Trust Funds. Based in Geneva, Switzerland, under the overall direction of the Special Assistant to the Director of Division the intern reports to the Human Rights Officer in the assigned work team. This assignment shall be offered for an initial period of three (3) months, possibly renewable for a combined period of six (6) months, upon further approval by the supervisor. At the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the recruitment and employment of staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, with due regard to geographic diversity. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. The United Nations is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. The United Nations recruits and employs staff regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, religious, cultural and ethnic backgrounds or disabilities. Reasonable accommodation for applicants with disabilities may be provided to support participation in the recruitment process when requested and indicated in the application. This internship is an UNPAID and full-time engagement that provides a framework through which individuals from diverse academic backgrounds gain exposure to the work of the United Nations by way of their service within Secretariat entities. Applicants should have a demonstrated keen interest in the work of the United Nations with a personal commitment to the ideals of the Charter, and have the demonstrated ability to successfully interact with individuals of different cultural backgrounds and beliefs - which includes willingness to understand and be tolerant of differing opinions and views. RESPONSIBILITIES: The intern shall support OHCHR in fulfilling its mission: to work for the protection of all human rights for all people; to help empower people to realize their rights; and to assist those responsible for upholding such rights in ensuring that they are implemented. Daily responsibilities of the intern in the Civil Society Team, Office of the Director of the Human Rights Council and Treaty Mechanisms Division may include but are not limited to: assisting in supporting the work of the Human Rights Council, its subsidiary bodies and Treaty Bodies and civil society's engagement with them; assisting in facilitating the organization of non-governmental organizations (NGO) related meetings in the context of the Human Rights Council and Universal Periodic Review Working Group sessions and other meetings, as appropriate; assisting with the review of NGO written statements submitted at the Human Rights Council, preparing notes and statistics, keeping track and compiling information on the engagement with human rights mechanisms; maintaining relevant database and webpages; drafting correspondence, conducting a variety of research, collecting and disseminating, as appropriate, information pertaining to the Division; contributing to outreach and human rights mainstreaming initiatives; attending to queries/ requests from the Director, the Branch Chiefs and stakeholders; facilitating internal exchange of information and practices as well as coordination on relevant human rights mechanisms and with the other parts of the Office and the United Nations (UN); assisting in the dissemination of information about the work of human rights mechanisms; undertaking research on issues of relevance to the work of the Division; assisting with collaborative work and activities organized with other Divisions, United Nations agencies and bodies; performing other related duties as appropriate.
Qualifications/special skills
To qualify for the United Nations Secretariat internship programme, applicants must, at the time of submission, be a graduate or enrolled in a graduate school programme (i.e. Master's degree or equivalent degree, or higher) or, be a graduate or enrolled in the final academic year of a first-level university degree programme (i.e. Bachelor's degree or equivalent degree) preferably in the area of law, political science, international relations, social sciences or a related field, OR have graduated with a university degree as defined above and, if selected, must commence the internship on the date specified in the Acceptance letter. However, a field of study that is closely related to the type of internship that you are applying for is required. Please explain how you meet this criterion using examples. Do you meet any of the above criteria? If yes, please indicate which one and attach proof to the application. Please note that you will have to provide an official certificate at a later stage. Please explain how you meet this criterion using examples.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this internship fluency in English or French is required, knowledge of the other is desirable. Knowledge of another United Nations official language would be an advantage (i.e. Arabic, Chinese, Russian or Spanish).
