Org. Setting and Reporting
The position is located within the United Nations Support Office in Haiti (UNSOH). Pursuant to Security Council resolution 2793 (2025), UNSOH has been mandated to provide support; primarily to the Gang Suppression Force (GSF), the United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH), the Haitian National Police (HNP), and the Haitian Armed Forces in the context of any joint operations with the GSF. Additionally, UNSOH is tasked with delivering technical assistance to the Organization of American States (OAS). This position is located in the Human Resources Section in Port-au-Prince. Port-au-Prince is classified in the "E" category and as a non-family duty station. The incumbent will report to the Chief Human Resources Officer P-5.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Human Resources Officer will be responsible for the following duties: Recruitment and Staff Selection: • Manages recruitment processes including coordinating with client offices in forecasting and identifying vacancies, preparing job openings, reviewing, and screening of candidates. • Reviews job openings in consultation with hiring managers, ensuring that the evaluation criteria and responsibilities are in line with the approved or classified documents. • Conducts preliminary review, prepares, and submits recruitment cases to Field Central Review Bodies (FCRB). • Arranges and conducts interviews for selection of candidates. • Reviews recommendation on the selection of candidate by client offices. • Participates in task forces and working groups identifying issues/problems, formulating policies and guidelines, and establishing new procedures on recruitment and staff selection. • Administer the recruitment of affiliate personnel such as Consultants, international Individual Contractors, Gratis personnel Staffing Table Management/Post Management: • Updates staffing table on regular basis ensuring all staffing changes are properly and accurately processed in Umoja system. • Coordinates with Budget and Finance Section in preparation of the staffing component of mission's annual budget. • Initiates, prepares, and processes posts and staff movement forms to reflect actual assignments of staff and in compliance with approved reassignment and deployment of workforce. • Reconciles staffing discrepancies and returned borrowed posts in coordination with hiring sections. • Certified requests for extension of appointment against approved and budgeted international and national posts. • Liaises with counterparts in UNHQ on post management and staffing issues including extension of posts in UMOJA. • Provide responses to legislative bodies (ACABQ and Fifth Committee) on HR related questions during budget deliberation. • Liaises with counterparts at UNHQ in reconciling the staffing levels in line with Allotment Advice and approved budget document from General Assembly. • Prepares and submits classification documents when staffing changes are proposed in the budget (established, reclassified, redeployed, reassigned, converted). HR Audit: • Provides HR related documents to Board of Auditors and Resident Auditors during audit exercise. •Prepare responses to recommendations issued by Board of Auditors and Resident Auditors. •Work closely with Risk Management and Compliance Unit and provide responses to all Audit queries related to Human Resources. Performance Management: • Supports the supervisor in the implementation of the performance appraisal system and monitors its compliance with the proper implementation of the performance management system, providing guidance and substantive support to mission components on standards for the development of service, section, unit and individual work plans. • Liaises with the Integrated Mission Training Center to organize training/orientation programmes in performance management and supervisory skills as well as work plans. • Monitors the compliance of Performance Management System and provides input to the establishment of a Management Review Committee, Joint Monitoring Committee as well as Rebuttal Panel and acts as their facilitator and ex-officio member. • Counsels staff and managers in cases of underperformance and facilitates the implementation of a Performance Improvement Plan to improve performance. Administration of Entitlements and Benefits: - Advises the CHRO on the development, modification and implementation of United Nations policies and practices on entitlements. - Receives and reviews grievances and complaints related to entitlements and benefits, assessing and evaluating merit of each case and makes recommendation for resolutions - Reviews and recommends level of remuneration for consultants. - Represents the office in joint bodies and working groups relating to salaries and other conditions of service. - Participates in the process of knowledge/awareness building amongst manager and staff members with regard to the staff rules and regulations, and related guidelines in the administration of entitlements and their strict implementation authority. - Monitors and evaluates the effectiveness of related guidelines, HR rules, regulations practices and procedures, and recommends revisions where necessary.Reporting and Data Management: •Prepares a wide range of HR related business intelligence reports and statistical reports, such as but not limited to gender and geographic distributions, TCC/PCC contributing countries, long-term vacant posts, deployment schedule, recruitment, and workforce planning, etc. •Propose and develop reporting templates based on new or ad hoc information requirements for HRS and the Mission. •Prepare the monthly vacancy planning assumptions based on recruitment status reports enabling management to undertake data decisions and set strategic priorities pertaining recruitment. •Prepare and submit information on monthly staffing complements •Implement and established a mechanism for recording and tracking recruitment cases •Serves as focal point for coordination and deployment of new HR Recruitment Innovation systems/applications involving extensive liaison with technical support teams •Maintain and report on a month basis long-term vacancy reports and updates to Pillar Heads. •Draft reports and presentations for staff and senior management. Administration of Justice •Researches and compiles the mission’s responses to formal and informal requests coming from different entities under the Administration of Justice (AoJ) system •Contributes to the efforts and measures aimed at addressing and mitigating staff grievances with the purpose of resolving them at the lowest practical level. •Contributes to the development of preventive activities such as training and sharing best practices and recent jurisprudence related to human resources management. Other: - Under the supervision of the CHRO, contributes to the monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of delegated authorities, Service Level Agreements, HR indicators, and the Senor Manager's Compact. - Assist with the development of a communication strategy with a dedicated intranet page on HR issues and regular formal and informal meetings. - Conducts research on precedents, policy rulings and procedures. - Maintain human resources information systems, including constant update and generation of information and reports for use by management. - Assists in preparing policy papers, position papers and briefing notes on issues related to human resources management. - Performs other duties as required.
Competencies
PROFESSIONALISM: Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines, and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. PLANNING AND ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. CLIENT ORIENTATION: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be "clients" and seeks to see things from clients' point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients' needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients' environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client.
Education
High-school or equivalent diploma is required. The minimum year of qualifying experience can be reduced to 5 for candidates who possess a first level university degree.
Job - Specific Qualification
Technical or Vocational Certificate and/or training in human resources management, business or public administration, social sciences, education or related field experience is desirable.
Work Experience
At least ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in human resources management, administration or related area is required. The minimum years of relevant experience is reduced to 5 years for candidates who possess a first level university degree. At least five (5) years of experience working as a Recruiter in talent management platform is required. At least five (5) years of hands-on experience with the recruitment and onboarding of Affiliated Personnel such as International ICs, Consultants, Individual Uniformed Personnel and Gratis Personnel is required. Experience in the management of HR Budget, Staffing table/post management and Audit is required. Experience in supporting staffing review, redeployment or nationalization of positions and downsizing is required. Experience in the Administration of Justice is desirable. Experience with supervising a team is desirable.

Org. Setting and Reporting
This position is located in the General Legal Division of the Office of Legal Affairs. The Legal Officer reports to a Senior Legal Officer, Principal Legal Officer and the Director of the General Legal Division.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Legal Officer will be responsible for the following duties: •Handles a range of issues related to international commercial law, public and private international law, and administrative law, including the interpretation and application of constitutive, legislative and other instruments governing United Nations activities and operations. •Conducts extensive legal research and analysis and prepares briefs, memoranda, reports and correspondence. •Undertakes extensive review of legal documents, instruments, or other material; identifies important issues, similarities, and inconsistencies, etc. •Prepares or assists in the preparation of legal opinions/advice on a wide range of substantive and procedural questions, which may include those related to administration and management, institutions support, procurement and contracts, peacekeeping and other operational matters, separately administered programmes and funds, claims and arbitrations, administrative appeals, accountability and judicial cooperation, etc. •In particular, prepares and assists in providing analysis, advice and support in resolving (i) disputes arising out of contracts with commercial vendors, consultants, individual contractors, and other personnel, and (ii) third-party claims of a private law character involving the operations and activities of the Organization, its organs or its separately administered funds and programmes. •Assists in advising on and participates in negotiations and settlement of claims and disputes, to include establishing strategy and approach, terms and conditions of settlement, and recommendations on the merit of claims and the Organization's risk exposure in arbitration, etc. •Prepares or assists in the review, advice on, drafting and negotiating of complex contracts with commercial vendors and agreements with NGOs and other public and private entities, as well as in the development of institutional and operational modalities to meet unique needs/circumstances. •Prepares, and provides substantive input on to, motions/submissions in the course of arbitral proceedings or administrative proceedings. •Services or assists senior colleagues in servicing committees, ad hoc working groups, task forces, expert groups and other bodies, including preparation of background materials, summaries of issues and views of members, meeting reports, etc. •Assists in representing the Organization before arbitral tribunals or in administrative proceedings, including disciplinary cases, before the United Nations Appeals Tribunal. •Provides legal advice on the interpretation and application of financial and staff regulations and rules, including the review of administrative decisions and the drafting administrative issuances; prepares analyses and evaluations of human resources policies and other administrative policies and practices. •Provides guidance to more junior staff. •Performs other duties as assigned.
Competencies
•PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of, and ability to apply, legal principles, concepts and procedures and terminology for review, examination, and processing of a range of legal documents. Knowledge of various legal research sources, including electronic, and ability to conduct research and analyze information on a wide range of legal issues. Knowledge of the civil law and/or common law legal systems and principles. Ability to interpret and apply legislative instruments, develop and present results, recommendations, and opinions clearly and concisely. Proficiency in legal drafting skills and ability and ability to draft legal papers and work under pressure. Ability to apply good legal judgment in the context of assignments given. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. •COMMUNICATION: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. •TEAMWORK: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others' ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings.
Education
Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in law is required. A first-level university degree in law in combination with two additional years of qualifying work experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.
Job - Specific Qualification
Admission to the practice of law, or otherwise qualified to practice law, in a Member State of the United Nations is required.
Work Experience
A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in the practice of law, including international commercial law, legal analysis, research and drafting to be obtained either in a law firm or in a legal office of an international intergovernmental organization or in a legal office of a government or court is required. Qualifying years of work experience are calculated following the receipt of the university degree in law recognized by the United Nations. Substantial experience in claims analysis and in international commercial arbitration is required. Experience in the practice of law with an international intergovernmental organisation is desirable. Experience in publishing articles on topics of international commercial law, public or private international law, administrative law or international arbitration is desirable. Experience in advising on the status and the privileges and immunities of international intergovernmental organizations is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. Either French or Spanish is desirable. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult https://languages.un.org for details).

vacancies.jobTitle: Consultant for the Development of the Medium-Term Programme and Resource Mobilization Framework (2027–2030)
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
The ECA Medium-Term Programme and Resource Mobilisation Framework (2027–2030)
Work Location
Addis Ababa
Expected duration
4 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The main objective of the assignment will be to develop an integrated, results-oriented Medium-Term Programme and Resource Mobilization Framework (2027–2030) that defines ECA's strategic priorities, outcomes, programme portfolio and implementation architecture, and strengthens alignment between planning, budgeting, programme delivery and institutional accountability. Specifically, the consultant will 1. Develop a results-based strategic framework for ECA (2027–2030) that articulates the Commission's strategic priorities, theory of change, outcomes, outputs, performance indicators, and alignment with Agenda 2063, the 2030 Agenda, UN mandates, and member States' priorities. 2. Design an integrated and prioritized programme portfolio and implementation architecture that promotes coherence across programmes, divisions, subregional offices, IDEP and initiatives, while enhancing alignment between strategic planning, budgeting, resource allocation, and programme delivery. 3. Develop a sustainable resource mobilization, financing, and partnership model that links resource mobilization, allocation, and utilization to strategic priorities and results, and identifies innovative financing and partnership opportunities to support implementation. 4. Establish robust coordination, monitoring, evaluation, learning, and accountability mechanisms to support effective implementation, performance management, organizational learning, results reporting, and institutional accountability for the delivery of the Framework. 5. Perform any other tasks and responsibilities that would ensure the development and implementation of an effective and results-oriented MTPRMF
Qualifications/special skills
. Advanced university degree in development studies, public policy, programme management, public finance, business administration, international development or a related field . At least fifteen years of progressively responsible experience in the development of multi-year strategic plans, medium-term programme frameworks, results frameworks, and resource mobilization strategies is required. Demonstrated familiarity with the policy frameworks, implementation mechanisms, and priorities of Agenda 2063 and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development will be essential to ensure alignment of the Framework with continental and global development commitments. . The assignment requires a highly qualified development professional with demonstrated expertise and substantial experience in strategic planning, programme design, results-based management, and resource mobilization in support of sustainable development objectives. Strong knowledge of the African development landscape, including regional and continental policy frameworks, institutional mechanisms, development financing, and partnership-building approaches, is highly desirable.
Languages
Fluency in written and spoken English is required; working knowledge of French is desirable.
Additional Information
Not available.

vacancies.jobTitle: Procurement Officer (Head, West and Central Africa Procurement Hub)
vacancies.jobDescription:
Org. Setting and Reporting
This position is located in the Regional Office for West and Central Africa (ROSEN), Division for Operations (DO) of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) in Dakar, Senegal. As Head of the West and Central Africa Procurement Hub, the Procurement Officer works under the direct supervision of the Chief (Procurement), UNOV/UNODC Procurement Unit in Vienna, and the overall supervision of the ROSEN Representative. The incumbent also supports and provides technical oversight for procurement functions at the UNODC Country Office in Nigeria (CONGA). The incumbent will execute his/her functions as part of the ROSEN Operations Team and work in close coordination with the Operations Officer. For more information on UNODC, please visit the website www.unodc.org.
Responsibilities
The incumbent is expected, upon request, to support other UNODC offices and Global Programmes in the West and Central Africa region where UNODC operates. Within assigned authority the Procurement Officer will provide the following specific duties: • Serve as a senior procurement and contracting expert with responsibility for the procurement of a wide variety of supplies and services associated with technically and legally complex contracts and procurement activities; lead and support the procurement work of Regional Offices. • Plan, develop and manage all procurement and contractual aspects of projects of significant complexity related to diverse services and commodities (e.g., information technology, specialized electronic equipment and instruments, medicines, safety and security equipment including PPE, foodstuffs, building maintenance materials, refurbishment work, office supplies, furniture, etc.), taking into account local economic and other conditions. • Plan, develop and manage procurement activities related to infrastructure and major construction projects, including those of significant value, in consultation and supported by UNOV/UNODC Procurement Unit, in close cooperation with UNODC architects, engineers, national authorities to ensure that all local, state, and national building codes and regulations and safety precautions are followed. • Lead the preparation and implementation of procurement according to the United Nations Secretariat Financial Regulations and Rules; when applicable, oversee procurement processed by other UN entities — including through the Common Back Office (CBO) arrangement following the upcoming relocation to the UN House in Dakar — ensuring conformity with their respective rules, regulations, and the UN system principle of Mutual Recognition. • Coordinate procurement functions between ROSEN and CONGA (UNODC Country Office in Nigeria) under the West and Central Africa Procurement Hub arrangement, including harmonizing delegation of authority thresholds, ensuring equitable workload distribution among buyers across both offices, and formalizing arrangements for ad-hoc mutual support with the UNOV/UNODC Procurement Unit. • Provide technical advice and quality assurance on procurement activities to officials, buyers, and focal points during all phases of the procurement cycle; analyze and evaluate procurement requests and ensure appropriateness of technical specifications. • Develop and prepare complex contracts for procurement of non-routine and technologically advanced commodities or long-range services; vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
A more strengthened, accurate and enhanced performance in Jordan’s Environmental Performance Index (EPI).
Work Location
Amman, Jordan
Expected duration
42 days within 6.5 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. The Regional Office for West Asia (ROWA) delivers advisory services and capacity building support to countries to achieve environment and sustainable development objectives. As part of implementing national environmental priorities, the Ministry of Environment in Jordan (MoEnv.) strives to improve Jordan’s standing in global environmental indices, most notably the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) issued by Yale University. The EPI, published biennially by Yale University, provides a comprehensive assessment of countries’ environmental health and sustainability. Jordan’s remarkable 23-place leap in the 2026 EPI is not only an environmental achievement but also a strategic enabler of the Economic Modernization Vision (EMV). To support this national priority, UNEP ROWA seeks to hire a qualified expert/consultant to review and assess the methodology of the 2026 Environmental Performance Index (EPI), analyse Jordan’s performance and ranking across EPI indicators, conduct comparative and gap analyses, develop a coordinated action plan and institutional framework for improving data availability and reporting, and support the Ministry of Environment in strengthening the systematic collection, updating, and communication of environmental data with relevant national entities and global databases.. The Consultant will report to the Science and Policy Regional Coordinator in UNEP West Asia Office and coordinate closely with the EPI focal point in the Ministry of Environment of Jordan. Duties and Responsibilities: The Consultant will carry-out the following duties & responsibilities: •Working methodology and action plan (Deliverable 1) -Review the methodology employed by the entity producing the Global Environmental Performance Index (EPI) report (Yale University) for the 2026 edition; identify the sub-indicators included within the three main components; and propose a working methodology (an action plan for the EPI report). •Analytical comparative report on Jordan’s ranking and performance (Deliverable 2) -Conduct an analysis on Jordan’s ranking in the 2026 report compared to previous years. -Compare Jordan’s performance across the indicators with neighboring countries and countries sharing similar circumstances. •Comparative and gap analysis (Deliverables 3 and 4) -Identify gaps related to data, whether related to outdated information or a lack of data covering specific report indicators, to enable the Ministry of Environment to formulate a plan to address them. -Analyze the interlinkages between EPI indicators and other global indices utilized by the Ministry of Environment (such as the Legatum Index, the Future of Growth Index, and the Global Green Growth Index) and identify shared sub-indicators. •Update of the report and communication on the global databases (Deliverables 5 and 6) -Align the report’s three main components (Environmental Health, Ecosystem Vitality, and Climate Change) and their sub-indicators with the data update cycles of the global databases used by Yale University. -Assist in communicating with the administrators of these global databases to ensure the information covering the sub-indicators is kept up to date. •Matrix of local partner entities (Deliverable 7) -Develop a proposed matrix identifying local partner entities (a task force) —such as ministries and institutions— to compile the data required for the report’s sub-indicators within their respective scopes of work. •Quarterly Progress reports (Deliverable 8) -Prepare progress reports. -Present regular updates to the Ministry of Environment and UNEP ROWA. •Final Report (Deliverable 9) -A final comprehensive report including all previous deliverables, summaries of correspondence, exchange, matrix, etc.
Qualifications/special skills
Advanced university degree (master’s or equivalent) in International Relations, Economics, Environmental Studies, Natural Resource Management, Sustainable Development, Public Policy, or a related field is required. A first-level university degree, combined with two (2) additional years of qualifying experience, may be accepted in lieu of an advanced university degree. PHD degree is also desirable Minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience in environmental policy, climate action, or sustainable development is required. In-depth knowledge of global environmental indicators and sustainability metrics, especially those included in the EPI is required. Strong analytical, organizational, and interpersonal skills is required. Proven experience in environmental data analysis and reporting at national or international level is required. Demonstrated knowledge of Jordan’s environmental context and national priorities is required. Familiarity with Yale University’s EPI methodology and data requirements is an asset. Ability to coordinate with high-level institutions and maintain effective partnerships is an asset.
Languages
Fluency in Arabic and English (written and spoken) is mandatory.

Not available.

Result of Service
Mid-Term Review Report of the Project; “Promoting the safe application of biotechnology through Multi country Cooperation in the implementation of National Biosafety Frameworks in Asia.” The results are expected to guide the execution of the project in its remaining term.
Work Location
Homebased
Expected duration
4 Months Part Time
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment". Its mandate is to coordinate the development of environmental policy consensus by keeping the global environment under review and bringing emerging issues to the attention of governments and the international community for action. UNEP’s Ecosystems Division works with international and national partners, providing technical assistance and capacity development for the implementation of environmental policy, and strengthening the environmental management capacity of developing countries and countries with economies in transition. This consultancy post is in UNEP / Ecosystems Division / GEF Biodiversity unit and reports to the respective GEF Task Manager. UNEP is implementing a GEF-funded projects: “Promoting the safe application of biotechnology through Multi country Cooperation in the implementation of National Biosafety Frameworks in Asia, (GEFID 10463)” executed by The Korea Institute for Promoting Asia Biosafety Cooperation (KIPABiC) The project is a UNEP/GEF-funded regional initiative in Asia that aims to strengthen the safe use, transfer, handling, and regulation of living modified organisms (LMOs) and biotechnology products by improving National Biosafety Frameworks (NBFs) in Bangladesh, India, Mongolia, and the Philippines. The project supports countries in meeting their obligations under the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety (CPB) by building institutional, regulatory, technical, and human capacity; enhancing risk assessment, monitoring, and enforcement systems; promoting regional cooperation and knowledge sharing; and improving public awareness and access to biosafety information. Through collaboration among participating countries and partners such as the Korea Institute for Promoting Asia Biosafety Cooperation (KIPABiC), the project seeks to establish effective biosafety governance, strengthen decision-making tools and laboratory capacities, and create sustainable mechanisms for information exchange and cooperation across Asia, ultimately ensuring that modern biotechnology can contribute to development and food security without compromising biodiversity and environmental safety. The Unit would like to recruit a consultant to conduct a Mid-Term Review of this project. The Mid-Term Review will use a participatory approach whereby key stakeholders are kept informed and consulted throughout the review process. Both quantitative and qualitative evaluation methods will be used as appropriate to determine project achievements against the expected outputs, outcomes and impacts. It is highly recommended that the consultant maintains close communication with the project team and promotes information exchange throughout the review implementation phase to increase their (and other stakeholder) ownership of the review findings. vacancies.postingTitle: UNEP Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) - Banking Policy & Stakeholder Engagement Manager
vacancies.jobTitle: UNEP Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) - Banking Policy & Stakeholder Engagement Manager
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
• Strengthen engagement and collaboration between UNEP FI members, central banks, banking regulators, supervisors, policymakers and other strategic stakeholders as relevant. • Coordinate and support dialogue, knowledge exchange and relationship-building initiatives that advance mutual understanding of sustainable finance challenges, opportunities and emerging regulatory developments. • Help translate policy and regulatory developments into practical insights for members, while communicating member perspectives and implementation experiences across relevant stakeholder groups. • Support the development of resources, engagement approaches and partnerships that strengthen the connection between voluntary banking commitments and the evolving policy and regulatory landscape. The consultant’s work will also contribute to upholding UN core values, ensuring that a human rights-based approach, the principle of leaving no one behind and gender equality and women’s empowerment are integrated throughout their work at UNEP FI.
Work Location
Working remotely / Home-based
Expected duration
12 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. UNEP’s work is firmly grounded in the UN core values, including the human rights-based approach, the commitment to leaving no one behind, and the promotion of gender equality and women’s empowerment across all activities. The overall objective of the UNEP’s Industry and Economy Division is to encourage decision makers in government, local authorities and industry to develop and adopt policies, strategies and practices and technologies that promote sustainable patterns of consumption and production, make efficient use of natural resources, ensure safe management of chemicals and contribute to making trade and environment policies mutually supportive. It promotes the development, use, and transfer of policies, technologies, economic instruments, managerial practices, and other tools that assist in environmentally sound decision-making and the implementation of corresponding activities. The United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) is the strategic partnership between the United Nations and over 500 banks, insurers and investors. For over 32 years UNEP FI has been shaping and driving the international sustainable finance agenda, setting global standards and growing a global network of leading financial institutions. Through its workstreams and regional activities, peer learning, methodology development, training, and research, UNEP FI promotes sustainable finance and helps the financial industry align with and contribute to the Paris Agreement and the Sustainable Development Goals. Global policy and regulatory measures on sustainable finance have increased substantially over recent years. Public policy critically affects the ability of financial institutions to generate sustainable positive and reduce negative impacts through financing decisions. It affects the sustainability and stability of financial markets, as well as social, environmental and economic systems. Sustainable finance policies have become central to enabling and accelerating a successful transition. Launched in 2019 by UN Secretary-General Guterres and bank CEOs from around the world, the UN Principles for Responsible Banking (PRB) guide the transition towards a sustainable global banking industry that plays a key role in helping society achieve its goals for a sustainable future. With these Principles, banks commit to strategically aligning their business with, and scaling up, their contributions to the Sustainable Development Goals and the objectives of the Paris Agreement on Climate. A strong implementation framework defines clear accountabilities and requires each bank to set, publish, and work towards ambitious targets, and to report publicly on their positive and negative impacts and on progress in implementing their commitments. Over 350 banks from more than 90 countries, jointly representing about half of the global banking sector by assets, are now Signatories of the Principles for Responsible Banking. Banks play a key role in supporting the transition to the real economy; however, systemic change requires the engagement of diverse actors. Properly engaging with stakeholders, with a special focus on Banking sector regulators, Governments, and non-financial policymakers, is critical to enabling member banks to deliver on their commitments and better support their clients. UNEP FI can act as a convener between the member banks and the relevant stakeholders. UNEP FI requires the consultant to work in tandem with subject matter experts and the UNEP FI Secretariat to support policy-related developments and projects and strengthen UNEP FI's relationships with key stakeholders. The consultant will carry out this role as part of UNEP FI’s policy and banking teams and, where relevant, in close collaboration with other UNEP FI's teams. Purpose of the Assignment: The consultant will support UNEP FI's Banking and Policy teams in strengthening dialogue and collaboration between the responsible banking community and the regulatory community, including central banks, supervisors, and policymakers. Acting as an interface between UNEP FI members and regulatory stakeholders, the consultant will facilitate trusted exchanges, support strategic convenings, develop substantive briefing and discussion materials, and help translate regulatory and policy developments into practical implications for member banks. The consultant will contribute to building mutual understanding between regulators and the banking sector on emerging sustainability-related risks, transition challenges, implementation experiences, and the policy conditions needed to support real economy transition, while helping identify areas for continued engagement and collaboration at global and regional levels. The consultant will also strengthen the connection between voluntary banking frameworks, including the Principles for Responsible Banking (PRB), and the evolving policy and regulatory landscape, helping members better understand how these frameworks interact in practice and equipping them to anticipate, prepare for, and respond to current and emerging regulatory and supervisory expectations. Objectives: The result of the consultant’s work will be the following successful high-quality outputs defined under the outputs and deliverables section. Specific tasks and responsibilities: Engagement and dialogue between central banks and members • Coordinate the planning, delivery and follow-up of global or regional dialogues between central banks/supervisors and the UNEP FI governance bodies, including agenda development, stakeholder outreach, input briefing papers, facilitation support, meeting summaries and follow-up actions. • Support the development of future dialogue outputs, including discussion papers, publications or other knowledge products for the wider PRB community and central banks. • Develop and implement a roadmap for continued engagement with central banks, supervisory authorities and relevant networks. Member support on policy and regulatory developments • Contribute to research, guidance notes, events and/or capacity-building activities that strengthen members’ understanding of the relationship between regulatory developments and voluntary banking commitments, including the Principles for Responsible Banking, helping banks interpret and respond to evolving policy and regulatory expectations. • Facilitate coordination between policy, banking and regional teams to ensure consistency of messaging and member support. Governments and non-financial policymakers • Support selected policy engagement and/or capacity building initiatives that bring together financial institutions, governments and other non-financial policymakers to advance sustainable finance and real economy transition objectives, including by bringing practical market perspectives into policy implementation discussions. • Identify priority policy processes where UNEP FI members can contribute practical banking sector perspectives. • Work closely with the UNEP FI Banking Board, regional teams and relevant stakeholders to coordinate and amplify responsible banking perspectives in policy discussions. • Raise awareness of the value of the PRB and the achievements of the UN Responsible Banking Community with policymakers. • Ensure that all communications outputs reflect UNEP and UN core values, including a human rights-based approach, the principle of leaving no one behind and gender equality and women’s empowerment, and contribute to internal awareness of these values. • Support the implementation of UNEP FI’s 2026–2029 Social Action Plan by including all relevant measures from the plan in their work. Outputs and Deliverables: Engagement between central banks and members · One global Strategic Dialogue between central banks/supervisors and UNEP FI governance bodies successfully planned, delivered and followed up. The global dialogue can be substituted by a regional dialogue, as relevant. · Two regional central bank-member bank policy dialogues successfully organised and documented. · Briefing papers, discussion notes, stakeholder mappings, meeting summaries and recommendations prepared to support the global or regional dialogues. · At least one knowledge product, such as webinars, discussion paper, publication or synthesis report developed to disseminate insights from central bank engagement activities to the broader PRB community. · A draft stakeholder engagement plan for continued engagement with central banks, supervisory authorities and relevant networks developed and periodically updated. Member support on policy and regulatory developments • At least one resource, guidance notes, webinar, workshop or capacity-building activity delivered to support member understanding of the relationship between regulatory developments and voluntary banking commitments, including the Principles for Responsible Banking. • Inputs provided to UNEP FI projects, publications or member-facing resources that clarify the implications of emerging policy and regulatory developments for banks. Governments and non-financial policymakers • Contributions to at least one policy engagement activity delivered, such as dialogues, capacity building, publication, event, roundtable or other engagement mechanism, as appropriate. • Contribute to identifying current and potential engagement opportunities between UNEP FI members and policymakers, including observations and recommendations for future engagement, as appropriate. • Support with coordinating real economy policy engagement activities across UNEP FI teams relating to the Banking sector. The above deliverables will be developed and implemented in alignment with UNEP FI’s Social Action Plan and guided by the UN’s core values. The consultant will report to: Overall supervisor: The Head of UNEP FI. Direct Supervisor: 1) The Banking Programme Manager, UNEP FI. 2) The Policy Lead, UNEP FI.
Qualifications/special skills
Education: A master’s degree in finance, law, economics, public administration, business administration, marketing or communications, or international relations is required. A bachelor’s degree could be taken in lieu of a master’s degree, provided the selected candidate has 9 years of relevant experience. Professional Experience: At least 7 (seven) years of relevant professional experience and expertise in banking regulation, supervision, stakeholder management, policymakers, banking, or sustainable finance is required. Work experience in an international setting or different world regions is desirable.
Languages
Languages: English is the working language of UNEP FI. Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish or other United Nations languages is an asset.
Additional Information
Skills & Knowledge: • Excellent drafting, communication and presentation skills in English. • Strong project management and coordination skills, including the ability to manage multiple stakeholders and workstreams simultaneously. • Ability to work effectively in a multicultural and geographically dispersed environment, collaborating horizontally within the team. • Experience working in an international organization, membership organization, financial institution, regulator or policy-focused environment is desirable. • Professional networks among regulators, policymakers, banking associations or financial institutions would be an asset. • Ability and willingness to travel up to once per quarter. • Knowledge of global sustainable finance policy and regulation, prudential regulation and other policy developments affecting the banking sector. • Experience engaging with central banks, financial regulators, supervisors, policymakers, financial institutions or industry associations. • Strong stakeholder management and convening skills, including the ability to facilitate dialogue among diverse stakeholders. • Ability to analyse sustainable finance policy and regulatory developments and translate them into concise, practical insights for financial institutions. • Knowledge of the Principles for Responsible Banking, sustainable banking practices, or related sustainable finance frameworks is desirable.
No Fee

Org. Setting and Reporting
In its Resolution A/RES/72/279, the United Nations General Assembly endorsed the transformation of the Development Coordination Office (DCO) as a stand-alone coordination office within the United Nations Secretariat. DCO exercises managerial and oversight functions of the resident coordinator system under the collective ownership of the members of the United Nations Sustainable Development Group (UNSDG). In 2026, DCO undertook a comprehensive organizational recalibration to ensure the RCS remains optimally configured to support the acceleration of the 2030 Agenda in its final years, and fully embodies the UN 2.0 shift—anchored in data, digital, innovation, behavioral science, strategic foresight, and a mission-driven organizational culture. The position is located in the United Nations Development Coordination Office (DCO) in New York and reports to the Chief, Complex Settings Support. The Complex Settings Support Section is one of four teams within the Sustainable Development Goal Coordination, Policy and Programme Division, and is responsible overall for guiding RCs and RCOs on the UN sustainable development offer in complex settings, including crisis and mission contexts. The team is responsible for the policy interface and collaboration with the UN Peace and Security Pillar, UN humanitarian entities, as well as the Inter-Agency Standing Committee and broader collaboration with humanitarian partners. The team also oversees support to RCOs on programme criticality, ensuring that UN country teams are well prepared to adapt their operating footprint in the context of rapid change to the development landscape.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Sustainable Development Officer will be responsible for the following duties: • Develops sustainable development databases and qualitative information required for recurrent or ad-hoc assignments. • Drafts inputs for technical papers and analytical studies on sustainable development issues. This includes analytical inputs on sustainable development challenges and opportunities in complex settings, including mission settings, and relating to humanitarian-development-peace cross-pillar linkages. • Formulates, identifies and analyses proposals on sustainable development issues. • Attends international, regional, and national meetings for consultations with colleagues in other institutions dealing with sustainable development issues. Consultations may include relevant UN development, humanitarian and peacebuilding counterparts. • Assists in the organization and servicing of expert group meetings, seminars, etc. on sustainable development issues. • Prepares speeches and other inputs for presentations by senior staff on sustainable development issues. Such inputs may include briefings and key messages for DCO leadership on sustainable development coordination in complex settings. • Prepares inputs for reports to High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development and other intergovernmental bodies, inter-agency or expert groups on issues relating to sustainable development. This may include inputs to UN policy and reporting processes relevant to sustainable development in complex settings. • Follows intergovernmental meetings, prepares summary reports and provides substantive support, as needed. This may include substantive support to relevant inter-agency consultations and policy forums. • Participates in missions on sustainable development issues relating to complex countries. • Organizes training seminars/ workshops on sustainable development issues with a focus on complex countries and cross-pillar collaboration. • Monitors, backstops and assesses the implementation of capacity building projects in sustainable development. • Performs other duties as required, including administrative tasks. • Undertakes on-the-job and other training activities both internally and externally. • Collects and analyzes data to identify trends or patterns and provide insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting
Competencies
PROFESSIONALISM: Ability to apply sustainable development theories, concepts and approaches. Ability to conduct independent research and analysis on sustainable development topics, determine suitability, validity and accuracy of data provided by different sources. Shows skill in developing sources for data collection. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. PLANNING AND ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. COMMUNICATION: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed.
Education
Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in sustainable development, economics, public policy, public administration, finance, natural resources management, engineering, law, social sciences or related field. A first-level university degree in combination with qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

This position is based in the Office of Legal Affairs (OLA) of the International Seabed Authority in Kingston, Jamaica. The International Seabed Authority is an international organization established under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and the 1994 Agreement relating to the Implementation of Part XI of UNCLOS. Pursuant to these instruments, the Authority is the organization through which States Parties organize and control activities in the Area, namely the seabed, ocean floor and subsoil thereof beyond the limits of national jurisdiction, particularly with a view to administering the mineral resources of the Area. The Office of Legal Affairs provides legal advice and support to the Authority's organs and the Secretariat on matters arising from the interpretation and application of the Convention, the 1994 Agreement and the rules, regulations and procedures adopted by the Authority.
Responsibilities

Regulatory development and legal leadership i) Leads and coordinates the development of the Mining Code and associated standards and guidelines, providing expert legal analysis and advice on complex, multidisciplinary and sensitive regulatory matters, including issues involving competing legal interpretations, institutional considerations and policy objectives. ii) Coordinates and directs the work of legal officers and other assigned personnel engaged in regulatory development; establishes priorities, reviews legal work, provides guidance and supervision, and ensures the consistency, quality and timely delivery of assigned outputs. iii) Advises on the legal coherence of proposed regulatory provisions and their relationship to UNCLOS, the 1994 Agreement, applicable decisions of the Authority and other relevant rules and procedures, identifying legal gaps, ambiguities and implementation issues and proposing appropriate solutions. 2. Legal advice, research and analysis i) Provides authoritative legal advice to the Secretary-General, the Director of the Office of Legal Affairs/Legal Counsel, the Council and the Legal and Technical Commission, as appropriate, on complex substantive and procedural questions relating to the development and application of the regulatory framework for activities in the Area, including exploration and exploitation. ii) Conducts and supervises extensive legal research and analysis on complex, novel or sensitive questions of international law, the law of the sea and the law of international organizations relevant to the Authority's regulatory mandate; prepares and reviews legal opinions, studies, briefs, reports, memoranda and correspondence, and develops recommendations for consideration by the appropriate decision-making bodies. iii) Advises senior officials and relevant units of the Secretariat on legal and regulatory matters within the incumbent's area of responsibility, including the legal implications of proposed measures and the options available to address identified issues. 3. Management, negotiation and coordination i) Assists the Director of the Office of Legal Affairs/Legal Counsel in the management and administration of the relevant legal work programme, including the planning, prioritization, allocation, coordination and review of assignments, and the monitoring of progress against agreed priorities and deadlines. ii) Advises on and supervises the review, negotiation and drafting of complex contracts and other legal instruments related to the regulatory work programme, including agreements with consultants, experts and researchers; identifies appropriate legal and institutional arrangements and develops solutions to address novel legal requirements and operational circumstances. iii) Coordinates, as appropriate, with relevant offices and units of the Secretariat, Member States, experts and other stakeholders to facilitate the effective preparation, review and implementation of regulatory proposals, ensuring that legal considerations are appropriately reflected in the relevant processes. 4. Support to intergovernmental and technical bodies i) Services meetings of the Council, the Legal and Technical Commission and relevant intersessional working groups, expert groups, task forces and other subsidiary or ad hoc bodies, as assigned; prepares and reviews legal and background materials, analytical summaries of issues and positions expressed by delegations, draft texts, road maps, meeting reports and other documentation required to facilitate deliberations. ii) Provides legal and procedural guidance during relevant meetings and negotiations, as appropriate, and advises on drafting options, outstanding legal questions and possible approaches to resolving differences, while respecting the respective mandates and decision-making authority of the bodies concerned. 5. Representation, reporting and other duties i) Represents the Office of Legal Affairs and, as authorized, the Authority at meetings, conferences, seminars and other relevant fora; contributes to the presentation and dissemination of the Authority's work on regulatory affairs and prepares substantive written and oral briefings for senior officials. ii) Prepares and reviews reports, recommendations and other submissions for senior management and the relevant organs of the Authority on progress, emerging legal issues, risks and priorities relating to the development of the Mining Code and associated standards and guidelines. iii) Performs other duties within the scope of the post, as requested by the Director of the Office of Legal Affairs/Legal Counsel or the Secretary-General.

Demonstrated ability to work at the intersection of multiple scientific disciplines and connect across seemingly disparate fields, as well as a good capacity for synthesis. Strong programme management skills with the capability to advise the Secretary-General and other senior officials on approaches and techniques to address highly complex issues relating to activities in the Area. Excellent policy analysis skills and the ability to produce reports and papers on scientific and technical issues and to review and edit the work of others. Knowledge and ability to apply ISA rules, regulations, policies, and guidelines in work situations. Shows pride in work and in achievements. Demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter. Is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines, and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns. Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges. Remains calm in stressful situation; Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
The Agriculture Expert Roster aims to give UNTB a structured, searchable pool of qualified experts aligned with LDC priority areas and UNTB’s areas of work. By maintaining this pool, UNTB will be able to respond faster and more consistently to country requests, support TNA follow-up and project design, and avoid repeating the search process each time expertise is needed for different programme work, while building its credibility as a practical, service-oriented partner for STI capacity development. Specifically, it will allow UNTB to: • enable timely identification of specialists for technical assistance, policy advice, research, capacity development and project design; • match agricultural expertise with country needs identified through TNAs and other forms of engagement; • support LDCs in assessing, adapting and scaling appropriate agricultural technologies and innovations; • strengthen the development of policies, strategies, technical assessments, implementation plans and project proposals; • facilitate knowledge exchange and partnerships among governments, research institutions, academia, the private sector and development partners; • provide access to expertise across different agricultural technology areas, regions, languages and levels of experience; and • reduce repeated expert searches by maintaining structured and updated information in one place.
Work Location
Remote
Expected duration
Experts included in the UNTB Expert Roster will remain listed for a period of four years.
Duties and Responsibilities
The UN Technology Bank for Least Developed Countries (UNTB) is the United Nations entity dedicated to strengthening the science, technology and innovation capacities of least developed countries (LDCs). Its mandate includes supporting LDCs to identify, absorb, develop, integrate and scale technologies and innovations in line with their national priorities. Under its Strategic Plan 2025–2027, UNTB organizes its work around three strategic areas: high-impact policy and technical advisory services; capacity-building for transformation; and knowledge services for results. Through these areas, UNTB supports LDCs in developing and implementing effective science, technology and innovation policies and programmes, strengthening the capacities of policymakers and institutions, and accessing knowledge and expertise relevant to their development needs. UNTB aims to serve as a hub that connects LDCs with technical assistance, policy advice, capacity-development opportunities, research and analysis, technology-transfer support and specialized expertise. By mobilizing knowledge and expertise from research institutions, academia, the private sector, international organizations and development partners, UNTB seeks to help LDCs translate identified technology needs into practical policies, programmes, partnerships and solutions. Application structure and area of expertise To ensure a structured and searchable pool of qualified experts, applicants will be selected based on a combination of their ‘primary technical domain’ and their ‘functional scope of work’. Applicants may select multiple primary technical domains. For each domain selected, you must specify one or more functional scopes of work that reflect your expertise, along with corresponding evidence. When applying, candidates will be required to: 1. Select one primary technical domain and, if applicable, one secondary technical domain (Section A). 2. Select one primary functional scope of work and, if applicable, one secondary functional scope of work (Section B), and provide supporting evidence for each selection. Section A: Primary technical domains • Agricultural water management and irrigation • Agricultural data, digital agriculture and knowledge systems • Crop production, plant breeding and agricultural biotechnologies • Post-harvest management, agro-processing and agricultural value chains • Sustainable farming systems including climate-smart technologies • Fisheries, aquaculture and aquatic food systems Section B: Area of expertise Please specify the specific functions qualified to perform within the chosen primary domain(s). 1. Agricultural technology and engineering expertise • Identify, screen and prioritize agricultural technologies and innovations that fit national and local agro-ecological conditions, infrastructure, resource availability and development priorities, using clear technical criteria and evidence. • Evaluate technology's relevance, technical feasibility, maturity and readiness, performance, indicative cost ranges, and operation and maintenance needs, to establish its suitability for local conditions in LDCs. • Quantify the economic, social, environmental and climate benefits of priority technologies, including productivity gains, resource-use efficiency, emissions reduction and climate resilience. • Define the technical requirements for adaptation, transfer and scale-up, including site suitability, standards and certification, supply chains and spare parts, local fabrication and repair capacity, and technician skills. • Lead the technical components of Technology Needs Assessments (TNAs) and author high-quality technical knowledge products, including technology factsheets and profiles, technical guidelines, operational manuals and training materials. 2. Policy, research, assessments and analysis • Review national development priorities, STI policies and agricultural innovation systems to assess local absorptive and adaptive capacities, and provide actionable, evidence-based recommendations to strengthen the enabling environment for agricultural transformation. • Design rigorous research methodologies, analytical frameworks, survey instruments and data-collection tools that combine qualitative and quantitative methods and suit data-limited LDC contexts. • Analyse complex data to identify technology needs, systemic bottlenecks, capacity gaps, regulatory constraints and development opportunities, and turn findings into clear priorities for action. • Assess the economic and social dimensions of technology adoption, including cost-effectiveness, affordability, adoption barriers, livelihood impacts, and gender and social inclusion, as part of TNAs, baseline studies and institutional assessments. • Author high-quality, policy-relevant knowledge products, including policy briefs, country profiles, technical reports, baseline summaries, comparative synthesis papers and thematic working papers, for UNTB and LDC stakeholders. 3. Stakeholder engagement and capacity development • Design and facilitate inclusive multi-stakeholder consultations, national validation workshops, focus group discussions, technical working groups and other participatory processes that bring together governments, research institutions, the private sector, farmer organizations and development partners to build consensus and national ownership. • Design, deliver and support training programmes, technical briefings, learning sessions, peer exchanges and interactive workshops, and develop tailored training materials and toolkits that strengthen skills for technology adoption and use. • Build partnerships and knowledge networks among national, regional and international actors to promote South-South and triangular cooperation, knowledge sharing, and the long-term sustainability of results. 4. Project design, development and implementation • Develop high-quality project proposals, that align with LDC national priorities and meet donor and financing requirements. • Translate assessment findings, diagnostics and technical recommendations into actionable implementation plans, action plans, project frameworks, results matrices and pilot initiatives. • Develop monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) frameworks, including indicators, baselines and reporting systems, to track progress, measure impact and inform adaptive management. • Identify and mobilize financing opportunities from donors, climate and development funds, and the private sector to support technology deployment and scale-up. Note: The listed functions are indicative and may be expanded to include other related tasks as required.
Qualifications/special skills
- An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or PhD) in agriculture, agronomy, agricultural engineering, agricultural economics, agribusiness, food systems, rural development, irrigation engineering, water resources management, natural resource management, environmental science, climate change, biotechnology, data science, public policy or another discipline directly relevant to the selected area of expertise is required. - A minimum of eight years of professional experience in agriculture, including substantial experience directly related to the area of expertise for which the applicant is applying in at least one LDC or developing country is required. - For Area 1 (Agricultural technology and engineering expertise): A PhD in a relevant technical or engineering field is preferred. Applicants with a Master's degree must have at least 12 years of relevant professional experience, including hands-on technical work in developing, testing, deploying or maintaining agricultural technologies. - At least one peer-reviewed publication relevant to the selected area of expertise, or an authored or co-authored publication published by UN or by a recognized international organization in which the applicant is clearly credited is required. - In-depth understanding of the agricultural, socio-economic and STI challenges in LDCs, including national development priorities, absorptive capacity constraints, and conditions affecting agricultural technology adoption and scaling is required. - Experience working with line ministries, national STI bodies, UN entities or international development organizations is required. - Mention which areas (primary and secondary, if any) within Section A you would be applying for, is required. (Only respond if relevant) Agricultural technology and engineering expertise: - Demonstrated hands-on experience designing, testing, piloting, deploying or maintaining agricultural technologies in the selected technical domain, preferably in LDC or developing-country settings. (Only respond if relevant) Agricultural technology and engineering expertise: - Proven experience conducting technology assessments, technical feasibility studies or technology readiness evaluations, or preparing technology profiles, specifications or technical standards. (Only respond if relevant) Agricultural technology and engineering expertise: - Experience supporting technology transfer, adaptation or scale-up, such as working with research institutes, extension services, the private sector or farmer organisations to build the local systems, skills and delivery channels needed for technologies to be adopted and sustained is desirable. (Only respond if relevant) Policy, research, assessments and analysis: - Experience conducting or leading research, needs assessments, technology assessments or similar assignments related to agriculture at the country, regional or sectoral level, using qualitative and quantitative methods. (Only respond if relevant) Policy, research, assessments and analysis: - Demonstrated track record of providing strategic policy, regulatory or institutional advisory services to line ministries, national STI bodies, UN entities or international development organizations. (Only respond if relevant) Policy, research, assessments and analysis: - Proven ability to gather and synthesize complex data from academic and non-academic sources, formulate evidence-based conclusions, and communicate findings effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences. (Only respond if relevant) Stakeholder engagement and capacity development: - Proven experience designing and facilitating national-level multi-stakeholder processes, such as consultations, validation workshops or technical working groups, involving government, research institutions, the private sector and farmer organizations. (Only respond if relevant) Stakeholder engagement and capacity development: - Demonstrated experience designing and delivering training programmes or curricula for policymakers, researchers, extension workers or farmers, including evaluating training outcomes. Certification in training, facilitation or adult learning is an asset. (Only respond if relevant) Stakeholder engagement and capacity development: - Experience conducting capacity needs assessments and developing capacity development plans or learning strategies for agricultural institutions, extension systems or national STI bodies. (Only respond if relevant) Project design, development and implementation: - Experience managing or coordinating the implementation of agricultural development or technology projects, including pilots, covering work planning, budgeting, partner coordination, risk management and donor reporting. (Only respond if relevant) Project design, development and implementation: - Demonstrated experience in designing successful, awarded project proposals, technical assistance packages, concept notes, or multi-year project documents for international donors, climate finance mechanisms (e.g., GCF, GEF), or multilateral development banks. (Only respond if relevant) Project design, development and implementation: - Proven experience developing results frameworks, theories of change, logframes and MEL systems, or managing the implementation of multi-year development projects.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations. For this position, fluency in written and oral communication in English is required. Fluency in French and Portuguese is desirable.
Additional Information
Application Information: - Completed responses to the open-ended questions in the application form, clearly outlining the applicant’s relevant technical domain(s), functional area(s), years of experience and demonstrated expertise. Responses should include examples of relevant assignments and outputs, such as positions held, technical assistance delivered, tools or systems developed, publications or guidance prepared, projects implemented, and countries or institutions supported. - Please include N/A for questions that are not relevant to your expertise. Travel: Most assignments will be home-based with possible travel depending on assignment requirements. *Please note that inclusion in the roster does not imply automatic deployment or guarantee any formal engagement with UNTB. When a relevant assignment arises, UNTB will contact suitable roster Experts with a specific Terms of Reference outlining the scope and duration of the assignment and will confirm interest, availability and the applicable fee.
No Fee

Org. Setting and Reporting The United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is mandated by the UN General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities. UN-Habitat is the focal point for all urbanization and human settlement matters within the UN system. UN-Habitat works with partners to build inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable cities and communities. UN-Habitat promotes urbanization as a positive transformative force for people and communities, reducing inequality, discrimination and poverty. The Local2030 Coalition is the United Nations system-wide initiative to support the localization of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The Secretariat, hosted in Bilbao, coordinates joint action, leverages local solutions, and drives strategic communications to accelerate SDG implementation at the local level. Under the direct supervision and guidance of the Communications Officer, the Knowledge Management & Communications Support intern will provide operational and administrative assistance to streamline digital asset management, structure internal and external communications repositories, support international media monitoring and reporting, assist with web and data visualization tasks, and facilitate smooth team workflows. Expected duration
6 Months
Duties and Responsibilities
Org. Setting and Reporting The United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is mandated by the UN General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities. UN-Habitat is the focal point for all urbanization and human settlement matters within the UN system. UN-Habitat works with partners to build inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable cities and communities. UN-Habitat promotes urbanization as a positive transformative force for people and communities, reducing inequality, discrimination and poverty. The position is located in the Capacity Development Section (CDS), Knowledge and Innovation Branch (KIB) at Global Knowledge and Advocacy Division (GKAD) of UN-Habitat at the duty station of Nairobi, Kenya. The intern reports to the Chief of the Capacity Development Section. UN-Habitat has long been a global leader in technical cooperation, with capacity development at the core of its mandate. It brings together decades of operational experience, technical and policy advisory services, and cutting-edge research with a strong track record in developing knowledge, tools, methodologies, and normative guidance. Anchored in the 2026-2029 Strategic Plan, capacity development is a central service and cornerstone of effective development cooperation - enhancing individual competencies, strengthening institutional capacity, and shaping enabling environments for systemic change. In doing so, it directly contributes to accelerating progress on SDGs, the New Urban Agenda, and other global commitments, while supporting countries to respond to evolving housing crises and urban challenges, such as informality, climate change, and rapid urban growth. The Capacity Development Section (CDS) serves as a strategic partner and technical advisor to member states and cities throughout this process. The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system, and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. UNEP’s Sectoral Transition Section supports the implementation of solutions to address climate change across five strategic pillars: near-zero-emission and resilient buildings and construction; sustainable cooling and extreme heat resilience; integrated energy transition with a focus on demand-side flexibility; food waste reduction and prevention; and subnational and multilevel climate action. The Section brings together science and knowledge, policy support, finance, partnerships and implementation. It also hosts the secretariats of multistakeholder platforms, including the Global Alliance for Buildings and Construction (GlobalABC), the Cool Coalition and the Food is Never Waste Coalition. Through engagement with governments, the private sector, international organizations and civil society, the Section promotes collaboration and mobilizes support for sustainable sectoral transitions. Its activities include high-level conferences, ministerial dialogues, technical workshops, international summits and stakeholder consultations, which provide opportunities to advance programme objectives, strengthen partnerships and increase visibility.
