Org. Setting and Reporting
The Sustainable Development Goals Multi-Partner Trust Fund (SDG MPTF) Kenya is a country-level pooled financing mechanism established in June 2022 to support the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development through integrated United Nations programming under the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). The Fund promotes joint programming, pooled financing and coordinated action by United Nations entities in support of Kenya’s national development priorities and the broader UN Development System Reform agenda. Since its establishment, the Fund has mobilized over USD 35.8 million in commitments and supported fifteen joint programmes implemented by seventeen Participating UN Organizations (PUNOs), spanning all three strategic priorities of the UNSDCF. Hosted within the Resident Coordinator’s Office (RCO), the SDG MPTF Secretariat serves as the central coordination mechanism for the Fund, providing strategic, technical, fiduciary and administrative support to the Resident Coordinator in his/her capacity as Chair of the Fund Board, to Participating UN Organizations, development partners and national stakeholders. The Secretariat is responsible for coordinating joint programming processes, supporting governance mechanisms, managing Fund allocations, overseeing monitoring and reporting, facilitating risk management, and ensuring compliance with MPTF Office policies and procedures. The incumbent will work closely with national government institutions, county governments, Participating UN Organizations, development partners, civil society organizations, private sector partners and other stakeholders engaged in Fund-supported initiatives. Regular travel within Kenya may be required to support programme oversight, monitoring missions, stakeholder consultations and strategic partnership engagement.
Responsibilities
1. Coordinate the Secretariat's day-to-day operations and advise the Fund Manager, Resident Coordinator and Head of RCO on pooled financing, the portfolio approach and UN Development System reform. 2. Serve as Deputy Secretary to the Fund Board; prepare agendas, briefing materials, minutes and follow-up for the Board and Technical Review Committees, and quality-assure proposals before they go to the Board. 3. Manage allocation rounds and calls for proposals, and ensure Fund-supported joint programmes sit within portfolio results frameworks and strengthen coherence across Results Groups. 6. Monitor portfolio implementation across partners against agreed indicators, flag bottlenecks and risks, and recommend corrective action. 7. Ensure gender equality, human rights, youth, climate resilience, disability inclusion, conflict sensitivity and Leave No One Behind are integrated into portfolios and programmes, and track trends that affect them. 8. Develop the investment pipeline aligned to portfolio priorities and support the resource mobilization strategy, building partnerships with donors, international financial institutions, foundations, climate funds and the private sector. 9. Act as secondary liaison between the RCO, the MPTF Office, PUNOs and development partners, and manage Fund agreements, disbursements and compliance with the Administrative Agent's procedures. 10. Oversee allocation and financial performance, and coordinate results-based monitoring, evaluation and risk management. 11. Consolidate PUNO and partner reporting into high-quality reports for the Board, Government, donors and the MPTF Office at portfolio and Fund level. 12. The project supports improved employment opportunities for young Iraqis, women and vulnerable groups by making technical and vocational education more closely connected to private sector demand. Org. Setting and Reporting
The Sustainable Development Goals Multi-Partner Trust Fund (SDG MPTF) Kenya is a country-level pooled financing mechanism established in June 2022 to support the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development through integrated United Nations programming under the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). The Fund promotes joint programming, pooled financing and coordinated action by United Nations entities in support of Kenya’s national development priorities and the broader UN Development System Reform agenda. Since its establishment, the Fund has mobilized over USD 35.8 million in commitments and supported fifteen joint programmes implemented by seventeen Participating UN Organizations (PUNOs), spanning all three strategic priorities of the UNSDCF. Hosted within the Resident Coordinator’s Office (RCO), the SDG MPTF Secretariat serves as the central coordination mechanism for the Fund, providing strategic, technical, fiduciary and administrative support to the Resident Coordinator in his/her capacity as Chair of the Fund Board, to Participating UN Organizations, development partners and national stakeholders. The Secretariat is responsible for coordinating joint programming processes, supporting governance mechanisms, managing Fund allocations, overseeing monitoring and reporting, facilitating risk management, and ensuring compliance with MPTF Office policies and procedures. Working under the overall strategic guidance of the Resident Coordinator and the direct supervision of the Head of the Resident Coordinator’s Office, the incumbent will lead the Secretariat’s support to the Resident Coordinator in developing and managing, with the Government of Kenya, the Cooperation Framework portfolios.

Serve as Secretary to the Fund Board and lead the Technical Review Committees and other governance mechanisms, ensuring compliance with the Fund's Terms of Reference and quality assurance of all proposals before they go to the Board. 3. Lead, with Government counterparts, the design of Cooperation Framework portfolios: convene national and county institutions, UN entities, international financial institutions, development partners and the private sector to agree each portfolio's results, theory of change and respective roles. 4. Co-manage portfolios with Government through joint coordination arrangements chaired or co-chaired by Government, tracking progress against national priorities and the overall resource gap across Government, partner and UN sources. 5. Keep joint programmes as instruments inside portfolios: convene the heads of programmes of Participating UN Organizations (PUNOs) to design and appraise a limited number of joint programmes where collective UN action adds value, and manage allocation rounds and calls for proposals. 6. Advise the Resident Coordinator and Head of RCO on pooled financing, the portfolio approach and UN Development System reform, and analyse political, economic and development trends to inform investment and adaptive programming. 7. Ensure gender equality, human rights, youth, climate resilience, disability inclusion, conflict sensitivity and Leave No One Behind are built into portfolio design, results and monitoring. 8. Lead the Fund's resource mobilization strategy and an investment pipeline aligned to portfolio priorities and Government financing plans, engaging donors, international financial institutions, foundations, climate funds and the private sector to unlock blended and innovative finance. 9. Act as principal liaison between the RCO, the MPTF Office, PUNOs, development partners and Government, overseeing Fund agreements, disbursements and compliance with the Administrative Agent's procedures. 10. Oversee financial performance, results-based monitoring, evaluation and risk management, and ensure consolidated reporting to the Board, Government, donors and the MPTF Office at portfolio and Fund level, drawing on Government data systems where possible. 11. Lead knowledge products and lessons learned from portfolios and Fund-supported programmes, and promote innovation in integrated programming, financing and partnerships. 12. Perform other related duties as required.

Result of Service
The goal of this job function is provide day-to-day administrative and operational support to the ITC project team.
Work Location
Islamabad, Pakistan
Expected duration
One year, with possibility of extension
Duties and Responsibilities
BACKGROUND: ITC will implement Pakistan Punjab Textile project through an ITC-led component focused on training, document development and offline support for textile and clothing enterprises in Punjab. The project will support enterprises through training, coaching and advisory support on sustainability standards, certification requirements, buyer expectations, environmental and social compliance, circularity, chemicals management, lean manufacturing and market linkages. The Administrative Officer will provide day-to-day administrative and operational support to the ITC project team. RESPONSIBILITIES: Under the supervision of the Programme Advisor, the Associate Administrative Advisor will: 1. Administration and Operations • Support administrative and operational activities of the Project Management Unit and field offices to ensure effective service delivery and business continuity. • Maintain administrative records, filing systems, correspondence, and documentation; coordinate visa processes, administrative clearances, and protocol requirements for official missions. • Support asset and inventory management, including periodic physical verification exercises. • Liaise with headquarters, field offices, government counterparts, service providers, and other stakeholders to facilitate operational support services. • Support the implementation of administrative procedures, internal controls, and operational practices. 2. Procurement and Contract Administration • Support procurement activities for goods and services in compliance with organizational and donor rules and procedures. • Prepare and process procurement documentation, including RFQs, ITBs, RFPs, purchase requisitions, and purchase orders. • Support procurement planning, bid evaluations, contract administration, and maintenance of procurement records. • Maintain supplier databases and procurement-related information in ERP systems and support reporting, cost recovery, and compliance activities. • Liaise with headquarters, the Legal Department, and relevant procurement networks on procurement matters. 3. Budget and Finance • Assist in the preparation, monitoring, and reporting of project budgets and General Operating Expenditure (GOE). • Monitor expenditures, prepare forecasts, reconciliations, analyses, and periodic financial reports. • Process payments and verify claims, invoices, travel expenses, and reimbursement requests in compliance with applicable procedures. • Support treasury, petty cash, reimbursement, and financial authorization processes, and maintain financial records in ERP systems. • Facilitate financial coordination between headquarters, project offices, and relevant stakeholders. 4. Human Resources Administration • Coordinate consultant recruitment and engagement processes in accordance with established policies and procedures. • Provide advice on recruitment procedures, documentation requirements, and administrative processes. • Draft Terms of Reference (TORs), prepare recruitment and consultant engagement documentation, and process related transactions. • Liaise with headquarters on consultant administration and recruitment-related matters. 5. Travel and Logistics • Coordinate official travel and logistical arrangements for staff, consultants, experts, and mission personnel in accordance with applicable policies and procedures. • Prepare and process Travel Requests, review travel expense documentation, and support reimbursement processes. • Arrange travel, accommodation, transportation, vehicle services, and related logistics for missions, workshops, and meetings. • Liaise with travel agencies and service providers, maintain travel records, and provide guidance on travel procedures and entitlements. • Provide logistical support to headquarters staff, consultants, and experts undertaking official missions. 6. Security Coordination • Serve as the designated Security Focal Point and support compliance with UNDSS security requirements and organizational procedures. • Disseminate security advisories, support security briefings, and maintain security-related records and reports. • Support security compliance, incident preparedness, business continuity arrangements, and security-related support for official missions and travel. 7. Coordination, Reporting and Partnerships • Participate in inter-agency operational meetings and working groups, as requested. • Support coordination with UN agencies, government counterparts, implementing partners, and service providers on administrative and operational matters. • Prepare operational reports, briefings, statistics, and other documentation, and support knowledge-sharing and capacity-building initiatives. • Monitor assigned operational activities and perform other related duties as required. The Focal Point is mandated to process delisting requests submitted by, or on behalf of, an individual, group, undertaking or entity designated on the lists of the Sanctions Committees established by the Security Council, with the exception of the ISIL (Da’esh) & Al-Qaida Sanctions List. This position is located in the Office of the Focal Point for delisting, a Special Political Mission administered and supported by the Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs. The incumbent will work under the substantive direction and guidance of the Focal Point for Delisting appointed pursuant to Security Council resolution 2744 (2024). The Legal Officer will report to the Chief of the Subsidiary Organs Branch of the Security Council Affairs Division while providing support to the Office of the Focal Point for Delisting.
Responsibilities
Under the general supervision of the Chief of the Security Council Subsidiary Organs Branch, the incumbent will work under the substantive direction and guidance of the Focal Point for Delisting in fulfilling the task set out in the annex I of resolution 2744 (2024). The major responsibilities for this position will include, but are not limited to: • Handles a range of issues related to constitutional, international, public, private, administrative, and, for Tribunals, criminal (substantive, procedural and comparative) law, including the interpretation and application of constitutive, legislative and other instruments governing United Nations activities and operations, in consultation with senior Legal Officers or Prosecuting Trial Attorneys. • Conducts legal research and analysis and prepare studies, comparative studies, briefs, reports and correspondence. • Assists with the drafting of factual and legal portions of the Comprehensive Reports of the Focal Point to the Security Council's Sanctions Committees. • Undertakes basic reviews of legal documents, instruments, or other material; identifies important issues, similarities, and inconsistencies, etc. • Assists in the preparation of interviews with petitioners for delisting and character witnesses, including drafting interview questions and supporting the Focal Point during such interviews, taking notes of meetings and drafting meeting summaries, and preparing legal documents as necessary in the course of information-gathering. • Ensures continuous flow of information between the Focal Point for Delisting, petitioners and/or their legal representatives throughout the delisting review process. • Assesses evidence for relevance and admissibility. • Prepares and assesses briefs of evidence. • Services or assists senior colleagues in servicing diplomatic conferences, commissions, committees, task forces, expert groups and other bodies, including preparation of background materials, summaries of issues and views of delegations, meeting reports, etc. • Provides legal advice on human resources matters, reviews administrative matter. • Administers programmes of legal technical assistance. • Prepares or assists in the preparation of legal opinions/advice on relevant issues of international public law, including related to the Security Council. • Provides guidance to more junior staff. • Collects and analyzes data to identify trends or patterns and provide insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. • Performs other duties as assigned.
Competencies
PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of the policies, procedures and practices of the Security Council. Knowledge of the procedures of the Focal Point for Delisting as set out in resolution 1730 (2006), renewed and strengthened in subsequent resolutions, including, most recently, resolution 2744 (2024). Knowledge of legal challenges to targeted Security Council sanctions and of the steps taken by the Security Council to ensure its procedures for adding and removing individuals to/from sanctions lists are fair and clear. Strong analytical skills and ability to conduct comprehensive legal research on a range of issues, including those of a unique and/or complex nature. Ability to interview witnesses and make substantial legal arguments. Discretion and sound judgment in applying legal expertise to sensitive, complex legal issues. Ability to appropriately handle confidential and strictly confidential information. Ability to draft and structure complex documents and to express fact summaries and concepts accurately and succinctly. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. PLANNING AND ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. TEAMWORK: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others' ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings.
Education
Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in law is required. A first-level university degree in combination with qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Month 1: Technical Assessment and Development Plan Deliverable: Complete a technical assessment of the existing ServiceNow configuration relevant to the prioritized workflows and produce an approved technical development plan, solution design, implementation sequence, and development backlog based on requirements provided by OIM. Measurable outputs: • Technical assessment completed. • Solution design documented. • Development backlog prepared. • Technical dependencies and risks recorded. • Development plan approved by OIM. The United Nations Secretary-General is responsible for the investment of the assets of the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund (UNJSPF). vacancies.jobTitle: Data Product and Engineering Consultant - Total Portfolio Analysis
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
1. Work Plan and Operating Cadence - Deliverable: Work plan and operating cadence. - Expected output / acceptance criteria: - Confirmed scope, timeline, stakeholders, decision points, risks, and escalation path. - Review of the current TPV dashboard plan and recommendation for an incremental delivery approach aligned with the data platform build-out. - Identification of key trade-offs, risks, and dependencies. - Weekly status updates covering progress, open decisions, blockers, and next steps. - Review and approval: Chief of Data. 2. TPV Semantic Layer and Data Dictionary - Deliverable: TPV semantic layer and data dictionary. - Expected output / acceptance criteria: - Agreed definitions for each TPV data point and metric. - Documentation of attributes, grain, formula, inputs, frequency, history, owner, lineage, and business context. - Definitions that are clear and actionable for both business users and engineers. - Review and approval: Chief of Data; TPA dashboard working group. 3. Source Assignment and Data POVs - Deliverable: Source assignment and Data POVs. - Expected output / acceptance criteria: - Each mapped data point, metric, and attribute linked to an authoritative source system, dataset, and field. - Documentation of competing sources, gaps, overlaps, conflicts, and data quality issues through Data POVs. - Recommended source precedence and documented decision rationale. - Review and approval: Chief of Data; source owners. 4. Technical Requirements and Data Model - Deliverable: Technical requirements and data model. - Expected output / acceptance criteria: - Backlog-ready requirements covering: - Data model and domain data product implications. - Data transformations. - Data refresh requirements. - Data quality checks. - Dependencies and implementation priorities. - SQL/Python prototype logic, where useful. - Review and approval: Chief of Data. 5. Dynamic TPV Dashboard Prototype - Deliverable: Dynamic TPV dashboard prototype. - Expected output / acceptance criteria: - Interactive prototype developed in Power BI or Sigma. - Use of source data from individual systems where available. - Validation of dashboard direction and user interactions. - Validation of drill-down paths. - Identification and prioritization of production build requirements. - Review and approval: Chief of Data; dashboard leadership. 6. Handover Pack and Knowledge Transfer - Deliverable: Handover pack and knowledge transfer. - Expected output / acceptance criteria: - Documentation of key deliverables and decisions. - Consolidated list of open decisions and risks. - Implementation backlog inputs. - Recommended next steps for the OIM team. - Completion of knowledge transfer sessions. - Review and approval: Chief of Data. Cross-Cutting Requirement - Review the current TPV dashboard plan, data inventory, and delivery assumptions. - Recommend an incremental delivery approach aligned with the data platform build-out. Identify: - Early release opportunities. - Dependencies and sequencing choices. - Key trade-offs. - Priority adjustments, where needed.
Work Location
New York; Remote
Expected duration
6 months
Duties and Responsibilities
This position is located in the Office of Investment Management (OIM) of the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund (UNJSPF). OIM is responsible for the investment of the assets of the Fund. OIM manages a $100+ billion multi-asset global portfolio, with about 85% actively managed in-house. OIM is starting its Total Portfolio Approach (TPA) journey as part of Project Blue Print 2030. TPA manages the Fund as one portfolio, judged against the Fund's overall goals, instead of as separate asset class portfolios. A Total Portfolio View (TPV) dashboard is expected to bring public and private markets, risk, performance, liquidity and cost into one place. A working group has defined the dashboard use cases and an initial inventory of about 220 proposed data points and metrics. The next step is to confirm what those items mean, where they should come from, how source conflicts should be resolved and which reusable data products are needed underneath TPV. The consultant reports directly to the Chief of Data, OIM, and works under the Chief of Data's overall guidance and oversight. The consultant is expected to operate independently, structure ambiguous requirements, lead stakeholder alignment, identify risks and escalate only material blockers or decisions requiring management direction. This consultancy is based in New York and in-office presence is preferred. Hybrid work may be considered. CONSULTANT PROFILE • Senior, autonomous consultant with direct experience in TPA, total fund, or total portfolio / multi-asset portfolio analytics. • Strong data product and semantic-layer capability: able to define metrics, attributes, grain, calculation logic, lineage, source precedence and decision rules. • Strong enough in data engineering to translate business requirements into technical requirements, SQL or Python prototypes, data models and delivery-backlog inputs. • Business-facing and facilitative: able to align Investment, Risk, Operations and Data stakeholders when the same metric has different interpretations across teams or systems. • Clear writer and structured thinker: able to produce Data POVs that compare source options, explain nuanced differences and support decisions. SCOPE OF WORK 1. Semantic layer and data product definition • Review and complete the existing TPV data inventory with the working group. • Define each TPV data point or metric with clear business meaning, attributes, grain, formula, inputs, frequency, history, owner, lineage and decision rules. • Identify reusable domain data product implications underneath TPV, including where common definitions, attributes or source data should support more than one dashboard or use case. 2. Source assignment and Data POVs • Assign each mapped definition to its authoritative source across systems, including but not limited to Northern Trust, Bloomberg, MSCI Barra One, Burgiss and internal registers, as applicable. • Identify gaps, overlaps, conflicts and data quality issues. For each source, dataset, field, metric or attribute proposed for TPV use, assess availability, authority, completeness, quality, timeliness, granularity, lineage, access feasibility, current-offering availability and business agreement. • Produce Data POVs, meaning short decision papers that compare source options for the same metric or attribute, including definition differences, calculation logic, timing, data quality, lineage, recommended source and decision rationale. 3. Technical requirements and delivery backlog inputs • Write technical requirements for the TPV dashboards and supporting semantic layer, including data model, transformations, source precedence, refresh needs, data quality checks and implementation dependencies. • Translate sourcing decisions and domain data product implications into prioritized inputs for the data platform delivery backlog. • Develop SQL or Python prototype logic where useful to validate data modelling assumptions or make requirements executable for the OIM engineering team. 4. Delivery sequencing and incremental implementation • Assess the current TPV dashboard plan, sequencing and delivery assumptions based on data availability, source readiness, semantic-layer complexity and implementation dependencies. • Recommend an incremental delivery approach that aligns TPV outputs with the data platform build-out, including what can be delivered early, what depends on platform capabilities, and which decisions or dependencies need to be resolved first. • Identify and document key trade-offs, including speed versus quality, prototype versus production readiness, available source versus authoritative source, short-term workaround versus reusable data product, and dashboard priority versus data platform dependency. 5. Dashboard prototype • Build or guide a mock-up of an active, dynamic TPV dashboard in Power BI or Sigma, using source data from individual systems where available. • Make the prototype interactive, with filters, changeable variables and drill-down paths rather than static charts. • Use the prototype as a proof point to validate semantic-layer decisions, dashboard direction and production build priorities. 6. Stakeholder facilitation and best practices • Facilitate working sessions, meetings and decision discussions across Investment, Risk, Operations, the TPA dashboard working group and the Business Intelligence Team. • Drive alignment where the same metric or attribute has different meanings across teams or systems. • Share practical approaches, lessons learned and best practices from comparable TPA, total fund or multi-asset portfolio analytics implementations. WORKING ARRANGEMENTS • The consultant joins the weekly TPA dashboard working group and gives a short written status update each week. • The consultant is expected to be available for regular on-site meetings, working sessions and stakeholder discussions in New York, as required. • The consultant must not share project details without written consent from UNJSPF, and must follow OIM data classification and information security rules. • The consultancy is administered by UNJSPF, and all relevant UNJSPF rules, policies and procedures apply.
Qualifications/special skills
Advanced university degree (master's or equivalent) in computer science, data science, engineering, finance or a related field. A first-level degree with additional qualifying experience may be accepted instead. Minimum 7 years of advanced data engineering, data modelling or data product delivery experience is required; 10 years or more is desirable. Direct experience with TPA, total fund, or total portfolio / multi-asset portfolio analytics, including total fund exposure, factor, risk, performance and liquidity views is required Experience with investment data at a pension fund, asset owner or large asset manager, covering public and private markets is required. Proven experience mapping data definitions to source systems and writing technical requirements is required. Experience translating business use cases into reusable data product requirements, source decisions and implementation priorities is required. Experience facilitating business and technical alignment across functions where definitions, source choices or implementation priorities require agreement is required Experience building or guiding interactive dashboard prototypes (Power BI and/or Sigma) from multiple sources is required. Ability to work across business lines and explain data topics clearly to non-technical senior stakeholders is required. SQL and Python; data modelling, semantic layer design, data warehouse and cloud data platform experience is required (Snowflake is an advantage). Power BI and/or Sigma is desirable. Familiarity with Bloomberg, MSCI Barra One, Burgiss, and custodian or accounting data is desirable.
Languages
Fluency in English is required.
Additional Information
Not available.
No Fee

Org. Setting and Reporting
This position is located in the Movement Control Unit of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), duty station Naqoura. The incumbent will report to the Chief of Unit, Movement Control or their designate.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Movement Control Assistant will be responsible for the following duties: Joint Movement Control Centre duties/Passenger Booking duties: Receives customer requests, through Movement of Personnel (MOP) and Cargo Movement Request (CMR) forms, for transportation of passengers and cargo (including dangerous goods requiring special handling) within and/or outside a field mission. Assists in planning and scheduling the movement of passengers and cargo from military and police units provided by Troop/Police Contributing Countries. Assists in determining the most efficient and cost-effective modes of transportation for passengers and cargo (including dangerous goods requiring special handling) within and/or outside a field mission Coordinates required transportation activities with the Aviation, Transport Units and/or commercial transportation service providers Liaises with other UN units/sections, non-government and government organizations and intergovernmental agencies on immigration and customs matters Assists in analyzing projected passenger and cargo flows in order to estimate required resources Records statistical data on the movement of passengers and cargo (including dangerous goods requiring special handling) within and/or outside a field mission Monitors contracts for the provision of transportation support and participates in the evaluation of vendor’s performance in coordination with the Contracts Management and/or the Procurement Unit. Cargo Warehouse duties: Supervises the activities of the Cargo Warehouse Monitors the process of excess personal luggage and cargo receipt and registration (including dangerous goods requiring special handling) Monitors the preparation of luggage and cargo for transportation and ensures that weighting, plastic wrapping and labelling are conducted in accordance with the established procedures. Ensures that luggage and cargo are labelled in accordance with required destinations Coordinates the transportation arrangements to the embarkation facility Airfield/Air Terminal/Transport/Riverine Movement Control Office duties: Supervises a team of movement control assistants, passenger clerks and cargo handlers Supervises the provision of passenger and cargo handling services (including dangerous goods requiring special handling) in support of a field mission from the established movement control facility and monitors that all activities are carried out in accordance with the UN rules, regulations and applicable safety procedures. Compiles passenger and cargo manifests and communicates them to the aircrew, surface transport and riverine personnel. Monitors that aircraft, vehicles and vessels are loaded in accordance with passenger and cargo manifests Briefs passengers on schedules, routes, timing and safety requirements Monitors check-in and check-out activities for outgoing and incoming passengers and cargo Participates in the in the integrated search and rescue operations for the UN assets and other assets upon request and coordinates the availability and operational readiness of the required personnel and equipment Administration and other duties: Maintains the electronic databases in accordance with the established procedures and deadlines Monitors that appropriate reference documents are current, readily available and accessible to all relevant personnel Participates int eh development of the standard operating procedures for the related movement control processes. Participates in the development of budget proposals for the mission’s movement control operations. Participates in the preparation of operational plans, performance reports, and response to internal and external audit observations Participates in the development of technical specifications for goods and services, provides inputs to the responses to bids and technical evaluations to ensure that vendor’s proposals meet technical requirements Conducts inventories and physical annual checks of relevant facilities and equipment. Performs other duties as required. In/Outbound Delivery Coordination duties: Assists in the coordination of in/outbound activities for freight into the mission in accordance with mission supply chain plan with Vendor, Procurement, Centralized Warehouse and all other parties concerned. Contacts vendor to confirm delivery status and to review shipment documents to secure that goods are delivered according to the agreed terms and conditions on the Purchase Order/ Assists with the collection, checking and updating of information (e.g. ETA, quantities, etc.) and documents (e.g. BoL, customs clearance, etc.), provided by commodity and freight forwarding vendors, in EROP system (Umoja) to facilitate downstream processes. Tracks and traces all deliveries and updates the Inbound Delivery with necessary information and shipment documents to provide all stakeholders with a constant status overview of incoming and Outgoing shipments. Search for issues which may delay and/or disturb the delivery of goods and seek for remedial solutions with all parties concerned (Procurement, Vendor, Centralized Warehouse) Confirms delivery dates and quantities received and provides delivery confirmation documents to support virtual and/or physical receipt in accordance to agreed Incoterms. Assists in planning Movements, raising shopping carts and drafting SOW for freight forwarding services, including technical evaluation of bids. Assists in the coordination of customs, transport and MOVCON activities, related to inbound and outbound shipments with vendors, customs and all other relevant local and national authorities. Ensure that daily activities are in compliance with the Environmental and Waste Management policies and in line with the Environment Strategy objectives
Competencies
PROFESSIONALISM: Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Knowledge of reverse logistics principles, processes, and operations. Ability to plan, coordinate, and oversee large-scale repatriation operations, ensuring the timely, safe, cost-effective, and efficient movement of personnel and cargo in complex and resource-constrained operational environments. COMMUNICATION: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; Listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; Asks questions to clarify and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; Tailors language, tone, style and format to match the audience; Demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. TEAMWORK: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. PLANNING AND ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently.
Education
High school diploma or equivalent is required.
Job - Specific Qualification
A valid IATA and/or IMO dangerous goods certificate is required. A valid driver's license license is required.
Work Experience
A minimum of eight (8) years of progressively responsible experience in movement control, multi-modal transportation, logistics management or a related field is required. Experience in the use of IATA and/or IMO rules and procedures for the transportation of dangerous goods including packaging and documentation is required. The Department of Operational Support was established to provide end-to-end operational support, advisory services and other solutions to operating entities across the Secretariat, including other departments, Offices Away from Headquarters, field missions, and regional commissions. The Uniformed Capabilities Support Division (UCSD) serves as the single point of entry within the Secretariat for operational and policy matters relating to support and reimbursement to military and police contingents deployed to United Nations field operations. Reimbursement payments to contributing countries are one of the largest costs of United Nations (UN) peacekeeping. RCMPS is responsible for administration of Troop/Police Contributing Countries reimbursement framework for Contingent-Owned Equipment (COE), Letter of Assist, Death and Disability, Personnel reimbursement processing and for ‘risk’ and ‘enabling’ premium. The section also leads on budget/cost center management, performance analysis and reporting, and IT systems (Uniformed Capabilities Management system (UCM) and Uniformed Capabilities Member States Portal) on major Equipment, Self-sustainment and Personnel. The Office of Supply Chain Management includes the Office of the Assistant Secretary-General for Supply Chain Management, the Logistics Division, the Procurement Division, Uniformed Capabilities Support Division, Global Service Centre, Aviation Safety Section and the Enabling and Outreach Service. Reimbursement payments to contributing countries are one of the largest costs of United Nations (UN) peacekeeping. Result of Service
• Supply Chain Diagnostic Assessment Report • Comprehensive assessment of current demand planning, forecasting, supply planning, inventory management, and identified gaps with recommendations for improvement. Demand Planning and Forecasting Framework • Standardized forecasting methodology, planning calendar, forecasting tools, governance structure, and KPIs to improve forecast accuracy across all UNRWA Fields. Supply Planning and Inventory Optimization Framework • Integrated supply planning process, inventory policies, safety stock methodology, min/max stock levels, replenishment parameters, and redistribution mechanisms. Implementation Roadmap and Capacity Building Package • Phased implementation plan (short, medium, and long term), SOPs, training materials, performance indicators, and recommendations for system and process enhancements to support sustainable implementation.
Work Location
HQ Amman
Expected duration
6 months
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Conduct a comprehensive review of the existing supply chain processes (with particular attention to medical supplies and other relevant inventory categories. Assess current forecasting methodologies, planning cycles, and replenishment practices. Analyze historical demand, consumption, procurement, and inventory data. Map current end-to-end planning processes and identify bottlenecks. Evaluate roles, responsibilities, and governance structures relating to supply planning. Benchmark current practices against WHO, UNICEF, and humanitarian supply chain standards. 2. Review forecasting approaches currently used across Field Offices and Health Programmes. Analyze forecasting accuracy and identify major drivers of demand variability. Propose a standardized demand planning methodology for medicines and medical supplies. Recommend forecasting models, segmentation approaches, and planning parameters. Establish forecast review and validation processes. Develop demand planning calendars and propose governance mechanisms. 3. Assess current supply planning and replenishment practices. Develop an integrated supply planning process aligned with procurement lead times and inventory policies. Recommend inventory planning parameters including: Safety stock, Reorder points Minimum and maximum stock levels Buffer stock requirements Recommend planning mechanisms for emergency and strategic stock management. Develop stock redistribution and balancing methodologies between locations. 4. Propose a future-state operating model for supply chain management. Recommend organizational structures and responsibilities for demand planning and supply planning functions. Propose decision-making governance and accountability frameworks. Develop a Planning and Supply Chain Control Tower concept to provide centralized visibility and coordination across UNRWA operations. 5. Conduct a comprehensive review of existing supply chain manuals, procedures, SOPs, guidelines and related operational instructions; identify gaps, inconsistencies, duplication and outdated provisions; and update and harmonize the documentation in line with applicable UNRWA policies, regulatory requirements and recognized good practices. Prepare a consolidated report and provide recommendations and report on the key updates and improvements introduced. 6. Review the human resources capacity and alignment with the operational workload, organizational requirements and evolving Logistics mandate. Assess actual workload, functional coverage, level of responsibility, duplication and gaps, in consultation with Human Recourses Management Services Division (HRMSD)-HRD in HQA.

An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) from an accredited educational institution in supply chain management, logistics, business administration or a related field A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) in a relevant field, combined with two additional years of relevant professional experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree A minimum of five years of progressively responsible and relevant professional experience in supply chain management, logistics, pharmaceutical logistics, health supply chains, inventory management, demand forecasting, or supply planning.

Very good knowledge of written and spoken English and Arabic.

Professional qualifications Knowledge of personal computer applications. Knowledge on supply and demand planning with previous organizations. Knowledge of SAP. The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) is the guardian of the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and the protocols thereto, which include the Trafficking in Persons and Smuggling of Migrants Protocols. UNODC is mandated to promote global adherence to the Protocols and to assist Member States in their efforts to effectively implement them. UNODC provides technical cooperation in assessing and strengthening national responses on prevention, investigation and prosecution of the crimes, developing international cooperation, and respecting the rights of migrants and victims of trafficking. The internship positions are located in the Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Section (HTMSS) of the Organized Crime and Illicit Trafficking Branch (OCB) of the Division for Treaty Affairs (DTA), United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), in Vienna. The Section is looking for several interns for its different teams (focusing inter alia on the delivery of technical cooperation, normative and policy work, knowledge development and innovation, survivor engagement and partnerships). The UNODC Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Section (HTMSS) works to advance the international agenda on countering trafficking in persons and the smuggling of migrants in all UN related inter-agency and inter-governmental processes and fora, and supports, among others, the activities relating to the provision of legislative assistance to UN Member States upon request. It further works to develop and disseminate knowledge on trafficking in persons and the smuggling of migrants through the publication of thematic and technical tools. Internships are UNPAID and full-time (40 hours, 5 days per week). The internships can be either in-person or home-based. For more information on UNODC, please visit our website: www.unodc.org This internship is located in the Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Section (HTMSS), Organized Crime and Illicit Trafficking Branch (OCB), Division of Treaty Affairs (DTA). Result of Service
The main objective of this study is to identify key sites for designing and implementing a variety of public spaces in Nahr el Bared camp. The study will ensure that public space projects implemented in the camp will work together in a complementary manner as part of a public spatial structure that can enrich the entire camps urban fabric – and is not an implementation of isolated public projects scattered across miscellaneous locations. It will also investigate what constitutes as successful public space within the specific realities in NBC and what are the main public space community needs through studying various realities and social practices on the ground today. This project will revisit the ideas on public space that were initially conceived in 2007-2009 (yet not implemented) in order to determine which of those ideas are still feasible, which need adaptation and what opportunities were missed. It will also factor in the tremendous developments that have been made in the past 18 years that will have significant impact on public space design and planning. These relate to changing social, economic, political and security related conditions within the camp and its surroundings. Three main Zones will be part of this investigation, the official UNRWA Nahr el Bared Camp; Edges/Borders of the official Nahr el Bared Camp; Adjacent Areas.

vacancies.jobTitle: UNEP Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) - Climate Transition Banking Implementation Expert
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
Through these services, the Initiative will be able to engage banks in implementing global finance sector principles to catalyse integration of sustainability into financial market practice. The consultant will assist members with their implementation of the Guidance for Climate Target Setting and associated climate guidance on target setting, policy engagement, transition planning and transition finance. UNEP FI supports signatories in implementing the Principles for Responsible Banking (PRB), now committed to by more than 350 banks collectively holding almost $100tn total assets, approximately half of the global banking sector assets. The services will also help promote sustainability into all aspects of the financial sector’s operations and services. The consultant’s work will also contribute to upholding UN core values, ensuring that human rights-based approach, the principle of leaving no one behind and gender equality and women’s empowerment are integrated throughout their work at UNEP FI.
Work Location
Working remotely / Home-based
Expected duration
12 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. UNEP’s work is firmly grounded in the UN core values, including the human rights-based approach, the commitment to leaving no one behind, and the promotion of gender equality and women’s empowerment across all activities. The overall objective of the UNEP’s Industry and Economy Division is to encourage decision makers in government, local authorities and industry to develop and adopt policies, strategies and practices and technologies that promote sustainable patterns of consumption and production, make efficient use of natural resources, ensure safe management of chemicals and contribute to making trade and environment policies mutually supportive. It promotes the development, use and transfer of policies, technologies, economic instruments, managerial practices and other tools that assist in environmentally sound decision making and the building of corresponding activities. The United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) is the strategic partnership between the United Nations and over 500 banks, insurers, and investors. For over 34 years UNEP FI has been shaping and driving the international sustainable finance agenda, setting global standards, and growing a global network of leading financial institutions. Through its work-streams and regional activities, peer learning, methodology development, training and research, UNEP FI promotes sustainable finance and helps the financial industry align with and contribute to the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals. Since the formation of Principles for Responsible Banking in September 2019, UNEP FI has been working with banks on climate mitigation. This work has involved co-developing with banks the Guidance for Climate Target Setting for Banks, associated sectoral target setting guidance for 9 sectors, guidance on transition finance, transition planning, and, more recently, guidance on real economy policy engagement. The Climate Transition Team at UNEP FI engages banks on how they can accelerate the climate transition and be best positioned to finance the economy of the future. We co-develop guidance in working groups, bring in expert voices to webinars, run technical sessions and provide peer learning opportunities. UNEP FI is looking for a sustainable finance expert to work with banks on technical work. i. Facilitate engagement with member banks to support progress towards their climate goals. ii. Support the work track in accordance with the workplan, including planning and facilitating meetings, working with members to develop approaches, tools and materials, running technical deep dives into priority areas. iii. Finalise the workplan for 2028 with banks and obtain sign off for this from the Leadership. Specific tasks and responsibilities: The consultant will assist in the following project/tasks for UNEP FI’s banking climate transition work: • Coordinate and support working group meetings with banks, preparing content, sharing with members and providing summaries of meetings. • Prepare reports that aim to assist banks’ implementation of climate mitigation work, drafting, coordinating bank inputs, and addressing bank representatives’ feedback. • Consider a strategy for bringing opportunities to banks on real economy policy engagement, targeting areas where the transition is held back due to policy barriers. • Arrange webinars and events with expert speakers, managing logistics, developing concept notes and content. • Arrange and prepare for meetings with co-leads, selected from the banking membership, to discuss the strategic direction of the work, what will be most useful for members and agree deliverables. • Assist with the review of the Guidelines for Climate Target Setting for Banks. • Project managing the delivery of the workplan for the climate transition track. • Ensure that all communications outputs reflect UNEP and UN core values, including human rights-based approach, the principle of leaving no one behind and gender equality and women’s empowerment, and contribute to internal awareness on these values. • Support the implementation of UNEP FI’s 2026–2029 Social Action Plan by including all relevant measures from the plan in their work. Outputs and Deliverables: • Recommendations for what UNEP FI can offer member banks to assist them with the development and implementation of their climate strategies. • Project managing and development of quality reports and guidance that are useful to and provide practical tools for banks. • Resources that support sustainability teams in working across their institutions, including front line banking and risk colleagues. • Webinars and events that deliver value to members, assisting them with their implementation. • Support the development of an ongoing programme of work for 2028. • Work closely with work track co-leads to further the aims of the track in supporting members to implement their climate commitments. • Liaise with the feedback and review team and advise on technical queries that may arise. • The above deliverables will be developed and implemented in alignment with UNEP FI’s Social Action Plan and guided by the UN’s core values. The consultant will report to: Overall supervisor: The Head of UNEP FI. Direct Supervisor: The Climate Transition Banking Lead, UNEP FI Close coordination: The candidate will work closely with the Climate Transition Implementation Lead and the Banking Team co-Leads.
Qualifications/special skills
Education: A master’s degree in economics, finance, environmental studies, international relations, business administration or related fields is required. A bachelor’s degree could be taken in lieu of master’s degree provided the selected candidate has 9 years of relevant experience. Professional Experience: At least seven (7) years of relevant experience is required, which may be in the public or private sector or with NGOs, examining the intersection between climate change and corporate impact, risk and opportunity. Experience of working on pathways for the alignment of real economy sectors with the goals of the Paris Agreement is desirable. Experience working with financial institutions, particularly banks, to assess their climate impact and develop transition strategies for Paris alignment is desirable.
Languages
Languages: English is the working language of UNEP FI. Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of other United Nations languages is an asset.
Additional Information
Skills & Knowledge: The candidate should have a proven and established track record on climate-change-related assessments and analyses, particularly from a financial services perspective. They should have in-depth knowledge of the various emerging approaches and methodologies to measure and set targets on climate alignment of financial, ideally banking, portfolios. They should understand the main issues around transition planning and transition finance. They should equally be familiar with the relevant ongoing discussions and institutions involved in this space. They should have a deep understanding of topics at the interface of climate change (or similar environmental challenges) and corporate/financial strategies. The candidate should be experienced in facilitating collaborative working groups with different stakeholder types, particularly on the theme and challenge of climate change, and particularly in the financial services industry.

Result of Service
This assignment strengthens the collaboration between UNDRR, MINEMA and UN Women. The primary objective is to design, validate, and deliver a comprehensive, actionable, and budgeted National GEDSI DRR Strategy for Rwanda. The strategy must operationalize UN Women’s localized assessment data and guidelines while aligning directly with the water-centric goals, multi-hazard early warning benchmarks, and community-resilience targets of the Water at the Heart of Climate Action project.
Work Location
Home based
Expected duration
3 months
Duties and Responsibilities
Background: Created in December 1999, the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) is the designated focal point in the United Nations system for the coordination of efforts to reduce disasters and to ensure synergies among the disaster risk reduction activities of the United Nations and regional organizations and activities in both developed and less developed countries. Led by the United Nations Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Disaster Risk Reduction (SRSG), UNDRR has over 150 staff located in its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, and in regional offices. Specifically, UNDRR guides, monitors, analyses and reports on progress in the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030, supports regional and national implementation of the Framework and catalyses action and increases global awareness to reduce disaster risk working with U.N. Member States and a broad range of partners and stakeholders, including civil society, the private sector, parliamentarians and the science and technology community. Climate change in Rwanda manifests predominantly through water-related hazards. The country experiences a high frequency of destructive floods, water-induced landslides in mountainous terrains, and prolonged droughts that threaten both food and water security. Vulnerable groups, including women, children, youth, elderly populations, and Persons with Disabilities, frequently experience the worst impacts of these water-related shocks due to unequal access to resources, adaptive capacities, and early warning information. To address these vulnerabilities, this assignment is launched under the regional "Water at the Heart of Climate Action" (WHCA) project. This initiative focuses on protecting vulnerable communities from water-related climate hazards through integrated water resources management, climate-smart water services, and inclusive early warning systems. This assignment will be implemented in close coordination with UN Women in Rwanda. In Rwanda, UN Women is currently conducting a localized Gender-Sensitive Disaster Risk Assessment in high-risk districts and is developing a Roadmap for Strengthening Gender-Responsive Disaster Risk Reduction and Inclusive Early Warning Systems. The two assignments are designed to be complementary: the UN Women assessment generates the evidence base and district-level roadmap, while the present assignment translates that evidence into a national strategy. UNDRR, as an executing partner of the "Water at the Heart of Climate Action" project, is collaborating with MINEMA to scale up these localized insights into a comprehensive Rwanda GEDSI DRR Strategy that links water security, climate adaptation, and social inclusion. The assessment covers case study districts in the Western Province and additional districts in other provinces so that the evidence base reflects the diversity of hazards affecting Rwanda, including floods, landslides, drought and storms, and the different risk and vulnerability contexts across the country. This assignment will build directly on the UN WOMEN assessment, using its findings, recommendations and roadmap as the evidence base for the Rwanda GEDSI DRR strategy, validating and operationalizing them through broader national consultation. The Strategy will be anchored in the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Policy, the National Gender Policy and MIGEPROF gender mainstreaming frameworks, and will contribute to Rwanda's commitments under the Sendai Framework, the Paris Agreement and the Sustainable Development Goals. This Rwanda GEDSI DRR strategy will be aligned with the UNDRR Sendai Gender Action Plan and forthcoming UNDRR Gender Equality and Disability Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan (GEDI-SAP) 2026–2030. Scope of Work The consultant will execute the following technical tasks: ● Water-Climate-GEDSI Nexus Desk Review: Synthesize the UN Women GEDSI assessments and localized DRR/EWS roadmaps, specifically analysing how water-related hazards (floods, landslides, droughts and storms) uniquely interact with gender dynamics, age, and disability, and review UNDRR GEDSI materials ● Institutional Project Alignment: Ensure the strategy structurally aligns with the overarching objectives of the Water at the Heart of Climate Action regional project, Rwanda's National Water Resources Management policies, MINEMA's Strategic Plan, and Rwanda's NDC climate targets. Alignment will also be ensured with the National Disaster Risk Management Policy, the National Climate Change Policy, the National Adaptation Plan (NAP), the National Gender Policy and the Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS) Strategy. ● Multi-Stakeholder Consultations: Facilitate strategic key informant interviews (KIIs) and focus group discussions (FGDs) with MINEMA, the Ministry of Environment (MoE), the Rwanda Water Resources Board (RWB), the Rwanda Meteo Agency, Ministry of Gender and Family Promotion (MIGEPROF), CSOs, and Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs). Consultations will also include the National Council of Persons with Disabilities (NCPD), the National Women's Council, the Rwanda Red Cross, District Disaster Management Committees in selected case study districts, and development partners supporting DRR and climate resilience. ● Inclusive EWS Strategy Formulation: Draft a five-year Rwanda GEDSI-DRR Strategy that treats water-security and inclusive, multi-hazard Early Warning Systems (EWS) as central pillars—ensuring hydrometeorological alerts are accessible to all, including individuals with sensory, physical, or cognitive disabilities. The Strategy will apply the four pillars of the Early Warnings for All (EW4All) initiative, ensuring that risk knowledge, detection and forecasting, warning dissemination and preparedness to respond are all designed inclusively. ● Action Plan and Budgeting Architecture: Develop a realistic, costed national implementation plan with a specialized Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) framework tracking sex, age, and disability-disaggregated data (SADDD) for water-disaster response and adaptation. ● National Validation Workshops: Lead technical validation sessions to consolidate and incorporate final institutional feedback from project steering committees, ministerial representatives, and civil society partners. This consultancy is home-based, and the consultant will work under the overall supervision of the Programme Management Officer at the Regional Office for Africa
Qualifications/special skills
An advanced degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Disaster Risk Management, Water Resources Management, Environmental Sciences, Gender Studies, Development Studies, or any other relevant field is required. A first-level university degree in any of these fields in combination with two additional years of qualifying work experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Five (5) years of progressive experience in developing national-level strategic policies within DRR, climate change adaptation, or environmental governance is required. Technical expertise in integrating GEDSI/Gender-responsive methodologies into water management, climate resilience, or emergency frameworks is required. An understanding of the water-climate nexus, hydrometeorological risks, and inclusive Early Warning Systems (EWS) is desirable. Experience working alongside UN agencies (e.g. UNDRR, WMO, UNICEF, UN Women) and national line ministries (e.g. MINEMA) in Sub-Saharan Africa is desirable. Experience working in Rwanda is desirable. Experience facilitating high-level policy consultations and validation workshops with senior government officials, communities and stakeholders is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this position fluency in English is required.
Additional Information
Due to the high volume of applications received, only successful candidates will be contacted.

Org. Setting and Reporting
UNRWA is a United Nations agency established by the General Assembly in 1949 and is mandated to provide assistance and protection to a population of some 5.8 million registered Palestine refugees. Its mission is to help Palestine refugees in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, West Bank and the Gaza Strip to achieve their full potential in human development, pending a just solution to their plight. UNRWA’s services encompass education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure and improvement, microfinance, and emergency assistance. UNRWA is the largest UN operation in the Middle East with more than 30,000 staff. UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions. If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to make a tangible difference for one of the most vulnerable communities in the world, UNRWA would like to hear from you. The incumbent is responsible to the Branch Manager.

Work Location
Bangkok Thailand
Expected duration
3 - 6 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) is the most inclusive intergovernmental platform in the Asia-Pacific region. The Commission promotes cooperation among its 52 member States and 9 associate members in pursuit of solutions to sustainable development challenges. ESCAP is one of the five regional commissions of the United Nations. The ESCAP secretariat supports inclusive, resilient and sustainable development in the region by generating action-oriented knowledge, and by providing technical assistance and capacity- building services in support of national development objectives, regional agreements and the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. ESCAP also provides support to partners at the national level. ESCAP's national offer is rooted in and linked with the implementation of global and regional intergovernmental frameworks, agreements, and other instruments. This position is located in the Communications and Knowledge Management Section (CKMS), in the Office of the Deputy Executive Secretary for Programme Support (ODESPS). The intern works under the direct supervision of library support staff and the overall supervision of the Chief Librarian. This internship is unpaid for a minimum of 3 months and maximum of 6 months and designed to be full-time (37.5 hours per week). The duration and modality can be adjusted on request of the successful candidate. The intern will support the Library and the CKMS team in various tasks related to library, information, and knowledge management to raise the visibility of library resources among staff and clients and ESCAP work among key stakeholders and the public. Daily responsibilities will depend on the individual's background as well as the internship period. Duties may include, but are not limited to: - Assisting in reviewing document retention policies - Taking part in the Library’s filing and knowledge management tasks and initiatives - Assisting in collection management activities (shelving, weeding, etc.) - Assisting in reference and circulation services - Designing and publishing publicity and training materials on the Library's e-resources, services and ESCAP publications, including online brochures, streaming video presentations, and curated email updates - Taking part in the Library's information management, knowledge management, and digital asset management tasks and initiatives - Assisting in organizing the storage area - Performing other related work, as required
Qualifications/special skills
Applicants must meet one of the following requirements: (a) be enrolled in, or have completed, a graduate school programme (second university degree or equivalent, or higher); (b) be enrolled in, or have completed, the final academic year of a first university degree programme (minimum bachelor's degree or equivalent). c) have studied administration or knowledge management is desirable. Applicants to the UN Internship Programme are not required to have professional work. However, a field of study that is closely related to the type of internship that you are applying for is required. Applicants must be a student in the final year of the first university degree (bachelor or equivalent), Master's or Ph.D. Programme or equivalent, or have completed a Bachelor's, Master's or PH.D. Programme. Do you meet any of the above criteria? If yes, please indicate which one and attach proof to the application. Please note that you will have to provide an official certificate at a later stage. Applicants must have good knowledge of standard software applications, especially MS Word, MS PowerPoint, ​and MS Teams
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. Fluency in English (both oral and written) is required for the internship programme
Additional Information
Not available.
Intern Specific text
Interns are not financially remunerated by the United Nations. Costs and arrangements for travel, visas, accommodation and living expenses are the responsibility of interns or their sponsoring institutions. Interns who are not citizens or permanent residents of the country where the internship is undertaken, may be required to obtain the appropriate visa and work/employment authorization. Result of Service
The consultant will provide high-quality technical expertise to support the implementation of the aforementioned projects through the design and delivery of technical assistance activities, capacity-building workshops, and regional awareness-raising materials on TIP for FC in scam operations. The consultant will also develop technical guidance and knowledge products, prepare high-quality reports and briefing materials for donors and counterparts, and provide technical support to ASEAN activities and relevant stakeholders to strengthen regional cooperation and criminal justice responses to TIP for FC.
Work Location
Home-based with travel to Southeast Asia countries
Expected duration
1 December 2026 - 30 September 2027
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Background of the assignment: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) provides technical assistance related to combating transnational organized crime, including on trafficking in persons (TIP) and smuggling of migrants (SOM), to requesting Member States. This assistance also aims to strengthen criminal justice systems of States and encourages ratification and successful implementation of international conventions and protocol related to transnational organized crime, in compliance with the rule of law and human rights. TIP and SOM are significant forms of transnational crime affecting the Southeast Asia and Pacific region and are key areas of UNODC’s regional work. As the guardian of the Protocol against the Smuggling of Migrants by Land, Sea, and Air and the Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, especially Women and Children, which supplement the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime, UNODC promotes global adherence to these instruments and assists States in their efforts to effectively implement them and combat the conduct that they criminalize. UNODC focuses, in particular, on assisting states in developing an effective criminal justice response to these crime challenges. The Regional Programme for Southeast Asia and the Pacific 2022 – 2026 is designed to address both present and emerging needs within these regions, with the ultimate objective, namely to secure and reinforce the rule of law in Southeast Asia and the Pacific and ensure vulnerable groups and communities in the region are protected from crime. Within this framework, UNODC’s Regional Office for Southeast Asia and the Pacific (ROSEAP) implements a number of projects addressing TIP and SOM, including initiatives responding to the rapidly evolving threat of trafficking for forced criminality (TIP for FC) linked to scam operations. These projects include: • Strengthening International Legal Cooperation on Transnational TIP Cases • Building Awareness for Coordinated Response to TIP for Forced Criminality • Enhanced screening and protection of victims of trafficking for forced criminality • Ensuring Decent Work and Reducing Vulnerabilities for Women and Children in the Context of Labour Migration in Southeast Asia (PROTECT) UNODC ROSEAP is going to undertake various TIP SOM activities, including stakeholder engagement, workshops, awareness raising campaigns, and trainings related to TIP and SOM, and is seeking a consultant to support their implementation. 2. Purpose of the assignment: The purpose of the assignment is to work closely with the Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Team at ROSEAP to support the implementation of TIP SOM project activities under the Regional Programme. 3. Specific tasks to be performed by the Consultant: Under the supervision of the Regional Coordinator for Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling, the consultant will undertake the following substantive tasks: • Contribute to the planning, oversight, implementation, management and delivery of technical assistance of the TIP SOM project activities, including through the organization and delivery of workshops, forums, clinics, and trainings as well as the preparation of substantive inputs for capacity development initiatives, under the above-mentioned projects; • Liaise and support activities with relevant ASEAN sectoral bodies (including SOMTC and its Working Groups) on TIP, including regional cooperation and policy development; • Support the design, coordination, and implementation of awareness-raising campaigns, including developing innovative approaches, technical materials, and implementation strategies; • Draft and review reports, guidance materials, project documents, concept notes, and other substantive outputs, ensuring high technical quality and consistency with UNODC standards; • Support the design and development of knowledge projects and briefing materials relating to TIP SOM, particularly TIP for FC; • Prepare briefings, presentations, and other materials on topics related to TIP and SOM, particularly TIP for FC.
Qualifications/special skills
- An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in business administration, governance, international relations, law or international relations or related field is required. A first level university degree in similar fields in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. - A minimum of five (5) of professional relevant experience in project management, coordinating and organizing capacity building workshops and trainings, including experience in the areas of human trafficking, migrant smuggling, and / or transnational organized crime at national, regional and international levels, is required. - Field-based work experience in developing and implementing TIP and SOM capacity building projects in Southeast Asia and the Pacific is required. - Experience engaging with ASEAN and ASEAN bodies (e.g. SOMTC; Working Groups) in the area of TIP and/or SOM is required. - Experience of liaising with mid- to high-level Southeast Asian government officials is required. - Demonstrated knowledge on trafficking in persons for forced criminality in scam centres is required. - Professional experience working within the United Nations system or other international organizations in Southeast Asia is required - Experience working with law enforcement and/or criminal justice practitioners in Southeast Asia is desirable. - Experience with donor relations, particularly Australia, the EU and the United States, is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this position, fluency in English, with excellent drafting and communication skills, is required. Knowledge of another United Nations official language is an advantage.

Not available.

Org. Setting and Reporting
