Result of Service
Effective and timely implementation of the South Sudan component of the EU Operational Support to the IGAD Platform in Aweil and surrounding areas, supported by coordinated field activities, meaningful stakeholder and community engagement, reliable field data and progress reporting, and strengthened local capacities in spatial planning, housing, land and property rights, and area-based durable solutions.
Work Location
Aweil
Expected duration
6 months
Duties and Responsibilities
BACKGROUND The United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is the United Nations agency mandated by the General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities, with the goal of providing adequate shelter for all. In October 2016, at the United Nations Conference on Housing and Sustainable Urban Development (Habitat III), Member States adopted the New Urban Agenda, an action-oriented framework that sets global standards for sustainable urban development and guides how cities are planned, managed, and lived in. Through partnerships with governments and other stakeholders, UN-Habitat advances sustainable urbanization, inclusive governance, climate resilience, and access to adequate housing, land, and basic services. UN-Habitat, in partnership with UNHCR, is implementing the EU Operational Support to the IGAD Platform, a regional programme covering Ethiopia, South Sudan, Sudan, and the IGAD region. The programme aims to strengthen the capacity of governments, institutions, and communities to address the challenges associated with forced displacement, return movements, and rapid urbanization, while promoting sustainable development and resilience. South Sudan continues to face complex humanitarian and development challenges driven by protracted displacement, climate-related shocks, rapid urban growth, and limited institutional capacities. In response, the programme supports integrated approaches that strengthen governance systems, advance housing, land and property (HLP) rights, empower local communities, and improve access to climate-resilient and environmentally sustainable services. Within South Sudan, the programme places particular emphasis on supporting displacement-affected communities and host populations in Aweil, Northern Bahr el Ghazal State. Through a long term urban and humanitarian-development nexus approach, the programme seeks to enhance institutional and community capacities to manage displacement and return dynamics while fostering inclusive, climate-resilient, and sustainable urban development. Interventions focus on improving local planning processes, strengthening land governance, promoting durable solutions, and supporting sustainable service delivery that contribute to social cohesion, resilience, and long-term development outcomes. To support the effective implementation of the South Sudan component of the EU Operational Support to the IGAD Platform, UN-Habitat seeks to engage a National Field Officer (Individual Contractor) based in Aweil, South Sudan. Under the guidance of the International Project Manager, the National Field Officer will support field implementation and coordination, provide technical inputs, facilitate stakeholder and community engagement, and support alignment of project activities with area-based durable solutions approaches.. The incumbent will play a key role in ensuring the successful implementation of the South Sudan component of the EU Operational Support to the IGAD Platform in Aweil and surrounding areas. Responsibilities This position is based in Aweil, South Sudan, within the Regional Office for Africa and the Sub-Regional Unit for Horn and Eastern Africa for UN-Habitat. Under the direct supervision of the International Project Manager based in Juba, South Sudan, and with technical guidance from the International Coordinator based in Nairobi, Kenya, the National Field Officer will undertake the following tasks: Field Coordination and Partnerships • Prepare regular field progress reports for the International Project Manager, with inputs to the International Coordinator as required, covering activities completed, progress against planned outputs, implementation challenges, lessons learned and recommended follow-up actions. • Serve as UN-Habitat’s field focal point in Aweil, maintaining regular communication with state and local authorities, communities, implementing partners and the Juba-based programme team. • Maintain effective working relationships with government counterparts, UNHCR, IOM and other partners, and participate in area-based coordination meetings in Aweil and surrounding areas to support coordinated implementation. • Participate in relevant field-level coordination forums, technical meetings and stakeholder consultations, and represent UN-Habitat when designated by the International Project Manager. Programme Implementation and Field Support • Coordinate field activities and support project missions in Aweil and other designated project locations in South Sudan, providing technical, operational and logistical support in collaboration with government counterparts, communities and humanitarian and development partners. • Support the implementation, monitoring, and reporting of project activities related to urban development, spatial planning, HLP, land tenure, and durable solutions. • Coordinate field activities with the Team in Juba and/ or with implementing partners, to ensure timely delivery of outputs. • Coordinate with government counterparts, UN agencies, implementing partners, consultants, and other stakeholders to support effective project implementation and partnership engagement. • Monitor progress against approved workplans and project outputs, provide technical inputs within the scope of the assignment, and report implementation issues requiring action by the International Project Manager, including matters relating to donor requirements and UN-Habitat standards • Organize and facilitate validation workshops, bilateral meetings and coordination sessions with government counterparts, partners and community representatives, and document agreed actions for follow-up. Capacity Building and Data Management • Support and facilitate training and capacity-building activities for local authorities and community stakeholders on spatial planning, HLP rights, land tenure, and participatory planning approaches. • Facilitate gender-responsive community consultations, participatory planning processes and stakeholder engagement, ensuring the meaningful participation of women, youth, persons with disabilities and displacement-affected and host communities. • Ensure that community priorities and feedback are reflected in programme activities and technical outputs • Coordinate data collection, mapping, verification, and validation exercises to support project planning and implementation. • Provide technical support for the preparation and validation of assessments, planning documents, and other project deliverables. • Contribute to the development of guidance materials, tools, and knowledge products that strengthen local institutional capacities. Programme Development Support • Contribute field information, stakeholder feedback and lessons learned to support the development of UN-Habitat’s programmes in South Sudan. • Support the identification of potential funding opportunities and contribute technical inputs to concept notes and funding proposals, under the guidance of the International Project Manager and International Coordinator.
Qualifications/special skills
Advanced university degrees (master’s or equivalent) in Urban Planning, Urban Management, Public Administration, Local Governance, Development Studies, or a related field is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced degree. A minimum of two (2) years of progressively responsible experience in local governance, field coordination, programme implementation or urban development is required. Experience working with local authorities and communities in South Sudan, including knowledge of local governance structures and the displacement context, is required. Experience working with United Nations agencies, international organizations or multi-partner programmes is desirable. Experience supporting urban development initiatives in humanitarian or displacement settings is desirable.
Languages
Fluency in spoken and written English is required. Knowledge of Dinka is desirable.

Not available.

Work Location
Montreal
Expected duration
This internship is for a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 6 months and designed to be in person, at the office of the MLF Secretariat, in Montreal, Canada. Desired start date is 18 January 2027. Full time - five days per week (35-40 hours).
Duties and Responsibilities
Organizational Setting and Reporting: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. The Multilateral Fund for the Implementation of the Montreal Protocol (MLF) supports projects to reverse the deterioration of the Earth's stratospheric ozone layer and reducing consumption of high global warming hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs). It was established in 1991 as the financial mechanism of the Montreal Protocol to assist developing countries (Article 5 countries in the language of the Protocol) in complying with their obligations under the Montreal Protocol. The Multilateral Fund is managed by an Executive Committee (ExCom) with an equal representation of seven industrialized and seven Article 5 countries that are elected annually by the Meeting of the Parties. The Committee reports every year to the Meeting of the Parties on its operations, and it is assisted by the Fund Secretariat, located in Montreal, Canada and administered by UNEP (www.multilateralfund.org). This internship is located in UNEP/MLF at the Montreal duty station. Interns work five days per week (35-40 hours) under the supervision of a staff member in the department or office to which they are assigned. Have demonstrated keen interest in the work of the United Nations and have a personal commitment to the ideals of the Charter. Have a demonstrated ability to successfully interact with individuals of different cultural backgrounds and beliefs, which include willingness to try and understand and be tolerant of differing opinions and views. Interns are not financially remunerated by the United Nations. Costs and arrangements for travel, visas, accommodation and living expenses are the responsibility of interns or their sponsoring institutions. The Multilateral Fund Secretariat is offering an internship with a start date of 18 January 2027, for a minimum duration of 3 months and a maximum duration of up to 6 months. Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Chief Officer, the intern will provide assistance to the Multilateral Fund Secretariat with the following duties and responsibilities: - Research, compile, analyse, summarize and present relevant data and information for the preparation of documents to be submitted to the meetings of the Executive Committee of the Multilateral Fund and the Interagency Coordination meetings; - Collect, compile and analyse data and information related to the activities of the Montreal Protocol and the Kigali Amendment, including those supported by the Multilateral Fund; - Prepare lists, tables and charts for use in the review of project submissions and preparation of project documents for consideration by the Executive Committee; - Assist with the extraction, analysis and preparation of datasets for migration of relevant data and information from existing databases to the new Secretariat’s Knowledge Management System (KMS); - Assist the KMS team, in consultation with relevant staff members, with the testing of the various solutions and features of the KMS, and with entering data and information in the various portals and dashboards, as required; - Assist with the coordination of relevant activities and the content creation and update of the Multilateral Fund website, and with the preparation of content and material for the meeting portal and the Multilateral Fund’s decisions handbook (QuiriO3); - Assist, in consultation with relevant staff members, with the development of country profiles for all Article 5 countries, and input the KMS, as required; - Provide support in the organisation and holding of meetings of the Executive Committee and any other events of the Multilateral Fund Secretariat; and - Assist with any other tasks, as required.

Be enrolled in a graduate school programme (second university degree or equivalent, or higher); b. Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (minimum Bachelor’s level or equivalent); c. Keen interest in the work of the United Nations and personal commitment to the ideals of the United Nations Charter; d. The ability to interact with individuals of different cultural backgrounds and beliefs. Have demonstrated keen interest in the work of the United Nations and have a personal commitment to the ideals of the Charter. Have a demonstrated ability to successfully interact with individuals of different cultural backgrounds and beliefs, which include willingness to try and understand and be tolerant of differing opinions and views. Applicants to the UN Internship Programme are not required to have professional work experience. However, a field of study that is closely related to the type of internship that you are applying for is required. Applicants must be a student in the final year of the first university degree (Bachelor or equivalent), Master’s or Ph.D. Programme or equivalent, or have completed a Bachelor’s, Master’s or PH.D. Programme. Do you meet any of the above criteria? If yes, please indicate which one and attach proof to the application. Please note that you will have to provide an official certificate at a later stage. Applicants should have proficiency in computer skills (good knowledge of standard software applications, especially MS Word, MS PowerPoint, MS Teams, and Excel), use of databases, population of websites, web-based platforms and relevant software. Ability to draft website content, stories and articles is desirable. Ability to design surveys and polls is desirable.
Languages

Knowledge of an additional official UN language is an advantage. Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish are the official languages of the United Nations Secretariat.

Duties and Responsibilities
The Central Planning and Coordination Division (CPCD) serves as the central coordinating body within the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management (DGACM), providing strategic planning, coordination and support for the scheduling and servicing of United Nations meetings and conferences. CPCD is also responsible for the preparation and publication of the Journal of the United Nations, which provides the official daily record of meetings and activities at United Nations Headquarters. The United Nations Secretariat is seeking a motivated intern to support project-based activities within the Office of the Director, CPCD, DGACM, in New York. The Journal of the United Nations provides a comprehensive and historical record of daily activities and meetings at United Nations Headquarters. This internship is intended to provide participants with practical exposure to information management, digital publishing, knowledge management and innovation initiatives supporting the Journal Unit. The duration of the internship is six (6) months. This internship is UNPAID, in person and full-time (35 hours per week), on the United Nations premises in New York. Under the guidance of the CPCD Office of the Director Senior Programme Management Officer, interns may participate in learning and project assignments that include: - Learning about the editorial, publication and dissemination processes of the Journal of the United Nations. - Assisting with the preparation and updating of instructional presentations, user guides, onboarding materials and training resources related to Journal operations. - Participating in projects designed to document Journal workflows, business processes and knowledge resources. - Assisting with the preparation of standard operating procedures (SOPs), process documentation and reference materials. - Contributing to projects that support organizational knowledge sharing, user support and continuous improvement initiatives. - Participating in projects involving the organization and management of digital records, electronic documents and Journal-related repositories. - Assisting with initiatives related to the archiving and organization of Journal PDF collections and historical documentation. - Gaining exposure to Microsoft 365 tools, SharePoint, Microsoft Copilot and other technologies used to support collaboration, information management and productivity. - Participating in projects that explore opportunities to improve information-management workflows, document organization and knowledge-sharing practices through the use of digital tools and emerging technologies. - Assisting with the review, organization and analysis of information used in dashboards, reports, presentations and other knowledge products. - Contributing to change-management and user-experience initiatives designed to improve access to information and resources. - Assisting with the preparation of briefing materials, presentations, reports and project documentation. - Participating in meetings, workshops and knowledge-sharing activities relevant to the work of DGACM and the Journal Unit. - The UNIC is responsible for promoting public understanding and support for the aims and activities of the United Nations by communicating about its work and disseminating UN information materials to a local audience in English and local languages, including Nepali; engaging local and regional partners; and, overall, bringing the United Nations closer to the peoples it serves. The UNIC Kathmandu has been integrated with the Resident Coordinator Office (RCO) in Nepal since the operationalization of the United Nations development system reform on 1 January 2019. The incumbent reports directly to the Chief of Office of the RCO in Nepal and is under the general supervision of the Director, UNIC New Delhi.

branding strategy, support the UNCT Communication and Advocacy Group (UNCAG) with the development and implementation of country-wide strategic communications plans, campaigns and activities targeted to local audiences, in consultation with the RCO, and/or UN partners as well as with DGC UNHQ. • Takes a leading role on communications issues within the UNCT by serving as the Secretariat for the UNCAG at the country level in consultation with DGC UNHQ and the RCO. • Provides substantive support to the Resident Coordinator and UN Country Team (UNCT) in designing, implementing and monitoring implementing UN development activities in the country, in support of the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. • Provides substantive support to the RC and UNCT, UN Programme activities and its operational requirements, including its budget and equipment; monitors the output of the UNIC and reports to DGC UNHQ and RC/O on a monthly, quarterly, annual and ad hoc basis. • Performs other functions and special duties as required by the Director of CCOD, the Chief of ICS/CCOD, and/or the UN Resident Coordinator, including providing crisis communications support; representing the UN at conferences; participating in seminars; coordinating and drafting op-eds, speeches and interviews including for the Resident Coordinator.

The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. UNEP is implementing a Digital Portfolio Overhaul to modernize and streamline its web ecosystem. The work includes enhancement of the corporate website, rollout of the UNEP Starter Kit, migration of child, campaign and project websites, improved search and content discovery, strengthened multilingual functionality and consistent technical standards across UNEP web platforms. Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the voice for the environment within the United Nations system, acting as a catalyst, advocate, educator, and facilitator to promote sustainable development through the effective use of the global environment. Its Industry and Economy Division (IED) plays a leading role in the Green Economy Initiative, which aims to shift national economies towards a sustainable trajectory. By doing so, it seeks to ensure growth is driven by increased investment in green sectors and a shift of consumers’ preferences toward sustainable goods and services. Located within this Division, the Finance and Economics Branch examines the manner in which economics, trade, and finance interact with the environment, thereby contributing to sustainable development at the local, national, regional, and global levels. It does so by working with countries through analytical studies in partnerships with UN agencies, intergovernmental institutions, governments, academic institutes, businesses, and civil society organizations to support the shift to an inclusive green economy. Among its areas of work, the Economic and Fiscal Policy Unit (EFPU) supports global efforts on green fiscal policy reforms by advising countries on how fiscal policies can support the inclusive green economy and thus the delivery of the Sustainable Development Goals across different sectors. Tasks: •Support programmatic tasks related to project design, implementation, monitoring, and reporting for projects on issues such as but not limited to net-zero and nature-positive integration as well as sustainable fiscal policy and public finance; •Support policy research and advocacy work related to the area of sustainable fiscal policy and public policy, which includes but is not limited to harmful subsidies, specifically those related to agriculture and fossil fuels, and sustainable budgeting. •Support the communications efforts of UNEP EFPU and the Green Fiscal Policy Network; •Support the programmatic, policy, and communications needs of the unit. •Support the team and unit with other activities as requested.

vacancies.postingTitle: International Environmental and Social Safeguards Expert
vacancies.jobTitle: International Environmental and Social Safeguards Expert
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
The ultimate result of the service is a strengthened and operational environmental and social safeguards framework for the Comoros Ecosystem-based Adaptation project, enabling planned project activities to proceed in compliance with UNEP/GEF safeguards requirements. Specifically, the assignment will result in strengthened project and site-specific safeguards screening, operationalisation of the approved Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), identification and preparation and/or review of the required site-specific safeguard instruments, strengthened Terms of Reference for priority technical studies and ESIAs, and enhanced capacity of the project safeguards specialist to implement, monitor and report on ESS requirements. These outputs will support informed decision-making, reduce environmental and social risks, and facilitate the timely and safeguards-compliant implementation of higher-risk activities, particularly under Component 2.
Work Location
Home Based
Expected duration
2.5 months
Duties and Responsibilities
Purpose The purpose of this assignment is to provide specialised international environmental and social safeguards (ESS) expertise to the GEF/LDCF-financed Comoros Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA) project. The consultant will strengthen the project’s ESS risk screening, support the operationalisation of the approved Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), including through additional site-specific safeguards screening and the preparation and/or review of required ESIAs, ESMPs and other management instruments, support the review and completion of Terms of Reference for required feasibility studies and ESIAs, and build the capacity of the project’s safeguards specialist. The assignment will help ensure that planned project interventions, particularly higher-risk activities under Component 2 (2.1.1 and 2.1.2), are implemented in accordance with UNEP/GEF environmental and social safeguard requirements and can proceed to procurement and implementation. Background The project "Strengthening the Climate Resilience of Coastal Areas of the Comoros through Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA)" is a full-size project of the Global Environment Facility (GEF), funded by the Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF) and implemented by UNEP in partnership with the Direction Générale de l'Environnement et des Forêts (DGEF) of the Ministry of Environment and Tourism (MET) of the Union of the Comoros. The Project Management Unit, located within DGEF, is comprises of a National Project coordinator, a Financial and Administrative Officer, a Monitoring & Evaluation Officer, a Gender and Environmental and Social Safeguard Officer and Communication Expert. The project (GEF ID 11111) operates across four coastal sites on three islands of the archipelago — Grande Comore (Site 1: Iconi/M'bachile), Mohéli (Site 2: Hoani/Mbatsé) and Anjouan (Site 3: Mutsamudu/Ouani; Site 4: Bimbini) — over a five-year period (2025–2029). It directly benefits approximately 141,541 people (49.1% women). The project is organised around four components: • Component 1: Integrated planning and capacity building for adaptation (Community Development Plans, Watershed Management Plans, vulnerability assessments). • Component 2: Implementation of EbA interventions and soft coastal engineering (mangrove restoration, ecological continuity, living breakwaters, agroecology, sustainable fisheries, stabilised earth bricks). • Component 3: Development of the blue economy and support to climate-resilient MSMEs. • Component 4: Knowledge management, communication and institutionalisation. Component 2 represents the largest share of the budget (USD 4.2 million, i.e. 47% of the GEF grant) and concentrates the activities with the highest ESS risk. It is in this context that the present ESS expert mission is situated. The project was approved at CEO Endorsement with three safeguard documents attached to the SRIF: an Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF, Annex F/Appendix 5f), a Gender Action Plan and a Stakeholder Engagement Plan. No ESIA, site-specific ESMP, Indigenous Peoples Plan or Cultural Heritage Plan was prepared at that stage. The SRIF, cleared by UNEP in June 2024, rated the project Moderate risk overall. Five standards were rated moderate: • SS1 Biodiversity, ecosystems and sustainable natural resource management (impact 3, probability 2) • SS2 Climate change and disaster risks (3/2) • SS3 Pollution prevention and resource efficiency (3/3) • SS4 Community health, safety and security (3/3) • SS6 Displacement and involuntary resettlement (3/2) Cultural heritage, Indigenous Peoples and labour were rated low. The SRIF also required an ESMP and project-specific ESIAs once the interventions were defined. Duties and Responsibilities Under the overall supervision of the UNEP Task Manager and the direct supervision of the Chief Technical Adviser (CTA), in coordination with the Project Manager and the project Gender and Environmental and Social Safeguards Specialist (GESS), the International Environmental and Social Safeguards Expert will provide specialized technical support to strengthen the environmental and social safeguards framework of the GEF/LDCF-financed Comoros Ecosystem-based Adaptation project. The consultant will undertake a detailed review of the project’s environmental and social risks, conduct field-based verification of priority intervention sites, strengthen project and site-specific safeguard screening, support the operationalization of the approved ESMF and the preparation and/or review of required site-specific safeguard instruments, support the preparation of safeguard-related requirements for key technical studies and ESIAs, and strengthen the operational capacity of the project team to implement and monitor environmental and social safeguards. Specific tasks and responsibilities 1. **Review project documentation and establish the safeguards methodology** * Review the approved Project Document, existing ESS screening and safeguard documentation, draft ESMP, relevant project budget and contractual-service information, ESIA screening documentation, and available field information. * Identify outstanding environmental and social safeguard issues, information gaps and areas requiring clarification. * Define the methodology and workplan for the assignment, including the approach for field verification, project re-screening, operationalization of the ESMF and preparation/review of required site-specific safeguard instruments. * Prepare an inception report setting out the principal ESS issues identified, clarification requirements and proposed methodology. 2. **Undertake field verification of priority project sites** * Conduct a field mission to priority sites in Grande Comore, including Iconi/Lac Kombé and M'bachile, and, subject to available resources and logistical feasibility, the Hoani/Mbatsé sites in Mohéli. * Assess environmental and social risks associated with the planned interventions, including ecological viability, coastal and hydrological conditions, land use, livelihoods, community health and safety, informal land tenure and potential maladaptation risks. * Consult relevant communities, fishers' associations, local authorities and technical services. * Collect the field information required to update the safeguards screening and inform the preparation and/or review of applicable site-specific safeguard instruments * Work alongside the project GESS specialist during the field mission to support practical knowledge transfer. 3. **Update and strengthen the project Environmental and Social Safeguards Risk Identification Form (SRIF)** * Re-screen project activities for environmental and social risks on the basis of the Project Document, consultations and field findings. * Re-screen relevant project activities against the four UNEP ESSF guiding principles and all eight Safeguard Standards, applying a clear methodology for determining the significance of identified risks and documenting the evidence and data sources supporting the risk rating. *Give particular attention to: (i) SS1 – Biodiversity, Ecosystems and Sustainable Natural Resource Management, particularly for mangrove restoration/ecological continuity under Output 2.1.1 and coastal restoration under Output 2.1.2; (ii) SS2 – Climate Change and Disaster Risk and the principle of sustainability and resilience, particularly the risks of sea-level rise, inundation, erosion and maladaptation at Iconi/Lac Kombé and Hoani/Mbatsé; (iii) SS3 – Pollution Prevention and Resource Efficiency in relation to road works, coastal infrastructure, construction materials and Output 2.1.5; (iv) SS4 – Community Health, Safety and Security for works under Outputs 2.1.1 and 2.1.2; and (v) SS6 – Displacement and Involuntary Resettlement, including potential land-tenure, access and livelihood impacts associated particularly with the Iconi/Lac Kombé intervention * Establish clear linkages between project activities and outputs and the environmental and social safeguard risks they trigger. * Identify the appropriate level of safeguard response for relevant activities, including activities requiring technical studies, ESIAs, specific ESMP mitigation measures or routine safeguard monitoring. * Incorporate relevant site-specific findings, including potential maladaptation and ecological viability concerns. * Submit the revised SRIF for review and formal validation by UNEP. 4. ** Operationalize the approved ESMF and support the preparation and review of site-specific safeguard instruments** * Review and operationalize the approved ESMF in light of the revised project-level and site-specific safeguard screening and available technical and field information. *Identify the site-specific safeguard instruments required for relevant project interventions, including ESIAs, ESMPs, OHS measures and other management plans, as applicable. *Support the preparation and/or review of the required site-specific safeguard instruments. * Ensure that the required safeguard instruments define appropriate mitigation measures, responsible parties, implementation timelines, monitoring requirements and indicative costs. *Ensure that the applicable safeguard instruments are submitted for the required review and clearance before the corresponding physical works commence. 5. **Review and complete safeguard-related Terms of Reference for priority technical studies and ESIAs** * Review and technically strengthen the draft Terms of Reference associated with Contract B19 for the feasibility study and ESIA related to restoration of ecological and hydraulic continuity at Iconi/Lac Kombé. * Ensure that the B19 ToR adequately addresses technical alternatives, environmental and social impacts, community consultation requirements, climate resilience and safeguards expertise requirements. * Ensure that the B19 ToR also includes, as foreseen in the Project Document, requirements for technical supervision of the associated works under Contract B33 and preparation of the corresponding progress and acceptance reports * Review and strengthen the draft Terms of Reference associated with Contract B21 for the hydro-morphological and technical feasibility study for Hoani/Mbatsé. * Review and strengthen the safeguards-related elements of the B21 ToR, ensuring that the technical study provides an adequate basis for environmental and social risk assessment, alternatives analysis, climate-risk and maladaptation assessment, stakeholder engagement, ESIA requirements and associated management measures, while the specialized hydro-morphological, coastal-engineering and technical design scope is defined and quality-assured through appropriate technical expertise. * Ensure that the B21 ToR includes requirements for the consulting firm to produce the technical design report and specifications for the works under Contract B34, provide technical supervision of those works, and produce the corresponding progress and acceptance reports * Review the proposed arrangements for Contract B22 covering the ESIAs for coastal works at Hoani and Mbatsé. * Provide a formal recommendation on whether the B22 ESIAs should remain a separate assignment or be integrated into the scope of B21, including justification for the recommended approach. * Where a standalone B22 assignment is recommended, advise on any necessary adjustment to the allocated budget; where integration of the ESIA scope into B21 is recommended, provide a justification note and proposed budget reallocation * Ensure that the final safeguard-related ToRs include appropriate technical qualifications, ESS requirements and deliverables and are suitable for procurement. 6. **Provide technical capacity building to the project GESS specialist** * Conduct practical working sessions with the Gender and Environment and Social Safeguards (GESS)specialist throughout the assignment: - Strengthen capacity to operationalise the approved ESMF and implement and monitor the applicable site-specific safeguard instruments - Provide guidance on implementation responsibilities, monitoring schedules and ESS data-collection tools. - Provide practical guidance on the completion and application of ESS screening forms for MSMEs supported under Component 3. - Strengthen capacity for the collection and reporting of sex-disaggregated ESS information. - Provide guidance on preparation of environmental and social safeguards sections for project progress reports, including quarterly reporting and the GEF Project Implementation Report (PIR). 7. **Provide final recommendations and follow-up guidance** * Consolidate the findings of the safeguards review, field mission, revised SRIF, ESMF operationalisation, site-specific safeguard work and technical ToR review: - Identify priority safeguard actions required before commencement of moderate- and high-risk project activities. - Provide recommendations on the sequencing of technical studies, ESIAs and related procurement processes. - Conduct a final debriefing with the CTA, Project Management Unit and UNEP Task Manager and provide a practical follow-up schedule for outstanding safeguard actions.
Qualifications/special skills
An advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in environment, earth sciences, coastal engineering, natural resource management, or a related field is required. Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in sustainable development, economics, public policy, public administration, finance, natural resources management, engineering, law, social sciences, or a related field. Successful completion of both degree and non-degree programs in data analytics, business analytics, or data science programs is an advantage.

Not available.

The DDI Section leads corporate data and digital initiatives, including applications related to UN 2.0, in support of the Resident Coordinator (RC) system. The incumbent works across UN INFO modules (IMS, CBSS, JWP, CF, etc.) and with structured and unstructured sources of information and data, including Cooperation Framework (CF) data, ensuring integration across the RC systems. The incumbent establishes communication and cooperation with Divisions, Branches, Resident Coordinator Offices (RCOs), United Nations Country Teams (UNCTs), and Regional Offices, and coordinates with the Data Analysis teams across the RC system. vacancies.jobDescription:
Org. Setting and Reporting
The Independent Institution on Missing Persons in the Syrian Arab Republic (IIMP) was established by the General Assembly in its resolution 77/301, adopted on 29 June 2023. Please note that while the position is currently located in Geneva, Switzerland, the duty station may be subject to change. Applicants should be aware that the position may be relocated to Damascus, Syria, or to another location relevant to the Institution’s operations. By applying, candidates confirm their willingness to accept such a reassignment in accordance with UN regulations and rules, should such a decision be made. The incumbent reports to the Human Rights Officer, Chief of Section, or his/her designated official.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Information Management Officer may be responsible for the following duties: - Contributes to the formulation of overall policies, procedures, objectives and guidelines affecting the development and maintenance of the Organization's non-current records and archives and delivery of reference services, archival description and systems management. - Determines the technical objectives of search, investigative and analytical tasks, developing ways to implement them, and planning and directing implementing activities. - Leads the analysis of technical data structures to direct staff on appropriate methods for information extraction while ensuring integrity and responding to complex queries from users. - Facilitates the resolution of issues relating to search queries and providing expert advice in the identification of material of interest. - Provides expert advice on complex system design of the Independent Institution's protocols and the related infrastructure. - Leads the development and oversees the delivery of training programs on eDiscovery and its tools for both internal and external stakeholders. - Conducts policy-oriented research and drafting on the applicability of information technology to records and archives using data from internal and external sources to: develop section policies, guidelines and procedures in keeping with technological developments, e.g., strategy for long-term preservation and retrievability of electronic records. - Assesses and makes recommendations relating to the use of information systems from the recordkeeping perspective. Provides reliable, up-to-date research and specifications for information management technology and innovations applications relevant to records management and archives. - Provides advisory services Organization-wide on recordkeeping practices based on needs, business process, workflow, technical architecture and information resources analysis; makes recommendations relating to recordkeeping practices, improvement and implementation strategies, resource requirements, file plans, retention schedules and procedures for transferring records to the section; organizes and maintains UN records; preserves and disposes, identifies and protects vital records; and informs management policies and procedures, with an emphasis on technological applications. - Monitors the progress of projects in client offices, ensures compliance with Section standards and guidelines and provides assistance in identifying consultants as required and associated project Terms of Reference. - Evaluates and pilots emerging technologies (including software applications and associated hardware, e.g., document/correspondence management products, imaging and digitization systems and optical disk storage media) to develop strategies for integrating records created in diverse systems into an electronic recordkeeping system; to plan and develop migration strategies for archival preservation of electronic records and to develop and maintain expertise necessary to advise Secretariat offices in the management of electronic records. - Evaluates applications and cost-effectiveness of services in relation to technology options and prepares data and recommendations for decision-making. - Provides technical services for the Section by evaluating hardware and software requirements, recommends purchases, tracks requisitions through Umoja and monitors expenditures; oversees installation of hardware and liaises with ITSD on the replacement of obsolete equipment; overseeing Section LAN Administrators and ensures that technical problems are resolved expeditiously; and oversees the implementation of the Section’s electronic recordkeeping system. - Ensures the preservation of information assets with continuing value by appraising records according to their administrative, legal, financial and/or historical value, develops and implements appropriate retention schedules with records-originating offices, monitors compliance with the requirement to transfer inactive records to Headquarters, and, where applicable, identifies non-core records for transfer to commercial storage and manages commercial storage contracts. - Ensures access to records with continuing value by managing the application of international cataloguing and indexing standards for intellectual control and retrieval; advises internal and external users regarding the use of the Section’s holdings; and assures the delivery of records and/or copies. - Develops and implements policies and guidelines relating to the preservation of and access to digital archives by establishing metadata requirements; retains schedules for incorporation into electronic recordkeeping systems; transfers, maintains security protocols; and selects standards for digitization of finding aids and records and their electronic dissemination. - Manages information security by enforcing security-classification restrictions; facilitates declassification reviews by liaising with records-originating offices; and ensures the physical security and safety of the Organization’s records. - Carries out managerial responsibilities at the unit level relating to compliance with administrative requirements, programme planning, policy and procedure recommendations, budgeting, human resources and facilities management. - Develops client outreach strategy and programme and coordinates its implementation. - Represents the Section, as required, in departmental offices and at working groups, task forces and other fora, advocating recordkeeping and/or archives perspectives and standards. - Participates in the planning and organizing of training for Headquarters and mission staff and users with respect to utilization of reference services. - Evaluates the performance of vendors and certifies invoices, as necessary. - Guides, trains and supervises professional and general service staff in the various records information management functions. - Collects and analyzes data to identify trends or patterns and provide insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. - Performs other duties as assigned.

This position is located in the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) in Amman, Jordan. The incumbent reports to the Head of the Occupied Palestinian Territory Office or his/her designate.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Human Rights Officer (Legal Advisor) will be responsible for the following duties: - Lead and provide expert legal advice to team and leadership on applicable human rights, international humanitarian law and international criminal law frameworks, standards, legal conclusions and accountability measures, identifying legal risks and recommending accountability measures. - Lead substantive legal research and analysis to identify and address cross-cutting patterns and violations of human rights, international criminal law and international humanitarian law, ensuring findings are integrated into broader strategic and policy frameworks. - Manage investigation planning oversee the formulation of legal opinions, establish and refine evidentiary standards, and validate the attribution of responsibility to alleged perpetrators. - Oversee the quality assurance and legal vetting of opinions, memoranda, and high-level briefing documents on human rights, international humanitarian law and international criminal law matters, to ensure strategic alignment and authoritative legal accuracy. - Define the legal framework for public reports on human rights, international humanitarian law and international criminal law matters, ensuring findings, conclusions and recommendations align with the mandate and legal standards, and take accountability for the quality of legal outputs. - Provide strategic advice on evidence preservation and lead coordinated information sharing with jurisdictions and other accountability mechanisms, ensuring alignment with office policies and established frameworks. - Lead and manage engagement with external actors, including human rights and accountability mechanisms, national and international courts and civil society organizations to advance office priorities in line with strategic objectives. - Manage and coordinate the activities of the team, including hiring, training, assigning tasks and responsibilities, evaluating performance, and ensuring that deadlines are met.

PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of international legal procedures and instruments, including criminal law, both substantive and procedural. Ability to apply legal expertise to analyzing a diverse range of complex and unusual legal issues and problems and in developing innovative and creative solutions in prosecuting complex criminal cases. Strong analytical skills and ability to conduct comprehensive legal research on a range of issues, including those of a unique and/or complex nature; proficiency in legal writing and expression and ability to prepare legal briefs, opinions, indictments or legal submissions/motions, and a variety of legal instruments and related documents. Ability to lead and cross-examine witnesses and make substantial legal arguments before Chambers of judges, or if required to take responsibility for the prosecution of criminal trials. Discretion and sound judgment in applying legal expertise to sensitive, complex legal issues. Strong negotiating skills and ability to influence others to reach agreement. Ability to work to tight deadlines and handle multiple concurrent projects/cases. Knowledge of contemporary international relations and of UN system, organization and interrelationships. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. COMMUNICATION: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. TEAMWORK: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others' ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings.
Education
An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in human rights, law, political science, international relations, social sciences, economics, public policy, sustainable development, humanitarian affairs or related field. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying work experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Not available.

Relevant experience may include, but is not limited to political affairs, public affairs, international relations, law, social sciences, economics, development, humanitarian affairs, or other related areas. Knowledge of international humanitarian law and its application is required. At least 5 years of demonstrated knowledge of human rights monitoring, documentation, analysis, research and reporting methodologies, including planning, coordinating and conducting field missions is required. Ability to conduct legal analysis is required. Skills in drafting human rights reports, policy and other documents is required. Skills to integrate digital, open-source, satellite, and forensic evidence into analysis and reporting is desirable. Knowledge of investigative methodologies related to international law and human rights is desirable. Knowledge of international human rights law, norms, and standards is desirable.

Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the United Nations system's designated entity for addressing environmental issues at the global and regional level. Its mandate is to coordinate the development of environmental policy consensus by keeping the global environment under review and bringing emerging issues to the attention of governments and the international community for action. The Subnational Climate Action Unit is part of UNEP’s Climate Change Division Mitigation Branch and based in Paris. Contributing to the UN system-wide strategy on sustainable urban development and the implementation of the New Urban Agenda, through sustainable buildings and construction, sustainable urban food systems, sustainable energy and cooling, and integrated urban planning with nature. The Subnational Climate Action Unit is advertising two internships in support of its Urban Food Systems and Food Waste workstream. Duration of the internship: 6 months. Preference for candidates able to start in January 2027 and July 2027. The internship is unpaid and full-time. Interns work five days per week (37.5 hours) under the supervision of the Urban Food Systems Lead, Programme Management Officer Clementine O’Connor. Kindly note that candidates will be responsible for obtaining necessary visas and arranging any travel to and from the duty station where the internship will be performed. Responsibilities: The intern will assist the programme manager in the coordination and implementation of the activities to promote sustainable food systems and food loss and waste reduction, at national and sub-national level. Duties may include, but are not limited to: - Support coordination of the day-to-day operations of UNEP-led coalitions and communities of practice on food systems and food waste, including organizing virtual meetings, drafting agendas, and preparing summaries and reports. - Contribute to environmental, climate and GHG impact assessment related to food waste, including analysing relevant data and translating findings into evidence in inform policy and programme development. - Assist in planning and implementing joint activities on sustainable urban food systems with UN agencies, civil society, cities, and private-sector partners. - Track key global food systems processes (e.g. Climate and Biodiversity COPs) and support the organization of advocacy events during these processes. - Liaise with thematic task teams and support information-sharing on UNEP sustainable food systems activities across the organization. - Conduct research on sustainable food systems policies, governance, and climate impacts, and draft briefing notes, policy summaries, and presentations. - Lead development of communications content, including newsletters, member updates, and event summaries. Support updates of the stopfoodlosswaste.org website. - Explore and support articulation of UNEP’s role at the nexus between biodiversity, nutrition, and climate change, including identifying entry points for integrated food systems action. Contribute to new project research and development. - Support administrative processes such as reporting and contracting of implementing partners.

vacancies.jobTitle: Consultant on Disability-Inclusive Urban Disaster Risk Reduction in Baguio City, the Philippines
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
The ultimate result of this assignment is to ensure effective and timely coordination of project implementation, fostering strong collaboration and communication among local government and relevant stakeholders, facilitating the effective follow-up of project activities in line with the project’s objectives and intended results.
Work Location
Baguio City, the Philippines
Expected duration
1 Dec 26-27 Jan 28
Duties and Responsibilities
Background Created in December 1999, the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) is the designated focal point in the United Nations system for the coordination of efforts to reduce disasters and to ensure synergies among the disaster reduction activities of the United Nations and regional organizations and activities in both developed and less developed countries. Led by the United Nations Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Disaster Risk Reduction (SRSG/ASG), UNDRR has over 150 staff located in its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, and in regional offices. UNDRR guides, monitors, analyses, and reports on progress in the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030. It supports regional and national implementation of the Framework and catalyzes action and increases global awareness to reduce disaster risk, working with UN Member States and a broad range of partners and stakeholders, including civil society, the private sector, parliamentarians, and the science and technology community. In alignment with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, the Making Cities Resilient 2030 (MCR2030) Initiative, and the Early Warnings for All (EW4ALL) Initiative, the Disability-Inclusive Urban Disaster Risk Reduction and Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (RICH-MHEWS) project aims to strengthen urban disaster resilience by integrating the needs of persons with disabilities into disaster risk reduction (DRR) and multi-hazard early warning systems (MHEWS) in Baguio City, Philippines. The project has been divided into two phases, with Phase 1 now completed. For this consultancy, UNDRR, Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific is seeking a consultant to provide technical support for Phase 2 of the project, aiming to 1. Enhance Inclusivity in DRR: Strengthen the participation of persons with disabilities in disaster planning and decision-making. 2. Improve Accessibility of MHEWS: Ensure disaster risk communication, infrastructure, and emergency responses are inclusive and accessible. 3. Foster Multi-Stakeholder Engagement: Build local and national capacities through collaborative planning with government agencies, Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), and civil society organizations. 4. Scale Up and Replicate Best Practices: Use Baguio City as a model for disability-inclusive resilience-building, informing national and regional DRR strategies. The objective of this assignment is to provide dedicated on-the-ground coordination support for the effective implementation of the project. The consultant will serve as a field-level focal point, supporting stakeholder engagement, logistical coordination, activity follow-up, field monitoring, documentation, and regular reporting to the project management team. Duties and Responsibilities This is a home-based consultancy which will be based in Baguio City and work under the supervision of the Associate Program Management Officer and Programme Management Officer (Disability) at UNDRR ROAP. The consultant will undertake the following duties in close coordination with the Persons with Disability Affairs Office (PDAO) and City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO) of Baguio City. 1. Overall coordination and implementation support – will provide overall coordination with the city government, project multi-stakeholder partners (e.g., women, youth, persons with disabilities, vulnerable groups, and other community representatives where relevant). This includes supporting the organization of meetings, consultations, workshops, trainings, drill, field visits, and community-level activities. 2. Support co-facilitation of training sessions - The consultant will support the delivery of training sessions as a co-facilitator, where appropriate. 3. Monitoring, Documentation, and Reporting - Collect and maintain relevant information and documentation from project activities, including updates, photos, attendance records, good practices, lessons learned, challenges, and recommendations from the implementation of workshops, training, consultations, drill, and other field activities. 4. Risk Management and Problem Solving - Identify and monitor risks and emerging issues at the local and field level that may affect project implementation, including delays, stakeholder concerns, and access constraints. Promptly inform the project team of significant risks and support practical measures to address issues and keep implementation on track.
Qualifications/special skills
Bachelor’s degree in development studies, disaster risk management, disaster risk reduction, climate change, urban planning, public administration, social sciences, environmental management, or a related field is required. Minimum two years of experience in the areas of early warning systems, disaster risk management, local resilience, disability inclusion, or public administration in the Philippines is required. Experience working with relevant national and sub-national stakeholders in the Philippines is required. Experience in drafting strategic planning documents, reports, and conducting consultations with stakeholders, and the ability to conduct training for local government and local communities is required. Experience with UNDRR tools, including disability inclusion checklist, Disaster Resilience scorecard, and its addenda, is desirable.
Languages
Fluence in English and Tagalog is required.
Additional Information
Due to the high volume of applications received, only successful candidates will be contacted.

Org. Setting and Reporting
With its 192 member countries, the Universal Postal Union (UPU), a specialized agency of the United Nations, is the primary forum for cooperation between postal sector players. It helps to ensure a truly universal network of up-to-date products and services.
Responsibilities
Under the general direction of the Director and direct supervision of the Coordinator, lead and manage the planning, implementation, monitoring and quality assurance of the UPU’s sustainable development pro-gramme, covering climate action, social inclusion, gender equality and disability inclusion. Translate Congress mandates and the UPU Strategy into programme activities and results aligned with the UN SDGs/UN-SWAP; provide substantive policy and technical advice within these areas; manage assigned human and financial resources; and support the development of partnerships and resource mobilization across the UN system and among governments, development partners, private sector players and postal stakeholders. 1. Under the direction of the Coordinator, plan, manage and monitor implementation of the sustainable development programme and its associated work plan deliverables. Develop the annual budget, work plans and results frameworks; monitor progress, expenditure, risks and achievement of results; and propose corrective actions and programme adjustments to the Coordinator as required. Manage the development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policy advice, recommendations and proposals for consideration by the Coordinator, Director, Executive Management and relevant UPU bodies on the following matters: i UN sustainable development cooperation – Input of the UPU as a UN specialized agency into the UN Development Agenda through written contributions, reports, studies and analysis, ensuring the visibility of the UPU. Duties and Responsibilities
Background: Established in Osaka in 1992, UNEP’s International Environmental Technology Centre (IETC) is part of the Industry and Economy Division and serves as UNEP’s hub for the waste and technology dimensions of the circular economy. Guided by the vision “Innovation Towards Zero Waste,” the Centre supports developing countries and countries with economies in transition in adopting environmentally sound technologies, policies and practices. IETC leads on electronics across the full value chain and addresses the waste dimensions of plastics, textiles and food, with expertise spanning circularity, innovation, critical minerals, and sustainable value chains; with special attention to the social, gender and youth dimensions of zero-waste and circular economy agendas. The Centre works closely with UNEP teams, governments, businesses and other stakeholders, including its key strategic partners Institute for Global Environmental Strategies and Osaka City’s Global Environment Centre Foundation. Through policy and technical advice, knowledge development, technology cooperation, partnerships, and demonstration initiatives, IETC aims to accelerate an inclusive, technology-driven transition towards zero-waste and circular economy systems. Recognizing waste reduction and the avoidance of waste generation as priority policy actions to prevent waste mismanagement, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, IETC provides technical and policy advice, develops knowledge and partnerships and implements demonstration projects. Working across UNEP and with key partners, including the Institute for Global Environmental Strategies and Osaka City’s Global Environment Centre Foundation, IETC advances inclusive, technology-driven solutions that accelerate progress towards zero waste and circular economy societies. This advertisement is seeking two interns to work in the UNEP-IETC headquarters, in Osaka, Japan during a 6-month period. The Internship is UNPAID and full-time. Interns work five days per week (35 hours) under the supervision of a staff member in the department or office to which they are assigned. Interns are not financially remunerated by the United Nations. Costs and arrangements for travel, visas, accommodation and living expenses are the responsibility of interns or their sponsoring institutions. Tasks: Under the direct supervision of IETC Officer, the Intern will: 1. Research and summarize scientific information on zero waste and circular economy solutions, including social and economic aspects such as informal sector integration, gender mainstreaming , behaviour insights and zero-waste job creation potential. 2. Analyse waste-related and circular economy policies, such as national waste management strategies and regulatory frameworks, from the perspectives of environmental sustainability and resource circulation. 3. Draft analytical briefs, policy reviews, research summaries, and technical reports that support evidence-based decision-making and knowledge generation addressing zero waste and circular economy matters 4. Organize and otherwise support meetings (e.g., notetaking, assisting in the management of participant travel, visitor management) and events organized by IETC or in which the Centre is involved. 5. Map out business opportunities and technology-based innovations that advance circularity, resource recovery and zero-waste objectives, particularly in high-impact sectors. 6. Assist in drafting or assessing documents related to UNEP’s programme of work, and develop technical documentation, guidance or tools related to IETC’s work. 7. Assist in populating digital platforms and knowledge-sharing platforms related to IETC’s work. 8. Support the collection, analysis and visualization of data and indicators of zero waste and circular economy. 9. Draft outreach, communication and educational materials related to IETC’s work. 10. Assist in stakeholder mapping and the development of partnership and networks. 11. Carry out other duties relevant to the Intern’s educational background and professional aspirations.

Org. Setting and Reporting
This position is located in the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) in the Regional Hub for East and Southern Africa in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia; The incumbent reports to the Regional Director or his/her designate.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Human Rights Officer will be responsible for the following duties: • Acts as early warning and prevention team lead; develops and carries out appropriate early warning analysis, identifies preventative measures to address human rights protection needs through remote monitoring or in country missions; feeds in analysis to global prevention processes, i.e. RMRs and UNOCC, in coordination with relevant Sections; establishes and nurtures partnerships with relevant early warning systems in the region. • Acts as emergency response capacity to be rapidly deployed and to provide immediate start-up capacity in relation to human rights and humanitarian emergencies. • Reviews, monitors and evaluates activities relating to the implementation of international human rights instruments, including recommendations of treaty bodies and mechanisms of the Human Rights Council. • Researches, collects and analyses information and documentation pertaining to emerging human rights concerns. In coordination with the Information Management Officer, finalises products to present analysis in visually compelling and easily digestible formats. • Guides and oversees the development of analytical human rights information products to support OHCHR’s work on early warning/prevention and humanitarian action. • Prepares relevant human rights parts of reports for the General Assembly, HRC, etc., and notes on the status of ratification of human rights instruments, etc. • Serves as team leader with responsibility for carrying out, in consultation with the Regional Director or his/her designate, work coordination and administrative functions relating to the staff, planning and budget on the subject matters of responsibility • Actively contributes to the community of practice of the regional Emergency Response Teams, the Crisis Preparedness and Response Section and other relevant Sections. • Works with UN and non-governmental programmes, and supports Country Leads in their work in the country/region to integrate human rights, including their gender dimensions, in their programmes; helps integrate human rights in humanitarian and development analysis, planning and responses. • Ensures up-to-date information regarding substantive matters in the field of human rights and makes recommendations on actions to take. • Makes contact with other sectors of the UN, other international organizations and governments on coordination and policy matters; briefs representatives and provides, as appropriate, suggestions and recommendations, in coordination with the Regional Director and/or Country Leads in the region. • Assists and build capacity and awareness of national (including governments and NHRIs) and international partners on the protection of human rights in humanitarian emergencies. • Trains and supervises new/junior staff. • Performs other related duties as required.
Competencies

This position is located within the United Nations Support Office in Haiti (UNSOH). Pursuant to Security Council resolution 2793 (2025), UNSOH has been mandated to provide support; primarily to the Gang Suppression Force (GSF), the United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH), the Haitian National Police (HNP), and the Haitian Armed Forces in the context of any joint operations with the GSF. Additionally, UNSOH is tasked with delivering technical assistance to the Organization of American States (OAS). The Finance and Budget Officer manages a complete and homogenous operation of the Mission’s financial system, including planning, preparation, monitoring and reporting on all budget submissions, fund redeployments, and performance reporting. The position is based in Port-au-Prince and is located in the Office of the Chief, Operations and Resources Management, Finance and Budget Section. The incumbent will report to the Chief, Finance and Budget Section.

Performance Monitoring • Perform analysis, preparation and delivery of strategic support and business intelligence to operational counterparts and mission leadership on financial resourcing and stewardship, and organizational performance of the mission, in line with mission priorities. Actively participates and engages in planning, monitoring and reporting of financial and operational performances. Other • In the absence of a Chief, Finance and Budget Section, oversees the daily operations of the Office. • Performs other duties as assigned.

Experience in directly supporting senior leadership during the presentation of budget proposals to legislative bodies is required. Has knowledge of various research methodologies and sources, including electronic sources on the internet, intranet and other databases. Good analytical, planning and organizational skills. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns. implementation of information programs to publicize priority issues and/or major events, to include drafting information strategies, coordinating efforts, monitoring and reporting on progress, taking action/responses. • Undertakes activities to promote media coverage (e.g. press conferences, interviews, press seminars and other special activities) of priority issues and/or major events, to include development of a media strategy and action plan, initiating pro-active media outreach efforts, proposing and arranging press conferences/media coverage, disseminating materials and consulting with press on approach/story angle and other information requests, undertaking appropriate follow-up action and analyzing and reporting on the impact of coverage. • Produces or oversees production of a specific type or types (e.g. print, broadcast, etc.) of information communications products (e.g. press kits, press releases, feature articles, speeches, booklets, brochures, backgrounders, audio-visual materials, radio spot program, etc.), to include proposing topics, undertaking research, determining appropriate medium and target audience, preparing production plans, writing drafts, obtaining clearances and finalizing texts, editing copy, and coordinating design approval, printing procedures and distribution. • Prepares, on the basis of official UN documentation and other sources, initial drafts of articles or chapters for inclusion in UN newsletters, periodicals, reports and books. • Initiates and sustains professional relationships with key constituencies. • Acts as focal point on specific issues, monitoring and reporting on developments, responding to inquiries, etc. • Participates in selecting the information transmitted to key constituencies. • Provides guidance to, and may supervise, more junior staff. • Collects and analyzes data to identify trends or patterns and provide insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. • Performs other duties as assigned.
