Duties and Responsibilities
The internship is located in the Chinese Language Unit of the Social Media Section, Outreach Division, Department of Global Communications. The Section is responsible for the Department’s social media activities and the integration of its social media platforms, including major social networking and content-sharing platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X, YouTube, WeChat, Weibo, Bilibili and Kuaishou. These platforms are critical components of the Department’s overall communications strategy. Fluency in Chinese is essential, as the intern will support research, monitoring, analysis and other project-based activities related to Chinese-language social media platforms. We encourage candidates who can ideally commit to a full-time schedule for a minimum duration of three months and work with us in person in Vienna. Within delegated authority, the Digital Communications Intern will report to the designated Public Information Officer and, under their guidance and supervision, may be responsible for the following project-based duties: • Conduct research and compile basic information, including text, images, videos and infographics, to support the preparation and production of Chinese-language social media materials. • Monitor and analyze statistics related to social media performance, including engagement metrics (likes, shares, comments, reposts and saves; click-through rates on links in posts; video views, watch time and completion rates); audience analytics (demographics such as age, gender, location and language; audience growth; and audience activity such as peak engagement times and device usage); content performance (post reach and impressions; top-performing posts based on engagement; and content types and their effectiveness); and platform-specific metrics. • Conduct research and document highlights from special events and activities promoting United Nations mandates in Vienna, for reference in communications and social media-related projects. • Research and analyze approaches to communicating United Nations priorities, including the Sustainable Development Goals, climate action and peacebuilding, on Chinese-language social media platforms, with particular attention to younger and broader audiences in the Chinese-speaking world. • Support research and basic post-production activities related to short-form and long-form video content for social media platforms, as assigned and under supervision. • Attend meetings as an observer, where appropriate, to gain exposure to the work of the Department and relevant communications activities. • Support the preparation of meeting agendas and meeting notes under the guidance and supervision of the Public Information Officer. The internship is project-based and is intended to provide opportunities for practical experience, learning and professional development. Interns will contribute to assigned projects and activities under the guidance and supervision of the Public Information Officer.

Org. Setting and Reporting
OSAA is mandated with the provision of advisory, advocacy, coordination and monitoring services in support for Africa’s development. More information about the Office can be found at www.un.org/osaa. This position is located in the Strategic Management Unit of the Office of the Special Adviser on Africa (OSAA). Under the overall supervision of the Under-Secretary-General, the Senior Programme Management Officer will lead the strategic coordination and management of the three substantive functions of the Strategic Management Unit (programme planning, monitoring and evaluation; data and analytics; and strategic communications), to ensure the timely and quality delivery of the Unit’s institutional outputs, and to align the Unit’s contribution with the value chain of knowledge production, advocacy and policy influencing of the Office and of Programme 9 in support of Africa’s development. The incumbent will also support the USG in assuring the coherence of Programme 9 (United Nations system support for the African Union’s Agenda 2063) across its implementing entities. The incumbent serves as the principal interlocutor between the Unit’s functions, the Front Office of the Under-Secretary-General and the Director of the Division for Policy, Monitoring and Advocacy on cross-cutting organizational priorities and deliverables.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Senior Programme Management Officer will be responsible for the following duties: • Takes the lead to develop, implement and evaluate assigned programmes/projects, etc. in particular related to the integrated workplan of the Strategic Management Unit across its three substantive functions (programme planning, monitoring and evaluation; data and analytics; and strategic communications), including the establishment of common frameworks and guidance and the integration of functional workplans, and the Unit’s contribution to the value chain of knowledge production, advocacy and policy influencing of the Office and of Programme 9; directs subordinates in programme/project development, implementation, monitoring and assessment; directs review of relevant documents and reports; identifies priorities, problems and issues to be addressed and proposes corrective actions; liaises with relevant parties; identifies and initiates follow-up actions. • Ensures implementation of gender mainstreaming guidelines by assessing the implications for men and women of any planned action, including legislation, policies or programmes, in all areas and at all levels. • Directs data-based research and programme evaluation and presents information gathered from diverse sources to assess the impact of the Office’s programme and knowledge products. • Coordinates policy development regarding programme planning, data management and strategic communications workstreams within the Strategic Management Unit; reviews the assessments of issues and trends, preparation of evaluations or research activities and studies; provides senior advisory support to the Under-Secretary-General on policy, programme and institutional matters, including organizational change and reform initiatives. • Undertakes survey initiatives to assess the impact of the Office’s products; guides design of data collection instruments to optimize the efficiency and quality of the communication function and the interaction with the Office’s stakeholders and target audiences; reviews, analyzes and interprets responses, identifies problems/issues and prepares conclusions. • Supervises preparation and publication of various written and digital multimedia outputs, e.g. background papers, analysis, substantive sections of reports and studies, inputs to publications, press releases, blogs, flyers, etc., and ensures that communication products effectively visualize data and knowledge. • Directs substantive support to consultative and other meetings, conferences, etc., including proposing agenda topics, identifying participants, preparation of documents and presentations, supervising the development and implementation of event communication and advocacy plans, etc. • Manages outreach activities; liaises with stakeholders; leads coordination with institutional partners on programme planning, data and communications frameworks; designs and conducts training workshops, seminars, etc., makes presentations on assigned topics/activities. • Leads field missions, including provision of guidance to external consultants, government officials and other parties and drafting mission summaries, etc. • Coordinates activities related to budget and funding within the areas of responsibility (programme/project preparation and submissions, progress reports, financial statements, etc.) and ensures preparation of related documents/reports (pledging, work programme, programme budget, submissions to the Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions and to the Committee for Programme and Coordination, inputs on the substantive intergovernmental track including resolution negotiations and Programme Budget Implications, the Integrated Planning, Management and Reporting instrument, and the Strategic Management Application, etc.). • Serves as an effective spokesperson and establishes collaboration and partnerships with key officials at all levels inside and outside the Organization, including counterparts in the entities implementing Programme 9. • Ensures effective utilization, supervision and development of staff; Guides, evaluates and mentors staff • Leads team members’ efforts to collect and analyze data and provides insight to identify trends or patterns for data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting; oversees the Unit’s data governance function and code-based analytical infrastructure, ensuring that everyone can discover, access, integrate and share the data they need. • May perform other duties as required.
Competencies
PROFESSIONALISM: Ability to identify key strategic issues, opportunities and risks. Ability to generate and communicate broad and compelling organizational direction. Ability to communicate clearly links between the Organization’s strategy and the work unit’s goals. Demonstrated ability to provide innovative technical leadership by performing and/or overseeing the planning, development, and management of operations. Demonstrated ability to negotiate and apply good judgment. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Provides leadership and takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work; demonstrates knowledge of strategies and commitment to the goal of gender balance in staffing. ACCOUNTABILITY: Takes ownership of all responsibilities and honours commitments; delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within prescribed time, cost and quality standards; operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules; supports subordinates, provides oversight and takes responsibility for delegated assignments; takes personal responsibility for his/her own shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable. TECHNOLOGICAL AWARENESS: Keeps abreast of available technology; understands applicability and limitation of technology to the work of the office; actively seeks to apply technology to appropriate tasks; shows willingness to learn new technology. MANAGING PERFORMANCE: Delegates the appropriate responsibility, accountability and decision-making authority. Makes sure that roles, responsibilities and reporting lines are clear to each staff member. Accurately judges the amount of time and resources needed to accomplish a task and matches task to skills. Monitors progress against milestones and deadlines. Regularly discusses performance and provides feedback and coaching to staff. Encourages risk-taking and supports creativity and initiative. Actively supports the development and career aspirations of staff. Appraises performance fairly. JUDGMENT/DECISION-MAKING: Identifies the key issues in a complex situation, and comes to the heart of the problem quickly. Gathers relevant information before making a decision. Considers positive and negative impacts of decisions prior to making them. Takes decisions with an eye to the impact on others and on the Organization. Proposes a course of action or makes a recommendation based on all available information. Checks assumptions against facts. Determines that the actions proposed will satisfy the expressed and underlying needs for the decision. Makes tough decisions when necessary.
Education
Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent degree) in business administration, management, computational social science, economics, policy analysis, data management, or a related field is required. A first-level university degree in combination with additional two years of qualifying work experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Successful completion of degree or non-degree programmes in data analytics, business analytics or data science is desirable.
Job - Specific Qualification
Not available.
Work Experience
A minimum of ten years of progressively responsible experience in project or programme management, administration or a related area is required. Experience advising a head of entity or equivalent senior manager on strategic direction or policy matters is required. Experience in managing teams coordinating strategic planning or organisational change processes within an international or intergovernmental organisation is required. vacancies.jobTitle: Development of a Biodiversity Data Collection Framework for Armenia
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
I. A comprehensive desk review of international best practices in biodiversity data collection frameworks, with particular focus on GBIF’s data infrastructure and Darwin Core standards, the national biodiversity data systems of the Czech Republic and Finland, and relevant CBD and KMGBF guidance on biodiversity data mobilisation and sharing, providing an evidence base for the design of Armenia’s framework; II. A Biodiversity Data Landscape Assessment mapping Armenia’s existing data assets, collection actors, methodologies, platforms, data standards in use, and known gaps – including an analysis of data flows between institutions and the legal and institutional constraints governing data access and sharing; III. A Needs and Priorities Assessment identifying Armenia’s most critical biodiversity data gaps by thematic area and NBSAP target, prioritising needs according to policy relevance, data availability, and technical and institutional feasibility, and articulating the key requirements that the national framework must address; IV. A Legal and Institutional Mapping Note identifying the specific legal and/or administrative acts required to establish the data collection framework under Armenian law, including the type of instrument, responsible authority, and indicative process and timeline for each; V. A stakeholder consultation report documenting the priorities, capacities, and proposed roles of key data producers and users – including government institutions, the National Academy of Sciences, universities, civil society organisations, protected area administrations, and international partners (Czech Republic, Finland, GBIF); VI. A Phase 2 Roadmap document outlining the recommended scope, structure, and key questions to be addressed in the feasibility study, to guide the design of the Phase 2 contracting process; VII. Strengthened national capacity and inter-institutional dialogue on biodiversity data governance, contributing directly to NBSAP ARM T26 and KM-GBF Target 21.
Work Location
Remote
Expected duration
2.7 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. Its mandate is to coordinate the development of environmental policy consensus by keeping the global environment under review and bringing emerging issues to the attention of governments and the international community for action. UNEP’s Ecosystems Division engages with governments and other partners to develop and promote ecosystem-based solutions for sustainable development. This assignment is in the Nature Frameworks Support Unit of the Biodiversity and Land Branch, Ecosystems Division. UNEP is also one of the key agencies hosting the NBSAP Accelerator Partnership. The NBSAP Accelerator Partnership is a country-led global initiative that supports the development and implementation of ambitious National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) and collectively achieve the goals and targets of the Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) and, ultimately, the global vision of living in harmony with nature by 2050. The NBSAP Accelerator Partnership provides technical and financial support for the implementation of GBF-aligned NBSAPs. This includes strengthening country-driven coordination, fostering collaboration among stakeholders, facilitating knowledge sharing and best practices, and addressing country-specific needs. It also helps raise national profile of countries' NBSAPs, and fast-track implementation through a matchmaking service, increased access to expertise, knowledge and capacity development, and in-country facilitation support. A National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) is a country’s principal document for implementing the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). It outlines a nation’s approach to conserving its biodiversity, ensuring its sustainable use, and fairly sharing the benefits derived from genetic resources. Armenia is a party to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). They signed and ratified the convention in 1992 and 1993, respectively. The Country also acceded to the Cartagena Protocol in 2004 and the Nagoya Protocol in 2026. Duties and Responsibilities The NBSAP Accelerator Partnership’s Facilitator Programme is looking for a consultant to support the Government of the Republic of Armenia to develop a biodiversity data collection framework for the country. Armenia’s National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2026-2030 is aligned with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) and sets out 30 national targets spanning habitat protection, ecosystem restoration, species conservation, sustainable use, governance, and monitoring. Effective implementation of these targets – and Armenia’s fulfilment of its obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) – depends fundamentally on the availability of reliable, up-to-date, and accessible biodiversity data. At present, biodiversity data in Armenia are collected by a fragmented set of actors – state institutions, national parks and protected areas, the National Academy of Sciences, universities, and civil society organisations – using different methodologies, formats, and platforms, without a unified national framework governing data standards, sharing, quality assurance, or long-term archiving. This fragmentation limits the ability of decision-makers to track biodiversity trends, report against KMGBF targets, and design evidence-based policies. Armenia has taken important steps toward strengthening its biodiversity data ecosystem. The country has established cooperation with the Czech Republic and Finland, which have relevant experience in biodiversity informatics and national data infrastructure development, and has engaged with the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) – the world’s largest open-access biodiversity data platform – as a key partner for data mobilisation and standardisation. GBIF’s framework, built on the Darwin Core data standard and its global network of national nodes, offers a proven model for aggregating species occurrence and ecological data across institutions and sectors. These partnerships provide Armenia with a valuable foundation of technical expertise, infrastructure models, and data-sharing tools upon which a national biodiversity data collection framework can be designed. NBSAP Target ARM T26 explicitly calls for strengthening Armenia’s biodiversity inventory and monitoring framework and advancing technology and data collection methodologies, underscoring the strategic importance of this work. A national biodiversity data collection framework – covering data standards, collection protocols, institutional responsibilities, data-sharing mechanisms, and the legal basis for data governance – is a prerequisite for transforming Armenia’s NBSAP monitoring from a reporting exercise into a dynamic, evidence-driven process. However, before such a framework can be designed and implemented, it is essential to conduct a rigorous assessment of Armenia’s current data landscape: what data exist, who collects them and how, what gaps and quality issues are most critical, what institutional and legal constraints govern data sharing, and what priorities should guide framework development. This activity (Phase 1) will recruit a consultant to conduct this needs and priorities assessment, drawing on international best practices and structured stakeholder consultations. Phase 1 will directly inform Phase 2, which will comprise a detailed feasibility study to guide the design of a dedicated project for developing and introducing the full biodiversity data collection framework in Armenia. In taking this work forward, it should be clearly understood that Phase 1 outputs constitute a needs and priorities assessment only, and should not yet be regarded as the establishment of a comprehensive national biodiversity data framework – that framework’s development and introduction will follow through Phase 2 and subsequent implementation. The eventual framework should also be fully aligned with Armenia’s existing spatial data governance and standardisation system – including thematic spatial datasets on protected areas, the Emerald Network, forests, and other relevant spatial layers – rather than developed as a stand-alone or technically incompatible system. It will further require clearly defined legal and institutional arrangements governing biodiversity data, covering custodianship, ownership, data-sharing obligations, update frequency, quality assurance procedures, publication requirements, and reporting arrangements for international platforms, and should distinguish between open-access data and sensitive biodiversity information – with precise locality data for rare, threatened, or illegally exploited species subject to sensitivity assessment and, where appropriate, released only in generalised form or through controlled access. Specific Task I. Review of international biodiversity data collection frameworks, with particular focus on: (a) GBIF’s global infrastructure, Darwin Core data standards, and national node models; (b) the national biodiversity data systems of the Czech Republic and Finland, including their governance structures, data-sharing mechanisms, and legal frameworks; (c) CBD and KM-GBF guidance on data mobilisation and the Open-access Data Policy; (d) comparable national frameworks from biodiversity-rich post-Soviet states. Analysis of the implications of these models for the Armenian context. II. Mapping of Armenia’s existing biodiversity data ecosystem, including: identification of all major data producers (state bodies, protected area administrations, National Academy of Sciences institutions, universities, NGOs, citizen science initiatives); assessment of data types, collection methodologies, formats, and storage platforms in use; analysis of current data flows, interoperability gaps, and quality assurance practices; identification of legal and institutional barriers to data access and sharing. The assessment shall incorporate a review of Armenia’s existing GBIF data contributions and identify priority datasets not yet mobilised. III. Design and facilitate structured consultations with key biodiversity data producers and users, including: the Ministry of Environment; the Statistical Committee of Armenia; the National Academy of Sciences (Institute of Botany, Institute of Zoology and Hydroecology, and others); Yerevan State University; the Armenian National Agrarian University; protected area administrations; relevant civil society organisations; and international partners (GBIF contact point, Czech and Finnish cooperation counterparts where accessible). Consultations to cover: data priorities, institutional roles, capacity constraints, data-sharing willingness, and requirements for a national framework. IV. Synthesis of the desk study and stakeholder consultations into a Needs and Priorities Assessment, identifying: (a) the most critical biodiversity data gaps by thematic area and NBSAP target; (b) priority data types and taxa requiring immediate attention; (c) key requirements for a national framework (data standards, collection protocols, institutional roles, data-sharing mechanisms, technology infrastructure, capacity building); (d) an analysis of how existing cooperation with the Czech Republic, Finland, and GBIF can best be leveraged in framework development; (e) recommendations for the scope and structure of Phase 2 (feasibility study). V. Identification of the legal and/or administrative acts required under Armenian law to establish the biodiversity data collection framework, including: the type of instrument needed (e.g. government decree, ministerial order, or inter-institutional agreement); the responsible authority for drafting and adoption; the applicable legislative process and indicative timeline; and any existing legal provisions (on environmental information, statistics, intellectual property, or data protection) that are relevant to the framework’s design. VI. Preparation of a Phase 2 Roadmap document outlining the recommended scope, key questions, methodology, and expected outputs of the feasibility study to be conducted under a separate Phase 2 contract. Consolidation of all Phase 1 outputs into a Final Report, incorporating NBSAP AP and government feedback, with a concise executive summary in Armenian and English. The framework should also be directly linked to the NBSAP monitoring and evaluation framework, with data collection driven by the indicators established under the national NBSAP targets to ensure that the resulting information supports implementation monitoring and national reporting. Consideration should further be given to incorporating financial and policy-related data relevant to the BIOFIN process, including public expenditures, subsidies, fiscal incentives, biodiversity-related impact assessments, financing gaps, and indicators tracking the implementation of biodiversity finance solutions. The consultant will report to the Programme Management Officer of the Nature Frameworks Support Unit in close coordination and collaboration with the NBSAP AP facilitator in Armenia and relevant government representatives.
Qualifications/special skills
Advanced university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in biodiversity informatics, ecology, environmental science, biology, computer science, or a related field. A first level degree with additional two years of qualifying experience maybe accepted in lieu of advanced degree. Minimum 7 years of professional experience in biodiversity data management, biodiversity informatics, environmental monitoring, or related fields, preferably in Armenia or the South Caucasus region is required. Demonstrated familiarity with GBIF’s data infrastructure, the Darwin Core standard, and biodiversity data mobilisation processes is required Knowledge of Armenia’s biodiversity institutional landscape, including the relevant scientific institutions, protected area system, and existing data collection actors is required Experience in designing or assessing data management systems, biodiversity databases, or environmental information systems is required Demonstrated ability to conduct stakeholder consultations and synthesise diverse institutional perspectives into actionable recommendations is required. Familiarity with the KMGBF and its data and knowledge requirements (Target 21, Target 26) is desirable Experience working with UN agencies, international organisations, or development partners is desirable
Languages
English is the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. Fluency in Armenian and English (written and spoken) is required.
Additional Information
Not available.

vacancies.jobDescription:
Org. Setting and Reporting
This position is located in the Web Unit/Communications Section in the External Outreach Service of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) in Geneva, Switzerland. The incumbent reports to the Web Officer, Head of the Web Unit.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Web Content Management Officer will be responsible for the following duties: 1. Works on maintaining and developing the OCHR website in the UN official languages: English/French/Spanish/Arabic/Chinese/Russian by: - working with the Web Unit to plan and develop, within the context of the Content Management System, dynamic, interactive web pages, site navigation strategies, and continuous improvement to www.ohchr.org; - regularly managing and coordinating translation progress and needs, and setting priority areas for multilingual development in the Arabic/Chinese/French/Russian/Spanish sites, using user feedback, web traffic reports, and ad hoc surveys; - developing strategic partnerships and negotiating agreements with academic brother institutions for high-quality translations of materials for the website; - consolidating contributed and/or translated material, as necessary, and in consultation with content providers, developing a standard format and layout for all language versions, and strategies for easy navigation within the website, ensuring the end-result is fully accessible by disabled persons in accordance with the relevant Guidelines; - coordinating content creation, updates, integration of contributed content, and organization of material, in text and multimedia formats, available on the relevant language website; - participating in discussions with ORCHR-wide Divisions, Sections, Field Offices, reviewing user requests and user feedback, and industry trends; - conducting preliminary review of contributed content with content provider to discuss location within the website, presentation, maintenance and updating of the content, contact person and posting rights for the contributing office, depending on the amount of contributed material and the frequency of updating; - monitoring procedures for checking websites for link integrity, updated information, accessibility and technical problems. 2. Coordinates the work of the multilingual Website team working in English/French/Spanish/Arabic/Chinese/Russian by: - providing direction and guidance to the Web Content Management Assistants; - participating in regular meetings to discuss: work in progress and plans for upcoming conferences, meetings and events; any difficulties encountered in presenting content on the site, and proposed solutions; needed resources: software, hardware, staff, training needs; - ongoing communication regarding work in progress; - recommending updates and expansion of published guidelines to reflect language needs; 3. In consultation with the Web Officer, functions as the thematic Focal Point for issues assigned to the Web Unit such as website accessibility-related issues. 4. Analyzes website usage logs (analytics) and prepares statistical reports; responds to user comments and/or reports of errors and problem areas. 5. Develops and maintains support services to users and contributors by providing assistance to first content contributors in the conversion of contributed material to appropriate Web format in the preliminary stage, as necessary. 6. Maintains constant awareness of the developments of the Web industry by reading the literature and participating in meetings, conferences, and workshops; prepares substantive papers, reports, articles, and online surveys; Makes presentations regarding the website to groups. Fills in for the Web Officer as needed.
Competencies
PROFESSIONALISM - Advanced knowledge in the field of user-centric Web design methodologies and information architecture, content organization and taxonomy concepts, including information management archival/hierarchy. Knowledge of Web content management systems, and the use of relevant information databases and/or Internet services, as appropriate. Proficiency in website creation software, HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Ability to establish and maintain productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect, identifying clients' needs and matching them to appropriate solutions, and keeping clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects. Ability to meet timelines for delivery of products or services to clients. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Displays creativity and accountability in executing his/her duties. Displays commitment to continuous learning to stay abreast of new technological developments in the Web field. COMMUNICATION - Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. Ability to translate technical/legal content into succinct language for public information Web materials. Excellent writing and editing skills in the relevant language. TEAMWORK - Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others' ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. Ability to maintain effective working relations.
Education
An advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Communications, Computer Science or related area is required. A first-level university degree, in combination with two additional years of qualifying work experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Not available.
Work Experience
A minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible professional experience in website development and management in a multilingual environment, is required. Not available.

A functional, secure and operational IDEP Alumni Platform is developed, tested, deployed and made available for use, with relevant existing alumni data successfully migrated and appropriate administrative, analytics, security and disaster recovery arrangements established. The platform enables IDEP to maintain and engage its alumni community, facilitate networking and knowledge sharing, support communities of practice, and monitor alumni engagement through relevant usage analytics. In addition, the ECA Fellowship Alumni Platform remains operational and technically maintained, with required improvements, security-related actions and Azure onboarding/deployment support implemented during the assignment.

Addis Ababa
Expected duration
Three months

Under the supervision of the Directors of SPORD and IDEP, IDEP's Head of Training and Research Division and Knowledge Management and IT section, the Information Systems Assistant will perform the following duties: • Provide technical assistance for the planning, design, development, configuration and implementation of the IDEP Alumni Platform. • Design and implement a robust, normalized, extensible and secure database architecture to support alumni profiles, programme information, networking, communities of practice, engagement and related platform functionalities. • Develop and configure required platform functionalities, including user and profile management, networking and collaboration features, knowledge-sharing functions, notifications, administration tools and analytics. • Deploy and configure the platform on Microsoft Azure Cloud, in coordination with relevant ECA technical teams and in accordance with applicable security and technical requirements. • Conduct migration and consolidation of relevant alumni data from the IDEP eLearning platform and other IDEP databases, ensuring data integrity, completeness and consistency. • Organize regular demonstrations of the platform with SPORD and IDEP staff, document feedback and implement agreed improvements. • Collaborate with ECA DITMS in conducting user acceptance testing, technical testing, security and compliance assessments and vulnerability testing, and implement required corrective actions and patches. • Coordinate technical arrangements for SMTP and notification services and support hosting and production deployment of the platform. • Collaborate with ECA translation services to extract and prepare relevant platform content for translation into French and support its integration into the platform. • Develop platform usage and user-data analytics functionalities to support monitoring of usage trends, engagement and performance. • Prepare and implement a disaster recovery approach to support data integrity, availability and continuity in the event of system failure or other unforeseen incidents. • Develop user and administrator documentation, including a practical how-to manual. • Provide tailored training to system administrators, forum moderators and other relevant users on platform administration and use. • Provide ongoing technical support, maintenance, troubleshooting and enhancement of the IDEP Alumni Platform. • Provide technical support for the continued maintenance and development of the ECA Fellowship Alumni Platform, including support for security clearance and Azure onboarding activities. • Perform other related technical tasks necessary for the successful implementation, deployment and operation of the alumni platforms.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Web Development, or a related field from a recognised and accredited institution. vacancies.postingTitle: Senior Investment Officer- Fixed Income (Credit), P5
vacancies.jobDescription:
Org. Setting and Reporting
The United Nations Secretary-General is responsible for the investment of the assets of the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund (UNJSPF). The Secretary-General has delegated this responsibility to the Representative of the Secretary-General for the investment of the assets of the UNJSPF (RSG). The RSG heads the Office of Investment Management (OIM), which manages a $100+ billion multi-asset class, global investment portfolio, about 85% of which is actively managed in-house. Asset classes under management comprise global equities, fixed income, foreign exchange, private equity, real estate, infrastructure, timber and commodities. OIM’s staff are all based in New York but come from over 40 countries. For more information please visit OIM's website at https://oim.unjspf.org/. This position is located in the Fixed Income Team. The Fixed Income portfolio of the UNJSPF consists of allocations to US treasuries, credit, securitized, high yield and local currency emerging market debt. The incumbent reports to the Director of Fixed Income.
Responsibilities
Under the overall supervision of the Director of the Fixed Income, the incumbent will be responsible for the following functions: 1. Provides leadership, decision-making and accountability of the credit portfolios in seeking superior investment returns against the respective benchmarks without undue risks over the long-term periods by: a. undertaking fundamental, valuation and technical analysis of credit markets, as well as economic trends, liquidity flows, political and regulatory frameworks relevant to security selection in credit markets. b. performing bottom-up investment research, utilizing multiple sources, and diverse platforms including primary research through sector and company visits. c. recommending asset allocation within the credit complex and relevant strategies to the Director of Fixed Income and actively exchanging views with the Internal Investment Committee and the colleagues of the Investment Section. d. recommending and implementing the transaction of specific securities to be purchased and sold. 2. Plans and oversees the management of activities undertaken by the unit by: a. Ensuring that substantive work programmes and programmed activities are carried out in a timely fashion. b. Coordinating diverse projects in the Unit, determining priorities and allocation of resources. c. Formulating investment policies and strategies to construct credit portfolios for fixed income. d. Analyzing outside market funds to recommend funds appropriate to the UNJSPF, when necessary. e. Preparing Investment strategies and contributing to asset allocation discussions and decisions within fixed income. 3. Manages, supervises and carries out the work programme of the Unit under his/her responsibility. Co-ordinates the work carried out by the Unit and provides programmatic and substantive reviews of drafts prepared by others. Ensures that output produced by the unit is of a high standard, is clear, objective and based on comprehensive data. 4. Provides comprehensive, clear, and accurate inputs in the preparation of position papers and reports for presentation to intergovernmental bodies such as the Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budget Questions, Pension Board, the General Assembly as appropriate by among others: a. Preparing reports on investment returns and strategy for review and discussion in regular scheduled internal portfolio review and staff-advisor meetings. b. Participating in Investments Committee meetings and preparing the required inputs. c. Initiating and leading special projects designed to improve the investment management decision process at OIM and enhance performance. d. Evaluating the advice and recommendations provided by external non-discretionary advisors and externally managed funds. 5. Carries out administrative tasks necessary for the functioning of the Unit, including: a. Monitoring of performance, parameters and critical indicators, reporting on budget performance, preparation of inputs, evaluation of staff performance b. Recruits staff for Unit taking geographical and gender balance and other institutional values into account. c. Manages, guides, develops and trains staff under his/her supervision. d. Fosters teamwork and communication among staff in the unit and across organizational boundaries. e. Represents the organization at interagency meetings, seminars, etc. on substantive issues. f. Participates in international, regional or national conferences and provides programmatic/substantive expertise on an issue or hold substantive and organizational discussions with representatives of other institutions. 6. Reports accurately and timely to the Representative of the Secretary-General Investments of the UNJSPF and Chief Investment Officer when requested. 7. Assists in reporting on investments and related matters to Governing Bodies, including the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Board, the Fifth Committee, the ACABQ, the BOA, and OIOS. 8. Leads team members efforts to collect and analyze data and provides insight to identify trends or patterns for data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. Ensures that everyone can discover, access, integrate and share the data they need.
Competencies
• Professionalism - Demonstrated ability and sound knowledge of fixed income, in particular corporate and government related sectors. Demonstrated ability and sound knowledge of applied macroeconomics, security analysis ESG and a successful track record of portfolio management. Ability to work under pressure and provide accurate, efficient and effective results. Ability to utilize various portfolio management and data processing tools; such as Bloomberg and familiarity with the use of Internet applications and MS Office programmes. The ability to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management; Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyse and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. • Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. • Accountability: Takes ownership of all responsibilities and honours commitments; delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within prescribed time, cost and quality standards; operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules; supports subordinates, provides oversight and takes responsibility for delegated assignments; takes personal responsibility for his/her own shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable. The internship is located at the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (UNOOSA) in Vienna, Austria. The intern will be placed in the Space Sustainability Unit (SSU). Org. Setting and Reporting
These positions (2) are located within the Common Administrative Platform (CAP) in New York at United Nations Headquarters, referred to as the One Executive Office ("One EO"), under the Division of Administration in the Department of Operational Support (DOS). One EO started its transition phase on 1 January 2026 as part of the UN80 reform initiative, which aims to consolidate common administrative functions across Secretariat entities into unified service platforms. The Department of Operational Support (DOS) was established to provide end-to-end operational support, advisory services and other solutions to operating entities across the Secretariat, including departments, offices away from headquarters, peace operations, and regional commissions. The Division of Administration (DOA) in New York provides administrative support functions (human resources, budget, finance and general administration) and facility management and commercial services to entities at United Nations Headquarters. It also provides financial operational services to entities across the globe. As Common Administrative Platform, the Division comprises the OneEO, the Financial Operations Service (including OnePayroll), and the Facilities and Commercial Activities Service. One EO provides the full range of administrative and operational services required by New York– based Secretariat client entities to fulfil their mandates, including human resources management, financial administration, travel, and general administrative support. c
Responsibilities
Within limits of delegated authority, the Human Resources Officer will carry out the following duties in the assigned regional portfolio, as applicable: GENERAL: • Develops and implements new human resources policies, practices and procedures to meet the evolving needs of the Organization and maintains effective and steady communication or working relations with UN Agencies to seek harmonization. • Monitors and ensures the implementation of human resources policies, practices and procedures and Represents HR in regional meetings as needed. • Keeps abreast of developments in various areas of human resources and serves as the first point of contact for regional human resources policy and administrative questions, supports implementation of Secretariat human resources reforms, and provides strategic advice on workforce planning and human resources arrangements during emergencies. • Prepares reports and participates and/or leads special human resources project and ensures active coordination of HR matters with other agencies. • May plan, organize, manage and supervise the work of the Unit/Section assigned and liaise with service providers to ensure continuity and coordination of HR matters. RECRUITMENT AND PLACEMENT: • Projects and monitors vacant posts of assigned level/group, Secretariat or mission-wide and ensures adherence to policies and procedures in filling these posts. • Recommends guidelines on promotion and placement of staff and supports requests for staff and affiliated personnel, including gratis personnel, United Nations Volunteers, consultants and individual contractors, and reviews position funding memoranda of understanding in consultation with the relevant offices. • Oversees preparation of vacancy announcements, reviews applications and provides short-lists to substantive offices and advises regional offices on the use of classified generic job descriptions and coordinates with Client Desk 5 on promotion and placement matters. • Arranges and conducts interviews for selection of candidates and advises on outreach strategies and provides regional leadership with regular geographic and gender representation data to support diverse candidate pools and gender balance. • Reviews recommendation on the selection of candidate by client offices. • Serves as ex-officio in or secretary to appointment and promotion bodies, examinations boards, and prepares and presents cases to these bodies. • Prepares job offers for successful candidates. • Participates in task forces and working groups identifying issues/problems, formulating policies and guidelines, and establishing new procedures. • Represents the Organization with full delegation of authority in discussions with senior government officials on recruitment and other human resources matters. • Plans, organizes, develops, coordinates and administers the National Competitive Examinations, G to P Examinations, Language professionals examinations and other programmes and tests related to recruitment of professional, general service and other categories of staff. Org. Setting and Reporting
ECA’s mission is to deliver ideas and actions for an empowered and transformed Africa; informed by the 2030 Agenda and Agenda 2063. The mission will be guided by ECA’s five strategic directions which are:(a) Advancing ECA’s position as a premier knowledge institution that builds on its unique position and privilege to bring global solutions to the continent’s problems and take local solution to the continent; (b) Developing macroeconomic and structural policy options to accelerate economic diversification and job creation; (c) Designing and implementing innovative financing models for infrastructure, and for human, physical and social assets for a transforming Africa; (d) Contributing solutions to regional and transboundary challenges, with a focus on peace security and social inclusion as an important development nexus; (e) Advocating Africa’s position at the global level and developing regional responses as a contribution to global governance issues. The African Institute for Economic Development and Planning (IDEP), located in Dakar (Senegal), is headed by a director who reports to the Deputy Executive Secretary (Programme Support). IDEP is the operational Arm of ECA in terms of capacity development and is responsible for translating the ECA "School of Thought" (research) into "Practice" (implementation). It is responsible for equipping African leaders and institutions with the skills necessary to develop effective policies for the management of the public sector, supporting the realization of the African Union’s Agenda 2063, the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and the Pact for the Future. IDEP aims to be positioned as a Regional Centre of Excellence for Capacity Development for the UN System (under the UN80 reform). This position is located in the African Institute for Economic Development and Planning (IDEP) in the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA). The Principal Programme Management Officer (Director) reports to the Deputy Executive Secretary – Programme Support (DES-PS).
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the Principal Programme Management Officer formulates and implements the substantive work programme of IDEP. Oversees the management of activities undertaken by the Institute, ensures that programmed activities are carried out in a timely manner, and co-ordinates work across the different areas of the Institute, with UNECA and with other organizations of the United Nations system, as appropriate. Specifically, the incumbent undertakes the following: 1. Strategic leadership and programme formulation • Assists the DES-PS in preparing the work programme of the Institute, determining priorities and allocating resources for the completion and timely delivery of outputs. • Leads, supervises and carries out the IDEP work programme, which aims to strengthen the capacity of Member States to: (i) formulate, implement, monitor and evaluate evidence-based socio-economic policies for the achievement of the 2030 Agenda or its successor framework, Agenda 2063 and national development agendas; and (ii) autonomously deploy modern digital and analytical development planning tools. • Co-ordinates capacity development efforts across ECA divisions and offices; and collaborates with other agencies and bodies of the United Nations system. 2. Management of human, financial, and other operational resources • Undertakes or oversees the programmatic and administrative tasks necessary for the functioning of the Institute, including the preparation of budgets and of inputs for results-based budgeting, and reporting on budget/programme performance. • Recruits staff, taking due account of gender and geographical balance. • Manages, guides, develops and trains staff under his/her supervision, including evaluating their performance (ePAS), and fosters teamwork and communication among staff within the Institute and across organizational boundaries. 3. Quality assurance, substantive oversight and programme delivery • Leads and supervises the substantive preparation and organization of meetings, seminars and similar events as well as the development of knowledge, research, training and communication products on substantive issues, with a view to enhancing the capacity of Member States for better development planning and policymaking. • Ensures that all outputs produced by the Institute meet high-quality standards and comply with the relevant mandates before completion, and that reports are clear, objective and based on comprehensive data; provides programmatic/substantive reviews of drafts prepared by others. • Ensures that these standards extend to the design and execution of high-impact leadership and policy dialogue programmes for mid-career and senior officials, and to the development and management of innovative financial and business models. 4. Intergovernmental bodies and governance • Co-ordinates and oversees the preparation of reports for intergovernmental bodies, such as the Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions, the Committee for Programme and Coordination, the Economic and Social Council, the General Assembly and other policy-making organs, as appropriate; reports to these bodies on budget/programme performance or on programmatic/substantive issues, particularly those presented in biannual and/or annual reports. • Organizes the statutory meetings of the IDEP Governing Council and the IDEP Technical Advisory Committee and submits annual reports to the ECA Conference of African Ministers of Finance, Planning and Economic Development. 5. Representation, partnerships, and resource mobilization • Represents IDEP at international, regional and national meetings, providing programmatic/substantive expertise, and holds discussions with representatives of other institutions to foster regional integration and collaboration in support of existing regional frameworks. • Promotes resource mobilization efforts by strengthening Member State contributions, developing targeted extra-budgetary programmes with the lead ECA section and ECA divisions, and building strategic partnerships with African Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) and Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs).

Ability to produce reports and papers on technical issues and to review and edit the work of others. Ability to apply UN rules, regulations, policies and guidelines in work situations. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. • Planning & Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. • Client Orientation: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client. • Leadership: Serves as a role model that other people want to follow: empowers others to translate vision into results; is proactive in developing strategies to accomplish objectives; establishes and maintains relationships with a broad range of people to understand needs and gain support; anticipates and resolves conflicts by pursuing mutually agreeable solutions; drives for change and improvements; does not accept the status quo; shows the courage to take unpopular stands. Provides leadership and takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work; demonstrates knowledge of strategies and commitment to the goal of gender balance in staffing. • Judgement/Decision-making: Identifies the key issues in a complex situation, and comes to the heart of the problem quickly; gathers relevant information before making a decision; considers positive and negative impacts of decisions prior to making them; takes decisions with an eye to the impact on others and on the Organization; proposes a course of action or makes a recommendation based on all available information; checks assumptions against facts; determines that the actions proposed will satisfy the expressed and underlying needs for the decision; makes tough decisions when necessary.
Education
Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in business or public administration, human resources, finance, accounting, economics, law, social sciences or related area is required. A first-level university degree in combination with additional two years of qualifying work experience may be accepted in lieu of an advanced university degree.

Experience in designing, delivering, or overseeing capacity-building programmes is required. Experience leading a substantive programme or institution within the UN system or another multilateral or intergovernmental organization, focused on development policy, planning or capacity building in developing countries, is desirable. Experience in reporting to intergovernmental or governing bodies, and in representing an organization in high-level policy dialogue with senior government officials, is desirable.

Result of Service
The Remote Sensing Data Engineer consultant will provide a reliable flow of satellite detections into MARS from both existing and newly integrated data sources; a healthy, monitored ingestion pipeline as data volume and automation grow; an owned and improved estimation of source persistency and total annual emissions for methane point sources; and automated public data products published on IMEO’s Data Platform.
Work Location
Remote
Expected duration
12 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority setting the global environmental agenda and advocating for environmental action across the UN system. UNEP’s International Methane Emissions Observatory (IMEO) is a data-driven initiative accelerating reductions in methane emissions, a major contributor to climate change. IMEO provides open, reliable and actionable data to support emissions reductions aligned with the Paris Agreement. To do this, IMEO is harnessing a methane data revolution under way thanks to rapidly advancing technology and momentum for methane action. IMEO collects, integrates, and reconciles data from methane-detecting satellites, scientific measurement studies, rigorous industry reporting through the Oil and Gas Methane Partnership 2.0 (OGMP 2.0), and national emissions inventories. These initiatives are game-changers for climate action – and as a core implementing partner of the Global Methane Pledge, IMEO is shaping the future of methane mitigation. Within IMEO, the Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) connects near-real-time satellite methane detections with notifications to stakeholders. The consultant will focus on integrating new satellite data sources into MARS, including high-temporal-frequency geostationary sensors, whose detections must be ingested as grouped plume events. This includes the adjustments to the MARS PostgreSQL database schema needed to ensure smooth ingestion, processing, and storage. The consultant will also share the day-to-day monitoring and maintenance of the MARS data ingestion pipeline, which runs on Azure: as the number of automated processes grows, so does the number of ingestion issues, which the consultant will triage in Jira and resolve in production, extending the MARS data quality monitoring checks to cover the new data sources and processing steps. In addition, the consultant will own the MARS source persistency pipeline, which estimates source persistency (the fraction of satellite observations in which a source is detected emitting) and total annual emissions for methane point sources, improving it in line with the latest research directions. The consultant will also maintain and automate the public data pipelines built on these results, such as plume and source exports, the top 50 emitters list, and detection and non-detection time series.
Qualifications/special skills
Required: First-level Degree (e.g. Bachelors) in Remote Sensing, Computer Science, Data Science, Physics Or a related field (optional) • High proficiency in Python and its scientific and geospatial stack, applied to data processing and analysis tools, for satellite remote sensing data. This is a hands-on coding role requiring comfort with, and enthusiasm for, software development • Experience with PostgreSQL, cloud platforms – preferably Azure, and ideally its ML and web app services – and software engineering best practices: version control (Git), maintainable and tested code, containerization (Docker), and CI/CD (Jenkins or similar) • Scientific expertise in remote sensing, demonstrated through open-source projects or scientific publications, with particular interest in the retrieval and interpretation of atmospheric trace gases from satellite imagery • Experience building or maintaining operational data pipelines and data quality monitoring systems, including issue tracking with tools such as Jira. • A genuine interest in environmental and climate-related challenges, demonstrated through academic projects, personal research, open-source contributions or independent learning.
Languages
English is the working language of UNEP's IMEO. Knowledge of additional languages is an asset.
Additional Information
• An operational ingestion workflow for high-frequency satellite data source, including the PostgreSQL database tables required to store it and the grouping of high-frequency detections into plume events. • An owned and documented source persistency pipeline running in Azure ML Studio, with improved estimates of source persistency and total annual emissions for methane point sources. • Data quality monitoring checks extended to the new data sources and processing steps, with ingestion issues triaged and resolved in production. • Automated generation of the MARS public data products for plumes, sources and top 50 emitters, further automating the existing workflows.

Result of Service
Purpose of the assignment: UNODC accordingly seeks a consultant with expertise in precursor chemicals and knowledge of the chemical and pharmaceutical industry/ industry associations in Lao PDR, for conducting a mapping of all industries in Lao PDR, which is relevant from the perspective of illicit drug manufacture. The industries concerned (hereinafter referred to as ‘relevant industry’) could be: • Relevant chemical/ pharmaceutical industry manufacturing internationally controlled precursors. • Relevant chemical/ pharmaceutical industry manufacturing chemicals included on the limited international special surveillance list, including stable intermediates of controlled precursors, pre-precursors, etc. and common derivatives, as well as other related substances that can be converted into a controlled precursor or a drug by readily applicable means. • Industry that can likely be approached for contract synthesis of such chemicals. • Related industry in the supply chain for the aforesaid chemicals, which are likely to be susceptible from the point of view of diversion. Specific tasks to be performed by the consultant: Under the supervision of and in close coordination with the UNODC staff, the incumbent will carry out the following activities on Lao PDR: • Conduct a country-wide mapping exercise of all the relevant industry manufacturing or trading in internationally scheduled and non-scheduled precursor chemicals, including pre-precursors, and the industry involved in contract synthesis of such chemicals. • Identify relevant Government stakeholders that would need to be involved/consulted beyond the stakeholders involved in narcotics regulation to include those on licensing, environmental aspects, trade, etc. and facilitate the convening of national coordination meetings as required.
Work Location
Home-based with travel
Expected duration
11/12/26-31/03/27
Duties and Responsibilities
Background of the assignment: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) provides technical assistance related to combating drugs and precursor trafficking to requesting Member States. The Regional Programme for Southeast Asia and the Pacific 2022 – 2026 is designed to address both present and emerging needs within these regions, with the ultimate objective, namely, to secure and reinforce the rule of law in South-East Asia and the Pacific and ensure vulnerable groups and communities in the region are protected from drugs and crime. As part of the Regional Programme, UNODC’s Regional Office for Southeast Asia and the Pacific (ROSEAP) is implementing a project entitled “Southeast Asia Precursor Control and Border Management Project”, which aims to enhance the institutional capacity of selected ASEAN Member States in detecting and identifying the illicit trafficking of drugs and precursor chemicals, addressing the gaps of frontline officers in recognizing non-controlled chemicals that are increasingly trafficked and used by organized crime groups to produce synthetic drugs. Recognizing the urgency of raising awareness among responsible authorities, the project focuses on targeted capacity-building through national law enforcement academies and authorities, ensuring sustainable knowledge transfer, and supporting the establishment of a proper monitoring system on chemical control, in alignment with the objectives of the CTCBP/ACCBP to counter transnational organized crime and illicit trafficking by strengthening land border security and cross-border cooperation. The activities under this project fall under one main outcome: Strengthened border security and precursor control measures to address the growing drug problem in countries where Canada engages. Resulting in 4 intermediate outcomes, as follows: 1. Enhanced use of investigative techniques on border security and precursor control by national law enforcement institutions in Southeast Asia to counter transnational organized crime and the drug problem. 2. Increased adoption of gender-inclusive human resource policies by law enforcement institutions in Southeast Asia. 3. Enhanced gender-sensitive and human rights-based regional cooperation on drug and precursor trafficking cases by national law enforcement agencies in Southeast Asia. 4. Enhanced cooperation/engagement on precursor chemical trafficking by public and private sector stakeholders in the lower Mekong Region. UNODC ROSEAP is going to undertake various activities under these outcomes, including capacity needs assessments, stakeholder engagement, training, and workshops related to drugs and precursor control, and is seeking a consultant to support their implementation. The purpose of this assignment is to strengthen capacities for drug and precursor control in cooperation with the Secretariat of the International Narcotics Control Board (INCB). INCB is an independent and quasi-judicial control organ, established by the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs, for monitoring the implementation of the international drug control treaties. Its Secretariat has developed a methodology to identify the chemical needs of a country, and the consultant will use the same to allow comparability between reports from different countries. Precursor chemicals play a vital role in the processing and illicit manufacture of drugs. However, in contrast to the harmful substances they are used to create, some of these same chemicals are extremely important in our daily lives as they provide the building blocks for innumerable commodities on which the modern world relies. It is this duality of licit and illicit applications for precursor chemicals that confronts Governments with the serious and difficult responsibility to exercise appropriate control over their use. The Board has also highlighted the issues of the use of non-scheduled chemicals and even ‘made-to-order’ or ‘designer chemicals’ in illicit drug manufacture. Actions to address these challenges were also proposed in various resolutions of the General Assembly, the Economic and Social Council and the Commission on Narcotic Drugs, most recently in Commission resolution 60/5 on “Increasing international coordination in relation to precursors and non-scheduled precursor chemicals used in the illicit manufacture of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances” and resolution 65/3 entitled “Intensifying efforts to address the diversion of non-scheduled chemicals frequently used in the illicit manufacture of drugs and the proliferation of designer precursors”. Oftentimes, these chemicals are custom-made in a form that makes it easy to transform them into the desired precursors (internationally controlled) or the drug itself. Traffickers have therefore sought to obtain chemicals that may be used as substitutes for those that are more closely monitored. Global chemical supplies rest largely in the hands of private and sometimes state-owned industry. Governments and industry can deny drug trafficking organization access to the precursor chemicals used in illicit drug manufacture through improved cooperation and industry engagement. In August 2022, INCB released a new resource document entitled “Global review of categories of industries involved in the manufacture, trade and distribution of chemicals used in the illicit manufacture of drugs”. The document highlights the peculiarities of the different categories of industry and is aimed at contributing to an understanding of the range of industries that might, often unknowingly, be targeted by illicit drug manufacturers. The document is intended to serve as a background and guidance document for mapping national industry landscapes and, eventually, sensitising the concerned industries. UNODC intends to work with Governments to map the relevant industry in selected countries and convene national level coordination meeting(s), as required, with involvement of relevant industry and other stakeholders, with a long-term goal of establishing a mechanism for Governments and industry to commit: 1. Promote appropriate internal control measures to prevent diversion of chemicals in their supply chain; 2. Enhance end-use monitoring to ensure that chemicals are not being resold to illicit drug manufacturing organizations; and 3. Not supply any chemical that could reasonably be used in the illicit manufacture of synthetic drugs, precursors and NPS if there is no known legitimate use.
Qualifications/special skills
An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in science, international relations, international crime prevention, international criminal justice administration, law or regulatory enforcement, public administration, or a closely related/relevant subject or related is required. A first-level university degree in similar fields, in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience, may be accepted instead of an advanced university degree. Excellent knowledge of the theory of and best practices in drug control, international relations, and at least 10 years of experience in the area of national and international drug and precursor control, policy formulation or advisory functions in related fields, is required. Experience of working as or closely with police, customs personnel, prosecutor’s office, court, and other relevant disciplines involved in the investigation and prosecution of serious organized crime, in particular drug and precursor-related crime, is required. Working experience with relevant industries, such as the pharmaceutical/ chemical industry, is desirable; specifically, relevant industries in Lao PDR. Experience in developing public-private partnerships, in particular with the chemical industry, is desirable. Experience in imparting capacity building, including training activities, is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this position, fluency in English and Lao is required. Knowledge of another United Nations official language is an advantage.

Not available.

The United Nations (UN) Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) is the UN Secretariat department responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to complex emergencies and natural disasters.
