vacancies.postingTitle: Development of biodiversity coordination mechanism for Armenia consultant
vacancies.jobTitle: Development of biodiversity coordination mechanism for Armenia consultant
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
I. A comprehensive desk review of existing biodiversity and environmental coordination mechanisms in Armenia and relevant international models, providing an evidence base for the design of a fit-for-purpose national biodiversity coordination mechanism; II. A Coordination Mechanism Concept document, developed through structured stakeholder consultations, proposing options for establishing or adapting an inter-agency coordination body for biodiversity in Armenia – including an analysis of the potential to build on the existing Inter-Agency Council on Climate Change and the feasibility of adding a dedicated Secretariat function; III. A Legal Mapping Note identifying the specific legal and/or administrative act(s) that will need to be developed to formally establish the proposed coordination mechanism under Armenian law (e.g. government decree, ministerial order, or amendment to existing mandates), including a description of the process and responsible authority for adoption of each act; IV. A stakeholder consultation report documenting the views of key government and non-government actors on coordination needs, institutional options, and governance design; V. Strengthened national institutional capacity for cross-sectoral coordination on biodiversity, contributing to more effective and inclusive NBSAP implementation aligned with KMGBF Targets 14 and 21.
Work Location
Remote
Expected duration
2.7 months
Duties and Responsibilities
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. Its mandate is to coordinate the development of environmental policy consensus by keeping the global environment under review and bringing emerging issues to the attention of governments and the international community for action. UNEP’s Ecosystems Division engages with governments and other partners to develop and promote ecosystem-based solutions for sustainable development. This assignment is in the Nature Frameworks Support Unit of the Biodiversity and Land Branch, Ecosystems Division. UNEP is also one of the key agencies hosting the NBSAP Accelerator Partnership. The NBSAP Accelerator Partnership is a country-led global initiative that supports the development and implementation of ambitious National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) and collectively achieve the goals and targets of the Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) and, ultimately, the global vision of living in harmony with nature by 2050. The NBSAP Accelerator Partnership provides technical and financial support for the implementation of GBF-aligned NBSAPs. This includes strengthening country-driven coordination, fostering collaboration among stakeholders, facilitating knowledge sharing and best practices, and addressing country-specific needs. It also helps raise national profile of countries' NBSAPs, and fast-track implementation through a matchmaking service, increased access to expertise, knowledge and capacity development, and in-country facilitation support. A National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) is a country’s principal document for implementing the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). It outlines a nation’s approach to conserving its biodiversity, ensuring its sustainable use, and fairly sharing the benefits derived from genetic resources. Armenia is a party to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). They signed and ratified the convention in 1992 and 1993, respectively. The Country also acceded to the Cartagena Protocol in 2004 and the Nagoya Protocol in 2026. Duties and Responsibilities The NBSAP Accelerator Partnership’s Facilitator Programme is looking for a consultant to assist the Government of the Republic of Armenia to develop a biodiversity coordination mechanism. The effective implementation of Armenia’s revised National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) requires more than strong policy commitments – it demands a fundamental shift in how biodiversity is governed across government and society as a whole. The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) explicitly calls for the application of Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Society approaches, recognizing that the drivers of biodiversity loss and the levers needed to reverse it lie across all sectors of the economy and all segments of society, and cannot be addressed by the environment sector alone. In practice, a Whole-of-Government approach requires that biodiversity considerations are systematically mainstreamed into the policies, budgets, and planning processes of all relevant government bodies – including the Ministry of Economy, the Ministry of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure, the Ministry of Finance, local self-government bodies, and others. A Whole-of-Society approach goes further, recognizing that civil society organisations, the private sector, academic and research institutions, indigenous and local communities, youth, and women’s groups are not merely stakeholders to be consulted but active partners whose knowledge, resources, and on-the-ground actions are indispensable to achieving the goals of the NBSAP. Their participation should be organized through clearly defined modalities, distinguishing formal decision-making functions from advisory and thematic working-group arrangements, so that inclusive engagement strengthens rather than dilutes the mechanism's governance function. Without a structured, inclusive, and legally anchored coordination mechanism that operationalizes both principles, NBSAP implementation risks remaining siloed within the environment sector, under-resourced, and disconnected from the cross-sectoral decisions that most consequentially affect biodiversity. Armenia has existing institutional structures that may offer a practical foundation for such a mechanism. The Inter-Agency Council on Climate Change ("IACC") already brings together relevant line ministries for climate-related coordination and policy coherence, offering one possible model for cross-governmental engagement. Expanding the IACC's mandate to encompass biodiversity is one option to be assessed: the consultant should assess and compare this option against alternatives, including the establishment of a dedicated interagency biodiversity council or other high-level coordination mechanisms, and recommend the model best suited to Armenia's institutional context. Whichever model is selected, it should be capable of supporting a dedicated Secretariat function to manage day-to-day coordination across governmental and non-governmental actors and to serve as the operational hub for Whole-of-Society engagement. A biodiversity coordination mechanism that is grounded in Armenian law, designed around Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Society principles, and owned by national institutions is essential for the long-term governance of biodiversity policy in Armenia. This activity will recruit a consultant to conduct a systematic analysis of existing coordination mechanisms, develop a concrete and inclusive coordination concept in consultation with key government and non-government stakeholders, and identify the legal and policy steps required to formally establish the mechanism. The assignment directly contributes to KMGBF Target 14 (mainstreaming biodiversity across all sectors and levels of government and society), Target 21 (ensuring knowledge and information are available to guide policy and action), and Targets 22 and 23 (equitable participation of indigenous peoples, local communities, youth, and women, and gender-responsive governance). It supports the broader goal of building durable, inclusive national capacity for NBSAP implementation that endures beyond the life of the project. Specific Task I. Review of existing inter-agency coordination mechanisms in Armenia (with a focus on the Inter-Agency Council on Climate Change and other environment-related bodies) and analysis of international good practices in biodiversity coordination mechanisms. II. Design and facilitate consultations (online or in person) with key government stakeholders (Ministry of Environment and relevant line ministries), civil society organisations, private sector representatives, academic institutions, and UN agencies including UN RCO. Consultations to cover: gaps in current coordination; preferred institutional model; legal anchoring options. III. Based on the desk study and stakeholder consultations, develop a Coordination Mechanism Concept document presenting: (a) recommended institutional model (including analysis of expanding IACC mandate vs. establishing a standalone body); (b) proposed mandate, membership, and governance structure; (c) role and functions of the proposed Secretariat; (d) resource and sustainability considerations. IV. In consultation with the Ministry of Environment and relevant legal experts, identify the level of legal and/or administrative act(s) required to formally establish the coordination mechanism under Armenian law. This may include a government decree, ministerial order, or amendment to an existing legal instrument. V. Prepare a consolidated Final Report integrating all workstreams, incorporating NBSAP AP and government feedback, and including actionable recommendations for the adoption and operationalisation of the coordination mechanism. The mechanism's objective should be defined in operational rather than purely advisory terms: it should facilitate coordination of NBSAP implementation, alignment of actions among responsible institutions, progress monitoring, data exchange, coordination of donor-supported initiatives, and annual reporting. Its legal basis and institutional status – whether established through a Government Decree, a Prime Minister's Decision, a Ministerial Order, amendments to existing legal acts, or another appropriate instrument – should provide it with adequate authority to engage multiple public authorities and require information or action from them. The respective roles of the Ministry of Environment, other government institutions, and any dedicated Secretariat should be clearly specified as part of this design. The mechanism should also be explicitly linked to the BIOFIN process, particularly with respect to biodiversity financing gaps, subsidy reform, review of harmful incentives, the efficiency of biodiversity-related public expenditure, and the implementation of biodiversity finance solutions. The consultant will report to the Programme Management Officer of the Nature Frameworks Support Unit in close coordination and collaboration with the NBSAP AP facilitator in Armenia and relevant government representatives.
Qualifications/special skills
Advanced university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in environmental law, public administration, environmental policy, political science, or a related field. A first level degree with additional two years of qualifying experience maybe accepted in lieu of advanced degree. Minimum 7 years of professional experience in environmental governance, public administration, or institutional policy is required Demonstrated experience in institutional analysis and/or the development of coordination mechanisms, inter-agency bodies, or governance frameworks is required Familiarity with Armenia’s environmental institutional landscape, including the mandate of the Ministry of Environment and relevant line ministries is required Knowledge of biodiversity policy and/or the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework is desirable Prior experience working with UN agencies, international organisations, or development partners is desirable
Languages
English is the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. Fluency in Armenian and English (written and spoken) is required.
Additional Information
Not available.

This position is located in the English Language Unit, News Section I, News and Content Branch, News and Media Division, Department of Global Communications. The News and Content Branch is primarily a multimedia service provided by the United Nations to promote the universal ideals of the United Nations, including peace, respect for human rights and development. It produces a range of audio, video and multimedia products across nine languages available to media organizations around the world. The Unit is looking for interns who wish to gain hands-on experience in the UN newsroom, particularly in the production of daily news, in-depth features and other multimedia products in English. The intern will undertake assigned project activities under supervision. The intern's duties will include:  Drafting English news articles by integrating and translating information from various sources, including reports, press releases, official statements, resolutions, etc.  Proofreading news articles before and after publication.  Assist with fact-checking and background research.  Assist in the production of graphic, visual and audio content.  The intern will be encouraged to work on feature stories and conduct research and interviews, and draft feature stories.  Reviewing the partnerships database by collaborating with the UN Partnerships Unit and looking for new digital media and other partners, including finding trustworthy entities that work on fact-checking and media literacy.  Perform other duties as assigned, including outreach.

The Office of Supply Chain Management includes the Office of the Assistant Secretary- General for Supply Chain Management, Logistics Division, Procurement Division, Uniformed Capabilities Support Division, Global Service Centre, Aviation Safety Section and the Enabling and Outreach Service. The mandate of the Procurement Division is to provide responsive, effective, and quality expert procurement services and business advice to United Nations (UN) Headquarters, field missions, and other UN organizations, while achieving best value for money, ensuring a competitive, fair and transparent process in accordance with established regulations, rules and procedures.

In its Resolution A/RES/72/279, the United Nations General Assembly endorsed the transformation of the Development Operations Coordination Office (DCO) as a stand-alone coordination office within the United Nations Secretariat. DCO exercises managerial and oversight functions of the resident coordinator system under the oversight of the Chair of United Nations Sustainable Development Group (UNSDG). In 2026, DCO undertook a recalibration to ensure the RC system remains optimally configured to support the acceleration of the 2030 Agenda and embodies the UN 2.0 shift anchored in data, digital, innovation, behavioral science, strategic foresight, and a mission driven organizational culture. The position is part of the Regional Office for Arab States and performs liaison functions based in New York, hosted in the Strategic Partnerships and Engagement Division. The position reports to both the respective Senior Programme Management Officer in the Regional Office and the Chief of the Inter-governmental Section in the Strategic Partnerships and Engagement Division. The Regional Director for Arab States is the second reporting officer.

Coordination and liaison support between Headquarters and the Regional Office • Under the guidance of the supervisor and in close collaboration with the the Regional Office and the Chief of the Inter-governmental Section, facilitates timely two-way information flow between headquarters and the Arab States Region, including the communication of country demand, regional perspectives, corporate guidance and agreed follow-up. • Supports the implementation and monitoring of the work plan of the Regional Office, as needed. • Supports selected Resident Coordinators Office and UN country team processes, including retreats and strategic planning exercises, as defined by the Regional Office. • Contributes to efforts to systematize and share knowledge, lessons learned and good practices among Regional Offices and Resident • Coordinator Offices on sustainable development and integrated policy support. • Undertakes on-the-job and other training activities both internally and externally. • Performs other duties as required.
Competencies
PROFESSIONALISM: Ability to apply sustainable development theories, concepts and approaches. Ability to conduct independent research and analysis on sustainable development topics, determine suitability, validity and accuracy of data provided by different sources. Shows skill in developing sources for data collection. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. TEAMWORK: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. COMMUNICATION: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed.
Education
Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in sustainable development, economics, public policy, public administration, finance, natural resources management, engineering, law, social sciences, or a related field. A first-level university degree in combination with qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Successful completion of both degree and non-degree programs in data analytics, business analytics, or data science programs is an advantage.

Not available.

A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in sustainable development, public policy, development cooperation, policy analysis of related area is required. Experience with inter-agency and/or intergovernmental collaboration in the development sector is required. Experience of initiating and developing partnerships is desirable. Experience in sustainable development issues of the Arab States region is desirable. Experience of integrating gender equality and other inclusion dimensions (youth, disability) is desirable. Experience in the United Nations system or a comparable international organization is desirable. Field experience in development cooperation is desirable. Two years or more of experience in data analytics or related area is desirable.

vacancies.jobTitle: YPP Exam: Development and Sustainability (for external applicants)
vacancies.jobDescription:
Org. Setting and Reporting
Candidates who successfully complete the Young Professionals Programme (YPP) examination process will be placed on a roster used to fill appropriate vacancies. Candidates may be selected from the roster as relevant vacancies become available across the UN Secretariat. The roster is valid and used to fill positions, for a period of three years. It is important to understand that placement on the roster does not guarantee an offer of employment. Candidates selected from the roster will be offered a two-year fixed term contract at the start of their Professional career with the UN. After two years, and subject to satisfactory performance, they may be granted a continuing contract. YPP placements are at P-1/P-2 level (entry level professional, Associate Officer positions). These positions may become available at various UN Secretariat offices, including, but not limited to: Addis Ababa, Bangkok, Beirut, Geneva, Nairobi, New York, Santiago, Vienna. Successful candidates must be willing to be placed in a position at any UN duty station or field operation. YPP positions in Development and Sustainability are located primarily in the Department of Economic and Social Affairs (DESA), United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), and the Regional Commissions, which are the regional branches of the United Nations Secretariat. These entities support the link between global policies and national and regional action across economic, social, environmental and sustainable development issues, guided by the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Positions may cover a range of functional and substantive areas, including economic affairs, social affairs, population affairs, statistics, data science, environmental protection, and related areas of sustainable development. Specific assignments may focus on particular sectors or areas of specialization. Associate Officers in these positions typically report to a Senior Officer, Head of Unit, Head of Branch or Section, or Chief of Section. Please be sure to carefully read the Special Notice section below and visit careers.un.org/ypp for more information.
Responsibilities
The Young Professionals Programme (YPP) examination in Development and Sustainability covers a broad range of topics, with a focus on economics, statistics, social affairs, environmental issues, and sustainable development, as well as skills related to technology and digital transformation, and programme management support. It also encompasses other areas within the Development and Sustainability field that are addressed by the various entities of the United Nations system. Candidates who are successful in the examination may be appointed to positions in a variety of functional areas. Responsibilities will vary by assignment but may include the following: Research, Analysis and Data • Conducts research and analysis on economic, social, environmental, statistical, demographic and sustainable development issues, including collecting, evaluating, analysing and interpreting quantitative and qualitative data and information from a variety of sources. • Contributes to the collection, validation, compilation, analysis, dissemination and visualization of statistical data and other information, and to the development and maintenance of relevant data platforms and information systems. • Applies appropriate research methods, statistical methodologies, analytical models and other tools, including statistical programming languages and software, to identify trends, assess developments and support evidence-based analysis and decision-making. • Contributes to the development and application of analytical methodologies and tools, including, where relevant, emerging technologies and data science approaches. • Analyses national, regional and global trends, policies and experiences, including progress in the implementation of internationally agreed development goals and frameworks, such as the Sustainable Development Goals. Policy Analysis and Written Outputs • Contributes to the preparation of analytical studies, research reports, background papers, technical documents and other written outputs on economic, social, environmental, statistical, demographic and sustainable development issues. • Prepares briefing notes, presentations, inputs to speeches and other materials, including the communication of technical and analytical findings in a manner accessible to specialist and non-specialist audiences. • Researches and maintains up to date information on relevant policies, methodologies, emerging issues and developments within assigned areas of work. Intergovernmental Support and Stakeholder Engagement • Provides substantive support to intergovernmental and expert processes, including preparing inputs to reports, statements and other documentation; following meetings and preparing summaries; and supporting panels, round tables, expert group meetings, seminars and conferences. • Liaises and collaborates, as appropriate, with governments, international and regional organizations, national institutions, academia, civil society and other stakeholders to exchange information and support substantive activities. Technical Cooperation and Capacity Development • Contributes to the design, preparation and implementation of technical cooperation and capacity development programmes and projects, including compiling and analysing relevant data and information and preparing project documentation. • Monitors and assesses the implementation of programmes and projects and contributes to the development of approaches and mechanisms for tracking progress and results. • Supports technical assistance and capacity development activities, including the preparation and delivery of training, workshops and other knowledge-sharing activities and, where applicable, participation in advisory or fact-finding missions. General • Contributes to outreach, knowledge-sharing and communication activities, including the preparation of publications, presentations and other materials for a variety of audiences. • Performs other related duties as required.
Competencies
Professionalism: • Shows pride in work and in achievements • Demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter • Is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results • Is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns • Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges • Remains calm in stressful situations • Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work Planning & Organizing: • Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies • Identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required • Allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work • Foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning • Monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary • Uses time efficiently Teamwork: • Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals • Solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others • Places team agenda before personal agenda • Supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position • Shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings
Education
At least a first-level university degree (i.e., Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent degree of at least three years) in an area of study relevant to economics, statistics, data science, social affairs, environment, and sustainable development. Candidates with an advanced degree are encouraged to apply. Degrees accepted must be in economics, statistics, data science, social affairs, environment, and sustainable development or a related field, in one of the following areas (to be selected from the “Main Course of Study” dropdown menu): Agriculture, Foresty & Fishery; Business & Administration; Computing; Environmental Protection; Humanities; Law; Mathematics & Statistics; Social & Behavioural Science Important: when preparing your application in Inspira, if you do not see your exact degree listed, please choose the field of study that is closest to your degree, from the “Field of Study” and “Main Course of Study” dropdown menus; then type the exact title in original language as well as its translation in English or French in the additional comment boxes. Do NOT select “other” for main course of study or field of study (or you will be automatically disqualified).
Job - Specific Qualification
Not available.
Work Experience
No work experience is required. Relevant work experience may be taken into consideration as an additional screening criteria when more than 90 candidates from the same country apply to the same exam area. 
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, either English or French is required. Oral examination / Interviews   Knowledge of UN languages may be tested at any of these stages.  Applications will be screened on the basis of the eligibility criteria in this Job Opening.    The written examination will be conducted via an online testing platform.  Candidates convoked for the written examination will be responsible for identifying and securing a location suitable for them to complete the examination (i.e., a computer with a reliable internet connection). Further information regarding the online testing platform and exam preparation guidance will be provided to those convoked for the examination. The written examination is planned to be offered in two parts, with the following tentative timeframe (exact dates to be announced):    Part I consists of 1) the General Paper, which assesses competencies and abilities critical to success in working in an international affairs context, and 2) first part of the Specialized Paper, multiple choice questions which assess knowledge and attributes relevant to the exam area.  Part I is currently anticipated for February 2027, exact dates to be provided for those invited. Org. Setting and Reporting
In its Resolution A/RES/72/279, the United Nations General Assembly endorsed the transformation of the Development Operations Coordination Office (DCO) as a stand-alone coordination office within the United Nations Secretariat. DCO exercises managerial and oversight functions of the Resident Coordinator system (RCS) under the collective ownership of the members of the United Nations Sustainable Development Group (UNSDG). In 2026, DCO undertook a comprehensive organizational recalibration to ensure the RCS remains optimally configured to support the acceleration of the 2030 Agenda in its final years, and fully embodies the UN 2.0 shift—anchored in data, digital, innovation, behavioral science, strategic foresight, and a mission driven organizational culture. The position is located in the Office of the Assistant Secretary-General of the United Nations Development Coordination Office (UNDCO) and reports to the Chief of Staff. The role is responsible for managing the UNSDG Secretariat.
Responsibilities
Within delegated authority, the incumbent will be responsible for the following duties: • Lead the effective functioning of the UN Sustainable Development Group and work planning, particularly the UNSDG Principals • Support to the UNSDG Chair and UNSDG Principals in the preparation of key meetings of the UNSDG, including organization of the meetings, preparation of relevant background materials, coordinating effectively with relevant offices of member entities in this process. • Provide direct line management BIG Secretariat, providing strategic direction, broad oversight and integration of these issues into servicing of the UNSDG. • Work closely with relevant teams in DCO, ensures monitoring and effective implementation of decisions of UNSDG Principals, including coordinating the timely delivery of guidance, tools and other products decided by the UNSDG and their effective utilization by UNSDG entities. • Provide substantive support to UNSDG-related interagency and intergovernmental processes, including overseeing DCO’s substantive engagement in the Quadrennial Comprehensive Policy Review, and the Operational Activities Segment of the Economic and Social Council and other related intergovernmental and interagency discussions. • Supervise preparation of various written output such as speeches, briefing notes, analyses and other inputs for the UNSDG Chair, Vice-Chair and DCO senior management on matters pertaining to UNSDG strategic priorities. • Advise DCO Director and Senior Management on the positioning of UNSDG strategic priorities in interagency and intergovernmental bodies, including the Economic and Social Council, and the General Assembly. • Conduct regular outreach, information sharing, consultations, and coordination activities with UNSDG focal points in UN agencies, funds and programmes, and other relevant colleagues within UNSDG entities to improve understanding of, and alignment with, UNSDG priorities. • In coordination with relevant DCO units, ensure timely monitoring and follow-up of UNSDG entities' cost-sharing commitments for funding of the Resident Coordinator system. • Ensure effective utilization, supervision and development of staff; Guides, evaluates and mentors staff. • Keep abreast of latest emerging trends and innovative approaches related to the UNSDG. • Work as a member of the DCO Front Office team, monitoring and providing quality assurance of relevant inputs from across the Resident Coordinator system and UNSDG member entities, ensuring consistency of message, current topics and rapid response to stakeholder inquiries and information requests. • Lead team members' efforts to collect and analyze data and provides insight to identify trends or patterns for data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. Ensure that everyone can discover, access, integrate and share the data they need. • Performs other related duties as required.
Competencies
PROFESSIONALISM: Ability to apply sustainable development theories, concepts and approaches to the work of the UNSDG. Ability to identify issues, analyze and participate in the resolution of issues/problems. Ability to conduct data collection using various methods. Conceptual analytical and evaluative skills to conduct independent research and analysis, including familiarity with and experience in the use of various research sources, including electronic resources on the internet, intranet, and other databases. Ability to coordinate and convene complex processes with multiple stakeholders. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines, and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. TEAMWORK: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others' ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. PLANNING & ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. MANAGING PERFORMANCE: Delegates the appropriate responsibility, accountability and decision-making authority; makes sure that roles, responsibilities and reporting lines are clear to each staff member; accurately judges the amount of time and resources needed to accomplish a task and matches task to skills; monitors progress against milestones and deadlines; regularly discusses performance and provides feedback and coaching to staff; encourages risk-taking and supports creativity and initiative; actively supports the development and career aspirations of staff; appraises performance fairly. LEADERSHIP: Serves as a role model that other people want to follow: empowers others to translate vision into results; is proactive in developing strategies to accomplish objectives; establishes and maintains relationships with a broad range of people to understand needs and gain support; anticipates and resolves conflicts by pursuing mutually agreeable solutions; drives for change and improvements; does not accept the status quo; shows the courage to take unpopular stands. Provides leadership and takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work; demonstrates knowledge of strategies and commitment to the goal of gender balance in staffing.
Education
Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in sustainable development, economics, public policy, public administration, finance, natural resources management, engineering, law, social sciences or related field. A first-level university degree in combination with qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.
Job - Specific Qualification
Not available.
Work Experience
A minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in project or programme management, policy-oriented work in interagency coordination, development system reforms or a related area is required. A minimum of five (5) years of experience in coordinating meetings and products related to system-wide application of development system reforms, impacting all UNSDG members, and the functioning of the Resident Coordinator system is required. Experience in UN and/or other inter-agency policy-making, programming and/or strategy development is required Experience in the design and/or roll-out of UN development system reform efforts is required. Broad understanding of the UN development system understanding of the efficiencies agenda including (BOS, CBO, CP) is desirable. Field experience in development cooperation is desirable. Experience working at the headquarters of a development cooperation entity is desirable. Experience in managing large multicultural teams at the country, regional or global levels is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult https://languages.un.org for details).

The term “sexual abuse” means the actual or threatened physical intrusion of a sexual nature, whether by force or under unequal or coercive conditions. Org. Setting and Reporting
The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. The overall objective of the UNEP's Industry and Economy Division is to encourage decision makers in government, local authorities and industry to develop and adopt policies, strategies and practices and technologies that promote sustainable patterns of consumption and production, make efficient use of natural resources, ensure safe management of chemicals and contribute to making trade and environment policies mutually supportive. It promotes the development, use and transfer of policies, technologies, economic instruments, managerial practices and other tools that assist in environmentally sound decision making and the building of corresponding activities. The Chemicals and Health Branch works closely with governments, industry, and civil society organizations around the world to develop mainstream solutions for the sound management of chemicals and waste. As part of the Industry and Economy Division, Chemicals and Health Branch, UNEP International Environmental Technology Centre (IETC) works with developing countries to implement sustainable solutions to environmental challenges, with focus on holistic waste management. IETC provides technical and advisory support to national and local governments to enhance their use of environmentally sound strategies and approaches. IETC also implement in- country demonstration projects using innovative waste prevention and management methods and technologies to improve human well-being, reduce the impact of climate change, increase resilience and create jobs. Working with a wide range of partners and in line with relevant multilateral environmental agreements, IETC mission is to serve as a global center of excellence on environmentally sound technologies with focus on holistic waste management. The position is located in the Industry and Economy Division, Chemicals and Health Branch, IETC at the Osaka duty station in Japan. Under the direct supervision of the Chief, Chemicals and Health Branch, and the additional supervision of the Chief, Industry and Innovation Branch, the incumbent will be responsible for the following duties:
Responsibilities

Ensure UNEP's value for the IETC outlooks provide strategic value for UNEP, member states and other stakeholders. b. Leads the IETC waste strategy to ensure impact at scale on waste reduction and recycling within a circular economy context, where waste becomes a useful resource. c. Ensures up to date waste data and trend analysis using a digital format for assessment and analysis. d. Participates in interagency and partner strategic meetings to scale impact beyond pilot initiatives, which will require leveraging innovative sources of financing and investment. 2) Develops the IETC programme of work arid associated portfolio on waste management in a circular economy context for sectors such as electronics and plastics, and growing this work to textiles and buildings and construction waste: a. Ensures implementation of gender mainstreaming guidelines by assessing the implications for men and women of any planned action, including legislation, policies or programmes, in all areas and at all levels. b. Provides technical guidance on the development of IETC's work program portfolio. c. Directs programme monitoring and oversight and presents information gathered from diverse sources. d. Coordinates policy development; reviews the assessments of issues and trends, preparation of evaluations or research activities and studies. e. Undertakes survey initiatives; guides design of data collection instruments; reviews, analyzes and interprets responses, identifies problems/issues and prepares conclusions. f. Supervises preparation of various written outputs, e.g. background papers, analysis, substantial sections.of reports and studies, inputs to publications. g. Directs substantive support to consultative and other.meetings, conferences; to include proposing agenda topics, identifying participants, preparation of documents and presentations. 3) Ensures quality oversight and supervision of the IETC portfolio. a. Develops and implements an oversight of the portfolio under implementation, with a view towards ensuring impact on the reduction of waste within the context of a circular economy approach. b. Leads field missions, including provision of guidance to external consultants, government officials and other parties with a view to ensuring the impact of the portfolio is at scale. c. Ensures programme and budget and funds use oversight (programme/project preparation.and submissions, progress. reports, financial statements.), reporting and ensuring corrective action across the IETC portfolio. d. Engages across UNEP and with partners to strenghten opportunities for impact on waste in a circular economy context to ensure leveraging of key internal and external actors. e. Ensures effective utilization, supervision and development of staff; Guides, evaluates and mentors staff. 4) Performs other duties as required.
Competencies
Professionalism: Excellent technical, analytical and interpersonal skills. Demonstrates expert knowledge of waste management, waste reduction and recycling, circular economy approaches, and their application across high-impact sectors, including plastics, electronics, textiles, and the built environment. Strong understanding of global environmental trends, waste policies, financing mechanisms, resource efficiency, lifecycle approaches, and the integration of waste considerations into broader sustainable development agendas. Ability to think strategically, and to bring colleagues and management on-board to a strategic vision at the institutional level. Ability to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. Shows pride in work and in achievements. Demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter. Is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results. Is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns. Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Provides leadership and takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work; demonstrates knowledge of strategies and commitment to the goal of gender balance in staffing. Technological awareness: Keeps abreast of available technology. Understands applicability and limitations of technology to the work of the office. Actively seeks to apply technology to appropriate tasks. Shows willingness to learn new technology. Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals. Solicits input by genuinely valuing others' ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others. Places team agenda before personal agenda. Supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position. Shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. Vision: Identifies strategic issues, opportunities and risks. Clearly communicates links between the Organization's strategy and the work unit's goals. Generates and communicates broad and compelling organizational direction, inspiring others to pursue that same direction. Conveys enthusiasm about future possibilities. Building trust: Provides an environment in which others can talk and act without fear of repercussion. Manages in a deliberate and predictable way. Operates with transparency; has no hidden agenda. Places confidence in colleagues, staff members and clients. Gives proper credit to others. Follows through on agreed upon actions. Treats sensitive or confidential information appropriately.
Education
An advanced university degree (Master's degree, or equivalent) is required. At least one university degree in the following fields: engineering, development, environmental or physical sciences, circular economy, material sciences, industrial studies, resource use or supply chain management, is required. A first-level degree (Bachelor's degree or equivalent) in the specified fields of studies with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Successful completion of both degree and non-degree programs in data analytics, business analytics or data science programs is desirable.
Job - Specific Qualification
Not available.
Work Experience
A minimum of ten years of work experience on environment and development issues, with circular economy, resource efficiency or waste management in key high impact sectors (inter alia electronics, plastics, textiles, buildings and construction sectors) is required. Experience in working through partnerships on the above-mentioned topics is required. Experience in programme management is required. Experience in waste, appropriate waste management technologies, waste mandates of relevant Multilateral Environment Agreements (MEAs), applicable funding mechanisms and instruments for waste management is required Experience in resource mobilization, donor engagement, and the development or management of large-scale international programmes and portfolios on waste management, circular economy, or resource efficiency is desirable. Experience in data analytics or related area is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. Either French or Spanish or Arabic or Russian or Chinese (Mandarin) is desirable. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult https://languages.un.org for details).

Org. Setting and Reporting
The Department of Operational Support (DOS) was established to provide end-to-end operational support, advisory services and other solutions to operating entities across the Secretariat, including departments, offices away from headquarters, peace operations, and regional commissions. The Division of Administration (DOA) in New York provides administrative support functions (human resources, budget, finance and general administration) and facility management and commercial services to entities at United Nations Headquarters. It also provides financial operational services to entities across the globe. As Common Administrative Platform, the Division comprises the OneEO, the Financial Operations Service (including OnePayroll), and the Facilities and Commercial Activities Service. This position is located within the Common Administrative Platform at United Nations Headquarters, referred to as the One Executive Office ("One EO"), under the Division of Administration in the Department of Operational Support (DOS). One EO started its transition phase on 1 January 2026 as part of the UN80 reform initiative, which aims to consolidate common administrative functions across Secretariat entities into unified service platforms. One EO provides the full range of administrative and operational services required by New York–based Secretariat client entities to fulfil their mandates, including human resources management, financial administration, travel, and general administrative support. The Associate Human Resources Officer will report directly to the Chief of Unit/desk.
Responsibilities
General: • Provides advice and support to managers and staff on human resources related matters. • Keeps abreast of developments in various areas of human resources. Recruitment and placement: • Reviews requests, signs job offers and coordinates onboarding of new staff. • Prepares and presents cases to appointment and promotion bodies. • Serves as ex-officio in examinations boards. • Monitors the work of the Human Resources Assistants in carrying out all human resources administrative transactions including preparation of personnel actions, transactions related to onboarding and separations, processing of contracts, and others. • Supervises and monitors the work of the human resources assistants in carrying out all human resources transactions related to onboarding, including preparation of personnel actions, onboarding clearances and other. Administration of entitlements: • Administers and provides advice on salary and related benefits, travel and entitlements. • Provides advice on interpretation and application of policies, regulations and rules. vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
The consultant will be responsible for contributing to the preparation of the Accessible-Ready Housing Guidance package and advocacy efforts, and for leading consultation and partner engagement processes. Under the guidance of the UN-Habitat Canada Office team, the consultant will ensure that the diverse perspectives and experiences of persons with disabilities meaningfully inform future refinement of the Accessible-Ready Housing Standard by managing co-creation activities, accessibility-focused policy analysis, and contributions to prototype development, checklists, and process maps. This contribution will support UN-Habitat Canada’s housing programme and contribute to national and global knowledge exchange on accessible housing and standards development.
Work Location
Montreal
Expected duration
6 months
Duties and Responsibilities
UN-Habitat is the agency for human settlements. It is mandated by the UN General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities with the goal of providing adequate shelter for all. UN-Habitat Canada Office strengthens the organization’s mission by serving as a focal point for partnerships, applied research, and policy engagement in Canada and across North America for the implementation of UN-Habitat’s 2026-2029 Strategic Plan. Operating from the City of Montreal, the office plays a central role in four domains: partner engagement and resource mobilization; research-policy-action interface; advocacy and communication; and the advancement of sustainable urbanization agendas within the Canadian and North American context. The UN-Habitat Canada Office places particular emphasis on knowledge and innovation with a view to accelerating housing solutions that are affordable, adequate, resilient, and compatible with national and global commitments. In alignment with its housing and urban development priorities, the Canada Office also contributes to UN-Habitat’s global efforts to strengthen intergovernmental dialogue and cooperation on housing in close cooperation with UN-Habitat's Land, Housing and Shelter Section in Nairobi, Kenya. This includes supporting the work of the Open-Ended Intergovernmental Expert Working Group on Adequate Housing for All (OWEG-H), which aims to advance a shared understanding and actionable recommendations for realizing the right to adequate housing within the framework of the New Urban Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. Through evidence-based research, policy engagement, and partnership-building, the Canada Office helps ensure that global innovations and lessons inform and enrich the OEWG-H’s deliberations and outputs. As part of its housing programme, the UN Habitat Canada Office is implementing a project on Accessible Ready Housing in Canada to advance inclusive design, standards and practice. The UN-Habitat Canada Office is seeking a motivated, highly skilled, and experienced mid-level professionals to join the project team as the Housing Accessibility Standards Specialist. The position is initially offered as a six-month contract, with the possibility of extension based on a positive performance evaluation. The Housing Accessibility Standards Specialist will support the development of the Accessible-Ready Housing Guidance Package, contribute to the engagement and co-creation with municipalities, persons with disabilities and their organizations (OPDs), conduct applied research on accessibility standards and policies in Canada and internationally and support project management in ensuring project delivery and workflow during the period of employment. The consultant will support the project management team in national and international advocacy efforts, prepare meetings of the project advisory committee, facilitate workshops and webinars, contribute to the development of training materials, organize project related events, and coordinate inputs between the Guidance Package and the Design Compendium to ensure that design strategies and policy pathways are aligned and mutually inform each other. Further, the consultant will contribute to ensuring consistent documentation and version control of all project materials. Reporting line This on-site position is fulltime, and is based in Montreal, Canada. This position reports directly to the Head of Office of the UN-Habitat Canada Office (or a designated supervisor). Applicants must be Canadian residents or citizens or have permission to work in Canada. Duties and Responsibilities The consultant will carry out the following tasks and responsibilities: 1. Contribute to the development of the Accessible-Ready Housing Guidance Package, ensuring that accessibility barriers and solutions identified by persons with disabilities are meaningfully reflected in standards review recommendations. 2. Contribute to consultations and co-creation processes with persons with disabilities, OPDs, Indigenous disability organizations, municipal staff, and technical experts to gather evidence on accessibility challenges across planning, permitting, and regulatory systems, to validate findings and ensure accessibility perspectives are central to the Guidance Package. 3. Analyze feedback from consultations to formulate standard and policy reformulation recommendations identifying systemic barriers, regulatory gaps, and opportunities and ensure alignment of co-creation inputs with prototype layouts by providing accessibility-focused interpretation of spatial, regulatory, and usability challenges 4. Contribute to the mapping of municipal, provincial, and federal regulatory workflows, identifying where accessibility considerations are overlooked or insufficiently integrated through reporting, compliance, and monitoring. 5. Contribute to reviewing feasibility and cost considerations from an accessibility perspective, identifying how design, regulatory, or financial barriers disproportionately affect persons with disabilities. 6. Contribute to developing knowledge and training products in accessible formats, plain-language summaries, and dissemination materials for national and international events (e.g., State of Cities Summit, WUF14), including visualizations, diagrams. 7. Prepare regular progress reports and contribute to the Canada Office’s housing programme and global knowledge exchange. 8. Support project management, knowledge management, coordination, and administrative tasks. 9. Contribute to strategic partnerships and alliances with academic institutions, housing design and standards agencies, Indigenous and community-based organizations, and international partners. 10. Contribute to resource mobilization and proposal development efforts related to housing research, innovation, and accessible housing solutions. 11. Provide support preparing inputs for major global events, including the World Urban Forum, the High-Level Political Forum and other key international convenings.
Qualifications/special skills
A Master’s degree in Social Policy, Architecture, Urban Planning, Housing Policy, or a closely related field, with demonstrated experience in leading community engagement and co-creation processes and translating results into policy-relevant recommendations is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Persons with lived experiences are strongly encouraged to apply for the position. Desirable specializations include demonstrated familiarity with the Canadian housing, planning, and building regulatory context (federal, provincial, and municipal jurisdictional divisions), as well as accessibility policy, disability inclusion, inclusive design, housing, or a closely related field. A minimum of 2 years of experience in accessibility policy, disability inclusion, inclusive design, housing, or a closely related field is required. Demonstrated experience designing or facilitating accessible and inclusive engagement processes with persons with disabilities and/or Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) is required. Knowledge of disability-inclusive and rights-based approaches to housing and the built environment, including the diversity of accessibility needs across disability groups is required. Demonstrated ability to conduct applied research on housing adequacy — including cultural adequacy, accessibility, and climate-smart housing — and to synthesize and present complex information in formats accessible to policymakers, practitioners, and diverse audiences is required. Experience translating stakeholder and lived-experience evidence into policy, regulatory, or practical guidance is desirable. Experience in accessible, adaptable, and/or universal housing design approaches and relevant Canadian or international standards and precedents, analyzing and applying frameworks or standards related to accessible, inclusive, and culturally responsive housing design and policy is desirable. Strong report writing, reviewing, and editorial skills are highly desirable. Progressively responsible work experience at the national or international level in the field of accessibility or housing systems, sustainable urban development, and knowledge management is desirable. Experience working with persons with disabilities and their organizations, Indigenous or community-led housing initiatives, or in culturally diverse contexts, is an asset. Experience working in the United Nations Common System or other international organizations is desirable.
Languages
English and French are the official working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this position, fluency in spoken and written English is required. Proficiency and/or fluency in French is highly desirable, and knowledge of another official UN language is considered an asset.
Additional Information
Not available.
No Fee

Contribute to the development of architectural typologies and site/building/unit-level spatial strategies aligned with accessible-ready design principles and recommendations synthesized from desk review (Phase 1) which will be provided as starting input, identifying a representative set of housing typologies for prototype development. 5. Support the integration of Accessible-Ready Standard requirements into spatial layouts, design criteria, and technical annotations. 6. Support developing and integrating adaptation pathways demonstrating how Accessible-Ready dwellings can respond to diverse or successively changing accessibility needs, distinguishing between features provided at initial construction and those intended to enable future modification. 7. The United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is mandated by the UN General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities. UN-Habitat is the focal point for all urbanization and human settlement matters within the UN system. UN-Habitat works with partners to build inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable cities and communities. UN-Habitat promotes urbanization as a positive transformative force for people and communities, reducing inequality, discrimination and poverty. UN-Habitat, as the lead agency for sustainable urbanization within the UN system, plays a pivotal role in South Africa's journey toward achieving its development goals. The Habitat Country Programme Document (HCPD) for South Africa 2024-2028 has been crafted to align UN-Habitat’s global expertise with the country's priorities, building upon a longstanding partnership with the Government of South Africa. This collaboration aims to address the challenges and opportunities of urbanization, ensuring cities and human settlements are inclusive, safe, resilient, and sustainable, in line with SDG 11. By working closely with the United Nations Country Team (UNCT) and under the framework of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF), the HCPD integrates urban themes into the national agenda. This approach emphasizes sustainable human settlements, affordable housing, and resilient infrastructure, guided by South Africa's National Development Plan (NDP) 2030 and the Integrated Urban Development Framework (IUDF). The HCPD serves as a platform to enhance collaboration between UN-Habitat, South African institutions, and diverse partners such as NGOs, academia, and private sector stakeholders. vacancies.jobTitle: Consultant to develop a new version of the Economywide Trade Simulator GETSI for Bahrain
vacancies.jobDescription:
Result of Service
The consultant will develop a national version of Economy wide Trade Simulator Interface for Bahrain. The required outputs to be delivered by the consultant are the following: The new global database to be used for the calibration of the national GETSI for Bahrain. The gams code for the calibrated GETSI Bahrain The required files for uploading the model on GAMS-MIRO.
Work Location
Remote
Expected duration
3.5 months
Duties and Responsibilities
Scope and Objectives Decision-makers require advanced tools that provide real-time, data-driven insights to effectively design optimal economic policies. The United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA) has been at the forefront of developing cutting-edge simulation tools to support Arab countries in aligning their trade policies with broader economic objectives and long-term national visions. One such tool is a user-friendly trade simulator that enables non-specialist trade experts and negotiators across the Arab region to utilize customized global Computable General Equilibrium (CGE) models for exante economic assessments of policy changes at national, regional, and global levels. At the request of the Ministry of Industry and Commerce of Bahrain, to develop a tailored version of the Global Economywide Trade Simulator Interface (GETSI) for Bahrain. The interface facilitates forward-looking analysis, particularly in evaluating the potential impacts of new trade agreements currently under negotiation as well as regional and global economic shocks and changes in global trade landscape. It will include specific sectoral and geographical disaggregation’s as well as updated baseline scenario, and policy instruments. Duties and responsibilities Based on the outcomes of discussions between ESCWA and the Ministry of Industry of Bahrain, the purpose of this consultancy is to develop a tailored version of the global CGE model for Bahrain to be used to develop the simulator interface on GAMS-MIRO. The consultant is expected to undertake the following tasks: Aggregate the GTAP 12 database to the sectoral and geographical dimensions agreed on with the Ministry of Industry of Bahrain. Calibrate (statistic calibration) the global CGE model with the new global database for all countries and regions individually integrated in the database. Calibrate the baseline scenario (dynamic calibration) for all countries and regions individually considered in the database using latest forecasts on GDP, population, labor supply, and productivity changes for the period 2024-2035. Test the functioning of the dynamic model through concrete simulations. Assist ESCWA’s project coordinator in preparing the required files for uploading the model into GAMS-MIRO platform. If required, support capacity-building sessions to the national team lead by the Ministry of Industry.
Qualifications/special skills
A Master's degree in applied economics or related area is required. A PhD is desirable. All candidates must submit a copy of the required educational degree. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed. A minimum of 10 years of experience in developing and applying global dynamic CGE models using GAMS is required. Proven experience in working with GTAP database is required. Hands-on experience in calibrating and running global CGE models and proficiency in GAMS and its applications in global CGE modeling is required. Knowledge of MIRO interface design and best practices in user interaction for economic modeling tools is desirable.
Languages

The Administration and Conference Management Division (ACMD) is headed by a Director and reports to the Deputy Executive Secretary (Programme Support). It is divided into seven main sections: Facilities Management Section (FMS), Finance and Budget Section (FBS), Digital and IT Management Section (DITMS), Human Resources Management Section (HRMS), Publications and Conference Management Section (PCMS), Supply Chain Management Section (SCMS) and United Nations Health Care Centre (UNHCC). Competencies

Org. Setting and Reporting
The United Nations Environment Programme is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. This position is located in the Executive Office of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) in Nairobi, Kenya. The incumbent reports to the Chief of Staff and will work in close coordination and collaboration with the relevant offices on the following responsibilities;
Responsibilities
1. Conduct and Discipline • Coordinate awareness initiatives and facilitate training (with the support of the Corporate Services Division) to ensure all personnel understand their conduct obligations, with a focus on discrimination, harassment, and abuse of authority. • Serve as an initial point of contact for the receipt of concerns of misconduct related to UNEP personnel and provide preliminary procedural information and guidance. Conduct initial assessments and advise complainants on appropriate mechanisms to address allegations appropriately. • Maintain confidential records relating to conduct and discipline matters within UNEP; support the identification of emerging trends; and contribute to the preparation of periodic reports, including the Annual Report on Conduct and Discipline, in collaboration with the Legal Section in Corporate Services Division. • Provide legal advice to the Executive Director on conduct and discipline matters, which will include providing recommendations to address systemic issues. • Liaise and coordinate, as appropriate: (i) within UNEP on conduct and discipline issues, including with the Legal Section, the Human Resources Section, as appropriate, and (ii) with other relevant UN Secretariat entities such as the UN Staff Counsellor, the Ethics Office, the Office of the Ombudsman and Mediation Services and OIOS. • Fulfil the responsibilities of the Conduct and Discipline Focal Point, as appointed by the Executive Director in accordance with ST/SGB/2019/8, “Addressing discrimination, harassment, including sexual harassment, and abuse of authority”. 2. Risk Management • Support the Chief Risk Officer and his/her alternate and the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Secretariat in accordance with United Nations Secretariat risk-management policies, standards and guidance and contribute to the implementation and continuous improvement of UNEP’s ERM framework, by: • Preparing and compiling documentation and guidance materials for ERM Committee meetings and providing administrative, analytical and coordination support to discussions concerning risk prioritisation, mitigation measures and planning horizons. • Supporting the preparation of periodic risk reports for consideration by the Executive Director, the Senior Management Team, the ERM Committee and UNEP’s governing bodies. • Updating of risk-management tools in line with United Nations Secretariat standards. • Collaborating with internal audit, ethics, legal, compliance, programme quality assurance and other relevant functions to support the review and effectiveness of risk mitigation measures. • Supporting efforts to promote a risk-aware culture across UNEP through training, communication and engagement activities, and contributing to capacity-building initiatives that assist personnel and partners in identifying and managing risks effectively. 3. Grievance Redress • In accordance with UNEP’s Stakeholder Response Mechanism Standard Operating Procedures, support the monitoring and receipt of complaints and undertake initial eligibility screening for further review. • Provide analysis and advice on possible protective measures to assess and minimise risks of retaliation against complainants or other participants in Stakeholder Response Mechanism processes, for consideration by responsible decision-makers. • Explain the Stakeholder Response Mechanism process, as needed, to potentially affected persons, complainants and other relevant stakeholders. • Maintain and update a roster of independent experts and consultants who may be engaged to support compliance reviews and dispute-resolution processes; contribute to the preparation of Terms of Reference for such assignments; and provide administrative, substantive and coordination support in relation to consultants engaged for these processes. • Support the preparation of reports for consideration by the Executive Director setting out findings and recommendations arising from compliance reviews and documenting the outcomes of dispute-resolution processes. Assist in monitoring and documenting the implementation of decisions taken by the Executive Director in relation to compliance reviews and dispute-resolution outcomes. • Maintain up-to-date information on the publicly accessible Stakeholder Response Mechanism website and Case Registry, including summaries of cases submitted directly through the Mechanism and through UNEP projects, in accordance with applicable confidentiality, data-protection and disclosure requirements. • Support the processing, tracking, documentation and archiving of eligible grievance cases through the Case Management System, in accordance with the Organization’s applicable records and information-management requirements. • Contribute to annual reporting on stakeholder complaints to the Executive Director, including through the compilation and analysis of systemic observations, trends and lessons learned from cases handled. • Support the review and updating of UNEP policies and procedures relating to the Stakeholder Response Mechanism, as required. • Collects and analyzes data to identify trends or patterns and provide insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. • Performs other duties as required
Competencies
Professionalism: Knowledge of, and ability to apply, legal principles, concepts and procedures and terminology for review, examination, and processing of a range of legal documents. Knowledge of various legal research sources, including electronic, and ability to conduct research and analyze information on a wide range of legal issues. Knowledge of the civil law and/or common law legal systems and principles. Ability to interpret and apply legislative instruments, develop and present results, recommendations, and opinions clearly and concisely. Ability to draft legal papers and work under pressure. Ability to apply good legal judgment in the context of assignments given. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Ability to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. Planning& Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. Client Orientation: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client
Education
An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in law or related field is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two (2) additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Successful completion of both degree and non-degree programs in data analytics, business analytics ordata science programs is desirable
Job - Specific Qualification
Academic or professional training in one or more of the following areas is desirable: administrative law, environmental and social safeguards, conduct and discipline, enterprise risk management, grievance redress, dispute resolution or compliance.
Work Experience
A minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible professional legal experience, advisory services, compliance, administration, programme management or a related field is required. Experience in supporting work in one or more of the following areas is required: conduct and discipline, enterprise risk management, grievance redress or accountability mechanisms, environmental and social safeguards, ethics, compliance or human resources policy. Experience in gathering and analysing information, preparing legal or policy advice, drafting reports and recommendations, and supporting the resolution of complex or sensitive matters is desirable. Experience working on confidential or sensitive cases, including the application of appropriate information-management and data-protection requirements, is desirable. Experience supporting coordination among legal, human resources, ethics, oversight, risk management, programme or compliance functions is desirable. Experience with stakeholder grievance mechanisms, dispute-resolution processes, compliance reviews or environmental and social accountability frameworks is desirable. Experience in the United Nations Common System or a comparable international, intergovernmental, public-sector or non-profit organization is desirable. Experience working in a multicultural setting is desirable. Two (2) years or more of experience in data analytics or related area is desirable.

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. The term “sexual exploitation” means any actual or attempted abuse of a position of vulnerability, differential power, or trust, for sexual purposes, including, but not limited to, profiting monetarily, socially or politically from the sexual exploitation of another. The term “sexual abuse” means the actual or threatened physical intrusion of a sexual nature, whether by force or under unequal or coercive conditions. The term “sexual harassment” means any unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature that might reasonably be expected or be perceived to cause offence or humiliation, when such conduct interferes with work, is made a condition of employment or creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, and when the gravity of the conduct warrants the termination of the perpetrator’s working relationship. Result of Service
